August's `tool_search` → `tool_call` route is the same idea at a different layer.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **Every tool carries provenance** — `packages/coding-agent/test/agent-session-dynamic-tools.test.ts:149-160` — `sourceInfo: { path, source: "builtin" | "inline" | "sdk", scope, origin }`. A UI can show where a tool came from, and a policy layer can decide per source. August already has per-tool capability rules; attaching provenance to the tool object is the missing half.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **The model can discover its own run context from the tool environment** — `packages/coding-agent/test/agent-session-dynamic-tools.test.ts:76-95` — the bash tool's child process gets `PI_SESSION_ID`, `PI_SESSION_FILE`, `PI_PROVIDER`, `PI_MODEL`, `PI_REASONING_LEVEL`, and the system prompt tells the model so. An opt-out (`exposeSessionEnvironment: false`) removes all five. This moves five facts out of the prompt and into the environment, where they cost nothing per turn.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **A display preference must not change what a tool did** — `packages/coding-agent/test/block-images.test.ts:73` and `:114` — the read tool and the CLI file processor always return image content; the `blockImages` filter is applied at the `convertToLlm` layer. August's `blockImages` equivalent (if any) must live at the same boundary, or a "show me images" toggle will silently change the tool result the model sees.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **Strictness is a provider-side conversion, not a schema change** — `packages/coding-agent/test/builtin-tool-strict-mode.test.ts:29-31` — `constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" }` is set on the five file-affecting built-ins while the **execution schema's `required` list is unchanged**, and `grep`/`find`/`ls` get nothing. The wire hint and the runtime validation are different contracts and the test pins them apart, so tightening one cannot quietly tighten the other.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **Do not report success for a write you could not verify** — `packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard.test.ts:197-207` — a local Linux failure **throws** rather than falling through to an OSC 52 escape that might not have been delivered; the same code path in a *remote* session does fall through, because there OSC 52 is the only transport (`:310-316`). Oversized payloads are refused outright (`:317-325`). August's `scrubOutboundBody` and the `is_error`/receipt vocabulary have the same shape of bug class: a marker that reads as success when it is not.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **A flag never consumes the next option as its value, and unknown flags are captured rather than rejected** — `packages/coding-agent/test/args.test.ts:182-188` and `:533-546` — `parseArgs(["--mode", "--version"])` reports "--mode requires text, json, or rpc" *and* still parses `--version`; an unknown `--flag value` lands in an `unknownFlags` map so a wrapper can forward it. August's own CLI is not the reference here, but the *rule* — an option-looking token is never a value — is a cheap correctness win.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **A "committed artifact" gate that compares byte for byte and names the command that fixes it** — `packages/coding-agent/test/config-schemas.test.ts:41-46` — the failure message is *"schemas/models.schema.json is stale; run npm run generate:schemas"*. August's `check:docs` and `check:brain-config` are the same genre; the transferable refinement is that the *generated* artifact is compared to the *committed* one, so "somebody edited the JSON by hand" and "the generator changed" are the same failure with one remedy.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **A reachability census, not a link check** — `packages/coding-agent/test/documentation.test.ts:150-185` — the gate walks from the `docs.json` navigation root through local markdown links (harvested with **marked's own lexer**, so a link in a code fence is not counted) and then fails if any `*.md` under `docs/` is unreachable, if a nav path is duplicated, if a public slug collides, or if a link is broken. The idea generalises to any "is this thing still reachable?" question August asks — a docs page, a skill, a brain key, a tool — and the implementation trick (use the *renderer's* lexer, not a regex) is what makes it accurate.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **A settled result must not force a full terminal redraw, and the preview must be reconstructible from the settled result alone** — `packages/coding-agent/test/edit-tool-no-full-redraw.test.ts:144-145` and `:153-200` — the second test deletes the file before the component settles, and the diff still renders, because the diff lives in the tool result's `details` and not in a live re-read. August's transcript re-renders on every stream chunk; the "reconstructible from the settled result" property is what lets a renderer skip work.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **Collapsed output is capped by WRAPPED lines, not logical lines** — `packages/coding-agent/test/codemode-renderer.test.ts:94-112` — 1 000 characters at width 50 is 20 visual lines, and the cap counts those. A logical-line cap would let one long line blow past the cap. August's collapsed tool output has the same choice to make, and the wrong answer is invisible until a user pastes a 200 KB single-line log.
- **[coding-agent-tests#1]** - **A running duration and a finished duration are worded differently** — `packages/coding-agent/test/codemode-renderer.test.ts:115-129` — "Elapsed 3.0s" while the script runs, "Took 5.1s" once it has settled, and "Elapsed" disappears entirely. The same distinction August already makes in the transcript ("Running a command 1m 18s" versus a settled line with no duration) — the test pins it so a refactor cannot quietly unify the two. ---
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **Capture what the subprocess SAW, and write the capture before the failure branch** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/fake-external-editor.mjs:11` — the fixture records `filePath`, `content`, `entries`, `directoryMode` to a capture file *before* it honours `--fail` (line 22), so a non-zero exit is still a fully observable round-trip. August runs approval surfaces, tool processes and MCP servers the same way; asserting only on the exit code throws away everything the callee knew. Port this shape: every external-process boundary in August should have a "what did it see" probe written before the failure branch.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **Assert the mode of a scratch directory, not only the file it contains** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/fake-external-editor.mjs:17` — `statSync(directory).mode & 0o777` lets the test assert `mode & 0o077 === 0` on POSIX (`external-editor.test.ts:46-48`). August writes prompts, patch previews and terminal buffers into temp directories; a `0700` assertion is the cheapest possible check that a credential-bearing temp file is not world-readable, and it is a single line to add to any door that materialises sensitive text on disk.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **The compaction summary is a fixed skeleton with `User Preferences` and `Commands` as first-class sections** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/before-compaction.jsonl:360` (first summary) and `:629` (second) — both are `# Context Checkpoint` → `## Branch` → `## Goal` → `## Key Decisions Made` → `## Completed Work` (a WP table) → `## Files Created/Modified` → `## Next Steps` → `## Key Files` → `## User Preferences` → `## Commands`. The lesson for August is *which* sections survive a compaction: the standing preferences ("E2E tests only", "keep old code working alongside new code") and the exact commands (`npm run check`) are the facts that must not be lost, while the narrative is what may be. August's `<<compressed_summary` note currently squeezes predecessors into 600 chars of prose; a section skeleton with dedicated `Preferences` and `Commands` slots would be strictly better than prose.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **A compaction cut may land mid-turn, and the surviving pointer is a user message** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/before-compaction.jsonl:360` (`firstKeptEntryIndex: 293`) and `:629` (`firstKeptEntryIndex: 551`) — both indexes resolve to a **user** message, never to a tool result, and both sit *before* the compaction record in the log. The rule in the code is explicit: cut points may be user or assistant messages but "never tool results" (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts:436-437`). August's compaction rotates and replays a verbatim head; the transferable invariant is that **the replayed head must start at a turn boundary, never at an orphaned tool result** — a head that begins with a tool result is exactly the pairing bug August's `_compactionCall` has to avoid.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **A positional pointer rewritten into a stable id by the migration, not by the writer** — `packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts:301-311` (exercised by the fixture at `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/before-compaction.jsonl:360`) — `migrateV1ToV2` converts `firstKeptEntryIndex` → `firstKeptEntryId` by indexing the *already-migrated* array and deleting the old field. When August changes how its `messages`/`turn_outcomes` rows are addressed (and it will), the conversion has to happen in the migration, keyed on the new id, and the old positional form has to be deleted — a file that keeps both fields is a file with two truths about where the live context starts.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **Truncate the tool result in the transcript and keep the full output in a file** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/before-compaction.jsonl:1002` — a `bashExecution` entry with a 51,199-character `output`, `truncated: true`, and a `fullOutputPath`; the sibling `ls` entries at `:640` and `:997` carry `truncated: false` and no path. The transcript stays small, the bytes stay reachable, and the *fact of truncation* is persisted rather than inferred from a length. August's tool-result truncation currently has to invent its own marker; pi's triple (`truncated` boolean + `fullOutputPath` + the message type that owns both) is a schema worth copying.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **Give every ambient layer a designated empty fixture** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/empty-agent/.gitkeep` and `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/empty-cwd/.gitkeep`, consumed at `packages/coding-agent/test/skills.test.ts:349-350` — the loader reads `<agentDir>/skills` and `<cwd>/.pi/skills` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/skills.ts:458-459`); passing two empty directories is what makes "exactly one skill" a fact instead of a hope about the developer's machine. August's skill catalogue reads `<dataDir>/skills`, `<dataDir>/bots/<id>/skills` and `<workspace>/.aug/skills` — that is at least three ambient layers, and each needs the same designated empty stand-in, plus an assertion that the layer's *scope* is what got loaded (`skills[0].sourceInfo.scope === "temporary"`).
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **A stored format keeps keys the reader no longer declares — and the fixture proves it** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/before-compaction.jsonl:1` (header carries `provider`, `modelId`, `thinkingLevel`, `branchedFrom`) vs `packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts:43-50` (`SessionHeader` declares only `type`/`version?`/`id`/`timestamp`/`cwd`/`parentSession?`) — the extra keys are silently ignored on load. August's `providers.json`, `config.json` and `secrets.json` readers should be checked against the same rule: an unknown key in a stored file is a compatibility bug that nobody will notice until the format has already moved on.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **Ship a captured real session as the golden artifact, not a synthetic one** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/before-compaction.jsonl` — the fixture is a genuine 1,003-entry pi run (real tool calls, real thinking blocks with signatures, real `usage`/`cost` on every assistant turn, real model and thinking-level switches, real compactions), and it contains **no credentials** despite containing real source code. The transferable decision is the *scrubbing policy*: a captured transcript is committable only because the credential-shaped content was checked; August, which stores transcripts in a database, should adopt the same check as a gate rather than as a habit.
- **[coding-agent-tests#2]** - **A fixture census is a gate, not a lint** — `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/before-compaction.jsonl` is referenced by nothing (repo-wide grep for `before-compaction` → 0 hits outside the file), while its sibling `packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/large-session.jsonl` is referenced at `packages/coding-agent/test/compaction.test.ts:35`. August already has the shape of this gate (`test_exactly_one_site_builds_a_compaction_request`, which also asserts its census is non-empty); the same census over the fixture directory would have caught 2.37 MB of dead weight in pi and would catch the same class of drift in August.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A committed baseline for an upstream conformance suite, where a newly-failing check breaks the build and a newly-passing check is only reported** - `packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-conformance/run.ts:339` - pi runs the official MCP conformance suite per protocol version and diffs every check against a committed `baseline.json`. The run fails when a baseline-passing check regresses, when a check fails that the baseline does not list, and when a baselined scenario did not run; a check that *starts* passing is reported so a human can lock it in (`README.md:25`). For August this is the shape of "we know our provider gateways are broken in these nine specific ways" — a file that records known-bad provider behaviour so a new provider SDK release turns into a diff instead of a mystery. Transfer it as a generated-but-committed expectations file plus a three-way diff rule (regression = fail, improvement = report, known-failure = visible).
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **One in-flight refresh shared by many callers, with per-caller abort** - `packages/coding-agent/test/model-catalog-refresh.test.ts:38` - `refreshModelCatalogs(runtime, signal)` coalesces concurrent callers onto a single `runtime.refresh()`; a caller that aborts rejects with `AbortError` but the shared refresh's own signal stays un-aborted while another caller is still waiting, and a refresh with no remaining waiters *is* aborted and a later one may start. August's provider/model refresh and its "re-check the catalog" button have exactly this shape; this is the reference implementation of "one door, many callers, cancel only when nobody is left".
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A turn-outcome reporter that reports only the outcome, never the content** - `packages/coding-agent/test/program-status-reporter.test.ts:67` - the reporter is a small state machine over `agent_start` / `message_end` / `compaction_end` / `agent_settled`: a retried error that later succeeds reports `done`, only the final error reports `error` (with the first line of the message), and an abort reports `idle`. The status object never carries model output (`expect(JSON.stringify(reports)).not.toContain("secret assistant output")`, line 64). August's `turn_outcomes` row and its amber stop-reason badge are the same idea, and the "never carry the content" rule is the part that keeps an external status surface safe to display.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **Availability published *before* the credential write resolves, and a failed post-login refresh that does not roll the credential back** - `packages/coding-agent/test/model-runtime-credential-sync.test.ts:63` and `:353` - `hasConfiguredAuth` and the availability snapshot flip as soon as the local operation succeeds, not when the whole promise settles, and same-provider credential operations are serialised. When the *post-login* catalog refresh fails, the error is a typed `CredentialSynchronizationError` but the credential remains stored. August's login/logout path needs both halves: the UI must not show a half-applied provider, and a failed refresh must not log the user out of a credential that actually succeeded.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **An MCP-style connection that degrades to "disconnected" and transparently reconnects on the next call, while a shape error (HTTP 400) fails permanently and a transient error (503) is retried** - `packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-extension.test.ts:598` and `:614` - the connection state machine distinguishes "the transport dropped" (recoverable: the next call reconnects, `opened() === 2`) from "the request was malformed" (fatal: state `failed`, one open attempt). Resource reads are retried after a transient error but **tool calls are not**, because a retried tool call could double-apply a side effect. August's terminal, MCP and provider transports should classify the same way: retry what is safe to repeat, never retry a mutation.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **Extension dialogs stack instead of replacing each other** - `packages/coding-agent/test/interactive-mode-extension-dialogs.test.ts:66` - a second confirm or inline component is shown *on top of* the first; answering it restores the first, whose promise then settles (regression #11166: "a second dialog replaced the first one and the first promise never settled"). An `AbortSignal` removes a hidden dialog without disturbing the one above it, and focus returns to the editor when the stack empties. August's approval/permission dialogs and the "one modal at a time" pattern have exactly this failure mode — a swallowed promise is an approval that never arrives.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **Re-check availability *after* an await, because the state can change while you wait** - `packages/coding-agent/test/interactive-mode-tree-navigation.test.ts:126` - the tree-navigation flow aborts the running response and then re-reads the busy flag, because compaction can start during the abort; the earlier check (before the await) was the bug. When the operation is busy, the rejection is reported as an error and the *active* operation's UI is left completely untouched (#9178: no status indicator created or cleared, the editor's escape handler not replaced, the leaf not moved). August's turn/compaction interlock has the same race and the same "do not disturb the running UI" requirement.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **Compaction is prepared from the *edited projection*, not from the transcript** - `packages/coding-agent/test/session-context-edit.test.ts:348` - a message removed from the model's view by `appendContextEdit(id, null)` is also absent from `prepareCompaction`'s summary input, and the original entry is still in the transcript untouched. A context edit is a separate entry; the latest edit per target wins, so an edit is undoable by a later edit. August's context relief ("edit what the model sees, keep the record") must prepare its summary from the same projection, or compaction silently re-admits the content that was just excluded.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A hard argument/error budget on a tool's own nested calls, with unfinished calls marked as such** - `packages/coding-agent/test/nested-tool-calls.test.ts:210` - `NESTED_CALL_LIMITS` caps the number of recorded calls, truncates each error to `maxErrorChars`, and imposes a 32 KiB total-argument budget; once the budget is exhausted, later calls keep their status but **lose their arguments**, and calls that never finished are marked `status: "unfinished"` with `complete: false`. That is a precise answer to "how much of a nested tool's internals may enter the transcript", which August's transcript has to decide too — the answer here is: bounded, and honest about what was dropped.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A size-capped system-prompt section that tells the model to *search* for what was omitted** - `packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-extension.test.ts:859` - `renderServersSection` never exceeds `MAX_SERVERS_SECTION_CHARS`; when the names alone do not fit, the tail is replaced with `- … N more servers; find their tools with searchTools()`. August's progressive-disclosure tool surface has the same shape, and the important detail is the *handoff*: the model is told which door to use for what it cannot see.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **Per-model, per-field settings resolution where zero is a value and an exact key beats a wildcard** - `packages/coding-agent/test/settings-manager-compaction.test.ts:16` and `:45` - `reserveTokens` and `keepRecentTokens` resolve independently through global → project → model override, the model key must match `provider/modelId` exactly (a `provider/*` wildcard exists but loses to an exact match), and **0 is a legitimate value** rather than "unset". August's brain-config keys have exactly this hazard (`0 = off` versus `absent`), and the field-level independence is what stops a project override from clobbering an unrelated global field.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **Settings writes preserve external edits by tracking which fields the session touched** - `packages/coding-agent/test/settings-manager-bug.test.ts:6` - the fix is stated in the file's own header: "The fix tracks which fields were explicitly modified during the session, and only those fields override file values during save()." Without it, changing the theme in the UI reverted a `packages` array the user had edited by hand. August writes `settings.json` and `providers.json` from the same process that reads them, and has the same last-writer-wins hazard.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A protocol negotiation whose result changes the wire format, pinned end to end** - `packages/coding-agent/test/model-catalog-protocol.test.ts:110` - the client asks for `types=chat,image,classifier` plus its `pi-version`; the server answers with the newest catalog revision the client satisfies; a revision that predates typed shards falls back to the chat-only shard, and the model's `api`/`baseUrl` — and therefore the final provider URL (`/api/v1/messages` vs `/api/v1/chat/completions`) — come from that revision. August's per-model `apiFormat` work is the same negotiation, and this test is the proof that the negotiated value actually reaches the wire.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **An ambiguity is reported, never resolved by catalog order** - `packages/coding-agent/test/model-resolver.test.ts:542` - when the same model id exists behind two providers and neither is authenticated, the error names both (`"openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, vercel-ai-gateway/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5"`) instead of picking the first; a stored credential may disambiguate, but an inline `--api-key` may not ("--api-key does not choose a provider."). August's gateway/priority work has the identical ambiguity when two providers expose the same model id.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A per-provider compat decision applied to *every* model kind** - `packages/coding-agent/test/model-runtime-classifiers.test.ts:88` and `packages/coding-agent/test/model-runtime-images.test.ts:107` - the image encoding of a request (`image_url` inside `state` vs `assets`) is a per-provider compat flag, and it applies to classifier models exactly as it does to chat models; an extension's model list replaces the undeclared models **of every operation**, so declaring only chat models removes the provider's built-in image models. August's provider adapters need the same "one compat table, applied to every model kind" rule, or the kinds drift apart.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A single-flight token refresh across processes** - `packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-oauth-refresh.test.ts:54` - three processes that share a credential file and a lock directory see the same token rejected, but the server rotates refresh tokens, so only **one** refresh may happen; the others wait for the running refresh to persist the new tokens and the lock is released. August's multi-process case (an unattended Bot plus the desktop app, or two workers on one credential store) needs the same lock, or the second refresh will fail with `invalid_grant`.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **stdout is a protocol surface** - `packages/coding-agent/test/stdout-cleanliness.test.ts:100` - with stdout redirected, `--help` prints "Usage:" to stdout, but `--mode json --help` keeps stdout **completely empty** and routes even the usage text to stderr, because a package install prints "changed 1 package in 471ms" during startup and that would corrupt a JSON consumer's stream. August's `/v1` adapters and CLI modes have the same obligation, and the fixture shows the real hazard is third-party chatter, not pi's own output.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A skill's description is the trigger, and a missing description is fatal while a name mismatch is not** - `packages/coding-agent/test/skills.test.ts:44` and `:77` - a skill whose frontmatter name differs from its directory loads without complaint; an invalid name and an over-long name are warnings; but a **missing description** means the skill is not loaded at all, because the description is the only thing the model sees before it decides to open the skill. August's `SKILL.md` spec should adopt the same grading, and the "first loaded wins + a warning naming the other path" collision rule (`skills.test.ts:405`).
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A single-flight refresh that is aborted only when no caller is left** and **a credential store that masks rather than mutates** - `packages/coding-agent/test/runtime-credentials.test.ts:7` - a runtime API key overrides the stored credential for the process without ever persisting it, `list()` exposes only `{ providerId, type }`, and a cancelled `delete` leaves the runtime override in place. August's `scrubOutboundBody` and the credential store want the same property: an override must not reach the file, and an enumeration must not leak a key.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **Extension packages that declare the host as a dependency are warned about, with the reason spelled out** - `packages/coding-agent/test/resource-loader.test.ts:59` - the warning says the host must be in `peerDependencies` with a `*` range, and explains why: "Installed copies can bypass the extension loader and create duplicate runtime modules." (#9863). August's plugin layer has the identical hazard, and the warning text is a good model — it names the mechanism, not just the rule.
- **[coding-agent-tests#3]** - **A regression test that keeps the *documentation* honest** - `packages/coding-agent/test/references.test.ts:7` - the generated reference page is compared with the committed file, and the failure message names the regeneration command. The regression it guards (#10790) is that `models.json` fields silently lost their reference documentation. August's `check:docs`-style gates are static, but this is the complementary idea: a *generated* artifact that is committed and diffed.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The summariser is a side request with its own context, its own session id and caching forced off** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-compaction.test.ts:356-363` — the compaction request must not go through the conversation's `transformContext`, must carry **no tools**, must use `cacheRetention: "none"`, must not reuse the active `sessionId`, and must not inherit the conversation's transport. Why it transfers: August's compaction shares the provider client with the live turn, so a summariser that shares the session id also shares the prompt-cache prefix and the price. The pairing is the point — the same file asserts the request body starts with `# Conversation` (`:360`), which is also the defence against a summary being read as a fresh user instruction.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **A refusal that names the door that would have worked** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-queue.test.ts:453-455` — `Extension command "/testcmd" cannot be queued. Use prompt() or execute the command when not streaming.` The refusal is a *teaching* event: it names the two legal alternatives in the same sentence. August refuses a lot (permission, policy, budget, authority); each refusal should say what the caller could have done instead.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **A hook whose result selects a privileged path fails closed** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/9068-user-bash-fail-closed.test.ts:150-175` — a `user_bash` handler that throws, or returns an empty object, denies the request with `Invalid user_bash handler result` and the command **never executes** (`executeCount: 0`); only an explicit `undefined` means "run it normally". The generalisation for August: any extension hook that can *route* an action must have its result shape validated exhaustively, and an unparseable result must deny rather than fall back to the default behaviour.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **One preflight abort cancels every prepared tool, but every call still gets a matched error result** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/8935-parallel-preflight-abort.test.ts:56-70` — `executions` is empty, `resultHooks` is empty, yet two `tool_execution_end` events and two `"Operation aborted"` tool results exist. August's parallel preflight (write gate, approval, sandbox) has the same shape: the abort must stop *all* pending writes, and the model must still receive one result per call it made, or the next turn carries an orphaned `tool_use_id`.

This is the check August needs for the exact class of bug its own AGENTS.md records (an orphaned `tool_use_id` surviving into persisted history bricks the chat) — a *structural* assertion catches it for any ordering, not just the one that broke.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The wire projection must be delta-only and its size must scale linearly** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/7290-json-stream-linear.test.ts:37-43` — doubling the text may cost at most 2.2× the bytes, and the projected event must contain no cumulative `message` and no cumulative `partial`. - **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **A session replacement subscribes before the new session's handlers can speak** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/5943-session-start-notify.test.ts:271-277` — the pinned order is `apply → render → subscribe → bind → notify`. - **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The shutdown order is different for a signal than for a quit** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/5080-signal-shutdown-extension-cleanup.test.ts:116-127` — on SIGTERM the order is `dispose → drainInput → stop` (extension teardown first, terminal untouched); on an interactive quit it is `drainInput → stop → dispose` (the final TUI frame first). The *reason* is in the comment at `:11-17`: extension teardown does not write to the tty, so it must not be skipped when a later terminal-restore write fails on a dead terminal. A harness with two exit paths needs two orders, chosen deliberately.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **A summary that is truncated must not replace the history** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/7048-compaction-truncated-summary.test.ts:40-47` — a length-stopped summary makes `compact()` reject with `generation hit the token cap` and **no compaction entry is written**. August currently admits a summary whose own footer says "decisions, constraints and next steps were not analyzed"; pi's rule is stricter and simpler: an unusable summary either refuses the compaction or keeps the original window.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The context-limit decision uses the *physical* model, and the request reason is explicit** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/virtual-models.test.ts:92-99` and `:217-226` — the route reason is one of `user | retry | continuation | direct`, and the compaction threshold is evaluated against the model that produced the **last response**, not against the declared (virtual) window. - **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **A forced system prompt is sent but never recorded** — `packages/coding-agent/test/system-prompt-updates.test.ts:112-168` — the transcript stores only the *structured sections*; the exact forced text rides on the request. This is the shape August needs if it ever wants a "run this exact prompt" door without polluting the transcript.
- **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The system prompt is a diffable structure, not a blob** — `packages/coding-agent/test/system-prompt-updates.test.ts:82-92` — `diffSystemPromptSections(previous, current)` returns `{ plan_mode: "<plan_mode>…</plan_mode>" }` or `{ plan_mode: null }` to remove a section, and `undefined` when nothing changed. - **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The loader must not load its compiler until it has something to compile** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/9540-extension-loader-lazy.test.ts:38-57` and `.../8237-node-sea-extension-loading.test.ts:51-70` — jiti and the virtual-module map are imported **only when an extension is actually imported**, and in a compiled binary the `tryNative: false` branch wins. - **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **A scoped-model list entry with no catalog entry must still be visible and removable** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/6949-unavailable-scoped-model.test.ts:85-91` — it is shown struck through and marked `[unavailable]`, it can be removed, and removing it does not clear the rest of the scope. - **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The deny set wins over the allow set, and both accept patterns** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/5109-exclude-tools.test.ts:62-98` — an excluded tool is absent from `getAllTools()`, from `getActiveToolNames()` *and* from the prompt, even when the allowlist names it. - **[coding-agent-tests#4]** - **The refusal to steer into a command is a refusal that names the alternative** — `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-queue.test.ts:440-474` — both `steer("/cmd")` and `followUp("/cmd")` throw the same message. - **[durable#1]** - **A durable task state machine whose "no progress" is a failure** — `packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts:1828` — the spec's fault rule is "Checkpoint unchanged: write terminal `faulted` because no durable progress" (`packages/durable/docs/spec.md:2010`). August's stall detection is argument-novelty-based and can be defeated by a model that calls a different no-argument tool every round; pi's rule is structural — a task that re-commits the *same* state has made no durable progress and is failed. That is exactly the invariant August's runaway backstop wants, expressed in a form that cannot be gamed by argument variety.
- **[durable#1]** - **A crash-loop guard that parks rather than retries** — `packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts:409` — "Task … was cut off N times without progress; it is parked until retryTask()", with the predicate at `packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts:1367` (a task whose abort was requested is never parked). August's runaway backstop counts rounds; this counts *state changes*, which is the signal that actually distinguishes work from spinning.
- **[durable#1]** - **A read-after-write ban inside a transaction, enforced by the type of the error** — `packages/durable/src/session/transaction.ts:953` — `ReadAfterWrite` is thrown by the transaction's own `#read` wrapper, so a commit callback that reads after writing fails loudly instead of reading a torn snapshot. August's backend has the same distinction but it is spread across call sites; one wrapper that decides fatality is both cheaper and testable.
- **[durable#1]** - **A replay-safe tool is one whose *intent* is committed before the effect** — `packages/durable/src/harness/tool.ts:76` — the `execute` phase records "the final arguments and the replay policy" before the tool runs, so a crash during the effect leaves a durable record of what was about to happen. The nested-call identity check at `packages/durable/src/harness/tool.ts:754` ("was already made with another tool or other arguments") then refuses to re-admit a call that changed shape. August's `run_command` and `write_file` have no such record.
- **[durable#1]** - **Overflow is never retried, only compacted** — `packages/durable/src/harness/generation.ts:560` — "An overflow is never retried: only a compaction can make the next request fit." August has a whole ladder for context overflow (auto-compact, budget rung, reactive rescue) and a separate retry path; pi's rule is one sentence and it removes the possibility of a retry storm against an oversized prompt.
- **[durable#1]** - **The compaction cut may never land between an assistant's tool call and its result** — `packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts:303` — the candidate predicate refuses a cut "that a result of the preceding assistant's calls that follows this entry, before the next assistant, belongs before it". - **[durable#1]** - **Only the first system message moves, to keep the prompt cache warm** — `packages/durable/src/harness/context.ts:208` — "Only the first system message moves, so replaying [the rest] does not change the request's tool list and invalidates the whole prompt cache." August freezes its memory index per session for the same reason; pi states the cache constraint at the point where the message list is built, which is where it can actually be enforced.
- **[durable#1]** - **The system-prompt planner has exactly three shapes, and the "head marker" case writes a full baseline** — `packages/durable/src/harness/prompt.ts:66` and `packages/durable/src/harness/prompt.ts:62` — a complete baseline when no later `pi.system` entry exists, a remove-all/re-add-all when a minimal patch would change the order, and otherwise the minimal patch. August's `<memory_policy>` and its per-turn section assembly would benefit from having the "what shape is this update" question answered once, explicitly, instead of per-surface.
- **[durable#1]** - **A bounded watch frame queue that degrades to a full replacement** — `packages/durable/src/session/observation.ts:229` — at 100 pending frames the queue is dropped and the consumer receives a root replacement. The durable live state is a *document*, so a slow UI can always resynchronise from the store; August's SSE stream has no such fallback.
- **[durable#1]** - **A snapshot diff instead of trusting the filesystem's events** — `packages/durable/src/env/node-watch.ts:134` — "native events only trigger a debounced rescan, and changes are the difference between snapshots plus the event paths", with a 500 ms settle on macOS because "about 2% of changes made right after the call" are never reported. Any August feature that watches a directory (skills, hooks, automations) should diff, not trust the event.
- **[durable#1]** - **One file-mutation queue keyed by the canonical path** — `packages/durable/src/tools/file-mutation-queue.ts:33` — "Serialize `edit` and `write` mutations of one file within this process", with the key built from the canonical path so a create and a later mutation share it even under a symlinked directory. August's `write_file`/`edit` have no such serialization; a lost update there is a silent data-loss bug.
- **[durable#1]** - **A cursor that carries its own order and refuses a different one** — `packages/durable/src/storage/scan.ts:32` — "The cursor continues a ascending scan; the query asks for descending". One 40-line file removes an entire class of pagination bug across four backends; August's `list_facts` offset pagination has the same shape of hazard.
- **[durable#1]** - **A runner-independent conformance suite, shipped as the package** — `packages/durable/src/testing/storage-conformance.ts:95` and `packages/durable/src/testing/env-conformance.ts:398` — the package ships the *cases* and the host supplies the runner, the assertions and the implementation. The argv case passes a deliberately hostile command and asserts that no `pwned` file appears. August has no equivalent: its rules live in prose in AGENTS.md and in scattered `if` statements, and August has no test suite at all.
- **[durable#1]** - **Seed the benchmark data through the public contract** — `packages/durable/src/testing/storage-benchmark.ts:88` — "Seed deterministic representative data through only the public `Storage` contract", with a fork chain 8 deep and several replay tails in the shape. A benchmark that measures a private bulk path measures nothing a real caller uses.
- **[durable#1]** - **A nonzero exit is an error *result*, not a throw** — `packages/durable/src/tools/bash.ts:133` — the exit code stays in the structured output and the result carries `isError: true` plus an `exit_code` diagnostic, while a *failure* (a timeout) throws. August's `run_command` surfaces exit codes in prose; making the distinction structured is what lets a UI colour a failing command without parsing text.
- **[durable#1]** - **The provider identity is a document, and a fork gets a fresh one** — `packages/durable/src/harness/provider.ts:11` — "every fork starts with a fresh identity instead of copying its parent", with `fork: "initial"`. If August ever forks a chat to a different upstream session, this is the rule that stops the two chats sharing a provider session id.
- **[durable#1]** - **Tool-search loads are sticky, and the search tool's description is fixed** — `packages/durable/src/tool-search/tool-search.ts:14` — the description never changes "while deferred tools are registered, for example as MCP servers connect", and a load writes the conversation's `modelTools`, so the tools stay offered "also after a compaction" (`:4-5`). August's progressive disclosure and its compaction do not currently agree about what survives.
- **[durable#2]** *Each idea names a mechanism, the exact place it lives, and why it transfers to the August harness. The `path:line` references were re-verified in this pass.*
- **[durable#2]** - **Never let a compaction cut separate a tool call from the result that answers it** — `packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts:299` — `isCandidate()` refuses a cut that would leave an assistant's `toolCall` in the summarised span while its `toolResult` stays outside. - **[durable#2]** - **A compaction cut is chosen by token budget but validated by message pairing** — `packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts:279` — `selectCut()` walks back from the tail until `keepRecentTokens` are kept, then snaps to the first *candidate* at or after that point, where a candidate is an entry whose contribution starts with a user or assistant message and never a tool result. The budget decides *where*, the pairing rule decides *whether it is legal*. August's compaction currently selects by token count alone; adding this predicate is cheap and removes a whole class of stuck conversations.
- **[durable#2]** - **Move only the FIRST system message to the front, and only when it is the baseline** — `packages/durable/src/harness/context.ts:212` — the stated reason is provider prefix caching: "providers treat only a leading system message as the initial prompt and tool set; without it, a later tool change rewrites the request's tool list and invalidates the whole prompt cache" (`context.ts:206-208`). A system message that was committed mid-conversation stays where it was, because moving it "would change what it means to the model". August's prompt assembly would benefit from the same rule: hoist the baseline, never reorder history. pi *proves* the rule against a live provider at `packages/durable/test/system-order-cache-e2e.test.ts:137` (cache-read share < 0.2 with the order flipped, > 0.8 with the fix) — the same measurement August could make against its own gateway.
- **[durable#2]** - **Patch the system prompt minimally so the provider's prefix cache survives** — `packages/durable/src/harness/prompt.ts:66` — `planSystemEntries()` computes the smallest set of `pi.system` entries that makes the *replayed* sections and tools equal the desired ones. Changed values are patched, removals are `null`, and **only** when the patched order would differ is everything removed and re-added (`prompt.ts:122`). Tool declarations are kept when byte-equal (`prompt.ts:100`). August rebuilds its system prompt on every turn; this mechanism keeps the prompt prefix byte-identical across turns unless the prompt genuinely changed. The pinned behaviour is `packages/durable/test/harness-prompt.test.ts:141` ("emits minimal value patches, removals, and additions").
- **[durable#2]** - **Derive the context incrementally from an immutable tail** — `packages/durable/src/harness/context.ts:73` — `readContextFrom()` reuses the previous range: with the same head marker only the entries after the previous tail are scanned, and a range that shrank is filtered rather than rescanned. The tail is captured in two O(1) reads **on the Session line** and the scan happens off it. August's context assembly re-reads the whole transcript per turn; this is the shape of an incremental reader that is safe under concurrency, and it is pinned at `packages/durable/test/harness-context.test.ts:426` ("extends a task's context read with only newer entries").
- **[durable#2]** - **A streamed partial is copied synchronously before it is committed** — `packages/durable/src/harness/generation.ts:466` — the comment is explicit: "Copy synchronously: the provider keeps mutating its partial." Both halves matter: the copy (the provider mutates the object you were about to serialise) and the await-on-teardown (a partial that lands after the final answer is a phantom message in the transcript). - **[durable#2]** - **Assign a streamed message leaf by leaf so the storage emits an append, not a full set** — `packages/durable/src/harness/json.ts:10` — `assignJson()` walks the object and assigns only the leaves that changed; Chord then records a string leaf's reassignment as an append. - **[durable#2]** - **Park a task that was cut off N times instead of retrying it forever** — `packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts:1366` — a task whose restart count reaches `settings.restartLimit` (default 5) is *parked*: it stops being a candidate, the graph shows `blocked: "restart_limit"`, the host is told, and `retryTask()` clears the count. - **[durable#2]** - **An abort cascade is derived from durable records, so a crash repairs it** — `packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts:776` — `#reconcile()` re-derives the abort marks below every live owner with cancellation intent from the committed task records: "The durable records are the intent, so this also repairs whatever a crash left unapplied" (`scheduler.ts:773`). The two-commit barrier that keeps a phase from advancing before the mark lands is pinned at `packages/durable/test/harness-cancellation-barrier.test.ts:79`.
- **[durable#2]** - **A wait may not close a cycle in the wait-for graph, and `failFast` may only wait on tasks you own** — `packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts:1973` — `#validateWait()` throws with the cycle path in the message (`A -> B -> A is a wait cycle`), and the abort handler may neither wait nor sleep. - **[durable#2]** - **Steering and follow-up are separate queues with separate modes, drained at two named boundaries** — `packages/durable/src/harness/inbox.ts:70` — `applyBoundary(tx, boundary, "postTools" | "final", now)` places writes first and user items after, each in ID order; the `steeringMode` and `followUpMode` settings decide whether **one** or **all** of each kind are taken; a selected reset promotes a `postTools` boundary to `final`. - **[durable#2]** - **A write whose head points before the active range is `stale`, not applied** — `packages/durable/src/harness/inbox.ts:145` — `isStale()` compares the write's `head` with the boundary's current head; a write that would resurrect context the conversation has already moved past is settled `unanswered` with reason `stale` instead of being applied. - **[durable#2]** - **Only the harness writes model context to a busy conversation** — `packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts:432` — the `REMINDER` there is the invariant: "nothing else may append to a busy conversation, so every non-blocking summary goes through admission." A generation-owned compaction appends directly (it holds the run); a conversation-owned one places its summary through a *write submission* that the normal admission path queues. - **[durable#2]** - **A wrapper that throws or renames its target DROPS the target and is reported** — `packages/durable/src/harness/agent.ts:336` — `applyWrap()` deletes the tool from the map and reports the error, so a broken plugin degrades to "that tool is not available" rather than to a tool that misbehaves at call time. - **[durable#2]** - **Watch files by snapshot diff, not by trusting OS events** — `packages/durable/src/env/node-watch.ts:139` — "A replaced file, a renamed or recreated ancestor, or a directory created with its contents therefore never depends on which events an operating system sends." - **[durable#2]** - **A phase that returns without changing its checkpoint is a FAULT, not a no-op** — `packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts:1829` — `#decide()` compares the committed state with the previous one and, if they are equal, writes `faulted` with "Task X phase Y returned without durable progress". A focused component emits a zero-width APC marker at the cursor; the renderer finds it, computes the *visible* column from the text before it, strips it, and moves the hardware cursor there. The fake cursor is a second marker pair that the renderer converts to reverse video (or drops when the hardware cursor is shown). *Why it transfers:* a component that knows its own cursor column should not have to know the terminal width, the padding, or the ANSI codes. It also keeps IME candidate-window placement correct, because the terminal positions the *hardware* cursor, not a drawn one.

The same "a query has an explicit terminator" shape works for HTTP long-polling or MCP capability handshakes.
