- **[tui]** - **The `undefined` vs `null` distinction carried from a C enum to the JS promise** — `packages/tui/native/clipboard.h:11-20` (`clipboard_format`: `UNAVAILABLE` vs `EMPTY`) and `packages/tui/src/native-platform.ts:9-18` (the same three states in the TypeScript contract: "Undefined means unavailable, null means no text; transfer failures reject"). *Why it transfers:* "the feature is not available here" and "the resource is empty" are different answers and a caller that cannot tell them apart will retry a capability that does not exist. August's provider registry has exactly this distinction to make.
- **[tui]** - **A "the tool must not block the event loop" assertion embedded in the fixture itself** — `packages/tui/test/fixtures/clipboard-reader.cjs:26` (a 10 ms timer must tick more than 5 times in 200 ms) and `packages/tui/test/fixtures/clipboard-worker-test.cjs:46-56` (20 concurrent reads must resolve promptly and filesystem I/O must stay available). *Why it transfers:* the assertion lives with the probe, so every test that uses the probe inherits it, and the "20 concurrent calls all return undefined" check is a precise statement of the "refuse rather than queue" policy from the JS side.
- **[tui]** - **Include the production C source in the test fixture with the allocators redefined** — `packages/tui/test/fixtures/clipboard-worker-test.c:20-24` (`#define calloc tracked_calloc` before `#include "../../native/linux/src/clipboard-worker.h"`) and `packages/tui/test/fixtures/clipboard-x11-test.c:41-45` (the same trick for `realloc`/`free`). The fixture exercises the *real* worker with a controlled blocking callback, and the allocation counters make a partial-transfer leak deterministic ("unlike RSS"). *Why it transfers:* it is the cheapest possible way to test a C/C++ path without a separate build system or a mocking framework — and it is exactly what August's `code_runner.py` port of a Python guard would need an equivalent for.
- **[tui]** - **A protocol-conformance encoder: control characters are removed because the terminal discards the whole report** — `packages/tui/src/program-status.ts:45-52` and `packages/tui/src/program-status.ts:32-43` (the UTF-8-boundary truncation to 2048 bytes, chosen so the base64 stays under the spec's 2732-byte limit). *Why it transfers:* the same "one bad byte loses the whole message" reasoning applies to any status/telemetry channel August might open to an IDE or a shell integration. The base64 + byte-limit pattern is directly reusable.
- **[tui]** - **Probe the multiplexer instead of guessing what it forwards** — `packages/tui/src/terminal-image.ts:54-68` (`probeTmuxHyperlinks` runs `tmux display-message -p '#{client_termfeatures}'` with a 250 ms timeout and falls back to `false` on any error). *Why it transfers:* capability detection by environment variable is a guess; a cheap runtime probe is a fact. The same move is available for August's own "is this running inside tmux / inside a Tauri webview / inside a VS Code terminal" questions.
- **[tui]** - **A fuzzy matcher that retries the query with its letters and digits swapped** — `packages/tui/src/fuzzy.ts:76-93`. "codex52" matches "gpt-5.2-codex" because the query is tried both ways at a +5 penalty, and `fuzzyFilter` splits on whitespace **and slashes** and requires every token to match (`:100-137`). *Why it transfers:* August's model picker has ids like `gpt-5.2-codex` and providers like `openai-codex`; the slash-separated multi-token filter is exactly the "provider/model" query shape, and the swapped-alnum retry handles the "which was the version, which was the name" ambiguity for free.
- **[tui]** - **Escape every segment of a path before handing it to an external search tool** — `packages/tui/src/autocomplete.ts:21-44` (`buildFdPathQuery` escapes each segment and joins them with `[\\/]`). The changelog records the bug this fixed: "`@` file autocomplete returning no results for queries containing regex metacharacters such as `[` or `(`". *Why it transfers:* August shells out to `fd`/`rg` for file search. Passing a user-typed path into a regex is an injection *and* a correctness bug; building the pattern segment-by-segment is the fix.
- **[tui]** - **A prefix that survives quoting, wrapping and cursor bookkeeping** — `packages/tui/src/autocomplete.ts:116-135` (`parsePathPrefix` keeps the opening quote in the prefix) and `packages/tui/src/autocomplete.ts:412-497` (`applyCompletion` adjusts the cursor for a trailing quote, distinguishes a slash *command name* from a command *argument* from an `@file` mention, and does not add a space after a directory). *Why it transfers:* completion in a live buffer is a text-rewriting problem, not a "replace the word" problem; the four cases (command / argument / mention / path) each need a different rewrite, and the cursor offset must be recomputed for each.
- **[tui]** - **A flash-message container whose timers are `unref()`ed** — `packages/tui/src/components/alt-screen-flash.ts:22-36`. The container renders *nothing* into the layout; the renderer composites it separately, so a transient message never perturbs the layout tree. *Why it transfers:* a toast in August's chat surface should not reflow the transcript. The `unref()` is the small detail that stops a pending toast from holding a process open.
- **[tui]** - **A packaging constraint can be pinned by a test that reads the shipped binary's own header** — `packages/tui/test/native-platform.test.ts:8-27` parses the ELF program headers of `native/linux/prebuilds/linux-arm64/linux-platform-x11.node` and asserts every `PT_LOAD` segment is 64 KB-aligned, because a system with 64 KB pages otherwise refuses to load the module. I verified the same property independently on the file in this shard. *Why it transfers:* the failure this prevents is invisible in CI on a 4 KB-page machine and only appears on a user's aarch64 Linux box. A test that reads the shipped artefact's own header turns a packaging rule into a checked invariant — the same trick applies to any prebuilt binary August ships.
- **[tui]** - **A protocol-negotiation reply that is buffered and re-flushed as *input* rather than misparsed** — `packages/tui/src/terminal.ts:339-388` and `packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts:29` (`TERMINAL_REPLY_HEADER_PATTERN`, which keeps a partially-received OSC/DCS/APC reply from being delivered as a batched Alt keystroke). *Why it transfers:* any code that reads a multiplexed byte stream has to decide "is this a partial reply or user input?" and the safe answer is to *keep buffering* until the header is complete. The 150 ms flush is the escape hatch that keeps a real keystroke from being swallowed.
- **[tui]** - **A defensive clone-on-push undo stack** — `packages/tui/src/undo-stack.ts:10-19`. `push` stores a `structuredClone`; `pop` returns the stored snapshot *without* re-cloning, because it is already detached. *Why it transfers:* an agent harness that offers "undo this tool call" or "revert this edit" wants the same semantics: the snapshot is a fact at push time, not a live view.

## simulide — 163 ideas across the shards read so far

- **[angel-jit]** - **The fast path is a plug-in with a two-method interface, and the engine never learns how it works.** `src/angel/include/angelscript.h:1211-1218` — `class asIJITCompiler { virtual int CompileFunction(asIScriptFunction*, asJITFunction*) = 0; virtual void ReleaseJITFunction(asJITFunction) = 0; };`, reached through `asIScriptEngine::SetJITCompiler` / `GetJITCompiler` (`angelscript.h:611-612`). SimulIDE installs it at runtime, conditionally, in one place (`src/microsim/modules/script/scriptbase.cpp:67-71`, `#ifdef __x86_64__`). **Why it transfers to August:** a skill or plugin surface with a two-method "accelerator" interface — `install()` / `uninstall()` — lets August add a compiled or native fast path for a hot operation without a build matrix, without touching the core, and without the core learning anything about it. The engine-side lesson is the *shape*: the interface is deliberately tiny, and the host decides at runtime whether it exists.
- **[angel-jit]** - **A marker instruction that says "native code may take over here" — the trick that lets a fast path and a slow path coexist in one program.** `src/angel/include/angelscript.h:1398` defines the opcode `asBC_JitEntry = 175`; the compiler emits it at the start of every function (`src/angel/src/as_compiler.cpp:132-133, 185-186, 562-563`) and the bytecode builder emits it after every call, every allocation and every suspend (`src/angel/src/as_bytecode.cpp:1618-1619, 1633-1634, 1649-1650, 1705-1706`); the interpreter treats it as a resume point (`src/angel/src/as_context.cpp:3650-3679`) and the optimiser refuses to fuse across one (`src/angel/JIT/as_jit.cpp:846`). **Why it transfers to August:** if August ever wants to accelerate a hot part of a workflow (a diff, a parse, a solver step), the same design applies — mark the safe re-entry points in the intermediate representation, compile the regions between them, and let the fallback handle the rest. The cost of the marker is one instruction, and it is *deleted again* when no accelerator is installed (`as_bytecode.cpp:1083-1088`), so the slow path pays nothing.
- **[angel-jit]** - **The fast path can hand the program back to the slow path at any moment, and the slow path can resume it — with a single, explicit register block as the contract.** `src/angel/JIT/as_jit.cpp:738-741` ("We can't handle this address, so generate a special return that does the jump ahead of time") returns control to the VM with the bytecode pointer in the return register; `src/angel/src/as_context.cpp:1028-1030` shows the VM calling straight back into native code with `asSVMRegisters`; the struct itself is public at `src/angel/include/angelscript.h:1197-1207`. **Why it transfers to August:** this is the shape a step-based simulator needs. A "model" can be executed by a fast kernel and, when it meets something the kernel cannot do (an I/O event, a suspension), return a *program counter* into a description of the model so the harness can resume later. The lesson is that the handoff state must be one small, explicit, versioned struct — not scattered variables — so that two independent implementations (fast kernel, fallback engine) can be written by different people and still interleave.
- **[angel-jit]** - **Speed trade-offs are named constants with the cost written next to them, not one "fast mode" boolean.** `src/angel/JIT/as_jit.h:16-33` — seven flags, each with its own sentence about what it gives up: `JIT_SYSCALL_NO_ERRORS` ("exceptions will generally be ignored, possibly leading to crashes"), `JIT_NO_SCRIPT_CALLS` ("can be used as a temporary workaround for angelscript changes"), `JIT_FAST_REFCOUNT` ("Reference counting functions which access the script context will produce undefined results"). SimulIDE picks exactly two (`scriptbase.cpp:68`). **Why it transfers to August:** August already has a "budget ladder" and a set of degraded modes; naming each degradation separately — with the consequence in the comment — is what makes a degraded mode *safe to enable*. A single boolean cannot say "this one is fine, that one can crash".
- **[angel-jit]** - **Compile-time feature removal, not runtime guarding.** `src/angel/src/as_config.h:77` — `#define AS_NO_EXCEPTIONS` removes the language's entire exception feature from the parser, the compiler, the VM and the JIT at once; line 352 adds `#define AS_NO_THISCALL_FUNCTOR_METHOD`. **Why it transfers to August:** a capability that a skill does not need can be switched off for that skill's whole build, which shrinks the code *and* the attack surface. August's `code` agent mode already restricts the tool surface at runtime; a compile-time switch is the stronger version of the same idea.
- **[angel-jit]** - **The build configuration is queryable at runtime as a string, so a bug report can state the configuration instead of guessing it.** `src/angel/src/as_scriptengine.cpp:73-128` — `asGetLibraryOptions()` appends a token for every `#ifdef`ed feature and the target system and CPU family ("AS_NO_EXCEPTIONS ", "AS_X64_GCC ", "AS_WIN ", …). **Why it transfers to August:** every August session should be able to emit one line that says exactly which features, paths and models were in effect. The August harness has an equivalent problem — a "capabilities line" — and the engine solves it by deriving it from the same macros that shaped the build, so it can never drift.
- **[angel-jit]** - **Every diagnostic is a named constant in one file, so the failure vocabulary is greppable and complete.** `src/angel/src/as_texts.h:40+` — ~300 `#define TXT_…` strings, including `TXT_NO_JIT_IN_FUNC_s` (line 338). **Why it transfers to August:** August's error taxonomy (the eight-family classification in the harness rules) could live in one table of constants rather than as literals scattered across handlers. The benefit is the same one this file gets: `grep TXT_` returns the complete list of things that can go wrong, and each message has a stable name that a test can assert on.
- **[angel-jit]** - **A vendored dependency that says, in its own licence file, that it has been modified — so the fork's divergence is discoverable at the point of use.** `src/angel/src/COPYING:31-34` — "All the files in this folder have been modified to meet this project's requirements. **Any error is most likely caused by these modifications.**" — plus the per-file marker `// Modified 2023 by Santiago González` at `src/angel/src/as_datatype.cpp:31`. **Why it transfers to August:** August vendors or wraps third-party code (parsers, model clients, protocol libraries). Writing the divergence statement *into the vendored licence file* means the next person who hits a bug in that code reads the warning before they debug it, instead of filing it against upstream.
- **[angel-jit]** - **Reference counting split into "the engine owns it" and "someone outside holds it".** `src/angel/src/as_typeinfo.cpp:44-45` — `externalRefCount` and `internalRefCount` are two independent counters; `as_module.h:183` exposes `HasExternalReferences(bool shuttingDown)` so a module can be discarded only when nobody outside still refers to it. **Why it transfers to August:** August's memory and skill stores have exactly this problem — a skill record is owned by the store but may be referenced by a running session. One refcount cannot express "the owner may go, the referrer may not".
- **[angel-jit]** - **A garbage collector that detects cycles, breaks them, and tells the host — and that does its work in bounded slices spread across allocations.** `src/angel/src/as_gc.h:62-64` (the host callback), `src/angel/src/as_gc.h:78-94` (an explicit, resumable phase machine: `clearCounters`, `buildMap`, `countReferences`, `detectGarbage`, `verifyUnmarked`, `breakCircles`), `src/angel/src/as_gc.cpp:87-100` (one step of detection per new object, with the reason stated: "This will maintain the number of objects in the GC at a maintainable level without halting the application"). **Why it transfers to August:** the August brain store and the session transcript can both hold cycles; a collector that refuses to run while the application is busy is worse than one that does a little work per allocation. And the phase-machine shape makes the collector interruptible, which is what a harness with a turn budget needs.
- **[angel-jit]** - **The allocator is the host's, and swapping it is done in an order that cannot free memory with the wrong allocator.** `src/angel/src/as_memory.cpp:66-77` — `asSetGlobalMemoryFunctions` calls `asThreadCleanup()` *first* with the comment "Clean-up thread local memory before changing the allocation routines to avoid potential problem with trying to free memory using a different allocation routine than used when allocating it." **Why it transfers to August:** any August component that lets the host install a custom allocator (a memory-budgeted allocator, a tracing allocator) has the same hazard; the fix is one line and the reasoning is worth copying verbatim.
- **[angel-jit]** - **Small containers do not allocate.** `src/angel/src/as_array.h:94` — `char buf[2*4*AS_PTR_SIZE];` gives `asCArray` an inline buffer for one or two elements; `src/angel/src/as_string.h:89-93` gives `asCString` a 12-byte inline buffer in a union with the heap pointer. **Why it transfers to August:** the harness's hot paths (per-tool-call records, per-turn message rows, per-file ledger rows) are dominated by single-element containers. An inline buffer removes the allocation and the free, and — more importantly — removes the failure case.
- **[build-root]** - **A headless mode that also stops writing next to the user's files** — `src/mainwindow.cpp:119-125` — `hideGui()` hides the side panel, the editor and the canvas, and then calls `Circuit::self()->setAutoBck( -1 )`. *Why it matters for August:* an agent-driven "simulate this and report" run must be indistinguishable from a human run to the engine but must not leave artefacts in the user's project directory. SimulIDE encodes that as a property of the headless switch itself, not as a separate code path that someone can forget to disable. Pair it with `src/mainwindow.cpp:135-137`, where `closeEvent` returns early in headless mode and therefore skips the save-and-prompt dance entirely.
- **[build-root]** - **A golden-file batch regression mode driven entirely from argv** — `src/main.cpp:97-107` (with `src/gui/testing/batchtest.cpp:36-52, 54-77`, which I read for context) — `-test <folder>` walks a directory tree for `*.sim1`/`*.sim2`, loads each circuit, powers it on, and prints `"All tests passed"` or `"N Tests failed:"` plus the failing filenames. *Why it matters for August:* this is the mechanism by which a *circuit simulation skill* could be graded — a folder of circuits each containing a self-checking test unit, run headless, exit-code-shaped, with no human present. The whole contract is four lines of argv parsing plus a folder scan. Note the honest limitation: the runner reports failures but does not set a process exit code, so a CI/harness wrapper has to read stdout, not `$?`.
- **[build-root]** - **The circuit file records the simulation parameters it was authored under** — `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:445-458` (read for context) — the `<circuit>` header carries `version`, `rev`, `stepSize`, `stepsPS`, `NLsteps`, `reaStep`, `animate`, `anicurr`, `ansi`, `width`, `height`. *Why it matters for August:* a saved artifact that fingerprints the *engine settings* it ran under is what makes a later run reproducible and a diff meaningful. An August circuit tool should write the same fields, so "the output changed" can be attributed to the circuit or to the settings — and `src/mainwindow.cpp:43` shows how the app's own revision number becomes one of those fields.
- **[build-root]** - **Three-tier resource resolution — user file, install file, compiled-in resource** — `src/mainwindow.cpp:423-436` — `getDataFilePath` tries the user data folder, then `<config>/data/<file>`, then the Qt resource `:/<file>`, and returns `""` only if all three miss. The header states the contract in one comment at `src/mainwindow.h:83`. *Why it matters for August:* a skill's reference corpus, its component library and its model data should resolve the same way — a user can patch one file in their data directory without reinstalling anything, and the built-in copy remains the floor. `src/mainwindow.cpp:438-453` adds the fourth case a coursework bundle needs: files relative to the *circuit's own* directory, then the circuit's `data/` subfolder, so a circuit ships as a self-contained folder.
- **[build-root]** - **A help system with locale fallback, includes and a cache** — `src/mainwindow.cpp:343-384` — six-step lookup (`<name>_<locale>` then `<name>`, across user dir → config dir → `:/help`), the name normalised by lowercasing and stripping spaces, the result composed by recursively expanding `#include "other.txt"` lines, and the composed text cached in `m_help`. *Why it matters for August:* this is the minimum viable shape of a *reference corpus* for a course skill — a base name, a per-locale variant, an include mechanism for composing a page out of parts, and a cache so repeated lookups are free. The include expansion is the part worth stealing: it lets a page be assembled from shared fragments without a full templating engine.
- **[build-root]** - **Every file-reading helper names its caller in the error** — `src/utils.cpp:158-216` — `fileToDomDoc(fileName, caller)`, `fileToString(fileName, caller)`, `fileToStringList`, `fileToByteArray` all take the calling site's name and emit `caller << "Error: Cannot read file:" << fileName`. The XML variant also reports the parse line and column. *Why it matters for August:* in a harness where an agent is told "the step failed", the difference between `Error: Cannot read file` and `Error: Cannot read file [circuit.cpp:412]` is the difference between a retryable step and a mystery. The Python analogue is one helper — `read_text(path, *, caller=...)` — with the caller's name baked into the exception message.
- **[build-root]** - **Prefix choice and display precision decided together** — `src/utils.h:24-43` — `valToUnit` picks the largest SI prefix that keeps the number under 1000 **and** sets the decimal count from the scaled magnitude (3 below 10, 2 below 100, 1 below 1000, 0 above), in one function. *Why it matters for August:* any tool that shows a physical quantity to a learner needs this; a separate formatter for "the number" and another for "the decimals" drifts, and the drift shows up as `0.000000001 F` in a UI that a student has to read. The same file shows the anti-pattern to avoid: `unitToVal` and `getMultiplier` are two unit systems with different bases and no shared definition.
- **[build-root]** - **A crash-recovery artefact with one fixed name and an explicit user decision** — `src/mainwindow.cpp:101-115` — the autosave is a single known file (`backup.sim2` in the config dir); on startup, if it exists, the app says "Looks like SimulIDE crashed…", offers Open or Discard, and **deletes it** on Discard. *Why it matters for August:* a long agent turn that dies should leave exactly one identifiable, recoverable artefact and the next boot should surface it as a decision rather than a silent overwrite. The "one fixed name" limitation is worth noting rather than copying: only the most recent crash is ever recoverable.
- **[build-root]** - **The GUI app's stdout must reach the parent terminal on Windows** — `src/main.cpp:54-58` — `AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)` followed by `freopen("CONOUT$", "w", stdout)` and the same for stderr. *Why it matters for August:* a Tauri desktop app launched by a harness on Windows will not see the harness's stdout unless it attaches to the parent console explicitly. This is three lines and it is the difference between "the app's output is visible to the orchestrator" and "it is not". Pair it with `src/main.cpp:16-39`, which routes `qDebug` into the app's own debug pane *and* stderr — one log, two sinks.
- **[build-root]** - **Generated artefacts are produced by the build, not committed, and the ordering is declared** — `SimulIDE.pri:157-164` with `.gitignore:1` and `src/application.qrc:11-25` — `runLrelease` is a `QMAKE_EXTRA_TARGETS` that compiles the `.ts` sources into `resources/qm/*.qm` and moves them into place, hooked in as `PRE_TARGETDEPS`; the outputs are git-ignored by the repository's single rule `resources/qm/*.*`; and the qrc lists those very files as resources. *Why it matters for August:* the same three-part contract (generate at build time, ignore the output, declare the dependency) is what an August skill-pack build needs — and this repo shows the failure mode too: because the dependency is expressed as a *pre-target* hook rather than as rcc's own dependency on the `.qm` files, a build without `lrelease` on `PATH` fails at the resource step with a missing-file error that points at the qrc, not at the missing tool.
- **[build-root]** - **A build that discovers its own sources** — `SimulIDE.pri:15-18` — `SOURCES = $$files( $$PWD/src/*.cpp, true )`, `HEADERS`, `FORMS` and `TRANSLATIONS` are all globs, with `true` meaning recursive. *Why it matters for August:* a plugin/component registry that is directory-driven means adding a component is one file rather than one file plus an entry in a list — the same property the `components-analog` and `components-digital` shards' `Component::construct` / `libraryItem()` pairs rely on. The paired cost is visible at `SimulIDE.pri:21-81`: a 61-line hand-maintained `INCLUDEPATH` that must be edited whenever a directory is added, which is exactly the maintenance a real registry would remove.
- **[build-root]** - **The build tells the developer what it is doing** — `SimulIDE.pri:166-176` — a `message()` banner printed at qmake time: target name, target OS, host OS, build date, Qt version and the destination folder. *Why it matters for August:* a skill that a user runs on their own machine should announce, in one block, which build of the skill is running, on what host, against which dependency versions, and where it will write. It is six lines and it is the difference between a reproducible run and a mystery.
- **[components-analog]** - **A non-linear element guesses its own next iterate instead of waiting for the matrix to converge** — `src/components/active/op_amp.cpp:150-171` — the op-amp declares convergence only when *both* the input difference and the output are within `m_accuracy = 5e-6` of the last step (`:150-153`); if not, it runs a two-phase guess: the first non-converged step perturbs the output by ±1e-6 to learn which way it should move (`:157-163`), and the second computes `out = (m_lastOut*dIn + vd*1e-6)/(dIn + m_k)` with `m_k = 1e-6/m_gain` (`:165-169`) — a damped extrapolation whose damping constant is the model's own gain. *Why it matters for August:* an iterative solver needs a rule for "what value do I try next"; this rule is model-derived (the damping is 1/gain), so it generalises across models instead of being a magic iteration count.
- **[components-analog]** - **A complete geometric under-relaxation policy in eight lines** — `src/components/sources/csource.cpp:212-228` — when the same simulation timestamp is seen twice, the new value moves only part of the way (`curr = m_lastCurr + (curr−m_lastCurr)/m_step`) and `m_step *= 1.8` (`:215`); a new timestamp resets the step to 1, and convergence is `|curr − m_lastCurr| < 1e-7` (`:222`). *Why it matters for August:* this is a complete, tiny, copyable shape for "iterate until stable" — a per-attempt step that grows geometrically, reset by the clock, with an explicit epsilon. August's `simulate_circuit` convergence ladder could use exactly this shape for the "same timestamp, try a gentler step" case.
- **[components-analog]** - **A reactive element is a resistor whose value is recomputed from the timestep** — `src/components/passive/reactive/capacitorbase.h:19-20` (`updtRes() = m_tStep/m_capacitance`, `updtCurr() = m_volt*m_admit`) and `src/components/passive/reactive/inductor.h:30-31` (`updtRes() = m_inductance/m_tStep`, `updtCurr() = m_curSource − m_volt*m_admit`), driven by `src/components/passive/reactive/reactive.cpp:51-60`. *Why it matters for August:* one line of arithmetic turns a stateful element into a stampable linear one, so the solver never needs a separate state vector for C and L. Any August-side model that needs memory can be collapsed the same way.
- **[components-analog]** - **A coupled multi-element device: invert the coupling matrix once, then do O(n²) work per step** — `src/components/passive/reactive/transformer.cpp:96-149` — the inductance matrix with mutual terms `k·√(L_i·L_j)·sign_i·sign_j` (`:92`) is inverted in place by a hand-written LU/Gauss-Jordan (`:97-113`), scaled by the timestep (`:135`), and then reused every step as a current-injection matrix (`current_i = Σ_j V_j·inva[i][j]`, `:157-162`). The coupling coefficient is clamped to `[0.0001, 0.9999]` (`:211-212`) so a perfect transformer is numerically impossible. *Why it matters for August:* a transformer, a coupled inductor, a multi-port or a thermal network is handled by pre-computing the inverse at setup and then never solving again — a large performance win that a naive Newton-per-step implementation would miss.
- **[components-analog]** - **A part's geometry can change at run time, and the electrical change is *scheduled*, not immediate** — `src/components/active/mux_analog.cpp:131-158` (changing the address width creates/deletes address pins and channel resistors, resizes the bounding box, and **powers the circuit off first** if the simulator is running, `:138`) and `:104-105` (the switch itself is deferred: `voltChanged()` computes the new address and schedules an event 10 000 ps later; `runEvent()` does the admittance swap). *Why it matters for August:* two separable lessons — (a) a topology change must not happen mid-solve, and (b) a change that has a propagation delay should be *modelled* as a delay rather than applied instantly. The `10000/*m_propDelay*/` comment shows the delay is intended to become a named property.
- **[components-analog]** - **A multi-part device specified by a tiny text grammar in one property** — `src/components/passive/reactive/transformer.cpp:238-262` — the "Primary" / "Secondary" property is a string where `:` separates sections (a centre-tapped winding), `,` separates coils, and the **sign of each number is the winding polarity** (`:301-306`); `getLeght()` derives the coil count, the topology string and the pin count (`nCoils*3 + nSections − 1`), and `create()`/`modify()` then build or re-lay-out the pins and coils. *Why it matters for August:* one editable field describes a whole multi-part device, and the same string is what the circuit file stores — a student-facing grammar and a serialisation format are the same artefact.

When several pins change in the same instant, an edge delivered as an event can be lost or double-counted; re-deriving the edge from (current pin state, previous pin state) on every callback cannot be. Any event-driven simulator an August harness builds should adopt this: the trigger is a *state comparison*, not a *notification*.
- **[components-digital]** - **A frequency meter's "wave lost" timeout is expressed in simulation time and knows the simulator's frame duration** — `src/components/meters/freqmeter.cpp:88-104` (`lost = max(m_period*2, psPerFrame*2)`) and the same pattern at `src/components/meters/oscopechannel.cpp:102-118` — *Why it matters for August:* a measurement that has no signal is not "zero", it is "no measurement". Both the frequency meter and the oscilloscope channel distinguish the two, and they do it by comparing against the frame time so that the timeout is meaningful at any zoom level. A tool that reports a frequency, a duty cycle or a latency should say "no signal" rather than print 0.
- **[components-digital]** - **The logic analyzer exports a standard waveform interchange format, including the timescale normalisation** — `src/components/meters/logicanalizer.cpp:322-415` (`dumpData()` writes `$timescale`, `$var wire N id name $end` and `$dumpvars`) and the gcd helper at `src/components/meters/logicanalizer.cpp:417-427` — *Why it matters for August:* the export is not a proprietary file — it is a format another tool opens. A course skill should emit something a student can open in an external waveform viewer and *also* open in the tool itself. The gcd normalisation is the detail worth copying: without it the exported timestamps are enormous and the receiving tool has to guess.
- **[components-digital]** - **A rotary encoder is decoded as true quadrature by keeping two counters a quarter period apart** — `src/components/micro/ky040.cpp:153-175` — *Why it matters for August:* the encoder's two phase outputs come from two counters that are 10 apart out of 20, so their threshold crossings are 90° apart by construction. The same file shows the input-side detail that matters just as much: the dial's wrap-around is detected and compensated before differencing (`ky040.cpp:130-133`), because a wrap would otherwise look like a huge jump.
- **[components-digital]** - **A component that owns child components (a keypad of push buttons, a relay's inductor) is a *composition*, and the children are real parts** — `src/components/switches/keypad.cpp:131-208` (the keypad builds `PushBase` children and `eDiode` children) and `src/components/switches/relay.cpp:42-52` (the relay owns an `Inductor` child and its pins *are* the inductor's pins) — *Why it matters for August:* composition over configuration is what makes a part library extensible. A keypad that is a matrix of buttons and diodes is a different part from a bag of buttons; a relay whose coil is a real inductor can have a real pull-in current. The cost is the index arithmetic in `MechContact::SetupSwitches`, and the payoff is a library where the interesting parts are built from the simple ones. ---
- **[gui]** - **Undo/redo as a diff over a text serialisation, not over a model** — `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:733` (`beginUndoStep` snapshots every item's `toString()`), `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:754` (`calcCircuitChanges` diffs the *lists* and records creations/removals as a special property `COMP_STATE_NEW` whose value is the whole serialised item), `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:789` (`restoreState` re-creates a removed item by feeding its text back through the loader). *Why it transfers:* a property-level undo record (`component, property, undoValue, redoValue`) plus a whole-item text record covers both "changed a number" and "deleted a wire" with one stack, and it survives re-implementation of the component classes. For August: an agent that edits a project can produce the same diff without owning a live object graph.
- **[gui]** - **One text format serves the file, the clipboard, paste, and undo** — `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:196` (`loadStrDoc` is the single parser for files, clipboard paste and undo), `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:857` (`copy` puts the *same* text on the clipboard), `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:445` (`circuitHeader` writes the `<circuit version= rev= stepSize= ...>` header). *Why it transfers:* it means an LLM can emit a valid circuit file by emitting text — no editor, no GUI, no binary format. That is the single most important thing in this shard for "circuit simulation as an August skill": **the circuit is a line-oriented, self-describing text file**.
- **[gui]** - **The property system is simultaneously the editor, the file codec and the scripting surface** — `src/gui/properties/boolprop.h:10` (a property is a template over the component type holding a getter/setter member-pointer pair), `src/gui/properties/propdialog.cpp:105` (the dialog instantiates a widget by the property's *type string*), `src/gui/circuitwidget/compbase.cpp:117` (`toString` serialises the property groups), `src/gui/circuitwidget/compbase.cpp:100` (`setPropStr` applies a property by name). *Why it transfers:* adding a knob to a component requires *zero* GUI code — one `new BoolProp<X>(...)` line at the component's constructor. An agent generating component definitions gets the editor for free.
- **[gui]** - **Golden-trace regression testing with the expected waveform stored in the circuit** — `src/gui/dataplotwidget/datachannel.cpp:52` (`doTest` compares the live sample buffer against a stored reference with a 0.1% relative tolerance and *exact* timestamps), `src/gui/dataplotwidget/datachannel.cpp:85` (`testData` serialises the reference as hex-time/value pairs), `src/gui/testing/batchtest.cpp:19` (the harness walks a folder of circuits, runs each, and collects failures), `src/gui/dataplotwidget/plotbase.cpp:145` (`runEvent` fires the comparison at a scheduled simulation time). *Why it transfers:* this is a complete, working test strategy for a circuit simulator that has no other tests: *the circuit is the test case, the expected waveform is a property of the circuit, and a folder of circuits is the suite*. For August: an agent could author a circuit, run it headlessly, and check the captured waveform against a stored expectation with no human in the loop.
- **[gui]** - **A measurement instrument whose user-facing condition string compiles into the embedded script engine** — `src/gui/dataplotwidget/plotbase.cpp:250` (`updateConds` expands `ch1l` -> `(pb.ch1==1)`, wraps it as `void pause() { pb.m_pause = <expr>; }`, compiles it, and caches the function), `src/gui/dataplotwidget/plotbase.cpp:276` (`conditonMet` calls the function and *pauses the simulation* when it is true), `src/gui/dataplotwidget/plotbase.cpp:49` (the per-channel condition variables are registered as AngelScript object properties `ch1`..`ch8`). *Why it transfers:* a 4-character syntax that maps to a real expression language is a superb teaching surface for logic simulation: "stop the simulator when channel 1 goes high" is exactly the kind of rule a student writes. For August: the same pattern gives an agent a natural place to inject "assert this signal" rules into a simulation.
- **[gui]** - **Numeric property fields that evaluate arithmetic expressions** — `src/gui/properties/dspinbox.cpp:30` (`valueFromText` pads trailing operators and runs `"return <expr>"` through the AngelScript engine), `src/gui/properties/dspinbox.cpp:25` (`validate` rejects anything that evaluates to NaN), `src/gui/properties/dspinbox.cpp:42` (`evaluate` uses `ExecuteString` and returns NAN on failure). *Why it transfers:* a student can type `4.7k*2` instead of `9.4k`, and a wrong expression is rejected rather than silently coerced to zero. The engine already exists in the product, so the cost is one class.
- **[gui]** - **The component registry is a flat list of entries carrying a factory pointer, and the palette is data-driven** — `src/gui/componentlist/itemlibrary.cpp:149` (`loadItems` adds ~130 `LibraryItem`s in category order), `src/gui/componentlist/itemlibrary.cpp:345` (`createItem` dispatches a type string to the matching factory), `src/gui/componentlist/componentlist.cpp:200` (`loadXml` parses `<itemlib>/<itemset>/<item>` component sets from disk so components can be added without recompiling). *Why it transfers:* this is the whole "plugin model" of SimulIDE and it is remarkably simple — a list of `(name, category, icon, types, factory)`. New components come in two flavours: a compiled one (one `addItem` line) or a data one (an XML file in the user's data folder).
- **[gui]** - **A mixin whose destructor unregisters it from the engine's per-step callback list** — `src/gui/circuitwidget/updatable.h:8` (the whole class is a virtual `updateStep()`), `src/gui/circuitwidget/updatable.cpp:12` (`~Updatable` calls `Simulator::self()->remFromUpdateList(this)`). *Why it transfers:* every GUI object that needs a per-simulation-step refresh (connectors, pins, the console, the memory table, the debugger, the serial monitor) derives from it, and cannot outlive its registration. A harness with a similar "tick" contract gets the same safety for free.
- **[gui]** - **Colour-by-pointer theme switching** — `src/gui/thememanager.cpp:96` (`getColorPtr` returns a pointer into a `std::vector<uint32_t>` that is rewritten in place on a theme change), `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuit.cpp:50` (the scene stores `m_background`/`m_foreground` as those pointers), `src/gui/circuitwidget/connectorline.cpp:27` (each wire line stores `m_foreColor` as a pointer). *Why it transfers:* a theme switch is one vector rewrite instead of a walk over every drawn object — the trick generalises to any hot-reloadable appearance (a "selected colour", a "net class colour").
- **[gui]** - **Sub-sample a dense trace into a min/max envelope instead of drawing every point** — `src/gui/dataplotwidget/plotdisplay.cpp:310` (points within 0.5 px of each other on screen are collapsed and only their extremes are drawn), `src/gui/dataplotwidget/plotdisplay.cpp:241` (the buffer is walked backwards from the trigger index and the walk stops as soon as it passes the visible start). *Why it transfers:* this is the standard technique for waveform rendering and it is worth having in any simulator: draw the envelope, not the samples.
- **[gui]** - **Throttle UI refreshes that are called once per simulation step** — `src/gui/memory/memtable.cpp:42` (`updateTable` refreshes only every tenth call), `src/gui/memory/mcumonitor.cpp:136` (only the *visible* tabs are refreshed), `src/gui/outpaneltext.cpp:39` (`appendLine` flushes immediately when the simulation is idle and otherwise waits for the next step). *Why it transfers:* the pattern "buffer the text, flush once per tick, and only paint what is visible" is the difference between a simulator that keeps up with real time and one that does not.
- **[gui]** - **A "file changed on disk" bar with four distinct resolutions** — `src/gui/editorwidget/docpage.cpp:62` (`showModifiedBar` warns and offers Reload / Keep Current / Close Tab / Keep Open), `src/gui/editorwidget/docpage.cpp:75` (`showDeletedBar` for a file that no longer exists), `src/gui/editorwidget/editorwidget.cpp:375` (`fileChangedOnDisk` re-arms the `QFileSystemWatcher` after the event, because Qt drops the watch on replace). *Why it transfers:* the four-way choice (discard mine / keep mine / abandon / keep as unsaved) is the right answer to "the file changed under you", and the re-arming detail is a real Qt trap that the code already solves.
- **[gui]** - **The external toolchain is described as data with token substitution** — `src/gui/editorwidget/compiler.cpp:82` (`loadCompiler` parses an XML `<compiler>` with `<step command= arguments= argsDebug=>` children), `src/gui/editorwidget/compiler.cpp:66` (`replaceData` substitutes `$filePath`, `$device`, `$family`, `$inclPath`, ...), `src/gui/editorwidget/compiler.cpp:131` (the dialog grows a property field only if the argument string mentions `$device`/`$family`/`$extraArgs`/`$inclPath`). *Why it transfers:* the "code" half of an embedded-code tool is a text template plus a token substitution table; the *settings UI is derived from the template*. For August: an agent can write or adapt a toolchain definition without touching the host.
- **[gui]** - **Two text dialects and one tolerant tokeniser** — `src/gui/properties/proputils.cpp:24` (`parseXmlProps` splits a quoted `<item a="1" b="2"/>` line into pairs), `src/gui/properties/proputils.cpp:59` (`parseProp` handles the older `name=value;name=value` form), `src/gui/properties/proputils.cpp:35` (the *rule* is "quoted values always come in pairs, and the name is the text after the last space before the quote"). *Why it transfers:* you can read a legacy format and a current format with two small functions and no XML library, and you can add a third dialect cheaply. The key is that the *writer* is the specification.
- **[gui]** - **Auto-connect by dragging with a modifier key** — `src/gui/circuitwidget/pin.cpp:191` (`isMoved` — when a component is moved and Shift is held, it looks for a colliding pin within 3 px and wires it automatically), `src/gui/circuitwidget/pin.cpp:153` (`connectPin` refuses to connect a bus to a non-bus and refuses an already-connected or unused pin). *Why it transfers:* shift-to-snap is a two-line interaction that removes the single most tedious step of building a circuit by hand, and the guard conditions (bus-ness, already connected, unused) are the correctness rules a course exercise would need anyway.
- **[gui]** - **The pin's eight-state visual language** — `src/gui/circuitwidget/pin.h:12` (`pinState_t { undef_state, driven_low, open_low, open_high, out_low, out_high, input_low, input_high }`), `src/gui/circuitwidget/pin.cpp:51` (the colour table), `src/gui/circuitwidget/pin.cpp:444` (the arrow drawing uses *numeric comparisons against the enum* to decide whether to draw an input arrow or a half output arrow). *Why it transfers:* a student debugging a logic circuit needs to see the difference between "driven low", "floating", "driving high" and "input high" at a glance. Encoding the semantics in an ordered enum and deriving the drawing from the order is a compact way to keep the visual and the semantics in sync.
- **[gui]** - **A drag-and-drop protocol that is one comma-separated string** — `src/gui/componentlist/componentlist.cpp:479` (the palette's MIME payload is `name,type`), `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuitview.cpp:96` (`dragEnterEvent` parses it and creates the component immediately), `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuitview.cpp:137` (`dragLeaveEvent` removes it and pops the undo entry so an abandoned drag leaves no history). *Why it transfers:* the palette-to-canvas contract is inspectable text, and the abort path cleans up its own undo entry — a detail that is easy to get wrong and that this code gets right.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Bake a 1-px light rim into a monochrome icon instead of shipping two icon sets or writing a runtime tint.** Every one of the 38 `mainwindow/` SVGs is *the same geometry drawn twice* — a translucent white copy at `opacity:0.6` offset 1.0007 px below a translucent black copy at `opacity:0.7` — e.g. `src/icons/mainwindow/new.svg:71-80`, where the white path starts `m 17.00003,1033.3622` and the black path starts `m 17.00003,1032.3615`. **Why it matters for August:** a harness that renders a schematic, a diff view or a tool palette in a dark theme otherwise has to ship a light and a dark asset for every glyph, or write a colour transform that has to know which pixels are "ink". The rim trick is one extra path per icon, needs no theme system at all, and — because both copies are pure greyscale — still survives the invert-per-asset rule described below.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Invert a themed icon per ASSET, abandoning the whole image on the first non-grey pixel.** `src/gui/thememanager.cpp:113-126`: the loop sets `ok = false; break;` the moment `!qIsGray(pixel)`, and `invertPixmap` returns the *original* pixmap when that happens (`src/gui/thememanager.cpp:125-126`). **Why it matters for August:** it is one boolean per image rather than a per-colour LUT, and it means a mixed-content asset (the LED icons, the motor icons, the two photographs `dsxxx.png` and `esp01.png`) is left alone rather than turning into a white blob. The corollary is a hard rule for the harness: *never put a saturated pixel in a greyscale asset*, because one stray colour disables the inversion for the whole image. The toolbar SVGs obey it (all 38 have only greyscale stops and fills).
- **[icons-assets]** - **Name a resource by its ROLE, not by its artwork, and let the manifest do the aliasing.** `src/application.qrc:65` serves the file `rotateccw.svg` as `undo.svg`; `src/application.qrc:66` serves `rotatecw.svg` as `redo.svg`; `src/application.qrc:71` serves `verify.png` as `setroot.png` — and the only caller asks for `":/setroot.png"` at `src/gui/filebrowser/filebrowser.cpp:157`. The flat `:/` namespace means no caller can get a directory prefix wrong. **Why it matters for August:** a visual redesign becomes a file swap with zero call-site edits, one drawing can legitimately serve two meanings (a rotation arrow *is* an undo arrow), and a "shipped resource" question is answered by one declarative manifest rather than by grep. The rule to steal: **the alias is the API; the filename is an implementation detail.**
- **[icons-assets]** - **Let the PROJECT's own folder win over the shipped asset, in a chain that is cheap to implement.** `Component::setBackground` resolves circuit folder → circuit `data/` folder → shared data folder → compiled-in resource (`src/components/component.cpp:642-644`, with `MainWindow::getCircFilePath` at `src/mainwindow.cpp:438-453` supplying the first two). **Why it matters for August:** this is what makes a *course* able to customise a tool without forking it — a teacher drops `dht22.svg` next to the student's circuit file and the schematic changes; a student drops their own symbol and gets it. It costs three lines and no plugin API. The caveat to steal deliberately: compose the chain on the **file**, not on the directory. `Chip::setBackground` gets this right by passing `"images/"+bck` into `getDataFilePath` (`src/components/subcircuits/chip.cpp:460`), while `Component::setBackground` passes `"images"` and appends the name afterwards (`src/components/component.cpp:643`) — and `getDataFilePath` tests `QFileInfo::exists` on whatever it is given (`src/mainwindow.cpp:423-436`), so a *directory* named `images` short-circuits the rest of the chain. Since the user data folder defaults to the home directory (`src/mainwindow.cpp:57-58`), that is a live hazard, not a theoretical one.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Let a project file EITHER name an image OR embed it.** `Chip` reads a `background` attribute (a *filename*) and a `bckgnddata` attribute (hex-encoded bytes) out of the `<Package>` element of a `.sim1` file (`src/components/subcircuits/chip.cpp:246`, `:259`, `:266-267`); `setBckGndData` decodes the hex string and calls `loadFromData` (`src/components/subcircuits/chip.cpp:390-413`), while `embeedBackground` loads it from disk (`src/components/subcircuits/chip.cpp:415-419`). **Why it matters for August:** a circuit file that travels (a student's homework, a Git commit, an LMS upload) must still render on the grader's machine. A name plus a tiered lookup gives you the small file and the ability to override; the embedded copy gives you the self-contained file. Offering **both** in the same format — and preferring the embedded bytes when present — is the part worth stealing, because it is exactly the tension a coursework tool has.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Organise a component palette by SIGNAL SHAPE, not by part family.** The 20×20 block pictograms `src/icons/components/1to1.png`, `2to2.png`, `2to3.png`, `3to2g.png` — a box with one 2-px stub per input and per output — are used as the *category* icons: "Converters" → `1to2.png` (`src/gui/componentlist/itemlibrary.cpp:305`), "Sensors" → `1to2.png` (`:263`), "Arithmetic" → `2to2.png` (`:287`), "Other Active" → `2to2.png` (`:213`), "Other Logic" → `2to3.png` (`:313`), "Other Outputs" → `1to1.png` (`:247`). **Why it matters for August:** a student told to "split one signal into three" does not know the part number of a demultiplexer, but can *see* the `1to3` pictogram and recognise it. A harness skill that offers "add a part" should offer it first by signal topology and second by part name. The pictograms are 20×20 bitmaps, trivially cheap to author for a whole family — and note the `g` suffix convention (`2to3g.png`, `3to2g.png`): the variant that **grows the box** so the input and output stubs stop sharing rows.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Ship a character-generator font as a single-row sprite sheet addressed by code point, and let a user-defined character be a PATCH of a base glyph.** `src/icons/font/font2.png` is a 2560×16 PNG — exactly 256 cells of 10×16, measured: ink in 189 cells, first at cell 33, last at cell 255 — and the lookup is one integer multiply and one `copy()` (`src/components/outputs/displays/hd44780_base.cpp:297`). The CGRAM path takes a copy of **glyph 0** and paints the user's 8 bytes onto it as 2×2-pixel dots (`src/components/outputs/displays/hd44780_base.cpp:277-296`). **Why it matters for August:** a harness that draws a simulated 7-segment/LCD display, or that lets a student define their own glyph, needs a font it can ship **without a font licence and without a font stack** — one PNG, one multiply, one blit. The CGRAM idea is the transferable part: a custom character is a byte array patched onto a known glyph, not a renderer. The trap to copy deliberately: make the cell pitch a **named constant** and clamp the code, because SimulIDE's `copy()` at `src/components/outputs/displays/hd44780_base.cpp:297` has no bounds check and a truncated atlas fails silently.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Make the "dead asset" set computable, then actually compute it.** `src/application.qrc:2` opens a **single** `<qresource prefix="/">` block that holds all 211 icon entries in one flat namespace — which is what makes the whole check *one diff* against the tree. The shard holds 224 files; the difference is exactly **13** files that can never load: `bug.svg`, `bus_p.png`, `hd44780_20x4.png`, `resistordip0.png`, `socket-H.png`, `socket-V.png`, `socket_p.png`, `subc_ico-0.png`, `subc_ico-1.png`, `termistor.png`, `up.png`, `src/icons/font/font.png`, `src/icons/mainwindow/zoom.svg`. Two are *byte-identical duplicates of live files* — `termistor.png` and `thermistor.png` have the same SHA-256 — and two are hyphen/underscore twins of live files (`socket-H.png` vs `socket_H.png`, `socket-V.png` vs `socket_V.png`). SimulIDE built the machinery and never ran the check. **Why it matters for August:** a harness that ships assets should have a CI gate that fails when a tracked asset is not in the manifest — a one-line diff that would have caught all 13 here, *and* would have caught the seven live references to `":/open.png"`, `":/save.png"`, `":/blank.png"` and `":/fileopen.png"`, none of which is a registered alias.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Make every resource reference resolvable, and make the miss visible.** `":/open.png"` is asked for at `src/gui/filebrowser/filebrowser.cpp:163`, `:169`, `:172`, `src/gui/filebrowser/filewidget.cpp:116` and `src/gui/memory/ramtable.cpp:154`, but the qrc registers `open.svg` (`src/application.qrc:50`) and no `open.png` exists anywhere in the tree; the same is true of `":/save.png"` (8 sites) against `save.svg`, of `":/blank.png"` (3 sites) against `blanc.png`, and of `":/fileopen.png"` (1 site) against no file at all. A `QPixmap` built from an unresolvable path is **null**, and `QIcon(null)` renders as nothing — so seventeen menu actions across the file browser, the memory viewer, the four memory components and the code editor have **no icon**, and nothing says so. The same class of defect is `":font2.png"` at `src/components/outputs/displays/hd44780_base.cpp:15` — one colon instead of two — with the counter-example three lines apart at `src/components/connectors/tunnel.cpp:207` (one colon) versus `:210` (two). **Why it matters for August:** an icon that silently fails to load is invisible in a screenshot and invisible in a test, and a *missing* icon in a palette reads as "this tool has no affordance" rather than "we broke a path". A harness should resolve every resource string at start-up against its manifest and refuse to launch on a miss — the same discipline August applies to its brain-config and doc-link gates.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Give the palette a second role for each drawing.** `gates.png` is the AND-gate artwork used as the *category* pictogram for "Gates" (`src/gui/componentlist/itemlibrary.cpp:281`) while `andgate.png` is the *component* icon (`src/components/logic/gate_and.cpp:22`); `subc.png` is the "Memory" category icon (`src/gui/componentlist/itemlibrary.cpp:295`) while `subcl.png` is the **same geometry in grey** `#515151` for the "Link to Component" menu (`src/components/linkercomponent.cpp:51`). **Why it matters for August:** a palette with 165 component icons and 20 category icons does not need 185 drawings; it needs 165 + 20 *roles* and a way to map artwork onto roles. The grey variant is the neat part — **the same drawing in a second colour is a second meaning**, and it costs one file and no new code.
- **[icons-assets]** - **Put the simulation's state in the *colour* of a badge — and let the icon be the state variable.** The four 32×32 state icons are `poweron.png` (olive `#8F820F`), `poweroff.png` (dark red `#750000`), `simpaused.png` (brown red `#A13028`) and `powerdeb.png` (blue `#435FC0`) — and the white-pixel counts differ (108 / 144 / 171 / 144) so the shapes are not identical either. `CircuitWidget::powerCircOn` sets `":/poweron.png"` and `powerCircOff` sets `":/poweroff.png"` (`src/gui/circuitwidget/circuitwidget.cpp:394`, `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuitwidget.cpp:410`), and the pause toggle switches between `":/simpaused.png"` and `":/pausesim.png"` (`src/gui/circuitwidget/circuitwidget.cpp:469`, `src/gui/circuitwidget/circuitwidget.cpp:479`). **The surprising part is the dispatch**: the next click is routed by *reading the action's own icon text* — `else if( powerCircAct->iconText() == "Off" ) powerCircOn(); else if( powerCircAct->iconText() == "On" ) powerCircOff();` (`src/gui/circuitwidget/circuitwidget.cpp:388-389`) — so the icon and the icon's text are the *only* state store, and the visual badge is what the user reads to know which branch the next click takes. **Why it matters for August:** a harness that shows "running / paused / stopped / debugging" gets a four-way distinction for free that survives greyscale printing and colour-vision deficiency, because the hue *and* the silhouette both change. That is a better answer than a text label or a single icon with a modifier. The *transferable* half is the dispatch idea done deliberately: one explicit state value that drives both the badge and the next action, rather than a state inferred from a widget property. ---
- **[microsim]** - **A device description as DATA, not code** — `src/microsim/mcucreator.cpp:175-202` — the XML `.mcu` descriptor is walked once and each tag dispatches to a `createXxx()` that instantiates a peripheral *by name and type*. A new chip for a course is a new XML file, not a new C++ class. The August harness could adopt exactly this: a course's "74HC595 shift register" or "ATmega328" becomes a declarative spec, and the skill teaches the spec format, not a code generator.
- **[microsim]** - **The register map as a named table with aliases** — `src/microsim/mcucreator.cpp:488-501` — registers carry a name, an address, a reset value, a write mask and a list of bit names, and a bit name may have **aliases** (`A|B`) so that the same bit can be called `WDTIE` on one chip and `WDTCSR.WDIE` on another. This is exactly what an agent needs to write firmware against a datasheet: the bit names in the datasheet become the lookup keys, and the alias list is the chip-family difference.
- **[microsim]** - **A typed, masked, LIFO callback list as the only extension point** — `src/microsim/mcusignal.h:67-78` — every register read/write hook is a `CallBack<Obj>` with a bit mask, and new callbacks are **prepended** so that a later-registered hook runs first; the comment explains that the interrupt flag must be cleared *after* the register-write callback. The transferable lesson is the *ordering contract*: a registration-order dependency is a real requirement, so it is documented at the mechanism rather than discovered as a bug.
- **[microsim]** - **A value-override backchannel on a register read/write** — `src/microsim/mcudataspace.cpp:50-80` — a callback may set `m_regOverride` to substitute the value the CPU sees. This is how a timer publishes its live count, how the AVR comparator clears ACO on read, and how an interrupt clears its flag on write-1-to-clear, all through one mechanism. An August harness that needs "the read of register X returns a computed value" can copy this three-line pattern instead of inventing a getter hierarchy.
- **[microsim]** - **Derive state from the clock, never count events** — `src/microsim/mcutimer.cpp:183-200` — `calcCounter()` computes the counter value from `m_ovfTime - circTime`, so the counter is correct even if the scheduled event was late or coalesced. This is a genuinely better model than "increment on tick" and it makes the simulator robust to event reordering. The August harness's timers/ledgers could use the same principle: compute from the clock, so a missed wake-up does not corrupt the state.
- **[microsim]** - **Only re-schedule when the absolute time changes** — `src/microsim/mcutimer.cpp:117-141` — the overflow event is cancelled and re-added *only if* the computed absolute overflow time differs from the previous one. A register write that does not change the schedule therefore costs zero event-queue churn. This is a cheap, transferable performance rule for any event-driven harness.
- **[microsim]** - **A single `.mcu`-style description for the whole chip, including the peripherals' pin wiring** — `src/microsim/mcucreator.cpp:567-600` and `src/microsim/mcucreator.cpp:1133-1218` — the ports, the timers, the USART pins, the SPI/TWI pins are all named in the XML, and the creator resolves them by name. A course can therefore ship a chip that "lights LED0 on PORTB bit 5 when the counter overflows" as a text file.
- **[microsim]** - **A complete MCU written in a scripting language, with the register file declared by the script** — `src/microsim/cores/scripted/scriptcpu.cpp:61-99` and `src/microsim/cores/scripted/scriptcpu.cpp:41-45` — the script declares its own registers (`addCpuReg`) and variables (`addCpuVar`) and they appear in the monitor; the script *is* the CPU. For an August skill this is the "write your own processor" track: a student implements a 4-bit ALU in a script and it runs on the canvas next to the real chips.
- **[microsim]** - **A script preprocessor with a bundled library path** — `src/microsim/modules/script/scriptbase.cpp:117-139` — `#include "x"` resolves relative to the script and `#include <x>` resolves to the bundled `scriptlib`, and the include is inlined textually before compilation. A course can therefore ship a standard library of teaching peripherals (`#include <twi-slave>`) without a package manager.
- **[microsim]** - **A generic peripheral whose behaviour is a script** — `src/microsim/modules/script/scriptmodule.cpp:43-47` — `configureA/B/C`, `callBack` and `callBackDoub` are looked up by exact *declaration string* after compilation, so the script's register writes drive the same `McuModule` contract the C++ peripherals use. That is how a new peripheral can be added to an existing chip without touching the chip's class.
- **[microsim]** - **A shared-memory arena as the protocol to an external CPU core** — `src/microsim/cores/qemu/qemudevice.h:12-25` and `src/microsim/cores/qemu/qemudevice.cpp:78-117` — the entire interface to `qemu-system-*` is one flat C struct in shared memory (time, register address, register data, IRQ number/level, action code), created with `shm_open`+`mmap` or `CreateFileMapping`+`MapViewOfFile`. The pattern transfers directly: an August tool that needs a real external tool (a compiler, a solver, a simulator) can expose a shared-memory arena rather than a socket, and get a cheap, inspectable protocol.
- **[microsim]** - **Model a chip from a citable book, with the figure numbers in the comments** — `src/microsim/cores/z80/ula_zx48k.cpp:33-47` and the "Figure 18-12"/"Figure 18-15" comments in the contention logic — the ZX Spectrum ULA is modelled from Chris Smith's *The ZX Spectrum ULA*, with the source named at the top of the file and each bus-contention equation tagged with the figure it came from. This is the model an agent should copy for course work: the authority is named, the equations are checkable, and the colour tables are data.
- **[microsim]** - **Decode a protocol from timing, not from a bit stream** — `src/microsim/modules/onewire/onewire.cpp:44-77` — a 1-Wire bit is decoded by measuring the pulse width (>480 µs reset, >30 µs zero, <15 µs one) on a single wire. Any bus whose information is in the timing can be simulated this way, and the model even records where the datasheet and the real device disagree ("Tested in real device 202 us").
- **[microsim]** - **Cycle-accurate bus modelling as the enabling layer for peripherals** — `src/microsim/cores/z80/z80core.cpp:855-873` plus `src/microsim/cores/z80/z80cycles.h:25-53` — the CPU does not just execute instructions, it issues bus *operations* per machine cycle, and the number of cycles/T-states per opcode comes from a table. This is what makes a real video ULA simulable at all; for course work it is the difference between "an LED blinks" and "the video chip sees the real bus".
- **[microsim]** - **Explicit bus timing constants taken from the datasheet** — `src/microsim/cores/mcs65/mcs65core.cpp:139-142` — `tHR = 10 ns`, `tHA = 25 ns`, `tHW = 20 ns`, named and commented. Small, but it is the discipline that makes a cycle-accurate model auditable.
- **[microsim]** - **Every family plugs into five fixed seams** — `src/microsim/cores/mcu8bits.h:46-60`, `src/microsim/mcumodule.h:23-31`, `src/microsim/mcudataspace.h:33-34`, `src/microsim/cores/cpu8bits.h:30-36` — `Cpu8bits` (PC/STATUS/stack), `Mcu8bits` (RAM + SFR + stack helpers), `DataSpace` (masked register file), `McuModule` (setup/reset/configure/callBack/sleep) and `McuCreator` (per-family factory). A course can add a new architecture by filling in five seams, and the repo's own seven cores are the worked examples.
- **[microsim]** - **A shared bus engine reused by every chip family** — `src/microsim/modules/spi/spimodule.cpp:128-146` and `src/microsim/modules/twi/twimodule.cpp:41-99` — the SPI and I2C protocols live once, in chip-agnostic modules, and each family only supplies its registers and its pin wiring (the AVR SPI is 130 lines on top of a 203-line shared engine). The August harness should build its simulation primitives at this level, once, and let the "chips" be thin.
- **[microsim]** - **Resolve a bit field by name, not by position** — `src/microsim/datautils.cpp:16-34` — `getRegBits("ADEN,ADPS0")` finds the base bit by rotating the mask, so no core ever hard-codes a bit index. This is what makes the register map data-driven, and it is the single change that would most improve an agent's firmware-generation accuracy.
- **[resources#1]** - **Three-tier resource resolution — user data folder, then install folder, then compiled-in resource, with the *existence* of the file as the whole selection rule** — `resources/data/codeeditor/compilers/compilers/avrgcc.xml:3` (the file that a user can override) with the resolution order at `src/mainwindow.cpp:423-436` — *Why it matters for August:* August's data directory, skills directory and provider store already have a user-overrides-install relationship, but the resolver is scattered. A single `resolveDataFile(name)` with the order *user → install → packaged* and no configuration is a two-function change that makes every shipped data file overridable without a recompile and without a migration. It is also exactly the shape that lets the harness ship a default `diodes.model`-like policy file the user can edit.
- **[resources#1]** - **The property sheet is a TEXT FILE, not a UI** — `resources/data/help/logicinputs.txt:1-9` (a 9-line fragment that every digital component reuses) and `resources/data/help/andgate.txt:7-11` (a component whose entire page is five `#include` lines) — *Why it matters for August:* a skill or a tool can render a component's full option set, defaults and units without linking against the component model. The same text drives the GUI, and an agent can read it to understand what a knob does. This is the cheapest possible "self-describing tool": the description, the default and the unit live in one place that both the UI and the model read.
- **[resources#1]** - **Composition by textual `#include`, resolved recursively** — `resources/data/help/flipflopfull.txt:7` (one include) and `resources/data/help/counter.txt:22` (an include whose target does not exist) — *Why it matters for August:* August's skills are markdown with an obvious include story; a help page that is *assembled* from fragments means N components can share one physics description and one UI description without either duplicating it. The counter.txt dangling include is also the cautionary half: the include graph has **no validation step**, so a typo becomes a silent "No help available" string in the middle of a user's dialog. If August copies this pattern it must add the check the repo lacks — a grep for `#include` targets that do not exist.
- **[resources#1]** - **A declarative, user-editable device model library in the SPICE parameter vocabulary** — `resources/data/diodes.model:5` (one line: `satCurr_nA`, `resist`, `emCoef`, `brkDown`) — *Why it matters for August:* this is a *policy file*, not a config file: four numbers per row, named after the physics, loadable without a recompile, and merged with hard-coded defaults so a missing file is harmless. August has no equivalent for anything as physical, but the same shape works for per-model pricing tables, token-cost weights or per-tool rate limits — named parameters in a flat TSV, merged over defaults, never a config that can leave a key unset.
- **[resources#1]** - **Derive the UI from the template, not from a form** — `resources/data/codeeditor/compilers/template.txt:7-14` (the substitution list) and `src/gui/editorwidget/compiler.cpp:144-154` (the property dialog *grows a "Device" field because the argument string contains `$device`*) — *Why it matters for August:* a tool that is declared as a template should grow its own options from the template. A "run this tool" declaration that mentions `${device}` should surface a device picker, and one that mentions `${extraArgs}` should surface a free-text field — with no per-tool UI code at all. This is a concrete, small mechanism that removes an entire class of hand-written forms.
- **[resources#1]** - **The type suffix is a BITFIELD, not an identifier** — `resources/data/codeeditor/compilers/types.txt:10-16` and the worked example at `resources/data/codeeditor/compilers/compilers/dummy_c.xml:3` (`type="c10"`) — *Why it matters for August:* when one registry has to carry several orthogonal facts, encode them in one short string and *write down the encoding in a 16-line file next to it*. The single page that defines the convention is what makes five different toolchain descriptors interoperable. August's own registries (tool definitions, permissions, model profiles) are exactly the place where a one-line type string with a documented bit layout would compress a config.
- **[resources#1]** - **A cookbook that is the FORMAT SPECIFICATION, written next to the files it describes** — `resources/data/codeeditor/syntax/readme_syntax:1-16` (the header states the loader function and the directory) and `readme_syntax:197` (the `_dark.syntax` theme convention) — *Why it matters for August:* when a harness exposes a user-extensible format, the format's documentation should live *in the directory the user will look in*, name the exact function that parses it, and include a minimal working example. The 239 lines here are the reason a new assembler is a 15-line file.
- **[resources#1]** - **The "one file per component, named by the component's registry id, lower-cased" convention** — `resources/data/help/touchpadr.txt:1` (the file whose name is the mangled id `TouchPadR`) and `resources/data/help/7-segbcd.txt:1` — *Why it matters for August:* a naming convention that is a pure function of the object's id means the help, the icon (`resources/data/images/ic2.png`) and the component itself cannot drift apart, and a new component needs no registration. August's tool surface would benefit from the same: the doc file's name IS the tool's id, lower-cased, with spaces removed.
- **[resources#1]** - **A "volts equal to metres" input convention instead of a dedicated sensor dialog** — `resources/data/help/sr04.txt:4` — *Why it matters for August:* for a course tool, the cheapest interaction is to reuse a general-purpose input and give it a *unit convention* rather than building a control per device. A potentiometer is a dial, a temperature is a dial, a distance is a voltage with a stated scale. Every one of those avoids a bespoke widget and is teachable in one line of documentation.
- **[resources#1]** - **The solver's knobs are documented as *user-facing settings*, with the accuracy/speed trade-off stated in words** — `resources/data/help/simulation.txt:15-17` ("Update step for reactive components. Icrease: better simulation speed but less accuracy") and `resources/data/help/simulation.txt:10-12` (Max Iterations, `0` for no limit) — *Why it matters for August:* August has exactly this shape of knob (model rounds, context window, budget). SimulIDE's formulation — *one named step, a plain-English statement of what you lose, and `0` meaning unbounded* — is the phrasing to copy, and it doubles as the documentation.
- **[resources#1]** - **The "unbounded by default, armed by absence" convention for a safety limit** — `resources/data/help/simulation.txt:10-12` (`0 for no limit`) versus `resources/data/help/circuit.txt:16-19` (`0 disables Auto Backup`) — *Why it matters for August:* it is the *opposite* of the AGENTS.md rule that an absent key means ARMED at shipped constants. SimulIDE is explicit that `0` disables and that the value is shown in the UI with its default in parentheses, so a user can always see whether a limit is on. The transferable part is the *visibility* (the default is printed next to every property in every help file) and the *unambiguous sentinel* (0 = off, never "absent means off").
- **[resources#1]** - **A per-component property sheet that states the failure mode in the same file as the feature** — `resources/data/help/led.txt:3` ("Blinks if maximum current is exceeded", with the Grounded option at `led.txt:11-13`) and `resources/data/help/elcapacitor.txt:2` ("Blinks if polarity is wrong") — *Why it matters for August:* when a tool has a physical failure mode, making it a *visible in-band signal* (the LED blinks) rather than a log line means the user learns the model by watching it. The same trick — a self-reporting widget instead of an error toast — is how an August tool should teach a failure the model can produce.
- **[resources#1]** - **A synthetic-component trick that lets a taught example be *executed*, not just described** — `resources/data/help/csource.txt:3` ("Feasible to make: VCVS, CCVS, VCCS, CCCS" — one component, four topologies, selected by two booleans at `csource.txt:7` and `csource.txt:11`) and `resources/data/help/function.txt:7` (the `i0 | i1` function list) — *Why it matters for August:* for logic-coursework viability, a "Function" component whose output is a Boolean expression over named inputs, and a single "controlled source" that spans all four controlled-source topologies, are the two abstractions that let a student build *any* analogue or combinational block from a small, learnable set of parts. Both are documented in a few lines each.
- **[resources#1]** - **A 2-digit bitfield plus a hand-trimmed translation subset as examples of "the smallest thing that carries the fact"** — `resources/data/codeeditor/compilers/types.txt:4` ("The key is in the last 2 numeric digits") and `resources/translations/qt/qt_de.ts:4-6` (three contexts only) — *Why it matters for August:* both are examples of *restraint*: a two-character convention instead of a schema, and eleven kilobytes of translation instead of a megabyte. A harness that ships a *curated* set of translated strings for exactly the surfaces it shows beats a full framework catalogue on every axis except completeness — and completeness is the one thing a coursework user does not need.
- **[resources#2]** - **A translation catalogue is a free, machine-readable index of an entire application's UI surface — 181 classes, 190 source files, 775 strings, no code execution required.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:4` — the `ADC` context alone names the class, points at `src/components/logic/adc.cpp`, and lists each user-visible label. For August: a harness that must reason about a GUI app it cannot run can parse one XML file to get the feature inventory (context = feature area) and the code hooks (`<location>` = where to look). This is the cheapest "what can this app actually do" index available, and it is already in the repo, version-controlled, and regenerated by a standard tool.
- **[resources#2]** - **The catalogue's `<location>` pointers are a SNAPSHOT with a measurable drift, and the drift is a uniform per-file line offset — so treat the catalogue as a feature index, not a line index.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:2080` says `editorwidget.cpp:708`; the actual `tr("&New\tCtrl+N")` is at `src/gui/editorwidget/editorwidget.cpp:768` — a clean **+60** offset held across 20 consecutive menu entries, because 60 lines were inserted above that block after the catalogue was cut. The same holds for `src/mainwindow.cpp` (+3, `resources/translations/simulide.ts:3878` → `src/mainwindow.cpp:105`) and `src/components/component.cpp` (+9, `resources/translations/simulide.ts:1265` → `src/components/component.cpp:346`). Overall accuracy is 73.3%, but **90.5% under `src/components/**` and 44.4% under `src/gui/**`**. For August: any skill that says "the string table tells you which file to open" is right; any skill that says "…and at which line" is wrong unless it re-verifies. A harness that trusts a stored pointer without re-checking will open the wrong function — and the failure is silent, because the file is still openable.
- **[resources#2]** - **Bind every user-visible string to its exact source line, so the string table doubles as a code map — but re-verify the binding, and score the binding.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:7` — `<location filename="../../src/components/logic/adc.cpp" line="25"/>`, which still resolves exactly (`src/components/logic/adc.cpp:25` is `tr("ADC")`). For August: "which file produces this label?" becomes a lookup instead of a grep. The *scoring* is the stealable part: because `lupdate` emits the pointer for free, you can measure, per file, how much of the map is still true, and treat a catalogue whose accuracy has fallen below a threshold as a signal to re-run the generator rather than as ground truth.
- **[resources#2]** - **The locale file itself is where UI-string defects live, and they are all detectable by comparing the TRANSLATION to the SOURCE's structural characters.** Two concrete instances: (a) `resources/translations/simulide_zh_CN.ts:2138` — `<translation>&amp;保存→Ctrl+S</translation>` where the source is `&Save\tCtrl+S`; the TAB (U+0009) was replaced by a literal U+2192 arrow in nine strings (`:2118`–`:2198`). (b) `resources/translations/simulide_es.ts:908` — `&Open Circuit\tCtrl+O` → `Abrir Circuito\tCtrl+O`; the `&` mnemonic was dropped in nine menu strings (`:908`, `:918`, `:928`, `:2211`, `:2221`, `:2231`, `:2241`, `:2251`, `:2261`). For August: a **l10n lint** that asserts "the translation preserves the source's tab, its `%n` placeholders and its `&` mnemonic" is a twenty-line check that catches two live shipping bugs in a mature 2.0.0 codebase. Note the false-positive boundary the data gives you for free: `Use RCO & RBO` → `Usar RCO y RBO` is *correct* (`&` before a space is a literal), so the rule must distinguish the two.
- **[resources#2]** - **An accelerator that is concatenated outside the `tr()` call is invisible to the translator — and the catalogue proves it.** `src/components/component.cpp:346` is `menu->addAction( m_theme->icon(":/copy.svg"),tr("Copy")+"\tCtrl+C");` — the label is inside `tr()` but the `\tCtrl+C` is not, so `lupdate` captures only `Copy`. The catalogue shows the consequence exactly: the `Component` context records bare `Copy`/`Cut`/`Remove`/`Rotate CW`/`Horizontal Flip` (`resources/translations/simulide.ts:1265`, `:1270`, `:1275`, `:1280`, `:1295`) while the `EditorWidget` context records the full `&Copy\tCtrl+C` (`resources/translations/simulide.ts:2130`). The same user action is therefore two different translatable strings depending on where the shortcut was typed.
