For August: when a harness generates or reviews UI, the rule "the shortcut must live *inside* the translatable string, or it will silently vanish in every non-English locale" is a concrete lint, and this repo is the worked example.
- **[resources#2]** - **The circuit project format is a wildcard family, and the format's own version history is retained in the data.** Live: `resources/translations/simulide.ts:778` — `Circuits (*.sim*);;All files (*.*)`. Superseded but kept as stale records: `resources/translations/simulide_zh_CN.ts:793`, `resources/translations/simulide_es.ts:856`, `resources/translations/simulide_zh_TW.ts:847` — `Circuits (*.sim1);;All files (*.*)`. So the app went from exactly one circuit extension (`.sim1`) to a family (`.sim*`), and the current generation is `.sim2` (the crash-recovery backup file is `backup.sim2`, `src/mainwindow.cpp:101`). The sibling formats are `.vst` (component sets, `resources/translations/simulide.ts:4975`), `.package` (IC packages, `:5905`), `.vcd` (waveform dump, `:3335`), `.hex` (firmware, `:4037`), `.img`, `.wav`. For August: a skill that teaches "how to open a SimulIDE circuit" can state the format family, the sidecar formats, and — because the format is suffix-versioned — can say "a `.sim1` file is the old single-version format" without reading any code.
- **[resources#2]** - **Localisation coverage is a per-locale completeness metric you can compute with one parse, and it exposes locales that ship but do nothing.** `resources/translations/simulide_es.ts` = 1,225 of 1,260 live strings finished, 178 of 181 contexts touched; `resources/translations/simulide_de.ts` = 544 of 1,260 and 103 of 181; `resources/translations/simulide_zh_CN.ts` = 1,115 of 1,260 and 165 of 181; `resources/translations/simulide_zh_TW.ts` = 1,075 of 1,260 and 164 of 181; `resources/translations/simulide_pt_BR.ts` = **0 of 1,260** (its 64 "translations" are all `obsolete`). For August: this is a ready-made template for a "feature completeness" readout on any localized surface — count live-and-finished records over live records, and report both a string percentage and a context percentage. pt_BR is the proof that the metric catches a real defect (a shipped, selectable, entirely inert locale) that no other check would notice. The `type=` attribute is what makes it a one-liner: finished = no `type`, unfinished = `type="unfinished"`, stale = `type="vanished"` or `type="obsolete"`.
- **[resources#2]** - **Provenance rides on the record itself: `unfinished` / `obsolete` / `vanished` are attributes of the value, not entries in a side ledger.** `resources/translations/simulide_zh_CN.ts:794` (`type="vanished"`), `resources/translations/simulide_pt_BR.ts:34` (`type="obsolete"`), `resources/translations/simulide_en.ts:9` (`type="unfinished"`). For August: agent-generated content can carry its own provenance in-band — "machine-drafted but unverified" vs "human-approved" vs "retired" — instead of a parallel ledger that can disagree with the payload. The stale-record mechanism here is exactly that, and it survives regeneration: the Spanish file still holds its own Spanish `*.sim1` translation at `resources/translations/simulide_es.ts:856`, long after the source string changed to `*.sim*`, so the history of the format survives the loss of the string.
- **[resources#2]** - **The keyboard map is recoverable from the string table, because the mnemonic, label and accelerator live in one token.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:829` — `<source>&amp;Open Circuit Ctrl+O</source>`; also `:819` (`&amp;New C&amp;ircuit Ctrl+N`), `:839` (`&amp;Save Circuit Ctrl+S`), `:849` (`Save Circuit &amp;As... Ctrl+Shift+S`), and the editor's own set at `:2080`–`:2160` (`Undo Ctrl+Z` at `:2150`, `Redo Ctrl+Shift+Z` at `:2160`). For August: an agent driving a GUI needs the shortcut map, and here it is in a machine-readable table with the accessible names attached — you can reconstruct the whole keybinding surface of an application by reading one file and splitting on the tab. (With the two caveats above: the tab only survives if the translator keeps it, and the accelerator only exists in the catalogue if the developer typed it inside the `tr()` call.)
- **[resources#2]** - **Undo depth is a user-visible preference, not a hardcoded constant, and undo/redo is exposed in both the canvas and the code editor.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:311` — `Undo Steps` (catalogue location `appdialog.ui:910`; the string is actually at `src/gui/appdialogs/appdialog.ui:941`) sits in the preferences dialog next to `Auto Backup` (`:301`, actually `src/gui/appdialogs/appdialog.ui:880`) and `Seconds` (`:306`). The canvas verbs are in the `Component` context (`resources/translations/simulide.ts:1260`–`:1300`: `Properties`, `Copy`, `Cut`, `Remove`, `Rotate CW`, `Rotate CCW`, `Rotate 180`, `Horizontal Flip`, `Vertical Flip` from `src/components/component.cpp`), and the canvas's own `CircuitView` context carries the `Undo`/`Redo` actions at `resources/translations/simulide.ts:791` and `:796` — the same two words the code editor uses at `:2150` and `:2160`. For August: an editor-shaped tool should make the undo budget a *setting* rather than a fixed constant — and should expose the same undo vocabulary in both surfaces it edits, so the user learns one word for one concept.
- **[resources#2]** - **The solver's whole numerical regime is present as human-readable preferences, and a restart is explicitly signposted.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:321`–`:361` (`src/gui/appdialogs/appdialog.ui`): `Speed` (`:321`), `Steps per Second` (`:326`), `Target Step` (`:331`), `Real Step` (`:336`), `NonLinear` (`:341`), `Max. Iterations` (`:346`), `Reactive` (`:351`), `Logic Outputs Edges` (`:356`), `Slope Steps` (`:361`) — and `Restart required to apply new settings.` at `:371`. (Each carries an `<location>` into `src/gui/appdialogs/appdialog.ui`; those `.ui` line numbers are themselves stale — the `.ui` files are only 64.2% accurate, same drift as the `.cpp` ones.) For August: these are exactly the knobs an agent needs to reason about simulation fidelity ("how many steps per second?", "is the timestep adaptive or fixed?", "what is the iteration ceiling?"). A catalogue like this tells you the *entire exposed parameter surface of the engine* without opening a single engine file — which is what makes a simulation skill writable rather than guesswork. The `Restart required…` string is the design lesson: a setting whose effect is deferred must say so in the UI, not just in the docs.
- **[resources#2]** - **Crash recovery is worded as a stated consequence BEFORE the question, and it names the file.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:3878`–`:3900` (`src/mainwindow.cpp:105`–`109`): *"Looks like SimulIDE crashed..."* / *"There is an auto-saved copy of the Circuit"* / *"You must save it with any other name if you want to keep it"* / *"This file will be auto-deleted!!"* / *"Do you want to open the auto-saved copy of the Circuit?"*. For August: an agent that rewrites a user's file needs exactly this shape — tell the user what the destructive default will do (auto-delete), tell them how to keep it (save under another name), and only then ask. Four of the five strings are the warning; the question is last. (The same discipline appears on the ordinary path: `Circuit has been modified. Do you want to save your changes?` at `resources/translations/simulide.ts:939`.)
- **[resources#2]** - **A template file and a translation file are different kinds of thing, and the build should know the difference.** `resources/translations/simulide.ts:3` (`<TS version="2.1">`, no language) versus `resources/translations/simulide_en.ts:3` (`<TS version="2.1" language="en">`); `SimulIDE.pri:17` globs `*.ts` into `TRANSLATIONS` and `SimulIDE.pri:157`–`SimulIDE.pri:161` runs `lrelease` on all of them, but `src/application.qrc:11`–`src/application.qrc:17` embeds only the seven real locales — the template's `.qm` is compiled on every build and never shipped. For August: when a harness drives a build, "the file that is an INPUT to a tool" and "the file that is an ARTEFACT" should be distinguishable by naming, not by which tool last touched it.
- **[simulator-core]** - **The element is the event record — a scheduled component is a node in a sorted intrusive list, and a double-schedule is refused, not merged** - `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:526-566` (refusal at `:530-534`), with the element-side fields at `src/simulator/e-element.h:40-44` - the queue is a singly-linked list threaded through the elements' own `nextEvent` pointers, so scheduling costs zero allocations and the element's `eventTime` doubles as the "already pending" flag. A second `addEvent` on the same element is *rejected* with a warning instead of being merged or silently corrupting the order. An August harness that schedules tool work (or a simulator tick) gets this for free: one pending job per handle, refuse the duplicate, and make the handle itself the queue node.
- **[simulator-core]** - **The four-hook component contract: `initialize` / `stamp` / `runEvent` / `voltChanged`** - `src/simulator/e-element.h:19-23`, dispatched at `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:266-273` (event) and `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:301-317` (voltage change) - a new simulated device implements four methods and the engine takes care of scheduling it, stamping it into the model, and waking it when its net's voltage moves. This is the minimal surface area a plugin has to implement, and it is why SimulIDE supports ~120 devices without a registry file: the class self-registers in its constructor (`src/simulator/e-element.cpp:20`). A skill that wants to add a new circuit primitive to an August tool should copy this shape, not invent a plugin manifest.
- **[simulator-core]** - **Dirty-bit stamping on two levels: per node AND per connected group** - `src/simulator/e-node.cpp:105-107` and `src/simulator/e-node.cpp:167-172` (node level), `src/simulator/circmatrix.cpp:120-137` (group level) - each node carries `m_admitChanged`/`m_currChanged` and each connected group carries its own pair, so a solve pass costs only what actually changed. The incremental update is **exact** (a dirty node is fully re-stamped, not approximately patched) and the group-level bit means an untouched island of the circuit is not even re-solved. This is the pattern to lift for any harness that re-solves a model after a small edit: dirty at the object, dirty at the partition, skip whole partitions.
- **[simulator-core]** - **Nodal decomposition into independent connected components, with a closed-form escape hatch for singletons** - `src/simulator/circmatrix.cpp:66-110` (the DFS) and `src/simulator/circmatrix.cpp:72-76` (the singleton case), closed analytically at `src/simulator/e-node.cpp:243-250` - the circuit is split into independent groups by a recursive walk of the connection graph, each group is factored and solved on its own, and a group of one node never enters the matrix at all (V = I/A). For August: split a problem into independent sub-problems by dependency, and give the trivial case an exact closed form instead of a general algorithm.
- **[simulator-core]** - **`gmin` — a guaranteed conductance floor that makes exponential models converge and the matrix non-singular** - `src/simulator/elements/active/e-diode.cpp:63-64` (and its use at `:85`), `src/simulator/elements/active/e-bjt.cpp:104-105` (and `:125-126`) - every non-linear element adds a small conductance that grows with the iteration count and is capped at 0.1 S, so an "off" transistor still conducts a little and the linear system is never singular. This is the single highest-value trick in the shard: a leak-to-ground that buys both numerical conditioning and convergence, at the cost of a physically negligible current.
- **[simulator-core]** - **Logarithmic step limiting on exponentials (damped Newton)** - `src/simulator/elements/active/e-bjt.cpp:141-152` and `src/simulator/elements/active/e-diode.cpp:99-109` - the junction voltage may not jump by more than about 2·Vt in one iteration; if it tries, it is pulled back to `vold + Vt·ln(1 + Δ/Vt)`, i.e. the *logarithm* of the requested step. Any August component that evaluates an exponential (a transistor, a rate curve, a sigmoid) needs this or it will oscillate or overflow on the first iteration.
- **[simulator-core]** - **Geometric relaxation of the conductance instead of a full Newton step** - `src/simulator/elements/active/e-jfet.cpp:126-129` - the new conductance is approached by only 0.1 % per iteration (`m_admit + 0.001·(tempAdmit − m_admit)`). Cheap, unconditionally stable, and a good default whenever a model's derivative cannot be trusted — the same idea as a learning-rate or an EMA, applied to a solver.
- **[simulator-core]** - **The solver owns the iteration budget; the element only says "not converged"** - `src/simulator/simulator.h:89` (`notCorverged()`) with the loop at `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:291-321` and the cap at `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:306` - a component never decides when to give up; it raises a one-line flag, and the engine owns the iteration limit (`m_maxNlstp`, default 100 000) and the "NonLinear Not Converging" warning. An August skill should have the same shape: the component reports a status, the engine owns the budget and the failure.
- **[simulator-core]** - **"Pause the simulation, mutate, resume" as the universal mutation protocol** - `src/simulator/e-element.cpp:45-59` (per-element), `src/simulator/elements/passive/e-resistor.cpp:47-52` (per-property), `src/simulator/elements/outputs/e-led.cpp:123-132` (from the GUI thread), `src/simulator/elements/e-clocked_device.cpp:71` (before a reconfiguration) - every change that can affect the model is wrapped in `pauseSim()`/`resumeSim()`, so a mutation can never land in the middle of a solve. This is the cleanest rule I have seen for "one thread is reading state while another wants to change it".
- **[simulator-core]** - **Voltage-change subscription instead of polling** - `src/simulator/e-node.cpp:259-277` (the fan-out) with the subscribe door at `src/simulator/e-pin.cpp:58-63` - a device registers on a net; when the net's voltage changes, the device is placed on the simulator's changed list and its `voltChanged()` runs. The `added` flag makes the fan-out idempotent. An August harness that must react to a changed world should offer this shape — *register on the thing, be woken when it moves* — instead of a poll loop.
- **[simulator-core]** - **"Give the time base a name and a divisor" — a single clock element that every time-domain element subscribes to** - `src/simulator/elements/analogclock.cpp:36-45` (the fan-out) and `src/simulator/elements/analogclock.cpp:47-51` (the subscriber list), consumed at `src/simulator/elements/passive/e-reactive.cpp:92-97` - instead of integrating continuously, the engine has one periodic clock; capacitors and inductors are re-sampled once per clock tick and their companion model is rebuilt from the step. A logic-circuit tool wants exactly this: one knob (period ÷ divider) that sets the resolution of time for the whole simulation.
- **[simulator-core]** - **An edge detector as a reusable base class, with "allow" aliased to "rising edge"** - `src/simulator/elements/e-clocked_device.cpp:47-67` and `src/simulator/elements/e-clocked_device.h:11-17` - a device that needs a clock edge, or an enable, derives from one base that keeps the previous level and classifies the new one into Low/Rising/High/Falling/Allow. Every flip-flop, counter, shift register, SPI and TWI module in the codebase reuses it. For logic-coursework tooling, an edge detector with rising/falling/enable semantics is the single most reusable primitive — and the deliberate aliasing of `Clock_Allow` with `Clock_Rising` is a good reminder to model "level-sensitive" and "edge-sensitive" as one enum with an explicit alias rather than as two parallel mechanisms.
- **[simulator-core]** - **The engine holds no netlist — the netlist is rebuilt from the editor's pin map at every start** - `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:354-390` (`createNodes`) with the ordering that makes it correct at `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:415-422` and the reason it is fragile at `src/simulator/e-node.h:71-73` - the simulation nodes are constructed from `Circuit::self()->m_pinMap` at start-up; node numbers are assigned, then `eNode::initialize()` wipes the connection lists, then `stamp()` re-creates them (because `Connection` captures its peer's node number at construction). The consequence for August: **the engine is a pure function of the editor state**, so anything that can produce a pin map — including a headless, file-driven or agent-driven model — can drive a simulation without touching the GUI.
- **[simulator-core]** - **Measure the engine's throughput instead of assuming it** - `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:183-196` (real speed: simulated ps per real second) and `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:139-143` (simulation load: the fraction of the timer tick spent in the solve) - the engine reports two distinct numbers: "am I keeping up with the requested speed?" and "how loaded is the solver?". A harness that drives a simulator in a loop wants exactly these two, and it wants them computed from one monotonic clock rather than from a stopwatch around the call.
- **[simulator-core]** - **Keep the GUI thread out of the solver: the work runs on a future and is joined at the tick boundary** - `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:147-148` (spawn) and `src/simulator/simulator.cpp:126-133` (join), with `volatile simState_t m_state` at `src/simulator/simulator.h:150` existing solely because of that split - the timer callback stops the future, waits for it, and only then launches the next frame; the shared state variable is `volatile` because the solver thread reads it. The same shape — a worker future, a tick-boundary join, and one volatile state word — is what August would need to keep a long-running simulation responsive without freezing the UI.
- **[simulator-core]** - **A device library as data, not code** - `src/simulator/elements/active/e-diode.cpp:160-201` (the parser) with `resources/data/diodes.model` - a small XML file holds every diode, zener and LED part; `setModel(name)` looks it up in a static map. Adding a part is a data edit, and the map is loaded lazily once per process (`src/simulator/elements/active/e-diode.cpp:30`).

## deepseek-harness — 2145 ideas across the shards read so far

- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A "strict definition withdrawn" must fail, not fall back** — `packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts:862` — The Gateway tracks whether an endpoint *ever* had a strict generated descriptor (`ctx.typert.local.hasSeen(endpoint)`) and, when the definition owner unloads, throws `gateway/definition-unavailable` ("its strict definition was withdrawn and SRC fallback is forbidden") instead of quietly switching to the permissive SRC path. For August: a method that was once strongly typed must never silently degrade to duck-typed dispatch — that is exactly how a "the validation got weaker" regression becomes invisible.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A reconnecting stream's opening item needs an explicit accept() handshake** — `packages/api/gateway/src/client/remote-stream.ts:16` — Each item carries a monotone `generation` number and the consumer calls `accept()` only *after* it has validated the opening baseline or cursor. The domain then classifies a generation end with `ended(accepted)`: accepted → retryable carrier loss; not accepted → terminal. For August: this is the missing half of "the model is mid-stream" — a dropped SSE is only fatal if the consumer never got a consistent starting point.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **One baseline per generation, and the previous baseline stays published while retrying** — `packages/api/gateway/src/client/snapshot-stream.ts:31` — `RemoteSnapshotStream` requires exactly one snapshot per generation, refuses a delta that arrives before it, and keeps the *previous* domain snapshot visible while the carrier reconnects; a replacement becomes accepted only after the domain's `replace()` succeeds. For August's transcript/projection surfaces: a reconnect must never blank the screen, and a half-applied replacement must be all-or-nothing.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **The journal validates continuity itself, using a domain-supplied cursor algebra** — `packages/api/gateway/src/client/journal-stream.ts:48` — the domain supplies `first`, `last`, `compare` and `follows`; the stream refuses a page whose entries are discontinuous or whose tail is not the requested cursor (journal-stream.ts:558, :574). For August: a compaction or a reconnect can produce a gap; the check belongs in one shared place, parameterised by the domain, not repeated per caller.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Every stream carries a byte-bounded inbox and overflow fails the stream, not the process** — `packages/api/gateway/src/stream-server.ts:61` — `streamInboxBytes` bounds the buffered uplink frames; exceeding it fails the logical stream with `gateway/uplink-overflow` (stream-server.ts:360), and the Gateway publishes the *window* but issues no credits. For August: a tool that produces output faster than the model consumes it needs a hard byte ceiling with a named failure, not an unbounded queue.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A liveness signal that counts buffered writes, not just pings** — `packages/api/gateway/src/stream-server.ts:114` — two missed heartbeats terminate a socket, but a *buffered downlink write* also counts as liveness, because a successful write only means the peer (or a proxy in front of it) accepted the bytes. For August's web/Tauri bridge: the same asymmetry exists between "the desktop shell wrote to the socket" and "the browser received it".
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Access control decided from wire identities, before any object is materialised** — `packages/api/gateway/src/access.ts:40` — the resource resolution chain (resources reader → lookup provider → Context adapter → default field) runs on the *already-validated* arguments, so a denied call never resolves a lookup or opens a Session. For August: the permission check belongs before the work, and it should be expressible in terms the caller can see (ids), not internal objects.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **One policy-failure log line per policy, not per call** — `packages/api/remote-access/src/index.ts:127` — a policy that throws yields `policy-failed` and is logged once until the next `invalidate()`, because snapshots and list filters ask many times per change. For August: a broken policy backend can be asked hundreds of times per frame; the log must not become the denial mechanism.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **"Never a default" — the caller names the Peer** — `packages/api/gateway/src/types.ts:26` — `InvokeRemoteRequest.peer` is required; the Gateway never supplies a default Peer, and a dispatch from a disposed Peer fails with `gateway/peer-disposed`. For August: an implicit identity (a default user, a default session) is a place where a "who is asking" question gets answered wrongly with no trace.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Reasoning effort as a first-class, per-turn-pinned selection** — `packages/acp/acp/src/model-control.ts:75` — `pinTurn(turn, selection)` freezes the route for every step of one admitted prompt and `releaseTurn(turn)` clears only that exact turn's pin; the option's value is `JSON.stringify([provider, model])` so two providers offering the same model id stay distinguishable. For August: changing the model mid-turn is a real hazard; pinning the route per turn makes the choice auditable.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Strict canonical base64 checked by round-trip, not by regex** — `packages/acp/acp/src/content.ts:52` — `data.toString('base64') !== block.data` rejects URL-safe aliases, whitespace and padding variants that a regex alone accepts. For August: any "decode this attachment" path should be round-trip checked, because a lenient decoder is a silent corruption path.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **`__proto__` is a legal env var and a legal header name** — `packages/acp/acp/src/mcp.ts:84` — the env/header map is built with `Object.create(null)` and the comment names the reason: *"a null prototype keeps that entry as data instead of invoking Object.prototype's setter"*. For August: any map built from user- or model-supplied keys needs a null prototype, and the test that proves it (`mcp.spec.ts:80`) is the one worth copying.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A freeze-the-route-per-turn plus release-only-the-exact-turn pair** — `packages/acp/acp/src/model-control.ts:83` — release is guarded by `if (this.turnSelection?.turn === turn)`, so a late release of turn 3 cannot clear turn 4's pin. For August: any per-turn resource (a lock, a route, a budget) needs the same "release only what you own" guard, because out-of-order teardown is normal.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Drain the children before the parents** — `packages/acp/acp/src/session.ts:461` — the bridge calls `subagents.drainDescendants([this.agent])` *before* releasing its own sessions, because a continuable activation outlives the turn that started it. For August: an orchestrated run's teardown order is a correctness property, and the spec (`dispose.spec.ts:65`) pins it.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A cancelled turn is `cancelled`; an aborted one is `end_turn`** — `packages/acp/acp/src/codec.ts:20` — the comment states the rule: *"`cancelled` is reserved for explicit client cancellation and disposal, both settled out of band; a turn aborted by a hook or another owner is ordinary quiescence"*. For August: distinguishing "the user stopped it" from "it died" is what makes a retry decision possible.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Every list read is a projection, and the work slice yields only between complete rows** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/list.ts:147` — the deadline is checked between whole rows and reset after each yield, so a row is never torn; cancellation is checked per row and after each yield. For August: a sidebar or a file list that reads 500 sessions must be cancellable and must not hand back half a row.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A "blank" bit that means "no turn has run", not "the log is empty"** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/list.ts:47` — `const blank = state.blank && event.type !== 'turn/start'`, so standalone plugin events (a command record, a title change) do not clear it. For August: any "is this conversation empty?" flag will be wrong unless it names the *event* that makes it non-empty, and a plugin that logs must not be able to clear it by accident.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **"A predecessor cache may supply only its version-compatible title, as a stale display fact, never as an authoritative fold seed"** — `packages/api/session-controller/README.md:44` — a current-format cache identity may supply every list hint, but a lifecycle-mismatched predecessor may supply only a title. For August: a cache from an older schema is a *display* hint; letting it seed a fold is how stale data becomes structural.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Prompt rejects empty content before resolving the Agent** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts:60` — `hasPromptContent` accepts a non-text part or non-whitespace text, and the check runs *before* the Agent is resolved or a Session event is appended. For August: validation that happens after side effects is validation that can be bypassed by the failure path.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A prompt retry with the same `requestId` returns the original acceptance** — `packages/api/session-controller/README.md:34` — a request whose id is already queued or logged returns the original acceptance without inserting another message. For August: an idempotent submit is the cheapest possible defence against a double-click, a retry and a reconnect.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **The Archived-session gate blocks at `pre-step`, so the turn ends `blocked` rather than cancelled** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/archived-session-gate.ts:30` — an archived Session (or a subagent descendant of one) cannot run a model step; the lineage walk follows durable header fields only, so a **fork** of an archived Session is independent, and a looping lineage terminates on a visited set. For August: "this work must not run any more" is best expressed as a pre-flight gate, not a kill.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Higher-seq-wins for projections, and a cached value never outranks a connected Host** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/projection-store.ts:161` — sequenced rows merge under higher seq wins; a `cached` row from a persisted checkpoint has no comparable seq and always yields; a baseline discards every cached row before it seeds. For August: this is the whole "server truth vs local cache" conflict resolved in one store, with no domain code.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A baseline merge that keeps the client's established order** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/ordered-baseline.ts:11` — baseline-only identities are inserted relative to the nearest *following* known identity and absent identities are removed, so an authoritative baseline updates values without reordering what the user is looking at. For August: a list refresh that reorders under the user's cursor is a UX bug that no test of "the data is right" would catch.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **The client owns the *shape* of the wire, the server owns the *content*** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/session-wire-event.ts:17` — the validator rejects an unexpected key rather than stripping it, and event names and payloads stay merge-extensible; range membership and source existence remain Host-side durable-log checks. For August: a lenient client validator turns a schema drift into silent data loss.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Notifications are batched by *kind*: structure in a microtask, stream by animation frame** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/notifier.ts:12` — and the snapshot rebuild is skipped entirely when there are no listeners. For August: token streaming and structural updates have different latency requirements, and one notifier that treats them alike either flickers or lags.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A local echo inserted synchronously, before the caller serializes and prompts** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/session.ts:1` — `beginSubmission` inserts the echo *synchronously* so the conversation can show the message on the submit click's own frame; the echo's placement is derived from the running state and then retained until the display handoff; each retirement fires `onRetire` exactly once. For August: an optimistic UI needs a local echo that is inserted at the click, not after the network round trip, and needs a retirement rule that fires exactly once.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A 128 KiB render tail with a `gapBefore` flag instead of an unbounded buffer** — `packages/api/job-controller/src/client/model.ts:16` — a bounded tail plus one boolean that says "bytes before this were dropped" is enough for a live preview, and the flag covers eviction, resume gaps and the render bound alike. For August: a live output view needs a bound and an honest "there is a hole here" signal.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Non-consuming observation: the browser's read never moves the model's cursor** — `packages/api/job-controller/src/rows.ts:15` — both job streams are projections of the registry; the model's `job_output` cursor and notice state never observe them, so a human watching a job does not steal its output. For August: a human-facing view of the agent's work must not be a *read* of the agent's read cursor.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A human's kill is not the model's kill** — `packages/api/job-controller/src/index.ts:125` — the reason is `cancelled by the user`, and because the notice ledger withholds only the *model's own* `job_kill`, the owning agent's completion notice still arrives carrying the reason. For August: a user-initiated stop should still be *reported* to the agent, not silently swallow the completion.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **The lookup and the kill share one synchronous span** — `packages/api/job-controller/src/index.ts:113` — the comment states the reason: nothing can remove the job in between, and a producer-cancel throw propagates per the registry contract instead of masquerading as `job-not-found`. For August: any "check then act" pair on shared state needs one span, and the failure taxonomy must not collapse "not found" and "the thing threw".
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Subscribe before the first read, or a commit can be lost forever** — `packages/api/job-controller/src/rows.ts:35` — the comment says it: *"Subscribe before the first read so a commit between the read and the wait cannot be missed."* For August: every read-then-wait loop in the harness needs this, and it is a two-line fix that is easy to lose in a refactor.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **One forwarded-event allowlist that both faces derive from** — `packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts:26` — the `emit`/`waterfall` mode is simultaneously the Host dispatch strategy and the legal key set of `ctx.remote.$on`; the file is listed in *both* compiler faces on purpose so the two cannot drift. For August: the set of events a UI may receive should be declared once and typed in both directions.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A forwarded waterfall must carry its routed Agent directly** — `packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts:67` — `request.agent !== carrierAgent` throws a `TypeError` before forwarding, because the Agent identity is what lets the client pick the right scoped context. For August: an approval or a question routed to the wrong session is worse than one that is not delivered.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A non-JSON event argument is rejected at the Host boundary, not at the serialiser** — `packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts:163` — `assertJsonArgs` throws on a non-lossless-JSON argument before the frame is enqueued. For August: fail at the producer, not at the transport, or the stack trace points at the wrong layer.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A terminal failure turns a non-owner's access answers false and leaves the owner's true** — `packages/api/remote-access/src/client/mount.ts:125` — the two log messages differ ("owner access answers are unaffected" vs "reload the page to reconnect"). For August: a UI's "can I do this?" must fail *closed* for a restricted user and fail *open* for the owner — and the two cases deserve different messages.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A model catalog isolates one failing provider instead of failing the whole list** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/catalog.ts:30` — each provider is resolved inside its own `try`, and a failure becomes a `failure` entry while the other providers still load. For August: a model picker must not lose every provider because one gateway is down.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Availability of a *key* is checked independently of availability of a *model*** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/catalog.ts:93` — `hasProviderApiKey` walks the configured credential references, skips the account provider and returns whether *any* provider has a key; it never substitutes another model. For August: "am I logged in" and "is this model available" are two different questions with two different answers.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A cold-readable skill catalog that never activates an Agent** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/skill-catalog.ts:44` — the working directory comes from the *projection*, the preset scope is acquired without creating an Agent, and only the winning provider's instruction-file `path` is returned. For August: a command palette must be able to list capabilities without booting a session.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **`/api/file` served with a sandbox CSP, `nosniff` and `no-store`, Range ignored** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/media-references.ts:12` — the base headers exist because HTML and SVG served from the authenticated API origin could otherwise execute with that origin's privileges. For August: any route that serves user content to a browser needs the same three headers, and Range being *ignored* is a deliberate simplification the doc states.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Every endpoint states its activation policy** — `packages/api/session-controller/README.md:34` — list reads only headers and cache rows; search, attachment, history, skill discovery and workspace-path opening may inspect persistence without activating an Agent; cancellation *requires* live state. For August: "does this endpoint wake the agent?" should be a documented, per-endpoint property — it decides latency, cost and side effects.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A per-endpoint access declaration with a default field** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/index.ts:152` — the controller registers the `session` resource kind with the default field `sessionId` through `typert.resources`, and `session/page`/`session/follow` declare a `resources` reader that picks `request.address.sessionId` or `request.address.childSessionId`. For August: a permission model needs a *default* (the obvious id) plus a per-method override, or every method re-derives it.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A non-owner's prompt records the principal; an owner's source does not** — `packages/api/session-controller/README.md:36` — `principalOf(this.ctx.invocation)` is read and recorded only for a non-owner, so a source without a principal belongs to the owner. For August: provenance in the transcript should be a fact, not an inference, and "absent means owner" is a clean rule.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A local submission echo carries the admitted attachment references** — `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/contract/session.ts:19` — an observed retirement includes the ordered durable attachment references so the composer can release successful cards while preserving failed drafts. For August: an optimistic UI needs to know which of its optimistic attachments the server *actually* accepted.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **Turn-aligned history pages with two minima, and a separate budget for the jump loader** — `packages/api/session-controller/README.md:69` — the initial follow, reconnects and `loadOlder()` request at least 50 append-origin messages *and* cross at least two `turn/start` events; `loadThrough()` uses the same rules with a 200-message minimum per page and the 500-message cap does not limit the whole jump. For August: a page of history is only useful if it contains whole turns.
- **[dsh-api#1]** - **A public `Remote` accessor that never leaks credentials** — `packages/api/account-controller/src/index.ts:26` — every Platform-reaching operation takes the *calling UI's* `AccountClientMetadata` (version, language, UTC offset), so the Host reports the requesting UI rather than the last caller it saw. For August: per-UI metadata (locale, timezone) is what makes a server-rendered message correct.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **An owned activity interval, not a prompt/answer pair** — `packages/sdk/client/src/api.ts:207-254`. `run()` queues the prompt, waits for the *durable inbox receipt carrying its own message id*, then collects until the next whole-agent `idle`. `finalResponse` is explicitly "the last committed assistant text in that interval — not a response causally assigned to the prompt, because steering, injected context, and other queued work may contribute before idle" (`packages/sdk/client/README.md:52`). For the August harness this is the right shape for any "run the agent and tell me what it said" API: bind the interval to an observable lifecycle edge (receipt → idle), and say out loud that the answer may not be the answer to *this* prompt.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **Abandonment is not cancellation, and the pending entry is deleted on abandon** — `packages/sdk/protocol/src/transport.ts:129-137` and `packages/sdk/client/src/client.ts:359-366`. A timed-out request *aborts* the pending entry (so a hung method retains no per-call state) while the server-side work keeps running to completion. The test pins the observable: three consecutive timeouts leave `transport.pending.size === 0` (`packages/sdk/client/tests/sdk-client.spec.ts:469-483`). August's tool-call layer needs this distinction: a timeout must free the *client's* bookkeeping without pretending the server stopped.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **The handshake is the readiness boundary, and it waits for the whole plugin tree** — `packages/sdk/server/src/index.ts:83-85`. `initialize` awaits `ctx.get('loader')?.await()` so that async sibling capabilities (an MCP client's initial tool discovery) are visible to the *first* prompt; there is no scheduler delay in readiness. Transferable directly: an agent harness that advertises "ready" before its tools are discovered will accept a first prompt that cannot see them.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **The model route is resolved and validated at the handshake; there is no fallback to constructor defaults** — `packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts:155-189` and `packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts:170-188`. `initialize` runs `llm.resolveCallConfig({provider, model, reasoningEffort, maxTokens})` and `session/prompt` rejects with "SDK server is not initialized" until that succeeds. A missing adapter, an unavailable model or an unsupported reasoning effort therefore fails *at the handshake* rather than degrading silently on turn 1. August's equivalent (per-model reasoning effort / max tokens) should fail the same way.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **A failed handshake that cleaned up successfully installs a fresh client; a failed cleanup retains the failed client** — `packages/sdk/client/src/api.ts:80-92`. The instance retries with a *new* subprocess because `HarnessClient.close` is permanent, but if the cleanup also failed it throws an ordered `AggregateError` and **keeps** the failed client rather than spawning a second process beside one whose exit was never proved. This is the same "don't create a second owner before the first is provably gone" discipline August's own project notes call for in the update path.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **A late stream frame from a replaced attachment is ignored, and the model never resurrects a removed row** — `packages/api/terminal-controller/src/client/model.ts:345-360` and `packages/api/workspace-controller/src/client/model.ts:79-80, 384-398`. The terminal view compares the *stream generation* and drops frames from an old one; the Workspace model tombstones removed ids and compares `updatedAt` so a newer Host row always wins regardless of which transport delivered it. August's transcript/UI layers need exactly this when a run is cancelled and a stale result arrives later.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **A reconnection creates a fresh command sequence and never replays unacknowledged input** — `packages/api/terminal-controller/src/client/model.ts:192-204` (each `connect()` builds a new attachment with `sequence: 0` and drops the old one) and the matching test `packages/api/terminal-controller/tests/model.client.spec.ts:401-421`. The byte budget of the *old* generation is discarded with it, so a reconnect cannot "resume" a half-typed command.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **Refuse the page, never shorten it** — `packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts:71-77, 367-381`. "A page above this fails; it is not shortened, because a silently cut page reads as the whole page." The same rule appears in the byte-window path, where an over-cap window is `workspace-file/too-large` rather than a truncated array. August's file-read tool has exactly this hazard (a 20 MB ceiling and a 200 MB paged escape hatch) and the refusal semantics are the transferable part.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **Only positively confirmed idle time counts toward reclamation, and an unknown observation clears the deadline** — `packages/api/terminal-controller/src/retention.ts:113-130`. A `busy` or `unknown` activity state resets the idle clock, a gap longer than twice the poll interval resets the evidence, and the clock is monotonic (`performance.now()`). This is the right shape for any "reclaim idle resources" policy in August: never reclaim on the *absence* of evidence.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **A slow consumer fails explicitly and recovers from the screen** — `packages/api/terminal-controller/src/stream.ts:24-34`. The bounded output queue refuses to drop frames: it fails the attachment with "reconnect to recover the current screen". August's streaming paths (SSE, event buses) should prefer an explicit failure over silent frame loss, and should keep a re-derivable state (the screen, the baseline) so a reconnect is cheap.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **The Host decides the file's identity; the Client needs no local state to authorize it** — `packages/api/workspace-files/src/client/provider.ts:52-110` and `packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts:202-222`. The address carries the Session id; the Host resolves the path, checks access, and returns `stat.absolutePath`; the Client binds its change-feed key to *that* path. The result is that the browser never needs a Session summary, a cwd mirror, or a copy of the access rules — and the `workspaceFileScope` Typert lookup resolves a cold session from persistence *without activating an Agent*.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **Field-by-field projection of any provider answer before it crosses the wire** — `packages/api/settings-controller/src/credentials.ts:45-51` and `packages/api/settings-controller/src/index.ts:48-60`. The reason is stated precisely: "the Gateway returns a business result without decoding it, so a provider whose descriptor carried extra enumerable properties would otherwise serialize them to the caller." The test uses a deliberately leaky provider to prove it (`packages/api/settings-controller/tests/credentials-controller.host.spec.ts:9-15, 101-106`). This is the cheapest possible defence against a secret riding along in an extra field, and it generalizes to every provider seam in August.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **A stale write is its own outcome, not a malformed request** — `packages/api/settings-controller/src/index.ts:257-268`. `SETTINGS_CONFLICT` becomes `settings/conflict {ns, expected, actual}` so the caller knows to re-read and re-apply, while every other provider refusal becomes `settings/rejected`. The same shape appears in the Workspace archive path, where the refusal carries the *activity list* so the surface can say what must stop first.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **Serialized mutation tail instead of a lock** — `packages/api/workspace-controller/src/commands.ts:235-239`. A promise tail makes a rename that lands after a delete fail as `workspace/not-found` rather than resurrecting the row, and it makes a rename's title-ownership check see the same registry state as the reorder that follows it. Cheap to add, and it removes a whole class of "two doors raced" bugs.
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **Subagent locality is decided by one snapshotted flag, never by names or lineage** — `packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts:129-147`. "The service snapshots the provider name and local flag through child disposal; matching ids or parent lineage alone never establishes locality." The test suite then walks the collision cases (a remote run id equal to a local child's id; a reused id across two parents; a provider re-registered under the same name). August's subagent layer needs the same single source of truth for "is this child mine".
- **[dsh-api#2]** - **A failure is bound to its session until a later committed terminal accounts for it** — `packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts:103-116`. The server records `agent/error` with the session's log offset and clears it only when a `turn/end` at or after that offset is committed, so `session/wait` can reject with a failure that happened *before* the wait while a later successful turn clears it. This is the missing half of "a wait must not hang and must not lie" — the same shape August needs for a turn that fails after the caller stopped watching. ---
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Draw a hard argument boundary instead of a flag list, and let the child own everything after it** — `apps/cli/src/args.ts:159-167` — Commander is configured with `.allowUnknownOption().passThroughOptions().enablePositionalOptions()` and a `[args...]` positional, so the *first token the launcher does not own* becomes the app's argument list. For August this is the cleanest way to let a host (`dsh`, a desktop shell, an SDK) own its own flags while sharing one boot: the host owns a fixed prefix, the runtime owns the rest, and no shared flag registry is needed. The companion rule is at `apps/cli/src/args.ts:122-127`: **a read-only/inspection mode must refuse the arguments it cannot honour**, because "printing a tree that differs from the same invocation's boot would mislead."
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Regenerate the base file from a constant on every boot so a partial write-back can never accumulate** — `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:180-200` — the empty root config is a literal string that is *always* rewritten, because the Loader writes back the composed tree when a plugin self-disposes, and a written-back root would duplicate every bundle insert on the next boot. August's August-side equivalents (a persisted prompt prefix, a saved tool list, a cached system prompt) have exactly this failure mode: any file the runtime may write back must be re-derived from a constant, never read back.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Freeze the launch environment once and serve it as a service** — `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:272-279` and `:326-328` — the proxy is resolved from a *snapshot*, not `process.env`, because "Node's fetch ignores the proxy environment on its own" and "Node samples the environment at start"; and the snapshot is provided to the tree **before any config-tree entry mounts**, so every plugin reads the same immutable values. August's gateway already has a layered-env concept; making it a *snapshot* that plugins receive as a service (rather than ambient `process.env`) is the transferable half.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A staging directory with a recoverable `previous` copy, and a concurrent-winner detection that does not trust the error code** — `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:132-176` — the new profile is assembled in a *sibling* staging directory so both renames stay on one filesystem; the old target is moved to `<staging>/previous` before the new one is moved in; a failed restore throws an `AggregateError` **naming the path where the old profile can be recovered by hand**; and because "Windows reports EPERM instead of EEXIST or ENOTEMPTY", a concurrent winner is detected by the *target's state*. This is the pattern August needs for any destructive state transition (profile reset, memory import, session replacement).
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Escalating shutdown: drain on the first signal, force on the second, and never let a repeated graceful call escalate** — `apps/cli/src/process-shutdown.ts:52-75` and `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:302-308` — `shutdown()` coalesces (the second call returns the same promise); only a *signal* escalates; SIGTERM exits 0 and SIGINT exits 130 because "the launcher does not know whether the app considered its work complete". August's desktop host and its unattended paths need exactly this vocabulary, and the "repeated graceful call must not escalate" rule is the part people get wrong.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A readiness signal committed only on four independent conditions, not on "boot returned"** — `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:341-345` — readiness is committed only if the shutdown was not already aborted, the fiber is `ACTIVE`, a `loader` service exists, and boot resolved. A progress indicator driven by "the process started" lies; one driven by these four conditions does not.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Save the diagnostic privately, print the summary, and never print a path you did not write** — `apps/cli/src/startup-diagnostics.ts:34-68` — a unique `startup-<ts>-<uuid>.log` under `$DSH_HOME/logs`, created with `flag: 'wx'` so a concurrent failure cannot overwrite an earlier report, modes `0700`/`0600`, a header that warns the report may contain credential values, and — if the write fails — the **whole** report goes to stderr instead of a claim that a file exists. The `inspect` settings (`showHidden: true`, `getters: false`, `customInspect: false`) preserve nested causes, aggregate members, cycles and symbols without ever evaluating an accessor.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Turn "the tool call was recorded but no result was" into an explicit, actionable error** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/expected/semantic-checkpoint/session.expected.jsonl:8` — the synthesised `tool/result` is `ToolOutcomeUnknownError` / `TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and says: "Its outcome is unknown. Decide whether to retry from the tool semantics: retry only if the operation is read-only or idempotent; if it may have side effects, first verify external state or ask the user. Do not retry blindly." August's crash-recovery path needs this: an ambiguous side effect must become a *named, actionable* tool result, not a hang, a silent retry, or a generic error.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Keep the prompt prefix byte-identical across a tool-registry change, and derive the transcript's tool history from what the provider saw** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/sdk/dynamic-tool-cache.e2e.ts:142-163` — after a runtime tool addition the system prompt is unchanged, the message prefix is byte-identical, the **tool list prefix** is byte-identical with the new tool appended last (`defer_loading: true`), and the provider's `cacheReadTokens` still covers the preceding conversation. The new tool is registered *scoped* so the registry diff is unambiguous, and the transcript's registry history is computed as the **diff of consecutive request headers** — "a model-chosen extra add/remove cycle changes both sides or neither" — not from call counts. This is the concrete recipe for August's prompt-cache hit rate: append, never reorder; and derive the "tools changed" message from the wire, not from the model.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A retry must not change the model-visible messages** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/fixtures/retry-snapshot-backend.mjs:30-32` — the fixture throws "retry snapshot changed the model-visible messages" if the second attempt's messages differ from the first. Combined with the `llm/retry` event, which records the *policy key* that produced the decision (`apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/headless.expected.e2e.ts:517-525`), this gives August both a cache invariant and an auditable retry ledger.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Verify the world, not the model's self-report — and check the test file is byte-identical** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/coding-task.e2e.ts:69-84` — "an agent that neutered the test instead of fixing the bug fails here, not just on a keyword probe". The same rule appears in the todo test (assert the `todo/write` event's contents), the ACP tests (assert the file on disk), the escalation test (assert the write landed) and the credential tests (assert the key the *server* received). August's evals should assert the same way: re-run the check yourself, outside the agent.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **An inspection path must be provably non-mutating** — `apps/cli/tests/dump-config-schema.expected.e2e.ts:25-32` and `:108` — every fixture plugin carries an `apply()` that writes `apply-ran` and throws, and the test asserts the file does **not** exist after the dump; `!!js` expressions that would throw are dumped without evaluating them. The same discipline belongs on any August-side "explain/diagnose" endpoint: it must be able to prove it changed nothing.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Absence of a capability is not a prohibition** — `apps/cli/tests/expected/dump-config-schema.json:108-110` and `apps/cli/reference/README.md:64` — `unknownConfig` is an *empty* schema whose `$comment` says "this is unknown configuration, not a prohibition on fields", and `complete: false` "does not guarantee successful boot". August's config introspection should make the same distinction explicit rather than treating "I don't know" as "invalid".
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Compose the agent's capabilities from a per-session scope, and keep the host plane minimal** — `apps/cli/tests/web-agent-presets.e2e.ts:248-251` and `:288-311` — the global layer exposes **only** `working_directory`; every action tool belongs to a preset; the preset's catalog is asserted **exactly**, because "an omission is this design's quietest failure mode, since a row that registers into the wrong layer mounts cleanly and simply contributes nothing". A delegated child inherits the parent's *live scope*, not the parent's creation header (`apps/cli/tests/web-agent-presets.e2e.ts:959-982`) — "The live scope chain is the authority, not the parent's creation header".
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A child's permissions must be armed before the child's first turn** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/expected/subagent-inheritance/child.expected.jsonl:3-6` — the child's log shows `sandbox/mode: { mode: 'read-only', source: 'delegation' }` and `approval/policy: { policy: 'never', source: 'delegation' }` **before** `turn/start`, and the write never reached disk. The injected runtime context also says "Do not refuse a required modification from this policy alone" — a denial must be scoped, not a blanket refusal. This is the ordering August's subagent path must guarantee: constraints are installed *before* the child can act.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A child that settles must notify its parent; the parent must not have to poll** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/headless.expected.e2e.ts:1137-1210` and `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/fixtures/subagent-settlement-fence.ts:16-19` — the settlement notice arrives as an `agent/inbox/spliced` with `source.kind: 'subagent-settled'`; the fixture holds the parent's second step until the notice is admitted, which pins *content order* rather than step placement. Push, not poll.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **The parent's catalog alone is enough to discover a cold child** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/subagent-diagnostic.expected.e2e.ts:134-137` — "Direct discovery must not read that child log"; the parent shows the child as inactive-but-known and never as corrupt. A registry entry, not a re-read of the child's log, is the discovery mechanism.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A failed hot-reload must keep the previous configuration live** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/web-failure-matrix.expected.e2e.ts:329-346` — a schema failure in a new patch generation does not apply the new row, does not dispose the old one, and does not interrupt the serving siblings; a later valid correction applies it and only then disposes the previous generation. The same matrix shows that a malformed *overlay* is rejected before readiness with a specific diagnostic per malformation ("failed to read overlay", "failed to parse overlay", "top-level YAML array", "must be a mapping").
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Separate required failures from optional failures, and say which is which** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/web-failure-matrix.expected.e2e.ts:233-258` — a required entry that fails to import aborts the process with the failed plugin's package, the pending plugins and the missing services; an optional one produces `warning: 1 entry did not activate` and the app keeps serving. "Optional" must be a *declared* property of a row, not an inference from the failure.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Prove an isolation check can fail — a negative control** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/web-default-isolation.expected.e2e.ts:48-54` — the test mounts a real experimental package at runtime and asserts the detector now reports it. A scanner that passes on zero matches is not a scanner; August's August-side gates should carry the same negative control (and the August workspace's own `check:sse` handler-supply rule is the same idea).
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A permission grant is bound to one call, and the request carries the call** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/acp/tests/escalation.e2e.ts:165-170` — the `session/request_permission` request must carry `prompt.toolCall.toolCallId` and offer exactly `['allow-once','reject-once']`; a scripted client that cannot find the requested option *cancels* rather than grants. For August: a permission prompt must name the operation it is approving, and a grant must expire with that operation — never become a standing permission for the session.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A denial must be a scoped, structured tool result that carries the escalation path** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/expected/subagent-inheritance/child.expected.jsonl:17` — the refused `write` comes back as a tool result with `isError: true` and a structured `error: { name: 'FsError', code: 'FS_SANDBOX_DENIED' }`, and the text offers the next step ("retry this exact operation once with sandbox_permissions (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) + justification"). The injected runtime context separately says "Do not refuse a required modification from this policy alone". August's policy engine should emit a *machine-readable* refusal plus a *human-actionable* remedy, and the model must be told not to treat a scoped denial as a reason to abandon the task.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **The failure summary must be a summary — assert the absence of the detail, not just its presence** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/web-best-effort-startup.expected.e2e.ts:301-303` — the stderr summary must contain exactly one `EADDRINUSE` and must **not** contain the stack, the `[cause]` chain, `at boot (`, `at runCli (` or the Node version banner; the full report lives in a separate file. August's startup failure path should split the one-line summary from the diagnostics dump and pin that split with negative assertions.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A required row's lifecycle is re-entrant, not one-shot** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/web-failure-matrix.expected.e2e.ts:466-486` — disabling a shipped *required* row disposes it; re-adding it while one of its dependencies is missing leaves the row **PENDING** (not failed), and providing the dependency later brings it to **ACTIVE** without a restart. For August: a disabled-and-re-enabled capability must be able to come back to life, and "waiting for a dependency" must be a distinct state from "failed".
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Compare the graph the client received with the graph the process built** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/web-default-isolation.expected.e2e.ts:20-24` — the test extracts `globalThis["__DSH_BOOT__"]` from the served HTML, parses it, and asserts it **equals** the process's own `ctx.clientModules.graph()`. The isolation claim is therefore "the browser and the process agree", not "the browser's list matches a hand-written expectation" — which is the form that rots the moment a feature is added.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A mock model should refuse to run under a composition it was not designed for** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/fixtures/team-llm.mjs:182-191` — the fixture throws "Team profile exposes a direct subagent tool" and "Team profile is missing teammate or workflow tools" instead of producing a plausible answer. For August's evals: a scripted model is also a *composition assertion*, and it should fail loudly when the tool surface it expects is not the one it was given.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A scripted-model layer needs a "hang" primitive, or cancellation is only testable with a real model** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/acp/tests/goal-expected/goal-round-driver/replay.override.json:42` — the replay override's last entry is `{"kind": "hang", "readyFile": ".dsh-snapshot-goal-cancel-ready"}`, which parks the turn until the driver writes the file and then cancels it. August's replay/record layer should be able to park a turn deterministically, so abort, cancel and escalation flows are testable without a provider.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **A mutating call that a user can race should carry an `expected` precondition, and the refusal codes must be distinguishable** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/schedule-timing.expected.e2e.ts:80-83` — `schedule/update` carries the record it expects; a stale precondition returns `code: 'schedule_conflict'` and a foreign owner returns `code: 'schedule_not_found'`, and the file on disk is proven byte-identical after both refusals. "Conflict" and "not found" are different problems and must not share a code.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Assert the world in three places: the action, the artefact, and the narration** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/full-loop.e2e.ts:37-47` — the test asserts that a `tool/call` for `bash` happened, that a `tool/result` contains `e2e-ok`, *and* that the final text contains it. A model can fake any one of the three; August's evals should check all three, in the cheapest one that can fail.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **The injected runtime context should be structured, not prose** — `apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/expected/headless-profile/session.expected.jsonl:11` — the runtime-context user message carries `source.kind: 'runtime-context'`, `form: 'snapshot'` and a `sections` array naming `working-directory:current`, `sandbox:policy` and `approval:policy`, so a consumer can read the policy without parsing English. August's equivalent (the workspace, the file policy, the approval policy) should be section-addressable too, so a UI can re-render one part of it.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **One test body, two execution lanes** — `apps/cli/tests/source-launch.compat.spec.ts:18` and `apps/cli/tests/built-bin.e2e.ts:345` — the same `testProfileResolution(mode)` helper is called with `'src'` and with `'lib'`, and the lane-specific differences are pinned explicitly (the source lane's `execArgv` is `['--import','tsx/esm']`; the built lane's is empty; only `src/index.ts` **or** only `lib/index.js` may be loaded, never both). One assertion set, two execution modes, and a "no duplicate module identity" check that the `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` symbol makes concrete (`apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/profile-resolution.ts:217`).
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Bilingual parity as a hash record per heading, not a translation memory** — `apps/cli/README.i18n.yaml` and `apps/cli/reference/README.i18n.yaml` — one `en`/`zh` hash pair per heading section, regenerated by `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <file>`. Drift is then reported per section instead of per file, and the "record" is data an agent can read and update. August's bilingual docs could adopt the same shape verbatim.
- **[dsh-apps-cli]** - **Ship a generated composition graph next to the launcher** — `apps/cli/composition.md:1-4` — a mermaid graph from the config node to every plugin row plus a `Plugin id | Package / module` table, produced by `scripts/gen-doc-graphs.ts` and marked "do not edit by hand". For August, an auto-generated map from "feature name" to "owning module" is the same artefact: it turns a 90-row configuration into something a human (or an agent) can navigate. ---
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A streaming credential redactor that survives chunk boundaries** — `apps/desktop/scripts/packaging-run.mjs:38` — the redactor holds back a buffer while it is still a *prefix* of a known secret and only emits a character once no secret can start with it, so a PIN split across two stdout chunks is still removed. Transferable to any harness that streams subprocess or tool output: a naive `output.replace(secret, '[REDACTED]')` per chunk leaks the tail of every split secret.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A durable interlock that a failure never unlocks** — `apps/desktop/scripts/windows-signing-state.mjs:43` — the attempt file is created with `wx` before the scarce resource is used and is removed *only* by `success()`; the `failure` callback leaves it in place even if recording the failure itself fails. Transferable to any operation that consumes a one-shot capability (a hardware token, a paid API key, a signing certificate): the next run must refuse and demand a human-reviewed recovery, rather than retrying and burning another attempt.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **Derive sequence numbers from observed state, and refuse to number against a partial answer** — `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-build-version-discovery.ts:133` — the build index comes from listing what was actually published, and a listing that cannot complete inside its deadline yields *nothing* rather than a partial list, because "Numbering against a partial listing could reuse a published index." Transferable to any harness that issues ordered identifiers (session ids, task numbers, memory keys): read the real prior state, and treat an incomplete read as "I do not know" rather than "there is nothing".
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **Reconcile remote state before mutating it, and distinguish the three refusals** — `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-publish.ts:98` — a newer version already owning the channel is `superseded`, the same version with different bytes is `conflict`, and a channel that changed between preflight and write is `remote-changed`. Each has a different remedy, and none of them is "retry". Transferable directly to any tool that writes shared state (a memory file, a session transcript, a scheduled job): read the current bytes first, and classify *why* they differ.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A distinct "published, tag pending" terminal state instead of a boolean** — `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-publish.ts:36` and `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-publish-record.ts` — the outcome is `complete | published-tag-pending | failed`, and the durable journal records a `feeds-complete` event, so a retry after a tagging failure is *tag-only* and can never re-publish old YAML over a channel that has since advanced. Transferable to any multi-step operation whose later steps are cheap and whose earlier steps are expensive and observable: model the partial-success states explicitly and make the retry resume at the right step.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **Bind the human approval to the exact bytes and destination** — `apps/desktop/scripts/publish-desktop-ci.ts:53` — the approval is a SHA-256 over `{manifest, plan}`, recomputed after approval; changed bytes or a changed destination reject rather than proceed. Transferable to any approval-gated harness action: the approval must cover the *content*, not the intent.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A tool that reports what it observed and what a human must still check, and never declares success** — `apps/desktop/scripts/installed-update-qualification.ts:241` — the evidence object has `recordedFlow: complete | incomplete`, a `missing` list of unobserved milestones, and a fixed `operatorVerificationRequired` list (installer completion, data retention, screenshots, network recovery). Transferable to any qualification harness: the machine reports the evidence it has; the acceptance decision stays with a human; and "the log says the flow completed" is never confused with "the flow worked".
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A content-addressed cache whose key includes the whole policy, and whose hits are re-verified** — `apps/desktop/scripts/macos-signature-cache.ts:53` and `apps/desktop/scripts/windows-signature-cache.mjs:148` — the key is the hash of the input bytes plus the mode plus the certificate, identifier, entitlements, tools and OS; a hit is re-verified for trust before use, and a corrupt entry rejects rather than being repaired. Transferable to any cache of an expensive or scarce operation (a model response, a compiled artifact, a signed blob): key on the *policy*, not just the input, and treat a hit as untrusted until re-verified.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **Content-addressed caching that never parallelizes the expensive part** — `apps/desktop/scripts/windows-signature-cache.mjs:217` and `apps/desktop/scripts/windows-runtime-signature.mjs:141` — `restore` (free, hardware-free) is a separate operation that the caller may run concurrently, while `sign` (the hardware token) stays a serial promise chain; the concurrent restores are drained and any failure is thrown before the serial leg starts. Transferable to any harness with an expensive bottleneck: split the operation into a parallelizable "reuse" leg and a serial "acquire" leg, and drain the parallel leg before the serial one.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **No ambient fallback for configuration, and a loader that will not echo a credential-bearing parse error** — `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-package-environment.mjs:20` and `:109` — every release-shaped environment variable is stripped from the inherited environment, a dotenv key outside the allowlist is an error, and a parse failure is reported without the parser's message because "Parser diagnostics can contain credential-bearing input". Transferable to any harness config surface: the effective config must be the file's, not the file's-plus-the-shell's, and a config error message must never contain the config.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A build gate that fails the *bundle* rather than the installed application** — `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-bundle-imports.mjs:83` — a rolldown plugin inspects every module's static, dynamic and `require()` imports and fails the build naming the offending specifier, because the alternative is an installed application that dies at launch with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Transferable to any harness that ships a bundle: a check that can only be run against the *installed* artifact should be moved to build time.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **Stage, back up, promote by rename, and roll back — retrying only the sharing violations** — `apps/desktop/scripts/installer-directories.nsh:51` and `apps/desktop/installer/uninstall-data.h:99` — the retry predicate is exactly Windows errors 5/32/33, ten attempts with increasing delay, and every other error stops immediately; a failed restoration preserves the backup and stops the recovery instead of retrying. Transferable to any harness that replaces a directory or a file in place: name the transient failure class explicitly and never retry the rest.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **Deleting data without ever following a link, and without touching the protected root** — `apps/desktop/installer/uninstall-data.h:64` — each ancestor is *pinned* with a handle that does not share delete access, reparse points are opened with `OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` and refused as roots, and the protected Harness home and the installation are refused as targets. Transferable to any harness that cleans up scratch space: a cleanup routine that can follow a symlink out of the tree is a data-exfiltration primitive.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A bounded excerpt in the UI, the complete report on disk and in the clipboard** — `apps/desktop/installer/extract-report.h:134` — the dialog shows at most 10 lines and 1000 characters and says how many more lines are in the saved file; the file keeps everything, capped at 16 MiB, with the truncation recorded. Transferable to any harness error surface: the user-facing message must be bounded *and* must say where the rest is.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A UI that cannot be tricked into accepting an action** — `apps/desktop/renderer/mandatory-update-frame.js:25` — the bridge requires a trusted event, the parent as source, the `dsh-app://app` origin, exactly one port, and no prior port; and the renderer derives the button's *action* from the phase rather than storing it, so a stale click cannot install what the current state forbids. Transferable to any harness UI that a model or a page might influence.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **Escape is cancellation, never acceptance, and out-of-order updates are dropped by revision** — `apps/desktop/renderer/update-dialog.js:27` — the dialog compares `state.revision` against the rendered revision and ignores an older one, and a single-flight `responding` flag prevents a double answer. Transferable to any streaming UI fed by a server or an agent: version the state, and make the destructive key mean cancel.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A toolchain preflight that exercises behaviour, not just presence** — `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-toolchain-preflight.ts:26` — the `tar` probe creates an archive and lists it *beside* the archive with a relative name, because GNU tar reads the colon in an absolute Windows path as a remote-host separator; the probe would have passed a mere `tar --version`. Transferable to any harness that shells out: probe the specific behaviour the run depends on, at the specific invocation the run will use.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A stage deadline that fails the run even when the child exits zero** — `apps/desktop/scripts/packaging-run.mjs:128` — the timeout is recorded separately from the exit status, and a timeout kills the process *tree* (taskkill /T on Windows, a process-group kill on POSIX). Transferable to any harness tool call with a deadline: "the child exited 0" is not the same as "the work finished in time", and a timeout must stop the whole subtree, not just the direct child.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#1]** - **A machine that publishes only what it built, and cannot publish another's package** — `apps/desktop/scripts/desktop-publish-route.ts:58` and `apps/desktop/scripts/publish-desktop-ci.ts:31` — the route is validated against GitHub's run, job and manifest evidence ("request does not match the successful packaging attempt"), the task must be dispatched to the *same* machine that built it ("task was dispatched to a different machine"), and each configured machine needs a unique label. Transferable to a multi-worker harness: a worker should be able to prove it owns the artifact it is about to act on.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Validate every message that crosses a process boundary before you act on it, and kill the peer if it is malformed** — `apps/desktop/src/host-process.ts:53-91` (`isDesktopHostEvent`). The Host's `platform-session` event is re-validated down to the request-header allowlist, the lowercase-only rule and the CR/LF ban, and the origin must be HTTPS or HTTP on loopback. *Why it matters for the August harness*: the same discipline applies to a tool result, a stream frame or a subagent message — a malformed frame is a protocol violation, not data, and the cheapest correct response is to refuse it rather than to coerce it.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **A diagnostic must be written to disk BEFORE the dialog that names it, and the write must be time-bounded** — `apps/desktop/src/fatal-recovery.ts:106-119` (`persist`) with `CRASH_REPORT_WAIT_MS = 1000`, and `apps/desktop/src/crash-report.ts:147-157` (write with `flag: 'wx'`, mode `0600`, failure yields `undefined` and the dialog proceeds). *Why it matters*: an August turn that fails fatally should leave a complete artifact (stack, cause chain, enumerable properties, recent renderer output) that the user can send, and a slow disk must not become an additional failure.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Bound the diagnostic tail from the FRONT, not the back, and keep one oversized entry whole** — `apps/desktop/src/crash-report.ts:60-86` (`RendererConsoleTail`) and `apps/desktop/src/fatal-recovery.ts:34-41` (the 1200-character budget, the last 8 lines, the lone-surrogate strip). *Why it matters*: when an August turn's error is rendered into a toast, a status line or a tool receipt, the most recent frames and the *last* log lines are the useful ones; truncating from the end silently drops the cause.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Bind a user decision to a fingerprint of the observed state, and refuse the action if the state moved** — `apps/desktop/src/command-installation.ts:116-128` (`readSnapshot` → fingerprint over the `lstat` fields and the receipt) and `:189` (`if (state.fingerprint !== expected) throw new CommandInstallationError('ESTALE', ...)`).
