The fingerprint uses `dev, ino, mode, uid, gid, size, mtimeNs` plus the symlink target, so a replaced file is detected even with identical content. *Why it matters*: this is exactly the shape an August approval needs — "the tool call you approved was for this exact file state" — and the same pattern generalises to a diff, a plan and a config edit.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Preserve, never destroy, on a failed mutation: rename the old entry aside and re-verify it afterwards** — `apps/desktop/src/command-installation.ts:165-177` (`withdraw`) and `:203-218` (the rollback that restores the previous entry, aggregating failures and naming the preserved path). *Why it matters*: when an August tool call fails halfway, the user's file must be exactly as it was, and the error message must say where the old version is — not "operation failed".
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Do not let a later, unrelated failure replace the first fatal one** — `apps/desktop/src/fatal-recovery.ts:65-67` (`if (this.reported) return`; "later reports cannot replace it or open another dialog") plus `apps/desktop/src/backend-controller.ts:138-142` (the attempt-generation guard `if (this.attempt !== attempt || attempt.cancelled) return`). *Why it matters*: in a long August turn, a cascade of secondary errors must not bury the root cause; the first failure owns the report and the recovery.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Give every long-running operation a deadline, and treat a timeout as an UNKNOWN state that fails conservatively, not as success** — `apps/desktop/src/host-process.ts:49` (`QUIT_INSPECTION_DEADLINE_MS = 2000`) with `apps/desktop/src/quit-confirmation.ts:15-21` (`'unknown'` → the "tasks are running" warning, not a silent quit); and `apps/desktop/src/update-http-executor.ts:18-52` (an *inactivity* deadline that is refreshed on every chunk, so a large but progressing download is never killed). *Why it matters*: the same rule applies to a provider call, a subprocess and a subagent: a hung call must surface as "unknown, assume the worst", and a long-but-alive call must not be killed by a total-duration timeout.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Escalate a child's shutdown: request → wait → SIGTERM → wait → SIGKILL, and treat "not acknowledged" as a different failure from "did not exit"** — `apps/desktop/src/host-process.ts:288-308` (`stop(requireGraceful)`) with the separate `DesktopHostUncleanExitError` ("confirmed exit but refuses installation"). *Why it matters*: an August turn that spawns a subprocess or a subagent needs the same three-stage teardown, and needs to distinguish "it exited but did not finish cleanly" (refuse to continue) from "it is still running" (a different error entirely).
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Keep the "affordance" and the "authorization" apart: the UI may offer a button, but the main process owns the target and re-validates it at the moment of use** — `apps/desktop/src/mandatory-update-policy.ts:101-107` (`desktopPolicyPage` re-validates the server-supplied page against the deployment allowlist immediately before the browser or clipboard uses it) and `apps/desktop/src/mandatory-update-window.ts:82-86` (a stale confirmation revision is refused). *Why it matters*: in August, a model-produced URL or a renderer-supplied path must be re-validated at the point of use, not only when it was rendered.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Strip the ambient environment before spawning a privileged helper** — `apps/desktop/src/command-management.ts:148-149` (drop `KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|^NODE_OPTIONS$|^NODE_PATH$` from the child env) and `apps/desktop/src/command-manager-entry.ts:11-12` (`process.umask(0o022)` on macOS because the worker writes *public* metadata, not secrets). *Why it matters*: an August tool that spawns a subprocess inherits the whole parent environment, which may carry provider keys; scrubbing the child env at the spawn door is cheap and total.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Make the failure classification a closed vocabulary, and derive the user-facing wording from the classification rather than from the raw error** — `apps/desktop/src/update-presentation.ts:12-38` (`desktopUpdateFailureKind` → nine `DesktopUpdateFailureKind`s → localized summaries) with `apps/desktop/src/update-journal.ts:20-30` (the same idea for evidence: eight known error codes, else `UNCLASSIFIED`, and no raw message on disk). *Why it matters*: an August turn-end record should classify the failure into a small taxonomy (timeout, rate limit, auth, …) so the transcript, the metrics and the receipt cannot disagree.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Model "the user is doing something else right now" as first-class state** — `apps/desktop/src/host-process.ts:59-64` (a `platform-session` may carry a `null` session: "a null session is allowed") and `apps/desktop/src/account-backend.ts:120` (an `account/watchExpiry` frame carries the literal `'session-expired'`, which the shell turns into a welcome-window notice). *Why it matters*: an August session that is interrupted, cancelled or handed to another window needs the same distinction between "the model has no credentials" and "the credentials expired mid-turn".
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **A background service that must not interrupt the user needs a *visible* state, not a silent one** — `apps/desktop/src/background-notice.ts:30-36` (one acknowledgement, persisted under `userData`, cancelled prompts stay eligible) with `apps/desktop/src/update-attention.ts:23-57` (one reminder per downloaded version, cleared on focus, never authorizing anything). *Why it matters*: an August background job (a scheduled task, a long tool run) should tell the user exactly once that it is still running and offer a way back, and the reminder must never be a shortcut for the real action.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Expose a *narrow, semantic* status to the renderer and keep the raw diagnostics on the main side** — `apps/desktop/src/ipc.ts:39-69` (`DesktopUpdateState` vs. `DesktopUpdatePresentation`: "Product documents cannot supply update versions, package URLs, or installation authorization") and `apps/desktop/src/update-presentation.ts:44-51` (`presentDesktopUpdate` returns phase, version, percent and a failure kind — no diagnostics, no controls). *Why it matters*: the same split — a semantic status for the UI, the full diagnostic for the report — is what an August turn-end frame should look like, and it is what keeps a renderer from being able to *ask* for something it should only *report*.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Rewrite a stale boundary explicitly: an overlay's `revision` counter makes consumers reset their own state instead of guessing** — `apps/desktop/src/update-overlay.ts:8-16` (`input(parent)` returns `{revision, blocked}`) consumed at `apps/desktop/src/keyboard.ts:128-131` (`if (overlay.revision !== overlayRevision) { resetInput(); overlayRevision = overlay.revision }`). *Why it matters*: an August turn that is superseded (a new user message, a policy change, a compaction) needs the same explicit epoch so the old turn's partial state is discarded rather than merged.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Do the work in a child process so the privileged step has a fixed, non-negotiable target** — `apps/desktop/src/command-manager-entry.ts:17-22` (the destination is a constant in the worker, so the elevation prompt in the parent cannot be steered) and `apps/desktop/src/command-manager-entry.ts:23-35` (the Windows path pipes JSON to a bundled PowerShell script through stdin instead of touching the filesystem from Node). *Why it matters*: an August tool that needs elevation (installing a skill, touching a protected path) should take its target from a constant, not from a model-authored argument.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Deny a whole class of navigation, not just the dangerous URL** — `apps/desktop/src/browser-guests.ts:141-169` (the guest session cancels any network request with embedded credentials, cancels any request to the app's own Host, denies all permission requests, display media and downloads, and refuses navigation to the Host by port+loopback alias). *Why it matters*: a model that can open a browser must not be able to reach the harness's own API, its own credentials, or a `user:pass@host` URL — a class-level deny is easier to audit than a per-URL allowlist.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Make the copy a type-level contract, and keep an unknown placeholder visible instead of rendering "undefined"** — `apps/desktop/src/locale.ts:172` (`DesktopMessages` is a mapped type over every English key), `:340` (`zh ... satisfies DesktopMessages`) and `:376` (`values[key] ?? placeholder` leaves an unknown `{name}` in the text). *Why it matters*: an August UI surface (a status line, a receipt, a tool summary) should have the same guarantee — a missing translation or a missing value is a compile error or a visible marker, never a silent `undefined`.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Present progress as a state machine the user can interrupt, with a named reason for every stop** — `apps/desktop/src/ipc.ts:39-49` (phases `idle|checking|available|downloading|verifying|installing|ready|error`, with `failedOperation` naming *which* step failed and `preparationFailure` naming the preparation cause) and `apps/desktop/src/update-journal.ts:8-10` (a closed vocabulary of milestones, flushed per record). *Why it matters*: the August turn should publish the same shape — a phase, a percentage, a named failed operation — so a stuck turn says which phase it is stuck in.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#2]** - **Make a stale cached credential set impossible by stamping the cache on every file that can hold one** — `apps/desktop/src/platform-view.ts:101-102` (a per-account persistent partition hashed from origin+userId, and a random non-persistent partition when the account id is unknown) with `apps/desktop/src/platform-view.ts:104-110` (the storage is sanitized *before* the view loads, "even after an unclean previous process exit"). *Why it matters*: an August install that caches a provider key in memory or on disk must re-stamp its cache on every file that can change it, or a "fixed" install keeps using the old key for the life of the process.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **A byte-streaming redactor that is tested at every possible chunk split** — `apps/desktop/tests/packaging-run.spec.ts:11` — the test feeds the same secret through the redactor at *every* split offset and asserts the output is identical. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **A total operation deadline that covers the SDK's own retries, and is NOT extended by ongoing bytes** — `apps/desktop/tests/cos-operation.spec.ts:37` — the deadline is one budget for the whole operation, not per attempt, and a download that trickles bytes still hits it. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **An inactivity deadline refreshed by real response bytes, and removed once the bytes are under verification** — `apps/desktop/tests/update-http-executor.spec.ts:25` and `:57` — a slow-but-live transfer must not be killed, and the transport's deadline must stop covering the hashing phase. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **A journal that DROPS details instead of redacting arbitrary text** — `apps/desktop/tests/update-journal.spec.ts:32` — the projector keeps `phase`, `targetVersion`, `failedOperation` and an error *code*, and throws away the message entirely, because a redaction that fails silently is worse than a missing field. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **One JSONL file per installed version, in a directory outside the installation tree** — `apps/desktop/tests/update-journal.spec.ts:8` — the evidence for "before" and "after" lives in two files that both versions can read, so an upgrade can be audited from outside. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **"100 percent is never readiness" and installation approval is a separate act from download** — `apps/desktop/tests/update-coordinator.spec.ts:132` and `:188` — a completed download is not a completed action; a second, explicit approval is required, and a stale approval for a superseded release is rejected. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **A publish/rollback sequence that recovers an ambiguous write without repeating it** — `apps/desktop/tests/desktop-publish.spec.ts:49` — if the connection drops *after* the server stored the bytes, the retry must not rewrite and must not publish the dependent object early. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **A per-channel cross-process lock plus an audit journal written outside the checkout** — `apps/desktop/tests/desktop-publish-record.spec.ts:42` — the lock is per *destination* (not global), and the journal records intent, before/after bytes and terminal state before any mutation. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **A persistent interlock that admits one hardware process and keeps its slot after that process exits** — `apps/desktop/tests/windows-signing-state.spec.ts:10` — the slot is *not* released by process exit; an interrupted privileged run needs an explicit human acknowledgement. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **Admission locking that refuses new work, drains admitted work, then re-checks the task set** — `apps/desktop/tests/host-update-tasks.spec.ts:85` and `:114` — work created *during* the confirmation window is discovered, so the privileged action is refused rather than racing it. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **Error copy chosen from a controlled vocabulary, never from the raw message** — `apps/desktop/tests/update-presentation.spec.ts:18` — the visible summary is selected by `failedOperation` (and `preparationFailure`); the message is dropped, and a message that merely *contains* the localised string is still classified generically. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **A fail-closed policy client that will not guess authentication mode from a response body** — `apps/desktop/tests/mandatory-update-policy.spec.ts:43` — "does not infer login from HTML or unrelated 401". - **[dsh-apps-desktop#3]** - **The "Open verification" list — what the evidence does *not* establish** — `apps/desktop/tests/README.md:16` and `apps/desktop/tests/installed-update/README.md:53` — the docs carry an explicit list of eight unproven items, and a sentence saying that `builderCompleted` does not establish package verification. - **[dsh-apps-desktop#4]** - **A retry policy that distinguishes "the command ran and refused" from "we don't know what happened"** - `apps/desktop/windows-signing/README.md:69` - "Timestamp completion retries only a normally exited timestamp command returning failure or warning, at most three times with one- and two-second delays. Each attempt starts from the same verified primary signature. Launch errors, uncertain termination and verification failures stop immediately." Three transferable properties: (a) retry only the *observable* failure; (b) every attempt restarts from the same **verified** prior state, so a retry cannot compound a partially-applied change; (c) the retry count is tiny and the delays are explicit. August's tool-retry ladder needs exactly this discrimination — a timeout ("uncertain termination") is not the same as a refusal, and retrying an uncertain termination can double-apply a side effect.
- **[dsh-apps-desktop#4]** - **A failure that the failure itself makes unrecoverable must never auto-retry** - `apps/desktop/windows-signing/README.md:75` - "`SignTool Error: No private key is available.`" is treated as terminal: "The device-specific PIN retry limit and remaining attempts are unverified; do not probe them with authentication attempts." - **[dsh-apps-desktop#4]** - **A canary that exercises the exact credential path with a throwaway payload, under one deadline, never executed** - `apps/desktop/windows-signing/README.md:65` - "The local .NET Framework C# compiler creates a small private probe; the production signer signs it once, and verification requires the configured certificate and a timestamp before building continues. The probe proves the *whole* path (sign → timestamp → verify) in seconds instead of discovering a dead token 30 minutes into a build, and the deadline covers the slow part. Three rules worth lifting wholesale: concurrency is spent on verification (cheap), the expensive resource is serialized, and **a corrupt cache is a stop, not a fallback** — falling back would burn the scarce resource exactly when the system is already untrustworthy. Why it matters: it keeps the durable log small and lets the summary be recomputed — a good shape for August's per-turn artifacts.

- **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **The send button unlocks only after the staged-attachment receipt lands, and a failed submission dumps the feedback regions and the event-type sequence** — `apps/web/tests/file-upload-round.e2e.ts:276-293`. - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **The "authorised suffix" release contract: the collector may see the log up to and including the consent event, and nothing after** — `apps/web/tests/feedback-release.e2e.ts:66-85` (the `expectFeedbackRelease` helper computes `authorized = events.filter(e => e.seq <= boundary.seq)` and asserts the collector received exactly that), and the negative twin at `:206-217` (command tails, provider changes and browser reloads must release nothing, proved by the last persisted event's `seq` being *greater* than the last authorised one). - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **A "the same model reviews every native tool call *and every inner call*" permission mode, with the refusal escalated to the human** — `apps/web/tests/expected/access-confirmation/auto-confirmation.expected.md:4`. - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **IME-safe Enter, with the `compositionend + 9ms` case pinned** — `apps/web/tests/expected/plugin-manager/ime-enter.expected.md:2-22` (five composition shapes all with `inspect=0, install=0; editable; value retained`; only a plain Enter at `:22` performs the action). - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **A per-model reasoning-effort TIER TABLE with per-tier wire values, not a flat enum** — `apps/web/tests/expected/models-settings/declared-edit.expected.md:62-88` (three tier comboboxes each with its own `API 参数值` textbox and a delete button) and `apps/web/tests/expected/models-settings/image-only.expected.md:62-88` where the semantic tier `high` carries the wire value **`deep`**. - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **The golden refresh is the ONLY writer; a missing golden fails with a healing command** — the mechanism lives at `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1710-1720` and is used by every one of the 229 expected files in this shard (e.g. `apps/web/tests/feedback-command.e2e.ts:87`). - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **Bind the recorded fixture to the driving script by exact equality on the user prompt** — `apps/web/tests/feedback-command.e2e.ts:56-59`, repeated at `apps/web/tests/feedback-release.e2e.ts:159-162` and `apps/web/tests/file-upload-round.e2e.ts:225-228` (`expect(fixtureUserPrompts(await readFile(FIXTURE, 'utf8'))).toEqual([PROMPT])`). - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **A console tripwire that treats "gap repair" and "discontinuous" as failures, and forgives only the connection-loss warning produced by an intentional reload** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1773-1796` (`watchConsole` / `acknowledgeReloadConnectionLoss`), asserted empty at `apps/web/tests/feedback-command.e2e.ts:95-96`. - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **A route-only adapter that throws if a scenario that declared no model call actually issues one** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:259-264` (`stream()` throws "a model call was issued by a scenario that declared no replay fixture") and `:899-909` (the route-only registration for a UI scenario that needs provider labels but must never call a model). - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **Express a hang/throw scenario as a chunk script via a replay override, not as a recorded session** — `apps/web/tests/expected/steer-all/replay.override.json:1-45` (block-start / reasoning-delta / tool-call-delta / block-end / usage / finish chunks for two turns). - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **One model-label table drives the composer trigger, the `/model` picker and the command-picker group headers** — `apps/web/tests/expected/default-model/model-labels.expected.md:1-42` (provider / model / name / **slot** / inline). - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **Let the model declare its context window and output cap, accepting both a human-formatted default and a literal override** — `apps/web/tests/expected/onboarding-deepseek-config/models.expected.md:37-43` (context window typed literally as `131072`, output cap `64K`) against the default catalogue's `1M` / `256K` placeholders at `apps/web/tests/expected/onboarding-deepseek-config/default-models.expected.md:36-41`. - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **The output-limit notice names the recovery verb and promises the earlier output survived** — `apps/web/tests/expected/max-tokens-notice/history-turn.expected.txt:1-3` ("The reply was cut off; earlier output is preserved in the conversation. - **[dsh-apps-web#2]** - **Measure the browser-facing geometry as *relations*, never as pixels** — `apps/web/tests/expected/composer-tab-geometry/geometry.expected.md:1-40` (a Chat-vs-Trajectory control that removes the scrollbar-gutter compensation in the page and shows the card then moving 2.5px, against the production 0px), and `apps/web/tests/expected/markdown-wide-table/geometry.expected.md:1-21` (fill / wide / long-cell relations at three widths, plus the "wrap-first engagement" assertion). - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **The replay fixture must be FULLY CONSUMED, or the scenario fails** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1003` — `replayHandle?.assertConsumed()` runs in teardown, *before* the world is disposed, so a scenario that drove fewer model calls than the recording contains fails loudly instead of drifting green. - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **An adapter that answers route queries but THROWS on any stream** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:234` (the `RouteOnlyAdapter`) and `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:259` (its `stream()` throws "a model call was issued by a scenario that declared no replay fixture") — the tree must still answer `listProviders()`/`resolveModel` because surfaces legitimately gate on whether any adapter serves a session's route, but a scenario with no fixture must not be able to make a model call quietly. - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **Capture an aria snapshot only when it has stopped changing** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1647` — `expect.poll` compares two consecutive *normalized* captures and only then returns one. - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **Console tripwires: a reconnect warning or a page error fails the scenario** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1778` — the regex `/connection lost|gap repair|discontinuous/i` collects warnings, and `pageerror` collects exceptions; both are asserted empty at scenario end. - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **A missing golden fails with the healing command; only refresh mode may write** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1717` — "missing golden … — run `DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh` … to generate it". - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **A boundary-aware path replacer, not a blind string replace** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1105` (`isWebCwdMatch`) — the cwd token is only substituted when the surrounding characters form a path boundary, so a cwd that is a prefix of a longer path is left intact. - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **Composition divergences are include patches over the SAME tree, never a second file** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:573` — "a patch id that stops matching a row fails the boot sweep loudly instead of drifting". - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **Split the configuration into "live fields" and "process-specific" fields** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:711` — live fields (agent, model, provider, preset, locale, permission…) live in a shared deployment layer, while ports, roots and file paths stay in CLI overlays; the scaffold moves the former into a synthetic "deployment defaults" bundle that sits *below* the editable profile values. - **[dsh-apps-web#3]** - **A real provider catalog with a deliberately large context window** — `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:214` — the replay provider publishes `contextWindow: 128_000` (and 1,000,000 for the vision model) specifically so that "compaction-basic's post-step pressure check would warn every step" does not fire on small fixtures; the comment at `:205-209` explains that a catch-all route would leave `resolveModelInfo` unroutable. August's plugin/skill loading could adopt this so a version-incompatible plugin is never imported, without the user's configuration being mutated by the refusal.
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Make the exemption file separate from every file it would otherwise touch** - `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-compatibility.ts:10` - exact `package-name@version` → exact-runtime-version grants live in the profile's own `compatibility.json`, so granting one never touches the dependency manifest, the bundle list or the patch file; neither a plugin upgrade nor a DSH upgrade inherits a grant; and a file the reader could not fully parse becomes **read-only** rather than being silently overwritten. The "read-only rather than discard the user's content" rule is the part worth stealing.
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Distinguish "cannot express" from "must not express"** - `packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts:55` - `engines.dsh` decides alone when present (peers ignored); otherwise every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer must match. This is the shape August needs for "which agent/extension protocol versions can this install talk to".
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **One queue for every reload, and nesting is an error** - `packages/boot/hmr/src/index.ts:268` (the `runExclusive` method) and `packages/boot/hmr/tests/coordination.spec.ts:37` - module replacement, Include refresh, profile recomposition and config edits all go through one `runExclusive` queue; a nested `runExclusive` is refused with "cannot be nested"; the queue stays usable after a failure; **package installation runs outside the queue**. August's HMR/agent-reload path would benefit from the same single-queue discipline: a config edit that races a module replacement is the classic source of a half-applied tree.
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Every projected event is a commit point** - `packages/bundle/headless/src/json-stream.ts:1` - text and reasoning come from *committed* `assistant/message` content, "never from a live attempt that may still be retried or discarded, so the stream never carries content the durable log does not contain." Alongside it: a per-string 8 KiB cap, a **depth cap of 64** ("a legal but pathologically deep argument would otherwise recurse until the stack overflows, and the isolated listener would silently drop the event"), a null-prototype payload so a literal `__proto__` key cannot pollute, and an explicitly untruncated terminal `final` ("the answer is the lossless terminal contract"). This is a directly reusable recipe for any streaming JSON surface August exposes.
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Detect a changed file by identity, not by mtime alone, and read the clock from the filesystem** - `packages/boot/hmr/src/module-files.ts:11` and `:50` - identity is `ino:size:mtimeMs`; change time is deliberately excluded because "creating a hard link to a file, as pnpm does when it imports from its store, changes it without changing content"; and the comparison clock is the mtime of a freshly written marker file, because "the system clock and file timestamps can differ by a clock tick in either direction". A 2 s allowance covers FAT's timestamp granularity. Transferable to any watcher in August that must decide "did this file really change?".
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Watch exactly one file, not its directory** - `packages/boot/hmr/src/watch-config.ts:38` - the watcher resolves the nearest existing ancestor, watches that root with a depth limit, and filters with `relative(resolve(path), target.filename)`, "so sibling files — including temporary writer locks — are excluded **before** native watcher creation". August watches user config files in several places; the writer-lock exclusion alone removes a whole class of spurious reloads.
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Never leak a private registry to a public one** - `packages/boot/plugin-manager/src/registry.ts:54` - pnpm's own registry joins the fallback set only when what it names is known to be public; while it names anything else, or is unknown, it is asked **alone**, and a public registry asked instead never falls back into it. A registry outside the configured set is also asked alone. And `attributeFailure` reads the spec's host **off error lines only**, so a deprecation warning that merely links to GitHub cannot misattribute a registry failure. Transferable to August's provider/model-fetch failover.
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Classify failures by stable codes, and order the table so a specific code beats a generic family** - `packages/boot/plugin-manager/src/install-failure.ts:21` - `timeout` and "pnpm missing" are decided from *how the run ended*; the output table is ordered (`build-blocked` before `network`); a Git 401/403/404 is `unknown`, not `network`; an offline cache miss is `unknown` because no registry would change it. - **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **Write only `disabled` into the profile, and remove the override entirely when the base already implies it** - `packages/boot/plugin-manager/src/patch.ts:25` - the last matching override is edited in place, an override holding only `id`+`disabled` is **removed** when the bundle layers already give the requested state ("so the profile patch records only departures from the bundles"), and the comment above a removed override is moved to the next item or the document header. Plan mode is a prompt section inside an `isolate`d group, not a smaller tool list. For August this is the cheapest available KV-cache lever: changing behaviour by changing prompt text keeps the request prefix byte-identical, whereas swapping the tool list invalidates the whole prefix.
- **[dsh-boot-bundle]** - **A refusal that would expose remote code execution is stated as such** - `packages/bundle/web-app/src/startup.ts:96` - a wildcard `--host` is refused with the reason spelled out: "binding every interface would expose remote code execution to the network; bind one concrete IPv4 or IPv6 address instead." Any August transcript that draws a separator or a marker row needs the same rule.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Cache the virtual row *structure* so a content-only update cannot invalidate the measurements** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTable.tsx:151` — `useStableVirtualRowStructure` reuses the previous `{key,height}` array when the row count and every row's key and height are unchanged. The observable effect is pinned by `tests/table.client.spec.tsx:806` ("does not re-scroll a virtual ledger when streaming only changes row content") — this is the difference between a transcript that stays pinned to the tail and one that jitters on every token.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Tail-following is opt-out and computed from the scroll position** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTable.tsx:2608` — the scroll handler sets `followsTableTail` from the distance to the bottom (2 px threshold), and only a following ledger writes `scrollTop = scrollHeight`. Scrolling up suspends following so an arriving record does not yank the reader away.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Bound the rendered window but keep the numbering session-wide** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryView.tsx:159` and `:209` — the React-visible slice is 50 nodes anchored at the tail, while the request numbers and the cumulative usage are computed from the *complete* resident snapshot. August needs the same split: the rows are a window, the numbering is the session.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Incremental search that reparses Markdown only when a record actually changed** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-search-index.ts:97` — `update()` compares each record's `sources` array and reuses the previous entry when unchanged; the whole update is throttled to 3 s after the first (`TrajectoryView.tsx:34`). This is how August can search a live transcript without re-parsing Markdown on every frame.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Cap the preview, not the data** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-preview.ts:5` — 2 048 characters of source in, 512 out, and the Markdown is *not* parsed beyond the slice. A truncated preview is marked with an explicit ellipsis so the reader knows.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Redact at the projection boundary, not at the render** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-event-projection.ts:127` — a failure with `code === 'AUTH'` keeps the code and drops the message, with the reasoning spelled out: "Provider AUTH messages may echo a masked or partially preserved credential. Keep the raw diagnostic in the Session log, but never retain it in UI state." This is the same class of defect August's own notes warn about — a credential that rides into the transcript once is re-sent on every later turn. Keeping the raw in the log and dropping it from the UI state is the right seam.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Internal error markers never become user text** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/copy-codes.ts:4` — a synthesized condition travels as `trajectory.compaction-interrupted` and is localized at the render site (`layout.ts:361`, `TrajectoryTable.tsx:751`). August's turn_end reason vocabulary should work the same way: a stable code in the log, a sentence in the UI.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **A call that never returned becomes an explicit interrupted result** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-tool-definition.ts:198` — a started tool whose step or turn closed without a result is projected to a tool-result with `error: {name:'Interrupted', code:'interrupted'}`, ordered at `boundary.seq - 0.8`. A spinner that never resolves is the alternative; August should name the interruption instead.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Bound the tool subtree in both directions** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-tool-definition.ts:123` — `acceptsEdge` refuses a self-edge, an edge to an ancestor (cycle) and an edge whose combined depth would exceed 256; the render path carries a `visited` set as well. Subagent tool trees can cycle; a naive recursive render hangs.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Derive "typed mid-turn" from durable event order, not from a heuristic** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-message-definitions.ts:84` — a splice chain is materialized only when a batch is claimed, and only the *current* claim can classify a later `user/message` as steering. August can answer "was this a mid-turn injection or a new turn?" from the same event ordering.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **A prompt change is anchored at the request that carried it and consumed exactly once** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-snapshot-builder.ts:246` — `consumedPromptChanges` ensures the first inheriting request carries the change and later requests carry only the prompt. A prompt/cache inspector that shows the change on every subsequent request is misleading; this is the rule for showing it once, at the right position.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **A prompt change can exist without a new request header** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-request-header-definition.ts:56` — the system-message Definition reads the previous header through `reader.previous` and synthesises the change itself, because an in-history prompt update logs no header. August's prompt-inspector needs the same "the change is a property of the prompt, not of the header" model.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **An uncertain surface yields an empty claim, not a wrong one** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/trajectory-request-header-definition.ts:46` — when the replacement order cannot be established, the header is emitted with `system: ''` and the record stays visible. The same rule is tested in three modes (replay / live / partial) in `tests/conversation-definitions.client.spec.ts:849` and `:885`. "I do not know yet" is a state the projection must be able to represent.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Never fabricate a duration for work in flight** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/timeline.ts:61` — a cell with no `startedAt` produces no span at all, and the overview renders a start marker rather than a growing bar. August's "working" indicator should show that something started, not a number it did not measure.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Split one assistant bar into TTFT and decoding** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTimeline.tsx:51` — the assistant span is drawn as a two-stop gradient whose split is the TTFT fraction (`TrajectoryTimeline.module.css:200`), and both metrics are refused unless all three timestamps are finite and ordered. Two different bottlenecks in one bar is a genuinely better read than one "duration" number.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Focus, do not filter** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/timeline.ts:194` and `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTable.tsx:2752` — a timeline drag marks the overlapping records `data-timeline-focus="inside"` and dims the rest to 0.24 opacity rather than removing them. A harness that hides the rows outside a focus range loses exactly the context the user was trying to read.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Sample a persisted preference when the surface opens, and write it back on change** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTable.tsx:2358` and `:2375` — `activateTab`/`selectRecord` read `stringWrapping.getDefault()` into a local state at open, and the toggle calls `setDefault`. Two open inspectors therefore do not fight over one preference (`tests/code-inspector.client.spec.tsx:70`).
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **A preference is browser-wide, not per session** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/duration-store.ts:9` — one store is created in `apply` and handed to every session injection; the test asserts the same object identity across two sessions and that no per-session key appears in localStorage (`tests/views.client.spec.tsx:480`).
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **The Chinese dictionary is the key set and the English one is typed against it** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/locales.ts:7` and `:217` — `en: Record<TrajectoryKey, string>` makes a missing English key a **compile error**, not a runtime fallback to the key name.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Per-section hashes keep a bilingual doc pair honest** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/README.i18n.yaml:1` — one hash pair per heading section, regenerated by `verify-translation-pairing --write`. A file-level hash would say "something changed"; a section-level hash says where.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Load the real built artifact, not a mock** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/tests/client-bundle.client.spec.ts:23` — the test reads `lib/client.js`, runs it through the real `window.__ModuleLoader__` handoff, resolves externals through a `require` that **throws on an unexpected specifier**, and asserts the manifest id, the inject list, the CSS injection and the ring registration. This is the only test in the shard that can catch a bundler misconfiguration; unit tests cannot see it.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **A plugin fiber's disposal must remove its tab and its registrations** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/tests/views.client.spec.tsx:445` — after `fiber.dispose()` the view ring holds only Chat and the event and view registries are empty. Hot-reload safety is a contract worth pinning.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Accessibility as a first-class part of the layout** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTable.tsx:2630` and `:2721` — the ledger is a real `<table>` with `aria-rowcount` that reports the *whole* ledger (not the mounted window), per-row `aria-rowindex` that survives prepends, `aria-selected`, and a per-row `aria-label` composed from the request number, kind and content. A virtualized table that lies about its row count is a table that screen readers cannot navigate.
- **[dsh-client-chat#3]** - **Fold the whole turn or the assistant's tool calls, but keep the first row** — `packages/client/ui-trajectory/src/client/TrajectoryTable.tsx:625` and `:689` — a folded turn keeps its first content row and replaces the rest with a one-line summary (`3 steps · 2 tool calls`); a folded assistant keeps the assistant row and summarises its calls (`2 tool calls · bash`). A fold that hides everything leaves the user with no anchor.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A late async settlement is revoked by binding identity, not by a flag** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/popup.ts:294` — the controller swaps its `binding` object on dismiss/reopen/dispose, and every late write checks `this.binding !== binding` and returns. A settling `onSelect` that lands after a dismissal writes nothing, consumes nothing and focuses nothing (`:300`). *Why it transfers*: August's UI fires async results all the time (a permission prompt, a model switch, a plan-mode confirmation). The generalisable rule is "the settlement carries the identity of the thing it was opened for; if that identity is no longer current, the settlement has no rights." Cheaper and safer than a boolean `cancelled` flag, because it cannot be forgotten.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Admission and outcome are different channels** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts:409` — "An unmatched line reports an error outcome (the composer's immediate admission feedback); an admitted command reports plain success regardless of its handler outcome, because the host executor durably logged the lifecycle and the outcome renders as a persistent flow node — the composer never echoes it." *Why it transfers*: August's harness has exactly this split — a tool call can be *admitted* (it reached the executor) and still *fail* (the handler threw). If the submit path returned the handler's failure text, the composer would echo an outcome that the durable event log is already rendering, and the user would see it twice. The admission channel should be an immediate, short-lived "did it get in?" signal; the outcome channel is the durable event.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Refuse loudly at the door, preserve the user's work** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts:332` — a submission carrying attachments proceeds only if the command declares `input.attachments`; every other route throws the localized refusal so the machine surfaces *one* notice and "the draft and attachments stay in place; nothing executes and nothing is dropped." *Why it transfers*: August's harness has several places where a route could silently drop the user's payload (an image on a text-only command, a file on a tool that cannot read it). The rule is: refuse at the boundary with a specific, localized reason, and never destroy the draft as a side effect of the refusal.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **An epoch guard on a per-session cache** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/directory.ts:109` — `const epoch = ++entry.epoch`; only the pull whose epoch is still current may publish its outcome. A superseded pull's success cannot overwrite a newer snapshot, and its failure cannot demote a newer success. *Why it transfers*: August has per-session caches too (model catalog, agent roster, permission presets). Without the guard, two in-flight refreshes for the same session can land out of order and the cache can end up holding the *older* catalog — or be marked failed by a stale rejection. The guard is three lines and the spec covers both directions.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A planner that returns nothing means nothing happened** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/engine/planner.ts:13` — "A planner returning no operations means the intent changes nothing; the caller records nothing and notifies nobody." The planner is a pure function from state to operations; the controller is a thin "plan → record → notify" wrapper (`:115` in `controller.ts`). *Why it transfers*: August's turn loop has the same shape available — a pure "what would this intent do" function that returns an empty plan, with the recorder and the notifier downstream. It gives August a testable "no-op intent" concept, and it means a planner can be exercised with no DOM, no clock and no random source (which the planner spec asserts explicitly).
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Capture the inverse at execution time, because the pre-state is gone by undo time** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/engine/operations.ts:3` — `applyOp(state, op)` returns the next state *and* the operations that undo it; the inverses are prepended in reverse order when they are collected (`packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/engine/sequence.ts:105`). *Why it transfers*: any August feature that needs undo/redo (a plan-mode edit, a subagent re-launch, a tool-argument correction) should capture the inverse when the operation runs, not reconstruct it later by diffing. The dockkit's `insertPane`/`insertTab`/`restoreFocus` operations exist *only* to express inverses exactly — a good precedent for adding inverse-only operation kinds.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Collapse a run of focus-only history entries into one undo step** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/engine/sequence.ts:126` — `stepBack` walks back over a consecutive run of entries whose operations are all focus-only, so the user undoes "I looked at three tabs" as one step, not three. *Why it transfers*: August's transcript has the same noise — a run of focus/selection/scroll events between two substantive steps. If August ever offers an undo or a "step back" affordance over agent activity, focus-only entries must coalesce or the undo is useless.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A measurement that would flip with the UI's own visibility must exclude that visibility's footprint** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/engine/geometry.ts:79` — the room rule reads the strip's fixed part; when the embedder hides a blocked split control, that control's own footprint is left out, because "a reading that counted it would flip with the control's visibility and re-render forever". The regression is recorded in the spec: `packages/client/ui-dockkit/tests/components.client.spec.tsx:427` — "re-render forever (React's update-depth limit, which crashed the surface)". *Why it transfers*: this is a general August bug class — any guard that measures the UI it is about to change creates a feedback loop. The fix is a design rule: *the measurement must not depend on the thing it decides.*
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **The right column is a track, not a box** — `packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/AppFrame.tsx:46` — "Zero-width unless the occupant asked for a track; the occupant's panel is positioned against the column's right edge, which never moves, so it can hang over the centre when there is no track." *Why it transfers*: August's UI will have a side panel (a task inspector, a diff view, a subagent trace). If the frame owns the panel's box, every overlay mode needs a second layout path. Making the *track* the negotiable thing and the *edge* the anchor lets one layout serve both "docked" and "floating" without a second code path.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Let CSS solve the squeeze; JS only makes discrete decisions** — `packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/AppFrame.tsx:234` — "The rendered template lets the grid solve the squeeze natively: the centre declares its protected minimum and the right column bids up to the clamped preference… The JS solve lags the viewport by a ResizeObserver + rAF frame; when it priced the squeeze itself, the centre column absorbed each width change whole and was corrected two frames later — visible jitter." *Why it transfers*: any responsive August UI that computes a layout in JS and then writes the result will visibly lag the window edge. Declaring the *constraint* (a minimum, a maximum, a ratio) in the template and letting the engine resolve it removes a whole class of jitter.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A presenter that retracts only what it wrote** — `packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/theme-presenter.ts:85` — the presenter keeps the list of token names it applied and removes exactly those on dispose, so "foreign attributes, metadata, and inline styles survive". *Why it transfers*: August writes global CSS variables (theme tokens, font sizes) and clears them on teardown or on theme change. A blanket "remove all inline styles" wipes whatever another component wrote; a retraction set does not.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A picker opens with the highlight on the value in use, not the top row** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/popup.ts:127` — `currentIndex` parks the highlight on the option marked `active`; the contract file states the reason: "so an accept gesture made without looking confirms the value in use." *Why it transfers*: August has model pickers, mode pickers and permission pickers. Opening a picker on the current value means the cheapest gesture (Enter) is the safe one; opening on the top row means the cheapest gesture is the *dangerous* one.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Search filters locally; the provider is never re-queried per keystroke** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/popup.ts:211` — options are loaded once per open and the search text filters them in the view; the spec asserts `options` was called exactly once. *Why it transfers*: a picker over a large catalogue (models, agents, skills) should fetch once and filter locally. It removes a round trip per keystroke and makes the picker feel instant; the cost is that the option set must be loaded up front, which the caller's `options()` contract makes explicit.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Focus lands on click, not on press** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/TabPanel.tsx:279` — "a state change between `pointerdown` and the first `pointermove` rebuilds the pressed subtree, and Chromium cancels the pointer when the pressed element is replaced — which would abandon every drag." *Why it transfers*: any August UI that both drags something and reacts to a press must not mutate the pressed subtree during the gesture. It is the difference between a drag that works and a drag that silently dies.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A menu that would hold no item never paints** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/TabMenu.tsx:99` and `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/dockkit.module.css:557` — the component returns null when there is no close item and no extras, and the stylesheet hides a menu with no `role=menuitem*` descendant (the kit *probes* for that role to decide the menu is empty). *Why it transfers*: an August context menu that opens and shows nothing is a dead control; the contract "an item must carry `role=menuitem`, because the kit probes for that role to dismiss a menu that would paint empty" makes the emptiness rule enforceable rather than advisory.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **One stylesheet per package, because consumers de-duplicate injected sheets by file name** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/dockkit.module.css:1` — "a consumer de-duplicates injected stylesheets by `<pluginId>/<basename>`, so a second sheet whose file name matches one in the embedding package would be dropped silently. Keeping a single `dockkit.module.css` makes that collision impossible." *Why it transfers*: if August ships CSS modules to the browser, a name collision is a *silent* style loss. One sheet per package removes the class of bug by construction.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **An identity, not a name, selects a first-party face** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/resolution.ts:23` — `builtinCommandName` matches on `descriptor.definitionId`, not on the command's name, so a same-name override keeps its own copy and gets no first-party alias; and `resolveCommand` (`:50`) resolves a bilingual alias by definitionId, "so an alias never selects an unrelated scoped override". *Why it transfers*: August's agent/tool registry will have scoped overrides of built-in tools. Selecting a built-in's *special behaviour* (the goal command, the plan command, the compact command) by name is a privilege-escalation shape: any package registering `plan` would inherit the first-party semantics. Selecting by a stable definition identity closes it.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **The claim keeps the typed spelling; the submission sends the canonical name** — `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts:395` — the `CommandClaim` carries the token the user sees (`/计划 `) while `submit` sends the catalog name (`/plan ship it`). *Why it transfers*: August's slash/command surface (and any localized UI) needs exactly this split, and the alternative — rewriting the user's typed text — breaks their expectation of what they typed.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A superseded navigation is aborted, but the underlying work is not cancelled** — `packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/service.ts:81` — `beginNavigation()` returns an `AbortSignal` that the next navigation, any valid panel selection, or disposal aborts; the docstring is explicit that this does **not** cancel the underlying Session creation, and consumers check the signal *before* committing UI state. *Why it transfers*: August's UI starts asynchronous navigation (open a session, switch a panel, spawn a subagent). A per-navigation abort signal lets the UI drop a stale result without tearing down work that is still wanted — and the check belongs *before* the commit, not after.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **An edit that changes nothing must not be recorded** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/DockSurface.tsx:272` — `if (sameSizes(sizes, drag.sizes)) return`: "A release that left the fractions where they were — a click on the divider, a drag returned to its start, or one pushed further into the clamp — is not a resize and reports nothing." *Why it transfers*: August's activity log / transcript should record *changes*, not gestures. A user who clicks a divider or a button that does nothing should not produce an entry, or the history becomes noise. The comparison is a tolerance-based equality (`SIZE_TOLERANCE = 1e-9`), which is what makes it cheap and exact.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A re-measure that changed nothing re-renders nothing** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/measure.ts:122` — `sameFits` compares two measurement maps so an unchanged reading returns the *same* state object. *Why it transfers*: any measurement-driven guard (a "does the pane fit" check, a "is the panel too narrow" check) should return the previous value when nothing changed, so React (or August's own diffing) can skip the update. This is the same principle as the previous idea, applied to measurements instead of intents.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A gesture is one intent, and the preview is local** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/DockSurface.tsx:218` — the drag previews in local component state while the gesture's own facts stay in its closure; on release "the net result leaves through one `DockIntents` call — a strip release reports the caret slot as drawn, the dragged chip counted, and `planPlaceTab` turns that into the reorder or the move." *Why it transfers*: August's agent loop records *tool calls*, not token deltas. The same discipline — preview locally, commit one net intent at the end — is what keeps a long drag from producing hundreds of history entries.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **Only the owning pointer counts, and capture is hardening, not the mechanism** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/pointer.ts:5` and `:47` — the window listeners carry the gesture whether or not capture succeeded, and every listener filters on `event.pointerId === pointerId`. *Why it transfers*: a second finger or a trackpad palm must not end a drag; and the gesture must survive an environment without pointer capture (jsdom, some embedded webviews).
- **[dsh-client-primitives#1]** - **A nested control stops its own press** — `packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/TabPanel.tsx:325` — `onPointerDown={event => event.stopPropagation()}` on the chip's close button: "otherwise the press starts a drag, captures the pointer, and the nested control's click never lands." *Why it transfers*: August's chat UI will have buttons inside draggable rows (a copy button on a message, a retry button on a tool card). Without this, those buttons are dead.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#2]** - **A terminal-accurate ANSI replayer with per-cell SGR state, emitting one canonical sequence per state change** — `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ansi.ts:242` (`replayLine`), `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ansi.ts:171` (`foldSgr`), `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ansi.ts:209` (`openSgr`) — the state is *normalised* ("current state", not "sequence history"), which is what keeps the output linear in cell count; the file records the bug that motivated it: *"output that switches color without a full reset emitted O(n²) characters (3200 such cells produced 25 MB and eventually a `RangeError`)"*. **Why it transfers to August**: `run_command` output is model-visible and routinely contains progress bars (`\r`), spinners and colour resets. August's transcript card must (a) never let raw escape bytes reach the DOM and (b) paint a redraw the way a terminal would, because a progress bar that leaves its previous frame's tail standing is text the terminal never showed. The "each cell is stamped with the state it was written with" rule (`ansi.ts:248-252`) is the subtle part: a later redraw must not restyle cells it does not reach.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#2]** - **Incremental block-level parsing that freezes the prefix, keyed by absolute source offset** — `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/incremental.ts:38` (`UNSTABLE_TAIL_BLOCKS = 2`), `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/incremental.ts:310` (`update`), `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/incremental.ts:349` (the freeze cut) — re-parsing the whole accumulated reply on every chunk is quadratic in the final answer length; CommonMark block parsing is line-based, so only the last block can be reshaped by appended text. **Why it transfers to August**: August's assistant turn is an append-only stream. A per-chunk full re-parse of the whole reply is exactly the cost this removes, and the *key* choice (a block's absolute start offset, stable from the frame it first appears through freezing) is what lets React reconcile instead of remounting — the difference between a streaming reply that stays smooth and one that flickers. The stated trade (reference-style links across the freeze boundary render literally until the settled parse) is the kind of limitation August should state rather than hide.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#2]** - **Two grammars, one per rendering phase: the streaming arm has no math** — `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/parse.ts:27` (`parseGfm`) and `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/parse.ts:40` (`parseGfmWithMath`) — the header explains it: *"the streaming arm's grammar: no math, so incomplete TeX never flashes KaTeX errors mid-stream"*. **Why it transfers to August**: this is a general rule for model output — a half-formed construct should not be *interpreted* while it is still growing. The same rule should govern a JSON argument, a diff hunk and a YAML block in the tool-call stream, not just TeX. The pair is also the cheapest possible "settle" test: the settled render is the streaming render plus one feature.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#2]** - **One highlighter, three boot grammars, ~57 lazy grammars, and a viewport gate** — `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/highlight.ts:42` (`LANGS`), `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/highlight.ts:53` (`LAZY_GRAMMARS`), `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/useViewportHighlighting.ts:55` — *only the three grammars every session renders load at boot; every other language is a dynamic import, so a session that never opens a code surface in that language pays neither the grammar module nor its synchronous init.* Highlighting is also deferred until the block **intersects the viewport**, permanently, with a single shared observer released when the last pending block unmounts. **Why it transfers to August**: a transcript with fifty code blocks should not cost fifty grammar downloads or fifty synchronously tokenized documents at open. August's file-read and diff cards are the same shape.
- **[dsh-client-primitives#2]** - **A streaming highlight session that re-tokenizes only appended text and keeps completed lines' DOM** — `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/highlight.ts:478` (`StreamingHighlightSession`), `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/CodeBlock.tsx:58` (`STREAMING_LINE_GROUP_SIZE = 32`) — the session resumes from **saved grammar state**, so a template literal that spans lines is coloured correctly mid-stream, and completed lines are sealed into fixed-size React groups so later chunks reconcile only the growing group. **Why it transfers to August**: shiki's `codeToTokens` on a growing string is O(n²); August's streaming code fences would pay the same. The "fixed-size groups" trick (reconcile the group, not the line) is the part that scales.

"One save = one atomic, revision-fenced write of every staged edit" is a much better contract than "each field writes when it settles", and *presence* semantics for overrides is the difference between "the user changed this" and "this happens to differ from the default". - **[dsh-client-primitives#2]** - **The streaming grammar must be a SUBSET of the settled one, and the difference must be the only difference** — `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/parse.ts:27` (streaming: `gfm()` + `cjkFriendlyStrong()`) vs `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/parse.ts:40` (settled: the same two **plus** `mathCompatibility()` and `math()`) — the settled grammar is the streaming one plus exactly the math extensions, and the file's header says the arms *"differ only where TeX delimiters begin a math construct"*. **Why it transfers to August**: this is the cleanest statement of the rule I found anywhere in the shard — *the live arm and the final arm must be the same renderer with the live one missing only what cannot yet be judged*. - **[dsh-client-primitives#3]** - **Repeated identical errors must not restart the toast timer** — `packages/client/ui-shortcuts/src/client/Reference.tsx:89` (`notify`) and its proof at `packages/client/ui-shortcuts/tests/reference.client.spec.tsx:346`. `if (error && previous?.error && previous.text === text) return previous` — the same error keeps the *same* toast element (and therefore its dismissal deadline), while a different error or a success replaces it immediately. *Why it transfers*: any August UI that surfaces transient failures (a tool refusal, a rate-limit notice) should not make a repeating problem look like a stream of new events; the audit-trail distinction between "still the same failure" and "a new failure" is worth carrying.

- **[dsh-client-settings#2]** - **A selection equal to the deployment's composed value CLEARS the override instead of storing a copy of it** — `packages/client/ui-settings-web-search/src/client/web-search-card-controller.ts:292-300` (`select`). - **[dsh-client-sidebar#2]** - **Version coherence: pages of two file versions must never meet on screen** — `packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/face.ts:159` and `packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/store.ts:187` — a page whose version differs from the pages already held, arriving past the first line, restarts the walk from line 1; and the store independently drops the older pages when a newer one arrives. - **[dsh-client-sidebar#2]** - **Fail a document preview *without reading it* when the format is known-binary and unrenderable** — `packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/document/unviewable.ts:10` and `packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/TextPreview.tsx:199` — the owner checks the suffix list before any read is issued. - **[dsh-client-sidebar#2]** - **The recourse, not the error, is what the user needs** — `packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/failure-line.ts:47` — `emptyFailureRecourse()` maps a failure code to `open` (hand the file to something that can render it), `retry`, or `none`. Why it matters: August's failure surfaces tend to show a Retry button on everything.
