August's tool layer currently conflates these; the split is what lets the model reason about side effects.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Admit a changed system prompt according to the *prepared route's* capability, so a KV-cache-friendly route appends and an incapable route consolidates** — `packages/core/agent-loop/src/runtime-context.ts:88` (`SystemPromptProjection.project`) driven by `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:416`. With `systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'` a changed prompt is **appended after the cached history**, so the prefix through that history stays reusable; on an incapable route or a new series the prompt is consolidated at node 0 through logged per-node empty replacements, and an empty rendering clears *every* active system node. August, which has no `in-history` route today, could adopt the "consolidate at the head" half plus the "clear every active node" rule, and keep the door open for the appending half.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Log the request header as a full canonical snapshot and only when it changed — then reconstruct the request from the log alone** — `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:616` (`buildRequest`) and `packages/core/session/src/request-header.ts:63` (`foldRequestHeader`). The header carries call config, adapter defaults and tool schemas, but *not* the prompt (the prompt is a surface node). The loop logs a header on first use, on change, on an explicit series start and on resume; unchanged steps inherit the latest snapshot, so no tokens are duplicated. The repo then asserts the central invariant as a test: "THEOREM: every request rebuilds byte-equal from the session log alone" (`packages/core/agent-loop/tests/request-reconstruction.spec.ts:856`). August could use the same shape to make every model request auditable and re-issuable.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Prove prefix stability against the *real* provider, not only in mocks** — `packages/core/agent-loop/tests/request-cache.e2e.ts:74`. The test is gated on `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, runs a multi-step tool turn plus a follow-up turn against the live API, and asserts `cacheReadTokens > 0` on **every** request after the first, using the per-step `usage` recorded on the durable `assistant/message` event as the observable. It also verifies the conversation itself (the tool's value reached the final answer), so a green run proves the cache and the turn. August has no such end-to-end cache check.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Freeze each derived message identity once, then reuse it** — `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:688` (`buildRequest` + the `frozenMessages` `WeakSet`). The loop deep-freezes a message the first time it is sent and reuses that frozen object for every later request; the request array itself is fresh per dispatch, but the *messages* are shared and frozen. This is what keeps the provider prefix byte-identical across steps, and it is why a later surface replacement can produce a new object with the same message id. August's context assembly could adopt the same "freeze the identity once" rule.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Canonicalise the model-facing tool order so registration order cannot leak downstream** — `packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts:674` (`orderTools`) with `TOOL_ORDER_REST`. Tools are ordered by an explicit `toolOrder` list (with one `'<unlisted-tools>'` rest entry) or lexicographically, and the loop builds its request header from that canonical list. The pinned behaviour is in `packages/core/agent-loop/tests/tool-order.spec.ts:70`: registering `zulu, alpha, mike` in any order produces the same header and the same dispatched request. Registration order is a concurrent-loading artifact and must not reach the provider.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Fail loud on an unresolved prompt variable rather than sending a malformed prompt** — `packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts:340` (`interpolate`). A `{{name}}` that is unregistered, registered-but-valueless, or malformed throws and names the contributing section; a lone `{{` with no later `}}` stays literal prose; substituted values are not re-scanned; and the lookup uses `Object.hasOwn`, so `{{constructor}}` is unknown. August's prompt templating currently risks sending a half-substituted prompt.
- **[dsh-core]** - **One relation, two directions: registration views inherit *down* the scope chain, event admission extends *up* it** — `packages/core/scope/src/index.ts:170` (`scopeTarget`) and `:98` (`scopeChainOf`). A child scope sees its ancestors' registered contributions (nearest wins); an ancestor-tagged listener receives a descendant's events; a descendant-tagged listener never receives an ancestor's. The parent link is set once and only its holder may re-link it, and every link rejects a cycle. August's per-agent isolation and its orchestrator-wide observation both fall out of this one primitive.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Attribute work causally with an `AsyncLocalStorage` initiator scope — and say plainly that it is process-local** — `packages/core/agent/src/index.ts:625` (`runWithInitiator`) and `:344` (`withoutInitiator`). The driver's whole lifetime runs inside the boundary so helpers below it can attribute their work without threading the agent through every call; `withoutInitiator()` hides it for shared timers and pumps. The teardown counts live boundaries, drains them, and *excludes the boundary that initiated the teardown from its own drain* — otherwise disposing a service inside a boundary self-deadlocks. The README states the limit: "Ambient presence is neither liveness proof nor authorization; explicit identity stays authoritative at worker, process, persistence, and wire boundaries."
- **[dsh-core]** - **Keep a fused dispatcher so the event's subject and its scope key cannot diverge** — `packages/core/agent/src/dispatch.ts:107` (`agentEvents`). The dispatcher injects the agent into the payload (the spread comes first, so a payload that happens to carry an `agent` field cannot override it) and passes the scope carrier as the `thisArg`; the type-level `AgentSubjectEvent` requires both a payload carrying `agent` and a `Scoped<Agent>` `this`, which excludes accidental events. The dispatcher also resolves the callback set *itself*, because Cordis's `emit` uses `Array.map` and one synchronous throw there starves later listeners. August's per-agent event surface would get subject/key consistency and non-vetoing notifications from one object.
- **[dsh-core]** - **A "consumed work" fold that a turn cannot fake** — `packages/core/agent/src/consumed-work.ts:69` (`foldConsumedWork`). A turn that stops before its first step leaves a `turn/end` shaped exactly like a balanced no-op turn, so reading turns in isolation either credits cut-short work as finished or convicts every no-op. The fix is to read the *inbox's* own record: a splice with `removedCount` and `outcome: 'canceled'` separates "claimed and ran" from "dropped unrun". August's turn accounting (the `turn_outcomes` ledger) has the same ambiguity and could use the same log-derived shape.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Tell the model when its own earlier turns came from a different model** — `packages/core/agent/src/model-selection.ts:113` (the `agent/pre-step` listener). The selection is captured at *assembly* and applied to the *same* step's request, so a concurrent switch takes effect on a later step rather than splitting the two surfaces; and a route change appends a durable user-role notice, `[model changed: assistant turns above this point were generated by <previous>; the session continues with <next>]`. August's model-routing work could adopt the notice — it costs one short message and removes a whole class of model confusion.
- **[dsh-core]** - **Trade N tool schemas for one generated SDK (PTC mode) and make the generated text byte-deterministic** — `packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts:32` (`RUN_CODE_NAME`) with `packages/core/tools/src/ts-types.ts` and `py-types.ts`. The model programs against `await tools.name(args)` inside a single `run_code` call, and the SDK text is generated from the same registry store that `schemas()` projects. The pinned requirement is "renders byte-identical SDK text across consecutive assemblies of an unchanged tool set" (`packages/core/tools/tests/ptc.spec.ts:434`) — non-determinism there would silently break the prefix cache. August's "progressive disclosure" of tools could adopt the same generated-SDK shape, and the same determinism requirement.
- **[dsh-core]** - **A "no tool policy in the model-facing schema" projection** — `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1290` (`schemaOf`). `schemas()` emits only `name`, `description`, `parameters` and `deferLoading`; `output`, `execute`, `finalizeContent`, `timeoutMs`, `isConcurrencySafe` and the presentation callbacks never reach the model. The pinned test asserts the exact key set (`packages/core/tools/tests/execution-mode.spec.ts:124`). August's tool schema projection should have the same "one projection, deliberately narrow" property.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **A content-addressed compatibility ledger for persisted records** — `docs/persistence-changes/README.md:76` — every persisted type root carries a SHA-256 over its *normalized* schema, and any structural change must be acknowledged by a dated record naming the predecessor and the before/after digests; the verifier then "rejects missing predecessors, cycles, duplicate successors for one root, digest mismatches, and current roots that disagree with their latest records". Why it transfers to August: August persists `messages` rows, `turn_outcomes` rows and `transcript_archive` blocks that other code reads back; a digest per record type plus a dated acknowledgement turns "did we break a reader?" from a review ritual into a mechanical question, and it catches the exact class of bug in AGENTS.md where a transcript field is pruned before archiving and is then in neither place.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **A change classifier that finds the shape of a change but refuses to decide safety, forcing a human to sign** — `docs/persistence-changes/README.md:61` — "The classifier identifies established same-version cases and changes requiring compatibility review; it cannot decide semantic safety. The latter require an explicit `--decision same-version` when recording or updating without a version increase." Why it transfers: August's brain-config and tool-surface changes have the same two-part shape (detect the delta, then reason about the reader) and the same failure mode (a detector that silently blesses a change). Making the safety judgement a *file* that CI reads means the judgement is reviewable, diffable and attributable.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **A retrospective structural diff of your own history, graded by the current rules** — `docs/persistence-changes/releases/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1.md:112` (the table) and `:110` (the framing) — every historical change is re-classified as `not-required` or `review-required` "using current rules for comparison only; it does not assert historical compliance, migration correctness, or runtime compatibility", and the release records refuse to authorise anything (`releases/README.md:68`: "A backfilled record cannot authorize a current PR to omit acknowledgement or a required version increase"). Why it transfers: August can run the same grader over its own migration history to find which past changes would today require a review — a free audit of the thing AGENTS.md worries about most.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Qualified attribution: a producer's unknown source kind is preserved and never interpreted, and the promise is recorded *in the schema*** — `docs/persistence-changes/README.md:67` (the prose) and `docs/persistence-changes/2026-10-13-user-rpc-principal.schema.json:101-112` (the machine form: `policy: session-source-attribution`, `discriminator: kind`, `unknownKinds: "preserve"`, and the qualified `attributionKinds` list). Why it transfers: August's `messages.source` and its Bot/remote principals need a way for a new producer to add a kind without every reader learning it. Making the *policy* a schema property means it is diffed and digested, so "readers must preserve and derive the recorded messages without that projection" is enforceable rather than aspirational.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Declare a deliberately forbidden field as optional `never` so that re-permitting it is a visible type change** — `docs/persistence-changes/README.md:71` — "When a reader rejects a JSON property by name, declare the property as optional `never` and mark it with argument-free `@persistenceReserved`. The extractor retains the forbidden field, so allowing a JSON value later requires an existing-field type change." Why it transfers: the V4 record uses this on the retired `system` key in `request/header` (`2026-09-16-session-format-v4.md:96`). August has the same need — a key the backend refuses today (a retired brain-config key, a blocked tool name) should be *typed* as forbidden so that relaxing it later shows up in a diff instead of appearing as a silent behaviour change.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **An empty value for a named config switch is REFUSED, not ignored** — `docs/user/guide/providers.md:209` — "a key left empty (`supportsDeveloperRole:`) is refused rather than ignored, because an empty value would erase what the catalog knows while saying nothing in its place." Why it transfers: this is exactly the `0`-vs-absent trap in August's brain-config (`0 = off` vs `absent = armed at the shipped constant`). DSH's rule generalises it: if you name a key you must give it a value, and the *absence* of the key is the only way to say "use the inherited default".
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Separate the advertised endpoint from the admitted one** — `docs/user/guide/public-deployments.md:25` — "advertising it with `--public-url` is display only and does not admit it"; the admission fence is `--trusted-host`, and "the fence only admits the request; the launch token in the printed URL and the signed session cookie authenticate it." Why it transfers: August's remote-access door has the same three layers (advertised URL, authority fence, credential), and conflating the first two is how a deployment ends up believing a printed URL is a security control.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **A rejected config value fails per-scheme, never by substitution** — `docs/user/guide/network-proxy.md:48` — "A `socks5://` value is reported at startup and skipped, and DSH connects directly for the scheme that named it — setting `HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://…` alongside a usable `HTTP_PROXY` leaves `https:` direct rather than borrowing the HTTP proxy." Why it transfers: the general rule is "a value you refused for one target must not be silently replaced by a different target's value", and the failure is reported at startup, not at request time. August's provider routing has the same shape (a refused `apiFormat` must not fall back to another format's request body).
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Adapter-owned reasoning vocabulary, not a core enum** — `docs/user/develop/practice/llm-adapter.md:116` — "preserve the adapter's authoritative selectable list, including `off` when its upstream capability API returns it, instead of promoting those values into a core enum"; and the wire side at `docs/user/guide/providers.md:155` — "Each key is a level the menu offers, and its value is the spelling sent on the wire as `reasoning_effort` … Only `off` may stay empty." Why it transfers: this is the exact shape of August's per-model `reasoning_effort` and its `thinkingFormat: deepseek` compat switch (`docs/user/guide/providers.md:157`) — the *menu* vocabulary and the *wire* vocabulary are different sets, `off` is the only universal member, and a model that thinks by default needs `off` to send an explicit disable.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Fail loudly rather than silently dropping an unhonourable provider field** — `docs/user/develop/practice/llm-adapter.md:114` — "If the provider cannot honor a field, throw `LlmError` with a stable code instead of silently dropping it." Why it transfers: August's tool loop has the same failure mode — a capability the model expects but the adapter cannot honour is dropped, and the model then loops on a field that will never arrive. A stable error code is also what makes the refusal countable.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Retain what you can no longer read, under a first-class "unknown" state** — `docs/persistence-changes/2026-09-20-unknown-child-catalog.md:38` (and the `mode: 'unknown'` literal in the sibling schema) — unreadable historical children stay in the catalog as `unknown`; complete facts keep payload version 0 while the migration emits version 1. Why it transfers: August's brain has a retired/consolidation-parked concept and its sessions have orphan records; a persisted record that is no longer readable should have a "we kept it and cannot interpret it" state rather than be deleted or silently downgraded into a valid-looking row.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Name a boolean for the claim, not for the fact** — `docs/persistence-changes/2026-09-30-job-session-lifecycle.md:42` — "producerReported describes completion-promise fulfillment, not verified resource release"; and in the same sentence, "historical sessions receive no fabricated job history". Why it transfers: August's job/process records need the same two properties — a field that says *who said it finished* rather than *it finished*, and a rule that a new record type applied to old rows must not invent a past.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **A `surface` boolean per event root — a machine-checkable answer to "what does the model actually see"** — `docs/persistence-changes/finalized/v4.json:17` (an event with `surface: false`) versus `:53-58` (an event with `surface: true`) — exactly five of the 65 roots are model-visible: `assistant/message`, `developer/message`, `system/message`, `tool/result`, `user/message`. Why it transfers: August decides every turn what enters the model's history and what is log-only (PTC dispatch, workspace changes, retries, title requests). A declared per-event boolean makes that set checkable, and makes "this log-only event accidentally reached the model" a diff rather than a reading.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **An archive must be a snapshot, not a re-derivation** — `docs/persistence-changes/historical-formats/README.md:60` — "The successor uses the current catalog; copying a new current catalog cannot satisfy the archived predecessor requirement." Why it transfers: August's DB migrations are the same shape; the pre-migration schema capture must be a frozen snapshot of the old state, and a rule that re-derives it from today's code cannot prove the old reader still works.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Say the disposal hazard instead of hiding it** — `docs/user/develop/framework/index.md:63` — "During unload, disposer invocation starts in reverse registration order, but multiple async disposers run concurrently and have no serial completion guarantee. Put order-dependent cleanup in one disposer returned from a single `ctx.effect()` and await its steps serially there." Why it transfers: any August shutdown path with more than one async cleanup has the same hazard, and the doc's remedy (collapse order-dependent work into one disposer) is the transferable part.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **The capability is the seam, not its parts** — `docs/user/develop/practice/index.md:9` — "When a capability is general enough to need replaceable providers … Harness separates three roles … The complete capability is its seam. No individual role is a seam."; and `:151` — "Explicit > implicit — resolve defaults in an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step rather than hiding `?? default` expressions inside `run()`." Why it transfers: this is the cleanest statement I found of how to make a tool surface swappable — and the explicit `resolve` step is the same shape August's "resolve, then run" gates would take.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **A waterfall listener's `next()` is mandatory, and the doc says omitting it is a feature** — `docs/user/develop/framework/events.md:66` and the warning at `:80` — "A waterfall listener **must call `next()`** … omitting the call short-circuits the pipeline by design, enabling interception and gateway behavior." Why it transfers: August's request path has interception points (scrubbing, retry classification, budget pricing). Declaring the short-circuit as intended behaviour — rather than a bug — is what lets a future maintainer change the interception chain without fear.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **A webhook's HTTP response is deliberately weaker than its outcome** — `docs/user/guide/github-review.md:69` — "`202` means the signature and JSON were accepted and rule calls were scheduled in memory. It does not mean this rule matched or that a Session was created." Why it transfers: any inbound-webhook door in August (a bot DM, a schedule trigger) should distinguish "accepted" from "done", because conflating them produces a retry storm.
- **[dsh-docs-persistence]** - **Per-heading bilingual hash pairs as a translation-drift gate** — `docs/persistence-changes/2026-09-13-working-directory.i18n.yaml:1-4` (the header comment names the regeneration command and the hashing rule) — every section of every doc carries an en hash and a zh hash, so a translation that lags is detected *per section*, and the machine declaration inside the code block is compared for equality rather than translated. Why it transfers: August's docs are bilingual too, and the failure this catches — a machine-readable block that has silently diverged between languages — is exactly the failure a file-level "both files exist" check misses.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Make every package document its own KV-cache and token effect as a gated README section.** `docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md:99` defines a mandatory `#### KV Cache effect` field under a `## Model Experience` section, and `docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md:108` specifies the four distinctions it must make: *append-only growth, a stable repeated prefix, replacement of earlier request tokens, and an independent model request* — plus "name the package-owned changes that can invalidate reuse". This turns "don't break the prompt cache" from tribal knowledge into a per-package, reviewable, machine-checked contract, and it is exactly the discipline August's prompt-assembly path needs (August's memory tail, tool schemas, and system-prompt sections each change the prefix). The audited escape hatches are also specified (`docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md:110`): a package with no effect writes `None, as ` / `Indirectly, through ` and *still* states its cache effect.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Separate durable model-visible facts from transient live frames, and make the durable log the only source of truth.** `docs/architecture.md:124` states the rule as "**Model-visible means logged.** Every model request must be reconstructable from the log. New model-visible inputs require session events." The loop keeps `agent/assistant-stream` chunk frames process-local and transient, and commits the complete compact stream as one `assistant/message` (success) or `assistant/attempt` (failure) before a committed end frame (`docs/architecture.md:106`). For August this is the difference between a transcript that can be replayed/audited after a crash and one that cannot — and the failure/attempt split is what makes a failed provider call visible instead of silently dropped.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Give the LLM adapter exactly two sanctioned error channels and make the runtime normalise them.** `docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md:30` allows only THROW from `stream()` (transport/protocol) or a terminal `finish {kind:'error'|'aborted'}` (provider in-band), and `docs/defensive-patterns/general.md:15` requires the *runtime* to expose model-request failures only as terminal finish chunks so "a consumer can name the source of a failure from the public API alone". August's provider layer currently has to guess whether a caught exception came from the provider, a wrapper, or its own assembly; this is a one-rule fix. The same page's `finish.replayState` rule (`docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md:33`) — minimal lossless-JSON native metadata, passed only when the *same adapter instance* owns both the historical and target route — is the safe way to do cross-turn provider state restoration.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Make the tool surface a typed, validated, frozen contract with one canonical JSON value.** `docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md:42` (args validated against the unified `ParameterSchemaSpec` before `execute` runs), `:44` (arguments materialised as detached lossless JSON, frozen before policy, an opaque `exec.token`, and only an around-dispatch wrapper allowed to replace — never remove — `exec.signal`), and `:45` (one canonical JSON value; the registry snapshots, validates and freezes it) mean a model cannot smuggle a mutable or unvalidated argument into a tool. The complementary rule at `:46` — *throwing or returning an invalid value means `isError`* — keeps a successful-but-unhappy outcome (a non-zero exit) a value rather than an exception, which is what lets August's UI and its receipts agree.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Split tool output into model-facing prose and replayable UI state, and make the UI presenters pure.** `docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md:88` ("UI-only formatting stays out of the model result") and `:87` (presenters "must be pure functions of `args` (+ the result) — NO I/O, NO reading session state, NO clock/random", because they run on live streaming *and* on session-log replay) plus the durable `output.presentationMeta(args, value)` channel (`:48`) give a three-way split: canonical value → model, `render` → model prose, `presentationMeta` → replayable card state. August's "one line in the transcript" cards and its persisted `result.meta` would benefit directly.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Bound context by a *policy*, not by a byte count, and give the policy a named headroom and retry ladder.** `docs/config-catalog.md:704-723` specifies `thresholdRatio` 0.8, `headroomTokens` 65536, `retainRatio` 0.16, `compactionRetries` 1, `maxOverflowRetries` 1 (`0` disables), and a separate summarizer provider/model that must be set together or inherit the conversation target, with exact per-model overrides that fail plugin load on duplicates. The separate tool-result pruner (`docs/config-catalog.md:745-752`: 8192 code points threshold, 4096 head, 1024 tail) prunes *before* summarisation. This is a directly portable compaction policy: the two knobs August currently conflates (how much to keep, when to compact) become four independent, per-model-overridable dials.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Detect a stuck loop on the *canonical* call identity, and bound the reminder, not the detection.** `docs/config-catalog.md:2625-2632` states that the repeat-reminder quotes at most 500 characters of canonical arguments, "the cap bounds the reminder, never the detection (the chain key always compares the FULL canonical string)", with thresholds `[3,5,8]` and `*`-wildcard include/exclude predicates that are valid even when they match no registered tool. August's self-heal reminder would otherwise grow unbounded exactly in the case it is meant to catch.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Keep the model's wire extensions *outside* the model-visible prefix, and make their delivery at-least-once with a monotone watermark.** `docs/deepseek-llm-api-wire-extensions.md:7` ("they do not add model-input tokens or alter the model-visible prefix"), `:37` (a contributor that fails to prepare is omitted while the others still ship; a body that fails to serialize sends the base body and *skips acceptance so contributors resend*), and `:154` (the watermark folds the greatest matching `throughSeq` for the current session id **and format generation**, so concurrent accepted requests cannot move the cursor backward) together give a telemetry/metadata side-channel that is free of prompt-cache cost and cannot lose events silently.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Cache the prompt by *reusing a system head* rather than by tuning a flag.** `docs/architecture.md:110` states the mechanism: "The first admitted step reserves the system head before user messages even for an empty prompt (no wire message).
