A "capable" route can therefore *append* a section (append-only prefix growth) while an incapable route must rewrite the head — and the doc says which is which. This is a much sharper statement of prefix stability than "keep the system prompt short".
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Compute conversation nodes incrementally and publish on a cadence, never per chunk.** `docs/defensive-patterns/conversation-and-session.md:128-135` forbids `immediate` publication and full recomputation on the high-frequency delta path, and names the vocabulary `none` / `animation-frame` / `immediate`; the wrong form "puts the whole node collection on the frame budget, and the transcript stalls behind the stream". Combined with "Projection is the only read and compute path" (`:9`) and "Cold reads are the last resort" (`:52`), this is the whole "long chat under streaming does not drop frames" story: one pushed read path, one fold, one cadence.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Hold a Session by explicit reference, and reclaim only on `refCount == 0 && inflight == 0`.** `docs/defensive-patterns/conversation-and-session.md:87` forbids enumerating business state to decide what may be reclaimed, "because that list has to be maintained by every feature that adds one" — an implicit holder makes reclamation unauditable. August's session/chat retention should carry the same explicit retain/release discipline.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Make a "one read path" law explicit: a session-derived value is read through a projection, never fetched by the component.** `docs/defensive-patterns/conversation-and-session.md:9` — "Two answers to the same question — one pulled, one pushed — drift apart, so a render can show a value the Session log no longer supports" — plus the `stateVersion` rule (bump on any fold-semantics change; registering one key twice with different `stateVersion` throws instead of merging) is a complete recipe for August's brain/memory read path.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Give every remote/API failure one class and one code table, and read the caller only from the invocation.** `docs/cookbook/adding-a-remote-api.md:53` ("Do not build a family of domain error classes"), `:57-60` (a code is declared next to its single producer, or in the lowest common domain package; carrier codes are used, never copied) and `docs/defensive-patterns/remote-and-api.md:53` ("access control never checks a resource they omit"; "The caller is read only from `this.ctx.invocation.peer.principal`, never from arguments") together make August's tool/API boundary auditable: every refusal has a code, a code has one owner, and the caller's identity cannot be forged by an argument.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Keep the plugin surface honest: four exports for a function plugin, no fifth.** `docs/defensive-patterns/package-surface.md:9` — "The rule stops a test convenience from freezing into published API" — combined with the ban on mixing the function and default-export forms (the Loader then discards the namespace) and the ban on a module-level store handle as "a disguised singleton across plugin reloads" (`docs/defensive-patterns/client-components.md:236`). For August's own plugin/tool surface this is a cheap, mechanical rule that prevents exactly the "one helper export added for a test" rot.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **State the review judgment condition for every rule, and forbid the self-approved exception.** Every defensive-pattern page carries a "judged by" clause and names *who* approves an exception, and `docs/defensive-patterns/general.md:52` makes it explicit that "a call site that cannot state both behaviors is a review blocker, not a style preference". `docs/defensive-patterns/remote-and-api.md:13` likewise: "Where the business boundary itself is contested, the domain owner settles it as an architecture question before the change lands." This is the difference between a rule and a slogan.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Prove a regression guard fails on the unfixed code before trusting it.** `docs/cookbook/responding-to-pr-review-on-a-stack.md:22` — "for a regression guard, prove it FAILS on the unfixed code (introduce the regression, watch red, revert) — a guard that passes both ways guards nothing", and "a sub-agent's report describes intent, not necessarily what landed". This is the missing half of August's static gates, several of which (by the workspace's own account) have been proven to catch real defects — the same proof discipline applies to them.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Keep bilingual documentation merge-safe with per-section content hashes instead of a translation-memory file.** `docs/i18n/README.md:11-22` — the record is one hash pair per heading section, so "edits to different sections change separate record lines, so Git's default text merge, including GitHub's, composes them", and an out-of-sync pair is repaired by "patching the counterpart minimally against the edited side's diff, never by re-translating whole files". The pairing record is the *reviewable act* of confirming consistency (`:22`), and the gate's limit is stated honestly (`:44`).
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Give the translation pipeline a two-pass, self-reviewing output contract with a machine-readable pending-term channel.** `docs/i18n/translation-prompt.md:153-199` — pass 1 writes the translation, pass 2 re-reads it *in the target language only* (which makes awkward phrasing visible), then compares clause by clause, writes only actual corrections to `<review>`, and emits the corrected whole document in `<final>`; unknown terms must be reported as `[Terminology: pending]` in `<review>` and "must not be silently adopted in `<translation>` or `<final>`" (`:124`). The pending channel is a review queue, not a footnote.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **State the model-facing cost of every capability in a fixed, checkable vocabulary.** `docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md:87-89` — the UI presenters must be pure; UI-only formatting must not ride in the canonical value; and `defineTool` soft-validates the display path so "display must never crash a replay". A renderer that can throw on a malformed replay is a liveness bug in the transcript; making the display path total is the fix.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Express the "one canonical reading" of the product as a feature→mechanism table so the microkernel claim becomes checkable.** `docs/cookbook/extension-cookbook.md:104-132` maps every product feature to a listener on a documented extension point — compaction, plan mode, MCP, skills, memory, scheduled tasks, sub-agents, the goal round driver, ToolSearch, and the monotonic terminal-turn policy — and the page's own framing is "Every product feature maps to a listener on a documented extension point — the microkernel claim made checkable". The table doubles as the architectural test: if a feature has no row, it either modified the loop or has no mechanism.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#1]** - **Give every "how do I add X" the same shape: a numbered checklist, an exact verify command, and a named template package.** `docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md:5` ("This checklist is validated against the bash and adapter packages as templates; if it drifts from them, fix it here") and `:161-168` (the verify block) — the *template package* is the drift oracle, which is a cheaper and more durable form of "keep the docs in sync" than a prose review.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A guard that cannot fail the regression is not a guard — prove it fails.** `docs/testing.md:40` — the rule is "A guard only guards if the regression fails it", and the prescription is concrete: for a plugin without `inject`, add `expect('default' in mod).toBe(false)` plus an `unwrapExports` round-trip, then *introduce the regression, watch red, revert*. This is the single most transferable practice in the shard for August: every static gate should have a documented, executed "red" proof, otherwise it is decoration.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **An "empty catalog" is a distinct, quiet answer — reserve it for "not configured yet", never for "misconfigured".** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/deepseek-model-discovery/guide.md:12` and `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.2/pi-ai-model-discovery/guide.md:12` — a route whose credential is missing returns an empty model list (hiding the group) while a *malformed* credential still fails discovery loudly, and a saved selection absent from the catalog shows "Select model" **without rewriting the stored value**. August's provider/model picker should adopt the same three-way split: absent → empty + quiet, wrong → error, temporarily unavailable → keep the stored selection.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **The "shadow price" protocol: price a replacement in the event immediately before it, so a consumer can subtract cost without retaining per-node prices.** `docs/persistence-catalog.zh.md:391-399` — a surface `replace` event is priced by the metering event directly before it (`compaction/summary` for a summarizing compaction, `compaction/prune` for a prune), and the replacement MUST be appended synchronously right after. August's compaction path could use the same trick: emit the shadowed range's token count once, adjacent to the replacement, and every consumer can compute "tokens freed" without keeping a per-message ledger.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **An unrecognized event type defaults to REQUIRED, not ignorable — over-refuse rather than resume a gutted session.** `docs/persistence-catalog.zh.md:149-156` — the `ignorable?: true` marker is opt-in; a reader meeting an unknown type without it MUST refuse to reconstruct the session. The stated reason is asymmetric cost: "defaulting to required means a forgotten marker over-refuses (an inconvenience) rather than silently resuming a gutted session." This is the right default for any append-only log August persists.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Tool schemas that teach a stable argument order are doing prompt-prefix stabilisation.** `docs/tool-catalog.md:654` (bash: "Provide `description` before `command`"), `docs/tool-catalog.md:1096` (write: "Provide `file_path` before `content`"), `docs/tool-catalog.md:1011` (edit: "Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string`") — the argument order is pinned so the serialized tool-call prefix stays byte-stable, which is exactly what a provider's prefix cache needs. Cheap, and invisible until you notice it.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A structured failure owned by a lower seam must survive the adapter above it.** `docs/postmortem/0004-landlock-partial-notice-misclassified-child-failures.md:54` — the bash-backed search caught every rejected run and replaced a structured `SandboxUnavailableError` with a generic `SEARCH_FAILED`; the fix moved ripgrep to a packaged binary through `ctx.subprocess`, outside the sandboxed bash seam. August should mark its error classes as *owned by the layer that raises them* and make the layer above re-raise rather than translate.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Attribution needs a CONJUNCTION of evidence; a shared prefix is not a protocol.** `docs/postmortem/0004-landlock-partial-notice-misclassified-child-failures.md:52` — the fix was a rule type carrying allowed exit codes, per-line fatal signatures and *exact* informational-line exclusions, not a longer string match. The same shape applies to August's marker tables: the pattern in your own AGENTS.md about a "400 marker" and the receipt vocabulary is the identical failure class.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Acceptance must name the exact origin and observe the world externally — HTTP 200, a successful build and a boot manifest are three different facts.** `docs/postmortem/0003-web-agent-gui-feedback-loop.md:51` — the Web agent declared success on a bare-Vite HTTP 200 while the browser showed a white screen, then validated a *replacement* server while the original page had already picked up the rebuilt artifacts. August's own rule ("verify production refresh and development HMR against external state") is the same idea; the postmortem shows the failure mode concretely and, valuably, cites exact session-log sequence numbers as the evidence trail.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A snapshot refresh is fixture production, not correctness review.** `docs/postmortem/0002-js-expression-disabled-filesystem-tools.md:46` — the filesystem scenarios passed because the refresh rewrote the expected stdout and session logs before any semantic assertion rejected the missing tools, and the shared header pin never proved *their* tools were registered. The shipped guards are semantic, not textual: reject `UNKNOWN_TOOL` results in fresh runs and committed fixtures. August's snapshot/eval pipeline needs the same "semantic assertion independent of the expected output" rule, or a refresh will happily certify a regression.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Do not ration real-API tests; a keyless test proves plumbing only.** `docs/testing.md:25` — "We are DeepSeek — do not ration real-API tests… Highest-value are smoke tests that boot a shipped `dsh` profile, send one prompt, and check the world — they catch the 'green unit tests, broken product' class that mocks cannot." And self-skip is explicitly "not a cost signal", so a missing key is not a licence to let the suite go quiet.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Prefer the real implementation; mock only the expensive or nondeterministic boundary.** `docs/testing.md:29` — "A hand-rolled stand-in proves the bridge moves bytes, not that the shipping tool behaves as asserted", and the concrete pattern is `makeBridgeHarness()`: the real loop, session store, tool registry and JSONL persistence behind a scripted `MockAdapter` as the *only* mock. August's bridge and tool tests should adopt exactly this seam.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Verify the world, not the self-report.** `docs/testing.md:33-35` — "an e2e assertion re-runs the command or re-reads the file externally; a keyword probe on the agent's own output lets a cheating agent pass", plus "Assert untouched files are byte-identical" and resource ownership in `afterEach` even on failure/retry/timeout.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A delegation id must be unique across the whole runtime, not per parent.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/subagent-activations/guide.md:55` — "each returned `SubagentRun.id` must be unique across parents, providers, and local Sessions in the runtime. Generate a fresh id for each execution instead of using a parent-local counter." A per-parent counter is unique only within the parent and collides in any runtime-wide `list_agents` view; a uuid suffix (as the job registry now uses, `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/job-id-identity/guide.md:12`) is the cheap fix.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Cancellation ownership transfers from the signal to the receipt.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/subagent-activations/guide.md:51` — "The startup signal stops owning cancellation after publication: retain the receipt and call `dispose()` to cancel that exact activation." Cleanup failures are reported by `dispose()` *separately* from the captured result, so a failed cleanup never rewrites the answer, and `stopReason` must be inspected before treating a result as success.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A send is not a delivery and not a completion — say what the acknowledgement does not mean.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/team-direct-inbox/guide.md:12` — `send_message` returns `{ "sent": true }` and the guide spells out the three things it does *not* mean: model processing, a synchronous storage flush, and resend de-duplication. August's inter-agent messaging should return an equally minimal receipt *and* document its limits.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Refuse a wildcard bind at load, and assert trust per authority rather than per address.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/web-listener-trust-config/guide.md:14` — `0.0.0.0` and `::` are rejected because "binding every interface exposes the port to the network"; the bind IP itself is accepted with no `--trusted-host` entry, while a proxy or DNS authority still needs one.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **One policy, one enforcement point — do not add a per-runtime sandbox setting.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/python-ptc-sandbox/guide.md:19` — "Do not add a separate Python-only sandbox setting", and `sandbox-unavailable` must be inspected *separately* from a denied file operation because they need different repairs. August's code-mode / tool-execution paths should share the one resolved policy.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Context providers are re-evaluated at request admission, and the refresh must not re-open the prompt.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/working-directory/guide.md:25` — dynamic context providers are evaluated again at request admission, after pre-step listeners and route preparation; the admission refresh replaces a provider's cached text while *preserving* assembly-only context and the accepted system prompt, tool schemas and variables. This is the mechanism that keeps a live context (working directory, memory tail, clock) correct without a per-step full rebuild.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Make the hidden runtime facts model-visible, not tribal knowledge.** `docs/postmortem/0003-web-agent-gui-feedback-loop.md:42` — the Web launcher publishes the canonical loopback URL in the logged `app:web-surface` prompt section and in the managed `$DSH_WEB_URL` environment variable. August's equivalent (the current URL, the runtime mode, whether the watcher is actually running) is exactly the same class of hidden prerequisite, and the postmortem shows the cost of leaving it hidden.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A generated catalog that boots the real thing, plus a completeness guard, is worth more than a hand-written one.** `docs/tool-catalog.md:8` — the generator boots each tool plugin on a real context and reads `ctx.tools.schemas()` (because a schema is not statically knowable), and a guard globs `packages/*/tool-*` and fails if any package is missing from the boot manifest, "so a new tool cannot be silently undocumented". The same shape applies to August's tool registry and its own prompt assembly.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Fingerprint the persisted types so a schema change is visible without reading the diff.** `docs/persistence-catalog.zh.md:18` — a normalized graph is hashed per type; comments, source locations, aliases, erased brand marks and readonly markers do not move the digest, while tuple order, property names, value types and optionality do. August can use the same canonicalization to make "did this change the wire format?" a one-line answer.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A tool-presentation mode is per preset, and the mixed mode is rejected rather than deprecated.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/tool-presentation-mode/guide.md:14` — `native` (direct function calls) or `ptc` (a `run_code` program calling a generated SDK), and different agent presets in the same application may use different modes. The parallel execution contract is spelled out at `docs/tool-catalog.md:23`: submission-ordered starts and policy, concurrency-safe bodies overlapping up to `maxParallelSubCalls`, each nested execution re-entering the complete guarded pipeline and linked to its outer result.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A parallel workflow must degrade per item, but fail loudly on misuse.** `docs/tool-catalog.md:2672-2677` — `pipeline` runs each item through the stages independently with no barrier (a stage throw drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages), `parallel` awaits all thunks (a throwing thunk resolves to `null`), and *misused hooks* (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The split between "an item failed" and "you used the API wrong" is the part worth copying.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Do not poll; the runtime tells you when a child finishes.** `docs/tool-catalog.md:2150` ("You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status") and `docs/tool-catalog.md:2543` ("Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling") — August's delegation surface already says this in its own tool descriptions, and the catalog shows the convention is applied consistently across both the subagent and the team-leader tool families.
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **A stored credential must beat an exported variable, and the check must not print the value.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.2/stored-credentials-precedence/guide.md:12-14` — the stored `refs` entry now wins, the Models page can save a key while the name is exported, and the verification step is "Check names and presence without printing credential values".
- **[dsh-docs-rest#2]** - **Compatibility has one authority, and a malformed manifest fails closed.** `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.3/plugin-engines-dsh/guide.md:12` — a package's own `engines.dsh` range decides alone; the peer rule is only the fallback; a non-object `engines` makes the manifest unreadable and the package is **refused**; the refusal record's key is renamed `peers` → `requirements` because the constraint's *name* and its *source* are now decoupled. The "fail closed on an unreadable manifest" half is the part August's own plugin/marketplace loader should copy. ---
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 1. **A tool guard that can only reduce permission, never grant it** — `docs/subsystems/tools.md:325` (and the pipeline at `tools.md:182`). `ToolGuard` returns `string | undefined`: `undefined` preserves the waterfall decision, a string denies. The doc states the reason outright — "Because guards have no allow result, listener ordering cannot turn a denial back into permission." *Why it transfers to August*: August's August-proxy harness gates every tool call through policy code that a model can sometimes influence. Making the guard type incapable of returning "allow" removes a whole class of ordering bug (a later listener re-granting what an earlier one denied) without needing a priority system or a second registry.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 2. **Make the model request a pure function of the durable log, and keep the system prompt OUT of the request header** — `docs/subsystems/llm-streaming.md:761` and `docs/subsystems/session.md:183`. The rendered prompt is derived history — surface node 0, plus any later in-history system node — so "a prompt change replaces or appends a system node and leaves the header unchanged". *Why it transfers*: this is exactly the prefix-stability property August needs from a provider that caches on a literal prefix. If the system prompt is a request *field*, every prompt edit invalidates the whole cached prefix; if it is a message slot, only the tail changes. August's frozen-boot-memory-index rule ("the boot memory index is frozen per session to protect the provider prefix cache") is a special case of this generalisation, and the in-history append rule (`llm-streaming.md:544`) is the general form.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 3. **Disjoint token accounting, with the provider's folded total subtracted back out** — `docs/subsystems/llm-streaming.md:336`. `inputTokens` is uncached input only; cache reads and writes are reported separately; billed input is the sum of the three; adapters whose provider folds cache hits into one number (DeepSeek's `prompt_tokens`) subtract them out. *Why it transfers*: August bills per model and shows a per-turn cache chip. A single "prompt tokens" number cannot distinguish a cheap cached turn from an expensive fresh one, and once the two are conflated no cache-hit-rate metric can be computed from the provider's own report.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 4. **Canonical error codes for the two failures that must never be misrouted** — `docs/subsystems/llm-streaming.md:303-304`: context overflow has ONE canonical code surfaced whether the failure arrives as a thrown HTTP error or an in-band finish, and "an empty completion is a retryable error, not a silent success" (`EMPTY_RESPONSE`). *Why it transfers*: August has exactly the bug class where a provider's 400 arrives in two shapes and one branch handles only the thrown form, so a context-overflow gets retried as a generic error until the transcript dies. One canonical code, produced at the final adapter boundary, means every downstream consumer (retry policy, compaction trigger, budget ladder) can route on the code instead of parsing text — the same discipline August already needed for `classify_error`.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 5. **One keep/drop decision covers content and its metadata together** — `docs/subsystems/llm-streaming.md:368`. A `max-tokens` finish drops every tool call (a truncated call is unsafe to execute), and the *same* decision prunes the replay envelope's per-block entry at each dropped position, so `blocks()` and `replayState` cannot disagree. *Why it transfers*: August persists both the assistant text and provider-private replay state. If a truncation path drops a block from one and not the other, a later request replays metadata describing content that is no longer there — the classic "history looks fine until you resend it" bug.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 6. **Keep the assistant's interrupted prefix, but omit its undispatched tool calls** — `docs/subsystems/session.md:82-85` and `llm-streaming.md:398-402`. A turn cancelled mid-stream finalises its delivered text/reasoning as `assistant/message` with `interrupted: true`; `interruptedBlocks()` omits tool calls "because interruption precedes dispatch; retaining one would require a fabricated result". *Why it transfers*: August's stop/cancel paths currently risk either losing the user's partial answer or emitting a `tool_call` with no matching `tool_result` — which is precisely the "orphaned `tool_use_id` surviving into persisted history bricked the chat" failure the August notes describe. The rule "never persist a tool call without its result" is a one-line invariant this design makes structural.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 7. **The compaction lock is released LAST, so a crash is a detectable orphan** — `docs/subsystems/compaction.md:19`. `compaction/start` is appended first and `compaction/end` only after the summary and the surface replacement have landed. *Why it transfers*: this inverts the usual bracket (open … close) which a crash leaves looking *open*. Releasing last means a crash mid-compaction leaves a `start` with no `end` — an unambiguous "incomplete" marker — rather than an `end` that falsely claims compaction finished. August's own context-relief paths would benefit from the same bracket discipline, and the same shape generalises to any long-running durable operation.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 8. **A compaction's shadowed range is a POSITION span, not a numeric seq interval** — `docs/subsystems/compaction.md:60-66`. After a prior replace lands a fresh high-seq summary node at an older range's position, `start` can be *greater* than `end`. The authoritative set is `shadowedSeqs`. *Why it transfers*: any August feature that replaces a range of history (context relief, turn folding, a "summarize this turn" tool) will hit the same inversion, and code that assumes `start <= end` will silently truncate or double-count. The doc's fix — carry the explicit ordered seq list and treat the numeric pair as advisory — is cheap to adopt.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 9. **Subagent settlement is a DIFFERENT message kind from a subagent-authored message** — `docs/subsystems/subagent.md:190-196`. `AgentMessageSource` is content the sender chose; `SubagentSettledMessageSource` is "the manager stating what became of the child". The stated reason: "a transcript that merged them would credit the child with words it never wrote." *Why it transfers*: August's agent-team/room transcripts collapse bot turns. Merging a machine-authored settlement into the same source as a model-authored relay would let a reader attribute a summary to the child that produced it — which is exactly the mis-attribution August's `BOT_TURN_PREFIX` machinery works to prevent on the inbound side.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 10. **The subagent stop-reason vocabulary mirrors the turn-end vocabulary** — `docs/subsystems/subagent.md:268-287`. The known cases (`completed`, `aborted`, `error`, `max-tokens`, `refusal`) mirror the harness's own turn-end reasons "so the tool layer can map a non-`completed` result to an `isError` tool result". *Why it transfers*: August's delegation tools currently need a translation table between "the child failed" and "the parent's tool result is an error". Sharing one closed vocabulary removes the table and makes every parent-side policy (retry, budget, escalation) work unchanged on a child result.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 11. **A provider's `available()` must be a cheap LOCAL check and must not make network calls** — `docs/subsystems/web.md:123`, with the selection rule at `web.md:125`: an explicit provider id, or auto-select when exactly one usable provider is registered; multiple usable providers with no configured id is `WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS`, "not first-wins". *Why it transfers*: August has several providers (LLM, web, browser, computer-use) and "first registered wins" makes behaviour depend on plugin load order, which changes on HMR. Making ambiguity a loud error plus a local-only health check means a provider's health is never a network round-trip inside a selection loop.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 12. **Check runner failure BEFORE denial, and keep the denial dialect per-backend** — `docs/subsystems/sandbox.md:134-148`. A consumer must match only *this* backend's stderr substrings ("the union claims denials a given backend never produces"), and must first establish that the runner failed (command never ran) rather than that confinement denied it (command ran and was blocked). *Why it transfers*: August's sandbox/ACL layers sit on Windows, macOS and Linux with different denial texts. A cross-platform union produces false "policy denied" reports for ordinary command failures — which then get logged as policy violations and make the real denial invisible.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 13. **A capability that cannot enforce a deadline should not accept one** — `docs/subsystems/filesystem.md:274`. File IO takes no `timeoutMs` and arms no deadline, "because a timeout could not force an in-progress `fsync`/`rename` to stop, so a `timeoutMs` here would be a deadline the seam cannot enforce, and an implicit default in the exact place explicit-over-implicit forbids". Contrast with bash and the subprocess-backed glob/grep, which *do* take a `timeoutMs` because a deadline can really kill the work. *Why it transfers*: August's file tools and shell tools share a tool schema builder. Applying the same "timeout only where the substrate can honour it" rule stops August from advertising a timeout it cannot enforce — a promise that silently fails exactly when it matters.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 14. **An intent changes presentation only, never the protocol** — `docs/subsystems/user-questions.md:26-34`, and the same rule at `permission-presets.md:55` (a derived `custom` value may be displayed but is "never a switch target or an event payload"). *Why it transfers*: August's UI keeps growing rich variants of the same interaction (plan review, permission selection, a timed ask). Encoding the variant as a *tag* on the same payload, so every consumer that ignores the tag still sends the identical answer, means a new UI variant can be added without a coordinated protocol change on every backend.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 15. **A "pending" answer is a first-class state, not an empty answer** — `docs/subsystems/user-questions.md:132`. `TimedUserQuestionResult` is `{pending: true, callId}`, and the doc is explicit: "Pending means the question is still answerable; it is not an empty answer, a refusal, a confirmation, or permission." The timeout aborts the foreground waterfall's *private* signal and returns pending **without cancelling the Turn**. *Why it transfers*: August has timed interactions and unattended runs. Collapsing "timed out" into `null`/empty makes the model read it as a refusal, which then changes the plan; a distinct pending state that keeps the question answerable (and keeps the turn alive) is the difference between a slow answer and a wrong answer.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 16. **Approval policy `never` is enforced inside the service, before the answerer waterfall** — `docs/subsystems/approval.md:86`. "The `never` policy is enforced inside the service before waterfall dispatch, so even an answerer registered later with `prepend` cannot bypass it." *Why it transfers*: August has several approval-ish paths (permission presets, sandbox escalation, one-shot wider retries). Any policy that is only enforced by the *dispatch order* of listeners is one `prepend` away from being bypassed. Enforcing the deny at the service boundary makes the policy unbypassable by construction — the same "monotonic" instinct as the tool guard in idea 1.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 17. **The approval request omits the tool arguments on purpose** — `docs/subsystems/approval.md:53`. "`callId` links to an already-presented tool call, so arguments are not duplicated here." *Why it transfers*: August's approval UI is rendered next to a streamed tool call. Re-sending the arguments in the approval payload creates a second copy that can drift from what was actually executed — the approver sees one thing and the harness runs another. Carrying only a correlation id removes the drift by construction.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 18. **A durable version token is equality-only and replaced by every material mutation** — `docs/subsystems/feedback.md:32-33` and `docs/subsystems/goal.md:9`. *Why it transfers*: August's brain rows and settings writes have optimistic-concurrency fields whose semantics are often unclear ("version" as a number to increment vs. a token to compare). One rule — equality-only token, replaced wholesale on any material change — makes stale-write detection mechanical and makes replay trivial.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 19. **A projection unit must return the SAME state reference when it is uninterested in an event** — `docs/subsystems/session-projection.md:38-44`. "an unchanged reference (`Object.is`) produces zero downstream work." *Why it transfers*: August folds session events into derived views (todos, goals, budget counters, projections) on every append. Returning a fresh object each time turns every event into a full re-render and a full re-serialisation. The `Object.is` contract plus a `stateVersion` invalidation counter (`session-projection.md:60-66`) is a two-line mechanism that makes derived state cheap *and* safely cacheable.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 20. **The write order is: durability → memory → notification** — `docs/subsystems/storage.md:126` and `docs/subsystems/storage.md:153`. A rejected backend write leaves memory untouched "so reads never diverge from the medium"; the `domain/changed` event is a notification, not a transaction participant, so a throwing listener is contained with a warning rather than rejecting the already-durable write. *Why it transfers*: August's own notes call out this exact hazard class (a durable write that later fails in a listener looks like a failure and gets retried, duplicating the write). Ordering the three steps explicitly and saying which of them may fail is the mechanism.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 21. **A contract with no rules of its own exports exactly what it captured** — `docs/subsystems/session-telemetry.md:144`: "The seam ships NO rules of its own: with no listener mounted, records reach the backend exactly as captured, so exported data is precisely as clean as the rules a deployment mounts." *Why it transfers*: August's telemetry/redaction story currently lives in one implementation. Making the *seam* rule-free and pushing redaction into a waterfall means the default behaviour is "everything, unmodified", which is honest, and a deployment that mounts no rules gets a visible, intentional posture rather than an accidental one.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 22. **The host decides a unique business id before the UI writes any code** — `docs/subsystems/conversation.md:58`. "the client must never assign an update to 'the latest unfinished' Context." The same file then makes the claim order-independent by evaluating every match before accepting any (`conversation.md:250`), keeps update-only contexts *pending* until their start arrives (`conversation.md:70`), and states a hard performance budget: with `D` definitions one event costs `D` matches and a constant-time lookup, and "Definition code must preserve that property" (`conversation.md:284`). *Why it transfers*: August's chat timeline renders tool calls, subagent activity, todos and compaction notices from the same log. Adopting "the producer owns the id" plus "all matches are evaluated before any claim" removes the class of bugs where one row's update lands on another's card.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 23. **Distinguish "the runner never ran" from "confinement blocked it"** — `docs/subsystems/shell.md:111-133` (orthogonal outcome fields) and `docs/subsystems/shell.md:121` (timedOut vs aborted are mutually exclusive first-cause fields). A process can both time out AND exit 0 because it trapped the signal; `timedOut` and `aborted` are exclusive because one fused deadline drives both and a race reports the single first-abort cause. *Why it transfers*: August's process tools and its turn budget both need to distinguish "the model ran out of wall clock" from "the user pressed stop" from "the provider gave up". One field per cause, never a bitmask, and the first-cause rule, makes the receipt honest.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 24. **A producer's `done` resolves after resources are released, not when work finishes** — `docs/subsystems/jobs.md:163-166`, with `producerReported` explicitly *not* certifying resource release (`jobs.md:60-61`). *Why it transfers*: August runs background work whose output the model reads later. A job that reports "done" while its subprocess is still alive produces a receipt the model trusts and a process that outlives the turn. Making the release part of the completion contract (and making the flag's limits explicit) fixes both.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 25. **A missing settlement stays missing** — `docs/subsystems/jobs.md:31`: "A missing `job/settled` remains incomplete even if the live registry reported termination; consumers must not invent a finish timestamp." *Why it transfers*: August's August-proxy sidecar kills sessions and processes on shutdown; a consumer that synthesises a completion from an in-memory view will report work as finished that never reached storage. Naming the asymmetry explicitly in the contract prevents the reader from "fixing" it later.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 26. **The next-occurrence rule must not depend on ambient time-zone state** — `docs/subsystems/schedule.md:121`: "Successful creation stores only canonical UTC `scheduledAt`, so replay never depends on ambient time-zone state." Combined with the cron canonicalisation that preserves each field's *star flag* so day-of-month/day-of-week stays Vixie-faithful (`schedule.md:165-169`), and DST gap/overlap rules stated once (`schedule.md:138`). *Why it transfers*: August's reminder/schedule feature (and any "run this at 9am" intent) inherits the same three problems — DST, replay, and cron semantics. Storing only a canonical instant and keeping the *rule* separately normalised is the pattern that survives a restart.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 27. **The tool surface is built by an explicit allowlist, not by omission** — `docs/subsystems/tools.md:11`: `schemas()` builds the model-facing `ToolSchema[]` from an allowlist, and "output/execute/projectContent/finalizeContent/timeoutMs/isConcurrencySafe/presentCall/presentResult must never leak into a model request". *Why it transfers*: August's tool definitions carry host-only fields (timeouts, concurrency classifiers, presentation callbacks, private paths). An allowlist means a new host-only field is *never* exposed by accident; a denylist means it is exposed until someone notices.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 28. **Tool arguments cannot be rewritten by policy** — `docs/subsystems/tools.md:428`: "Arguments cannot be rewritten because history, audit, UI, and execution must agree." The `PreToolDecision` union has no rewrite arm at all, so the compiler prevents it. *Why it transfers*: August's August-proxy has a pre-tool hook surface. If a policy can rewrite arguments, the logged call, the UI card, the audit row and what actually executes can be four different things. Encoding the ban in the *type* rather than in a comment is the transferable part.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 29. **Presentation callbacks must be pure and side-effect-free because they run during live streaming AND during replay** — `docs/subsystems/tools.md:88-93`. `presentCall`/`presentResult` "must depend only on `args`". *Why it transfers*: August renders tool cards from a live stream *and* re-renders the same card from the persisted log on reload. A presenter that touches mutable state produces a card that changes between the two renders — the "reloaded transcript looks different" bug.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 30. **Cross-session coordinates keep their original generation** — `docs/subsystems/session-reference.md:73`: "Their durable source records keep `capturedThroughSeq` as a coordinate in the referenced Session's original generation; they never reinterpret it as a seq in the containing Session." *Why it transfers*: August's "recall from another session" feature (and any context handoff between agents) will compact the source session; if the seq is reinterpreted in the destination's numbering, the pointer silently points at the wrong message. Carrying the format version alongside the seq (`capturedFormatVersion`) is the other half of the fix.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 31. **A request's tool list is an allowlisted projection and a failed refresh keeps the previous generation** — `docs/subsystems/mcp.md:54` ("A failed refresh retains the previous tool generation") and `docs/subsystems/tools.md:11`. *Why it transfers*: August's tool registry is refreshed at runtime (dynamic plugins, per-scope restrictions). Retaining the last good generation on a refresh failure means a transient error never leaves the model with an empty tool list — which it would read as "no tools available" and answer accordingly.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 32. **A deterministic request version, cached and singleflighted** — `docs/subsystems/attachment.md:170`. `readImageRequest()` derives and caches one deterministic request version at a route-chosen target; the local implementation "lazily encodes preferred candidates, singleflights equal request identities, lets each waiter cancel independently, stops shared work when no waiter remains, and bounds all transforms with its instance-level limiter, which defaults to two simultaneous transformations". *Why it transfers*: August's image/attachment path has the same shape (encode, resize, upload) and the same three failure modes (duplicate work, one cancelled waiter killing the shared job, unbounded parallel encodes). The singleflight-with-independent-waiters pattern plus a concurrency limiter is directly reusable.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 33. **A capability seam splits into Definition / Provider / Consumer, and the Consumer owns the model-facing surface** — `docs/subsystems/web.md:11`, `docs/subsystems/mcp.md:41`, `docs/subsystems/subprocess.md:5`. Providers register *capabilities*; the model-facing names, schemas, prompt guidance and presentation live in one consumer. *Why it transfers*: August's provider surface (LLM adapters, web providers, browser providers) currently leaks provider names into tool schemas. Centralising the model-facing vocabulary in one consumer package means a provider swap changes nothing the model sees — and August already relies on this for its `/v1` adapters.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 34. **A closed union of event types with a plugin extension path that does NOT use `assertNever`** — `docs/subsystems/session.md:292`: "Because `SessionEventMap` is merge-extensible, switches over `SessionEvent` must NOT use `assertNever` — a plugin-added variant is a valid unknown value; handle the known cases and fall through `default`." Contrast with the *closed* `StreamChunk` union, which does end in `assertNever` so adding a variant breaks every consumer (`docs/subsystems/llm-streaming.md:169`). *Why it transfers*: August needs to know which unions are safe to extend. The doc makes the distinction explicit and gives the rule for each — extendable maps fall through, closed unions break at compile time. That is a vocabulary August can adopt verbatim.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 35. **A reader that meets an unrecognized event must REFUSE to reconstruct rather than silently drop it** — `docs/subsystems/session.md:274-282`. The `ignorable?: true` marker is opt-in and defaults to required, "because an unrecognized required event may change how the rest of the log is interpreted … defaulting to required means a forgotten marker over-refuses (an inconvenience) rather than silently resuming a gutted session." *Why it transfers*: August's persisted session format will accumulate event types from plugins. A silent skip turns "one unknown event" into "the transcript is subtly wrong and nobody knows why". The asymmetry — over-refuse rather than under-refuse — is the transferable decision.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 36. **A crash mid-turn is repaired by the READER, not by truncating the log** — `docs/subsystems/persistence.md:110`. Persistence returns the physically valid contiguous log; repair computes `interruptedTurnClosers` (missing tool errors, an open `step/end`, and a synthetic `turn/end {reason:{kind:'interrupted'}}`) and appends them through the same write handle. The reason given: "a single turn can be huge in a long-horizon task … and those events were durably appended before the crash." *Why it transfers*: August's crash recovery currently risks either dropping the whole turn (losing the model's work) or leaving a dangling tool call (poisoning the next request). The "append closers, keep the events" rule gives both safety and preservation.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 37. **The format refusal is a distinct error from corruption** — `docs/subsystems/persistence.md:189`. `SessionFormatUnsupportedError` is separate from `SessionPersistenceCorruptionError` "because nothing is damaged". A future highest generation refuses even when an older readable generation remains, and the message names the raw log path so a user can find what a build refused to interpret. *Why it transfers*: August upgrades its session format. Conflating "too new for this build" with "corrupt" leads to the wrong remediation — a user deleting a perfectly good log because the app said "corrupt".
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 38. **Durable metadata whose runtime-only version would silently reset a budget** — `docs/subsystems/persistence.md:171-183`. `delegationDepth` is persisted "so a recursion budget survives restart and resume — a runtime-only depth would reset a resumed child to top-level"; `agentPreset` is durable "because a resume that restored a different composition would replay history the model can no longer act on". *Why it transfers*: August has delegation-depth and agent-preset concepts of exactly this shape, and the failure mode (a restarted child silently becoming a root) is invisible until a runaway happens.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 39. **A listing read must not become a body scan** — `docs/subsystems/persistence.md:325`: "Session listing does not use either field to open cold logs: it reads headers plus identity-checked projection-cache hints only, so a cache or Session-format upgrade never turns startup into a body scan." Plus the lightweight revision token that lets a derived read model compare a cheap opaque value before loading a full log (`persistence.md:294-296`). *Why it transfers*: August's session list is on the hot path of every UI start. A format or cache change that turns listing into a full log read is a startup regression that only shows up with a large corpus.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 40. **A hard rule that a component never receives the framework context** — `docs/subsystems/slots.md:79`: "Components never receive `ctx`." Owner point-in-time values arrive through the owner argument, shared state through a declared store, services stay in the `apply` closure and are projected into callbacks. *Why it transfers*: August's React layer already fights this. Declaring it as a typed boundary (owner props vs `inject` vs `store`) is what makes a slot registry possible at all.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 41. **The web server refuses to bind every interface at once, and the TLS pair is read once** — `docs/subsystems/web-server.md:42-43` and `:51-54`. The unspecified address is rejected at load; an unreadable/empty/mismatched TLS pair rejects initialization "rather than falling back to HTTP". *Why it transfers*: August ships a local server. A silent fallback from HTTPS to plain HTTP on a bad certificate is a security-relevant downgrade that most code does not guard.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 42. **A teardown must force-close connections a handler is holding open** — `docs/subsystems/web-server.md:86`: disposal pairs `close()` with `closeAllConnections()` "because a handler may hold its response open (SSE) and such connections never end on their own; without the force-close, teardown would hang." *Why it transfers*: August's server has SSE/streaming routes. A shutdown that waits for them hangs forever, which looks like a stuck app rather than a missing force-close.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 43. **A revision derived from `mtime`/`ctime`/`size` instead of hashing content** — `docs/subsystems/client-modules.md:88`: revisions come from file metadata "without hashing executable bytes", and "the same artifacts retain their revisions across Host restarts". *Why it transfers*: August rebuilds client bundles constantly. Hashing every bundle on every change is O(bytes); metadata is O(1) and — because ctime catches writes that preserve mtime — still correct.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 44. **A protocol's identifier grammar is portable across languages, and the reserved set is global** — `docs/subsystems/ptc-runtime.md:141-152`: binding globals must match a language-portable identifier subset "so the same namespace list works against every backend regardless of `language` — a JS-only spelling like `$tools` is rejected by design, not just by the Python backend". Backend-owned slots (`console`, `__dsh_main__`) are reserved *everywhere*. *Why it transfers*: August's code-mode / PTC-style tool namespaces have the same portability requirement, and the same trap: a name that is legal in one runtime silently breaks another.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 45. **The provider's own knowledge is the better answer than a network call** — `docs/subsystems/llm-streaming.md:722-726`: a route whose adapter already knows its models "answers from that knowledge instead of asking the endpoint — the adapter's own registry is the better answer, and it costs no network call." *Why it transfers*: August's model picker lists models per provider. Fetching the list from the endpoint on every open is slow, rate-limited, and pointless when the adapter ships the list.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 46. **A UI that does not recognise a new variant still answers correctly** — `docs/subsystems/web.md:106-119` (the closed `WebFetchBody` union with `assertNever` so adding a kind breaks every consumer until handled) and `docs/subsystems/llm-streaming.md:169` (the closed `StreamChunk` union). *Why it transfers*: August's tool-result rendering has a growing set of result shapes. Making the union closed means a new shape is a compile error at every consumer that must handle it, rather than a runtime "unknown" fallback that silently drops content.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 47. **A cancellation that arrives mid-flight is classified by its FIRST cause** — `docs/subsystems/shell.md:121-133`. One fused deadline drives both the timeout and the caller's cancellation, so a timeout and an abort racing before process close report the single first-abort cause, not both. *Why it transfers*: August has several competing deadlines (tool timeout, turn budget, user cancel). Reporting both causes produces receipts that contradict each other ("timed out" and "cancelled") and make the right remediation undecidable.
- **[dsh-docs-subsystems]** 48. **The transcript is derived, so a replacement shadows a range and the derivation re-folds** — `docs/subsystems/session.md:317-336` (`SurfaceOp` = `append` | `{op:'replace', startSeq, endSeq}`) and `docs/subsystems/session.md:340-360` (`SurfaceIntent` requires `sourceEventSeqs` to cite every shadowed node). The derived-history fold "is the single source of derived history: every message-producing append records its `surfaceOp`, so a raw event with no marker (a chunk, a turn boundary) is correctly absent". *Why it transfers*: August's history compaction and turn-folding need exactly this — one append-only log, one derivation rule, and a replacement that names what it shadows so replay can be audited. ---
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **A budget clock that counts only the hook's OWN running time, and pauses inside nested calls** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/chain.ts:50-131` (class `BudgetClock`) — the clock arms on `start()`, pauses on `pause()` (called while awaiting `next` and while awaiting any `$` call) and resumes on `resume()`. Why it matters for August: August's `MAX_MANAGED_TOOL_ROUNDS` counts *rounds*, so a single slow tool (a 3-minute `run_command`) and a fast one cost the same, and the harness has no way to say "this hook, not this tool, is the problem". A budget that excludes awaited work is the only kind that can distinguish "the model is thinking" from "the model is stuck". Transfer it as a per-tool-call or per-turn *own-time* budget alongside the round cap.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **"One run beneath per hook" + "the result from beneath stands when the hook had already called `next`"** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/chain.ts:222-224` and `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/chain.ts:284` — the second `next(e)` returns the *same promise*; if the hook fails after `next` resolved, the result from beneath is returned, not an error. Why it matters: August's `tools/execute` waterfall has the same double-execution hazard (a plugin that wraps `next` and also catches its error can re-run the tool). This is a five-line rule that makes wrapping safe, and it is testable in isolation (`tests/chain.spec.ts:133-159`).
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Refuse an argument rewrite that has already been logged, and name the deferred mechanism** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/index.ts:400-408` — `validateNext` compares the arguments the hook passes down with `JSON.stringify` of the *logged* ones and throws `RewriteRefusedError("rewrote the arguments of <tool>; argument rewrites need the pre-tool input rewrite mechanism (...)")`; a rerouted tool gets its own message. Why it matters: August already has a "the logged call runs as logged" invariant in its tool pipeline and a proposed pre-tool-input-rewrite note. This is that invariant expressed as a *plugin guard* rather than as a convention — and it converts a silent divergence between the audit log and the executed call into a named, one-line diagnostic.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Report every UNSERVED event at load time, by name** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/index.ts:519-523` — the bridge computes `registry.unserved(mod, SERVED_EVENTS)` and logs *"mod: on("turn.step") registered, but this host never raises that event"*. Why it matters: August's own `check:sse` gate exists because *"a dispatcher that calls `handlers.onX?.(...)` when nothing supplies `onX` — the optional call is a no-op"*. A plugin API that names its unserved surface **at load** catches the same class of defect on day one instead of after a gate is written in response to a shipped bug.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Reject unserved API members BY NAME instead of leaving them `undefined`** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/api.ts:192-218` — a `Proxy` makes any un-served `<namespace>.<member>` a function that rejects with `"no implementation for <namespace>.<member>"`, and the outer proxy's `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty` all return `false` so `$` is read-only. Why it matters: an unreachable member that is `undefined` produces a `TypeError` at the *call site*, far from the cause, and it disappears in production. A named rejection is a one-line diagnosis, and the read-only proxy means a plugin cannot mutate shared state even by accident.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **A `$` call raised by one plugin reaches only the plugins loaded BEFORE it** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/engine.ts:257` and `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/module.ts:61-65` — `registry.select(event, raisedBy)` filters on `hook.mod.order < raisedBy.order`. Why it matters: this is the acyclicity rule for a plugin API. August's own subagent spawn surface has exactly this hazard (a tool that calls a tool that calls the tool). One comparison in the registry makes re-entrancy structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **A surface generation counter, with stale presses reported rather than ignored** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/surfaces.ts:226-244` and `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/surfaces.ts:142-152` — each drawing gets a `generation`; a `pressBand` names the generation it saw; a press against a superseded drawing is **reported** (*"band press ignored: a0 of generation 0 is not on the current drawing (1)"*) and dropped; an unchanged tree keeps its generation but gets fresh callbacks. Why it matters: this is the UI/UX pattern for any async surface in August — a chat widget, an approval card, a progress banner. The UI is a snapshot; a click carries the snapshot id it was rendered from. Silent no-ops and wrong-button presses are both avoided, and the "wrong generation" report is a real diagnostic.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Redraw a surface because the drawing READ a value, not because the writer asked** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/engine.ts:370-384` (the `onStateRead`/`onStateWritten` hooks) and `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/surfaces.ts:159-172` — during a render, every `$.state` slot the drawing reads is subscribed; a write to a subscribed slot refreshes the band. Why it matters: this is read-dependency tracking, and it is how August could make a status/progress surface self-maintaining without every writer remembering to poke the UI. It also removes an entire class of bug (a value that changed but the widget did not).
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **"The logged call runs the tool it named" — a plugin may rewrite a RESULT but never the CALL** — `packages/experimental/claude-code-mods/src/index.ts:411-431` — a `{ deny }` becomes an error result with the reason; a `{ result }` becomes a success only when the tool is mod-registered or the value satisfies the tool's **own output schema** (otherwise it is error-shaped, `MOD_ANSWERED`); a rewritten result is installed through `tools/post-execute` so the pipeline's own block/accept decision still wins. Why it matters: this is a *schema-checked* plugin override. August's tool pipeline already has the output-schema machinery; the transfer is to validate a plugin's substituted result against the tool's schema instead of trusting it, and to route the replacement through the pipeline rather than mutating the result in place.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **A "dispatched, not verified" action result, as a universal convention** — `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/AXWorker.swift:190` (`static var actionResult: JSONValue { .object(["dispatched": .bool(true), "verified": .bool(false)]) }`) — and the same shape is returned by every input operation. Why it matters: this is the single most transferable idea in the shard. A harness that lets a model drive a real machine must never report a dispatched side effect as a completed one. August's `run_command` returns an exit code (a *verified* fact); a browser/CUA click returns only "dispatched". Encoding the difference in the result shape makes the model's next obligation — read fresh state — visible in the data rather than in prose.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **"Never retry uncertain input automatically" — a rule written into the model's own guidance, with a named error code for each case** — `packages/experimental/cua-macos/src/guidance.ts:40` — *"A successful action means dispatched, not verified. Cancellation may leave partial effects; never retry uncertain input without observing. STALE_APP requires getApp again; STALE_SNAPSHOT requires getState again."* Why it matters: August's self-heal ladder re-runs tools. The CUA guidance shows how to make a re-run *safe*: never re-dispatch blindly; require a fresh observation, and give the model a named code that says which observation to take. The error vocabulary (`STALE_APP`, `STALE_SNAPSHOT`, `WINDOW_CHANGED`, `SCREENSHOT_REQUIRED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `FOREGROUND_REQUIRED`, `PASTE_NOT_CONSUMED`, `CAPTURE_BUSY`, `CLIPBOARD_CHANGED`) is a model-actionable table, not a stack trace.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Every observation REPLACES the indices for its scope, and a stale index is a named error** — `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/AXWorker.swift:258-263` and `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/AXWorker.swift:145-150` — a new `getState` for a scope invalidates that scope's snapshot; an element index that is not in the named snapshot is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; a snapshot that is gone is `STALE_SNAPSHOT`. Why it matters: index-based addressing (element indices, message ids, file handles, attachment ids) is the most common source of "the agent acted on something that no longer exists". Making the address **scoped and versioned**, with a named staleness error, is directly transferable to August's tool results.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Two independent sources of truth must AGREE, or the operation refuses** — `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/WindowGeometry.swift:38-46` — the AX frame and the display frame are compared as integral point rectangles; a genuine disagreement is `WINDOW_CHANGED` with a message that says what to do next. Why it matters: August's own "one tokenizer / one door" rules are about *not* having two implementations of the same predicate. This is the opposite and complementary discipline: when two sources legitimately exist (the model's picture and the screen, the transcript and the store), compare them and refuse rather than picking one. The comment *"The helper preserves both coordinate sources rather than substituting AX geometry for CG geometry"* is the rule.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Permission bound to a code-signing identity, and durable consent only for properly signed code** — `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/ApplicationAuthorization.swift:9-26` — the grant id is SHA-256 of `executablePath + "\n" + authority`, where the authority is the code-signing designated requirement; ad-hoc or unsigned code gets a process-lifetime identity (or an executable-content digest) and `persistable: false`. Why it matters: a permission grant bound to a *name* or a *path* is revocable by whoever replaces the binary at that path. Binding the grant to a signature means "allow this app" means "allow this code". August's `allowedApps`/skill/hook grants should be reviewed against this bar.
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **One capture slot, but partial degradation instead of global failure** — `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/WindowCapture.swift:56-66` and `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/WindowCapture.swift:80-84` — an outstanding system capture holds the single slot; new captures get `CAPTURE_BUSY` while **AX and input remain available**; the slot is released by the *real* callback, and a late result is discarded. Why it matters: the failure mode a naive implementation has is "the whole tool breaks". Naming the contended resource and keeping the *other* capabilities alive is the pattern for any single-slot resource in August (one browser tab, one terminal, one file watcher).
- **[dsh-experimental-inspect#1]** - **Serialise the thing that races; do not serialise the thing that does not** — `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/RequestScheduler.swift:13-33` — a process-wide FIFO holds one complete desktop operation at a time, but *"socket writes do not hold it"*; a cancelled queued operation resumes with `NATIVE_CANCELLED` rather than waiting. - **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Port the provider's own image-token calculator instead of approximating it** — `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/image-tokens.ts:39-96` — the published `v41` calculator (14 px patch grid, 3:1 downsample, 544×544 scale-up floor, 1024-token cap solved aspect-preserving) is ported verbatim, and the projection is iterated to a fixpoint because the first pass is not one. If August ever resizes images for a provider, this is the difference between a real number and a guess.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **A credential-scoped model catalog with a bounded first-use wait and last-known-good retention** — `packages/llm/llm-deepseek-account/src/catalog.ts:75-135` — the scope is `url + sha256(token)`, the first access of a scope awaits the listing under the *request's own* deadline, later accesses refresh in the background, and a failing streak keeps the previous listing. This is the shape any per-account model list needs; August's provider models are static today.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Decode a provider listing defensively and count what you skip** — `packages/llm/llm-deepseek-account/src/listing.ts:46-52` and `packages/llm/llm-deepseek-account/src/listing.ts:60-72` — rows without a usable id and repeated ids are **counted** (`skipped`), not silently dropped, and "absent" capacity is distinguished from "declared but not a positive safe integer" so the two can be told apart downstream.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Gate a model on the client's semver version with the prerelease rule written down** — `packages/llm/llm-deepseek-account/src/resolve-catalog.ts:64-82` — a listed model declaring `min_version` is offered only when the client version is at least it in semver order, and the README states that a prerelease orders below its release (so a listing that admits prereleases must declare the earliest one it admits). August gates tools and models by harness version in ad-hoc ways; this is the explicit rule.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Turn every adapter throw into exactly one terminal chunk, and leave middleware/consumer failures thrown** — `packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:1064-1153` and `packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:1184-1192` — adapter selection, dispatch, iterator construction and iteration failures become `{kind:'error'|'aborted', failure}`; everything else stays a thrown plugin error. This is the boundary that stops a provider error from being misread as a plugin error (and the reverse) — the same distinction August keeps having to re-establish.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Validate a whole candidate registry before anything moves, then swap in one synchronous section** — `packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:495-548` and `packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:437-458` — a refused candidate leaves the previous entries serving, and no observer can see the registry between the release and the re-registration. August's settings writes and provider registration would benefit from the same "validate fully, then commit" shape.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **One plugin owns one top-level request field, with a prepare/accept transaction** — `packages/llm/deepseek-llm-api-extensions/src/index.ts:111-141` — the contributor prepares against the exact serialized body, the value is cloned and frozen (the provider keeps no mutable alias to the outgoing request), a failing contributor is omitted from that request with one warning, and the post-2xx commit runs exactly once even under concurrent calls. A clean template for "plugins may add provider metadata without touching the adapter".
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Distinguish "absent credential" from "malformed credential", and keep the malformed one out of the retryable set** — `packages/llm/llm/src/error.ts:43-51` and `packages/llm/llm/src/api-key.ts:36-41` — `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` means "supply one", `INVALID_CREDENTIAL` means "correct the stored value", and a malformed key fails identically on every attempt so retrying it is pointless.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Read provider errors through one classifier that also extracts the retry delay and the request id** — `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/transport.ts:22-43` — status plus provider `type`/`code` maps to a stable code, `Retry-After` is parsed in both its numeric-seconds and HTTP-date spellings, and the request id is looked up under three header spellings. Every consumer (retry, the receipt, the classifier) then reads the same string.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Compact the assistant stream instead of expanding it** — `packages/llm/llm/src/assistant-stream.ts:100-194` — consecutive deltas are packed into runs with time deltas, so the durable record is roughly ten times smaller than the expansion; the record-level readers answer "first token time" and "is there visible content" with an early exit and never expand at all. August's per-turn transcript storage would shrink the same way.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Normalize a failure without trusting a foreign error object's accessors** — `packages/llm/llm/src/adapter-failure.ts:16-28` — the carried `failure` snapshot is accepted only when it is an own data property and its `code` agrees with the error's own `code`; a hostile `Proxy` or a throwing getter degrades to `{message:'LLM adapter failed', code:'UNKNOWN'}` instead of escaping.
- **[dsh-llm-compaction#2]** - **Refuse an image-capability claim for an endpoint you cannot verify** — `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/model-info.ts:70-75` — an uncatalogued model is treated as text-only, because declaring an unverified image capability would let the host persist input the endpoint may reject on every later turn. Under-claiming fails early and names the model; over-claiming fails late and repeatedly. ---
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **A read-before-write guard must be enforced by the WRITER's atomic section, never by a prior check.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-26-file-context-as-event-gate.md:48` — the observation policy performs *no* filesystem I/O; it only chooses the compare-and-swap basis (`replaceIfVersion` / `createIfAbsent`) and gates on prior observation, and the provider detects staleness inside its mutation critical section. The note names the alternative explicitly: a policy-side `stat` would leave a TOCTOU gap between the check and the write, so the guarantee would be "a false guarantee that the provider's lock has to back up anyway" (`:165`). This is exactly August's read-before-write/edit guard — the freshness decision must live in the same critical section as the write, not in a separate "did you read it?" pass.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **A policy that can be dropped must not be in the tool's path.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-26-file-context-as-event-gate.md:35` — "bare `ctx.fs` performs atomic, unconstrained text I/O… Removing the policy therefore leaves the tools usable but unconstrained." The mechanism is the `expected?` parameter: *omit* it for an unconditional mutation, *supply* it for a guarded one, so both modes share one symmetric signature. August's `write_file`/`edit_file` and its hash-anchored edit gate could adopt the same shape (unguarded = unconditional write, guarded = CAS on the file hash) so the safety policy stays a pluggable layer instead of a hard-wired precondition.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Retry after a failed request must be authorized by a durable PROOF OF PROGRESS, not by the repair component's return value.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-10-after-call-compaction-pressure-and-overflow-recovery.md:38` — the recovery listener snapshots `session.surface.replaceGeneration` and returns `{kind:'retry'}` whenever pruning or summarization *increases* it; "a backend returning a result without replacement cannot authorize a retry, while pruning-only progress can authorize a retry without a `CompactionResult`" (`:52`). August's context-window overflow recovery currently trusts that compaction ran; this gives a checkable predicate.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Provider-reported token counts are only valid for the exact envelope that produced them.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-15-replay-token-meter-service.md:28` — usage is reused "only when the measured canonical request envelope equals the latest successful-call anchor"; any provider/model/system/prefix/tool/call-config change causes complete heuristic repricing, while surface growth is a *signed* delta. Transfer: August's `cost_estimator.price_for_model` and any token-pressure estimate — a cached price is a fact about one request shape, not about the conversation.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Do not freeze an abort reason; copy only the fields that become durable.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-16-explicit-turn-cancellation.md:16` — undici assigns a `stack` onto the abort reason it receives, so a frozen reason makes `fetch` reject with `TypeError: Cannot add property stack` *in place of* the abort reason. The loop therefore copies the declared fields only where the cause becomes durable data. Any August cancellation token that a transport may touch needs the same rule.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Cancellation must be cooperative and the reported idle state must be truthful.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-16-explicit-turn-cancellation.md:30` — the loop checks interruption before and after awaited boundaries but deliberately does *not* use `Promise.race` to abandon an in-process listener, adapter or tool promise; work that ignores the signal must settle before `whenIdle()` reports quiescence, because "returning idle while same-process work still runs breaks teardown and resource-ownership guarantees" (`:50`).
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Turn-scoped, not ambient, cancellation authority; and "one mechanism per independent fact".** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-16-explicit-turn-cancellation.md:16` and `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-12-agent-scope-runtime-design.md:18` — the signal is installed per prospective turn, retained through inbox claim, pre-step, prompt assembly, every step and turn-stopping, and cleared immediately before `turn/end`; ALS is rejected because "cancellation authority ends with one turn" and a leaked callback could observe a stale signal. The companion rule — one mechanism per independent fact, no second mechanism for every race — is the generalisation worth stealing.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **One durable boundary: every session event lives inside a turn.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-15-turn-enclosure-invariant.md:21` and `:25` — an idle injection becomes a one-shot `turn/start{trigger:{kind:'injection'}}` → `context/message` → `turn/end{completed}`, and the turn number is derived from the log each iteration so the one-shot turn cannot collide with the next real turn. The bug it fixed is the memorable one: an idle background-task notice was durably on disk but *silently dropped on resume* by the log scanner.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **A crashed turn is closed, never truncated.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-14-session-persistence.md:24` — flushed events are never rewritten; the *reader* owns balancing and appends synthetic `turn/end {kind:'interrupted'}` closers through its write handle, and only the incomplete fragment of a torn final append is discarded. A parse error or sequence gap in the committed prefix is corruption and makes the session unloadable rather than silently dropping the tail.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Tool schemas belong in the same assembly as the prompt text.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-11-tool-schemas-in-prompt-assembly.md:14` — `PromptAssembly { sections, tools }` means "what the model is told it can do" is one coherent concern, so tool filtering (progressive disclosure) is an *assembly rewrite* rather than a second listener on a second surface. August's `tool_search` → `tool_call` progressive-disclosure path and the system-prompt builder are currently two seams; this collapses them.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **One typed value per tool execution, projected explicitly into model-facing content.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-20-canonical-tool-output-contract.md:22` and `:38` — every tool declares `output: { schema, render(args, value), presentationMeta?(args, value) }`; the registry validates and deep-freezes the canonical value, and only `content`/`error`/`meta` are persisted, so "replay reproduces presentation but cannot reconstruct the programmatic result". The consequence August would care about: "content replacement is not a confidentiality mechanism" — a policy that must hide a value from a programmatic caller has to block the call, not rewrite the prose.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Adapter owns the reasoning vocabulary, as an opaque branded id, and the core never clamps it.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-24-adapter-owned-reasoning-effort-capabilities.md:14` — the core requires the selected effort to appear exactly in the adapter's published list; an unsupported value fails with `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT` *before provider I/O*, because "a silent substitution makes the user's selected control differ from the logged request intent". Transfer: August's per-model thinking/reasoning settings should be per-adapter capabilities, not a core enum.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Background work: complete all failable preflight before the work starts, and fence it on a controller being present.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-20-generic-long-running-tool-runtime.md:27` and `:71` — "a producer cannot start work that lacks a collectable job id", and `start()` fails before producer execution when no controller is attached. The check is at *start*, not at plugin load, because sibling plugins may activate concurrently.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Split the identity used for authorization from the identity used for lifecycle.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-20-generic-long-running-tool-runtime.md:51` — the snapshot stores the owner's branded `SessionId` (session equality grants access) while lifecycle operations retain the exact live `Agent` *instance* (object identity selects cleanup and completion delivery), so "reusing an agent or session id cannot redirect an old scope's cleanup or notices to a replacement". Directly applicable to August's background bash job ownership.
