- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **A derived read model needs no failure channel: absence is the signal.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-06-subagent-list-identity-projection.md:54` — "a unit never throws; a corrupt payload or an unrecognized version folds exactly like a log with no descriptor at all", and how "computed to nothing" is presented is the consumer's business. Cheaper than a per-key failure channel, and it keeps the read path allocation-free.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Read-time computation beats a derived index when there is one consumer.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-06-subagent-list-identity-projection.md:25` — a three-rung compute-and-discard ladder (live watermark cache → optional checkpoint cache → one body-bearing observation) replaced "values landed with the query index" wholesale, because the latter forced query infrastructure to learn domain vocabulary for a single consumer. Useful when a harness is tempted to build a denormalised store for one screen.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Classify every wire message by "who initiates × request/response", not by transport.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-19-gui-layering-and-rpc-protocol.md:87` and `:110` — exactly four message kinds, `rpcId` minted by the initiator and *echoed* by the responder, so swapping HTTP/SSE for WebSocket/IPC leaves the protocol unchanged. Transfer: August's `/v1/chat/completions` proxy, the ACP bridge and any future MCP transport all need the same discipline or they will diverge on correlation.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Two notification channels, chosen by change source.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-19-gui-web-client-architecture.md:75` — `markDirty()` batches frame-driven changes per microtask (N changes, one re-render); `notifyNow()` is for the direct echo of a user gesture, because "controlled inputs roll the DOM back and jump the caret if their echo defers to a microtask". Using `notifyNow` for frame-driven code collapses batching back to per-frame renders — the note bans it explicitly. This is the cheapest streaming-UI win in the shard.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Reconnect = rebuild, not resume.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-19-gui-web-client-architecture.md:77` — on disconnect, reopen the stream and refetch history, compare `subscribed.lastSeq` with the history tail and backfill once on a gap; there is no resume cursor. Exponential backoff (500 ms doubling to 10 s, jitter, unlimited) sits behind a *generation fence*.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Stream markdown by freezing everything but the last two blocks.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-06-web-markdown-incremental-ast-renderer.md:17` — the parser keeps the trailing two blocks unstable, freezes the rest and re-parses only the tail from the last frozen block's own `position.end.offset`; each source region then parses O(1) times per stream instead of once per chunk, and a single giant block degrades to the old cost and no worse. August's transcript renderer re-parses on every token today; this is the fix, with a DOM-fixture contract so the swap cannot silently restyle the transcript.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **Attribute every provider request with the standard header only, and prove it on the wire.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-06-21-mandatory-app-attribution-headers.md:28` and `:30` — every adapter sends a static, non-secret `User-Agent` (version read from the package manifest, never a hand-copied constant), asserted by a mock server on the wire; OpenRouter's `HTTP-Referer` and friends are explicitly *not* sent, because "even requests pointed at OpenRouter send only the shared `User-Agent`". A default-off attribution switch was rejected: "a default-off setting is exactly how adapters keep drifting".
- **[dsh-notes-arch#1]** - **One registry key for a capability; the access policy lives in the consumer.** `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-07-23-unified-session-query-service.md` (Decision section) — exact reads and full-text search over one corpus share a single `ctx.sessionQuery` key, while the *observation strategies* stay separate (exact reads hit authoritative sources per call; FTS reconciles a disposable index). Sharing a key does not make the derived index authoritative.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **One live service owns the ORDER of every first-party prompt section — no numeric literals in packages** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-25-sparse-first-party-prompt-section-orders.md:18` - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` keeps private named allocations; every contributor asks `ctx.systemPrompt.getSectionOrder(name)` for its typed placement, values are unique integers **at least ten apart**, and equal orders break by code-unit *name* rather than by plugin activation order. August's system prompt is assembled from many places, so a collision there is silent and produces a non-deterministic prompt; a single allocator with a spacing rule plus a name tie-break makes the order deterministic *and* gives future insertions room, and the note proves the point: an earlier local fix did not stop the next package from reusing the value.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **An identity field may only NARROW — a stream delta can never erase what the first delta established** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-01-streamed-tool-call-identity.md:16` - `acceptIdentity` accepts only a non-empty string for a tool call's `id`/`name`; `undefined`, `null`, `''` and non-strings leave the established value in place, and the wire type is *widened* to admit `null` so the guard is load-bearing rather than speculative. August's tool-call accumulator has exactly this shape, and the blast radius here is the reason it matters: an empty identity was written verbatim into the durable log, so a session was writable and no longer loadable.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Make an over-budget response a durable, only-forwarding SURFACE REDUCTION instead of a per-request projection** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-02-durable-image-offload.md:18` and `:22` - the offload of an image occurrence is recorded as a `surfaceOp: replace` node in the same log that compaction uses, a replacement **never reverts**, and the adapter *projects* the budget rather than deciding it (it fails the attempt with `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED` and a count). This is the direct fix for August's "model-visible input must be reconstructable from the session log" invariant: the old arithmetic was recomputed per request, so an inline fallback or a route switch silently moved the prefix and invalidated the provider cache — here the prefix only advances and the log alone determines what was sent.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Lossless packing on the wire: one record per delta run, with the page cut from LOGICAL events** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-15-packed-session-history-transport.md:16` and `:28` - a history page carries `SessionHistoryRecord[]` where consecutive same-block assistant deltas become one `{type:'chunks'}` row; the explicit outer discriminator selects the record class without interpreting the chunk kind, the page is selected from logical events *before* packing, and the journal validates inclusive logical ranges so packed records create neither false gaps nor hidden overlaps. Measured: 416,756 logical events → 696 top-level records, 90.8% less JSON, and client parse/validate/fold from 4,682 ms to 276 ms. August's transcript replay and its SSE history feed are the same shape of problem.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Live stream frames are NOT durable events: one settlement owns the durable stream, frames are branded and revisioned** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-31-live-assistant-stream-frames.md:14` - `agent/assistant-stream` frames carry a branded `LlmAttemptId` and a per-lifecycle revision; a settlement arriving after an active opening is owned by that attempt only when its seq follows `startedAfterSeq` and its turn/step match, and it stays staged until the matching end index/type/seq arrive. August needs exactly this separation: its "one run of tool calls is ONE line in the transcript" rule and its live spinner both want frame granularity, while "model-visible ⟺ logged" forbids durable token-level events.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Nearest layer wins a duplicate name OUTRIGHT; rank only orders duplicates WITHIN one layer** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-09-layered-skill-registry.md:18` - a rank pool across layers was rejected because a later-installed deployment plugin could silently displace a preset's own same-named skill on a registration-order tiebreak, changing a composition's behaviour remotely. August layers exactly this way (bundled skills, workspace `.aug/skills`, data-dir skills, per-agent skills) and the same rule gives each composition's author the final word.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **A capability definition's AUTHORITY and its TOOL EXPOSURE are two owners, not one switch** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-10-product-subagent-providers-in-shared-host.md:16` - providers stay process-scoped host-plane registrations (availability), presets contribute ordinary tool rows (exposure), and loading a provider registers a *dormant* backend — the product process starts on the first real delegation. August's own sub-agent hierarchy keeps the same split (the stable Subagent service owns child identity and teardown; an experimental Team service consumes it), which is how a stable layer avoids naming an experimental one.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **One process-table SNAPSHOT answers every question of a poll — and signals deliberately do NOT share it** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-27-process-table-snapshots.md:30` and `:12` - `ProcessInspector.snapshot()` returns one observation answering `tree`/`session`/`alive`, so a readiness poll costs one table read regardless of descendant count (measured: 18 ms at 0 descendants, 178 ms at 10 — the old N+1 reads saturated a 50 ms poll). The review explicitly *refused* to let the signal path reuse the snapshot, because an observation carries the original PID-to-start-time pairing forward and would defeat the PID-reuse fence; "what the table showed" and "what is true now" are different questions and only the second may decide a signal.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **A child process has NO PID and NO public startup state** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-28-subprocess-native-containment.md:18` - a Linux user-systemd scope or a Windows kill-on-close Job owns the *managed range*, `waitForExit()` succeeds only after that range is proven empty, and a failed native launch is never replayed because an ambiguous failure may be post-execution. August's `run_command` has exactly the "did it stop?" question, and the note's discipline — a range proof rather than a pid check, and no replay after an ambiguous failure — is directly transferable.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **One reader, many derivations — and a pinned budget of TWO reads** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-17-settings-describe-mirror.md:14` and `:20` - one mirror holds the whole `settings.describe` answer; fifteen independent readers became two reads, and a new preference-owning plugin now adds zero. The in-flight slot owns its run *before* its loading publication can re-enter `load()` and clears the rerun flag inside the same synchronous segment, because a `.finally()` on the returned promise runs a microtask later and lets a refresh in that gap mark a rerun nobody reads. The pinned second read closes the window where a commit lands between the eager read and the SSE subscription.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Make a capability KEYED by the thing it serves, so ABSENCE is the signal** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-12-plugin-owned-settings-surface.md:24` and `:26` - a `list` slot becomes a `keyed` slot whose key is the settings namespace the card edits, and what renders is the *intersection* of two ledgers (namespaces a live host plugin registered, and cards registered under those keys). A namespace another surface owns has no card under its key and therefore renders nothing without declaring anything anywhere — and the old "count the registered cards" empty state disappears with it.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **A type's identity and its KIND are different things, so an extension can replace a built-in in place** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-05-sidebar-tab-types-and-navigation.md` (`register(definition)` block) - `kind` is what `openTab` names and what tab identity is built from; `id` is one *implementation*'s identity, unique across registrations. The registry refuses a second `id`, a second registration in the same band of a kind, and any registration meeting a `fallback` of the same kind — while accepting the extension-over-builtin pair, with the built-in resuming on unregister. Priority is a *literal* band string, because a dynamically loaded plugin may not import a runtime constant.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Two ledgers, one intersection — and the *subject* is a projection, not the store** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-17-plugin-detail-page-extension-slots.md` - three region-keyed list slots (`actions`/`badge`/`section`) beat nine per-object slots, and each entry receives a subject carrying only the facts it decides on, so the page's store stays private; the host's read-only reasons, errors and fiber phases are deliberately excluded, because exposing them would make store internals a public contract.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Make the tool-call IDENTITY an event-local fact and let the *assembler* own the topology** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-11-trajectory-conversation-context-assembly.md:20` and `:59` - two views (chat and trajectory) share only exact-id matching, ordered matches, location facts, reader dependencies, publication scheduling and the replace/prepend/append lifecycle, while each keeps its own state and final node payloads. The complexity table is the transferable part: an older-page prepend costs `O(P × D + M)` instead of restarting the fold over the whole window, and a reader miss records a *window-gap dependency* so a later prepend replays only the affected chain in forward order.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **A sidecar row is bound to the session's LIFECYCLE IDENTITY, not to its id** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-10-message-feedback-sidecar.md:18` and `:24` - a row is bound to `{createdAt, cwd}`, so a recreated session id cannot inherit stale feedback and a fork gets its own identity with no copy; per-item opaque versions make the compare-and-swap *strict even when the desired value already matches*, which is what stops a stale request from crossing an ABA value cycle. August's Brain rows have the same "id can be reused" hazard.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **There is no `end` call — settlement is the only close** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-01-jobs-absorb-activity-record.md:21` - the dual-settlement pairing (`end` first-wins against teardown force-ends) was deleted rather than reimplemented, because two closers for one record is the thing that produces a frozen wrong terminal state. The same note pins the pump's constant-resource rule (subscribe to `done` once and keep one pending timer — racing the same pending promise every poll round retained a reaction per round, over a million closures on a day-long job) and the roster rule (a row *flags* a record, it does not count bytes).
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Split session POSITIONS into identity and offset with validating constructors** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-31-session-sequence-and-log-offset-brands.md:16` and `:26` - `SessionSeq` names one existing event, `SessionLogOffset` names a gap, prefix length or read offset; the compiler then refuses an offset where an event identity is required. The note also states the limit honestly: a compile-time brand cannot discover unknown numeric fields in an external event, so a format migration still needs an exhaustive owner disposition.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **The ROLE WORD is a contract, and a rename ledger makes it enforceable** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-11-repository-naming-contract-and-rename-ledger.md:46` - a seventeen-row table says when to use `Controller`, `Store`, `Directory`, `Registry`, `Runtime`, `Resolver`, `Binder`, `Engine`, `Policy`, `Executor`, `Gateway`, `Provider`, `Backend`, `Handle`, `Config` and when *not* to, with the operational test: "if callers mainly call `register()` and receive a disposer, use `Registry`". August's `app/services/` and `app/tools/` vocabulary is exactly this surface, and the note's "explicit non-renames" list is the part that makes the contract safe to apply.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **Exhaustive INDEPENDENT backstops, fail-closed in three directions** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-09-cordis-event-walk-backstop.md` - a separate `ts.createSourceFile` walk enumerates every declared event and every context key; the partition check fails when an event is invisible and unexempted, when an exemption names something that renders, when an exemption names nothing, and when the scan itself cannot see something the generator rendered. The scan deliberately shares no machinery with the projection, because a reachability bug in the projection is exactly what the backstop exists to catch.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#2]** - **A bilingual-pairing record pins the BLOB HASH of each side, so a translation cannot silently drift** - `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-08-19-projection-cache-per-session-files.i18n.yaml:5` - every note in this shard ships an `.i18n.yaml` holding the git blob hash of the English and the Chinese file plus the `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write` command. August's AGENTS.md and docs are far more valuable than a machine translation, but the *mechanism* — a per-document pair record that a gate can check — is cheap and directly reusable for any doc set that has a translated twin.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **An extension point is a slot list the owner also uses** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-17-session-row-menu-actions-slot.md:14` — `ui-workspace` declares `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` and `sidebar.workspaces.session.row.action` and registers its *own* `pin`/`rename`/`fork`/`archive` actions into them at orders 100/200/300/400, so a plugin lands "wherever its order says" and reusing a shipped id at another `priority` shadows it through ordinary registry cell rules; there is no privileged owner group (a group start is the entry's own `separatorBefore`). Transfers to August: any UI list a user might want to extend should be one ordered slot list with the shipped items *in* it, not a shipped list plus an append-only extension area — that removes the second rendering path and the "extension group" special case.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **The owner hands over state, not verbs** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-17-session-row-menu-actions-slot.md:16` — an entry receives only `{ sessionId, displayTitle }` and reads the Host state it needs through hooks its *own* registration injects (`usePinned`/`useArchived`, Sets derived once per Workspace snapshot); the behaviour lives in the registration's `inject` face, so the component calls exactly one callback, and `pinSession` reads the object-layer snapshots once at completion instead of subscribing to the whole Session list. Transfers to August: an extension should own its own behaviour and read shared state through injected selectors, otherwise every extension re-renders every row (the rejected alternative is spelled out at line 30).
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Progressive disclosure with the pruner threshold as a gate** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-21-creator-skills-progressive-disclosure.md:14` — the skill had exceeded the 8192-char threshold at which the preset's tool-result pruner keeps only head and tail, so `SKILL.md` keeps procedure + index, recipes move to `references/`, bundles to `templates/`, and **a test keeps the leading file under the pruner head and checks every referenced file exists and every template parses**. Transfers to August: August already truncates tool results (`maxToolResultChars` per model); the missing piece is the mirror-image gate — a check that a shipped skill/prompt file stays inside the truncation budget and that every referenced artefact resolves, so the head/tail truncation never silently eats the middle of a skill.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Ordered knowledge sources instead of forbidden ones** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-21-creator-skills-progressive-disclosure.md:16` — the skills no longer ban reading package sources; the order is inspect (`cordis_inspect_query`) → the package README under the `packageDir` `Config.listConfigs` resolves → built `lib/` declarations or checkout sources, with bundled packages resolving from the installation and profile-installed ones from the profile, plus `DSH_PROFILE`/`DSH_PROFILE_DIR` as reserved shell built-ins. Transfers to August: "read the source instead of restating it in the prompt" is a context-budget win, and it needs the *path* to be derivable at runtime (a registry lookup), not guessed from a directory name.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Peer-dependency rule for cross-instance identity** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-18-profile-plugin-host-runtime-instances.md:16` — a host runtime whose identity is compared across copies goes in `peerDependencies`/`devDependencies`, never `dependencies`; with `nodeLinker: hoisted` + `autoInstallPeers: false` the peer is not installed into the profile and the import reaches the installation's single instance through the interception layer. Line 18 extends the rule to the **writer** ("the writer mints the tag its readers compare"), and line 28 records why `Symbol.for` is not a fix — it repairs the tag lookup while scope parents and carrier keys stay per copy. Transfers to August: any mechanism that loads third-party code into the same process (plugins, MCP servers, skill runtimes) must guarantee single-instance for modules holding identity state; the failure mode (a per-Agent registration silently landing in a global layer, then an Agent rejected at startup) is invisible until two agents exist.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Publish once, buffer the rest** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-18-chat-navigation-performance.md:30` — `Session.loadThrough` retains accepted pages and a private paging cursor until the shared target is covered or loading ends, reverses the page list and flattens it **once**, and publishes one ordered prepend; a later page failure publishes the successful prefix once, and stream or window replacement discards obsolete buffered pages. Transfers to August: the same shape applies to any batched append into the transcript (history paging, compaction output, a tool that returns many records) — incremental publication multiplies the rebuild cost, because each intermediate publication re-derives growing indexes.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **State the work model, and refuse to over-claim it** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-18-chat-navigation-performance.md:34` — the note tabulates previous vs current work with named variables (`T`, `V`, `P`, `B`, `W0`), explicitly labels the table "work-count estimates, not timing measurements" (line 34), and states that 10,000 turns with ~50 mounted marks imply ~99.5% fewer rail marks, "not a 200× end-to-end speedup" (line 46); line 60 lists what was *not* eliminated. Transfers to August: when a performance note claims a win, the same table plus the residual-cost list is the format that survives review — and it is exactly the discipline August's own docs already apply to its file-size ceilings.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **A validator that mutates the value it validates** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-19-lossless-projection-checkpoint-json.md:14` — `z.json()` rebuilds objects and drops a valid own `__proto__` key, so a *successful* validation could change the checkpoint and reopening it would differ from replaying the log; the fix is the existing read-only `isJsonValue` predicate, and the alternative of validating-and-cloning was rejected because it copies already-immutable borrowed values. Transfers to August: any schema gate standing between a persisted artifact and a re-read must be checked for round-trip fidelity — validate without rebuilding, and prove it by writing/closing/reopening a fixture the real writer produced.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Mount-independent addressing, enforced by a static gate** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-17-web-feature-routes-and-route-gate.md:18` — every route keeps an absolute `*_PATH` registration key and derives a document-relative `*_ROUTE` for the browser; `verify-client-route-resolution` runs in `hygiene` and CI over every browser source and rejects root-absolute, protocol-relative and absolute app routes in request targets (request constructor, fetch-shaped call, dynamic import; assigned resource properties; JSX `src`/`href`), plus relative app routes resolved against a `location` read, and separately checks Host producers stamping a root-absolute `url`/`src`/`href`. Line 28 states the limit — inline literal fragments only, so composed references are untraced and owned by another spec. Transfers to August: the pattern is "one mount-relative rule + a gate that fails the build", and the stated blind spot with a named second owner is the part worth copying.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Read the live registry, not a dump** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-21-live-config-inspect-provider.md:14` — `Config.listConfigs` walks `ctx.loader.entries()` and each fiber's runtime Config and projects the mounted plugin's native Config into one self-contained JSON Schema, with inactive entries reporting `inactive` and no schema; the boot-free collector is deliberately not re-run because a running profile already holds the module-resolution interception that the collector installs and forbids overlapping (line 16), and teaching the skill to shell out to the CLI dump was rejected because the session guarantees neither the profile name nor `dsh` on PATH (line 22). Transfers to August: this is the same shape as August's `check:brain-config` (ask the backend which keys it accepts) generalised — the schema an agent writes against should be the running system's, read through an inspect tool, not a static document that can drift.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Give the model a sampled now, as a durable message** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-24-web-default-schedule-composition.md:18` — `time-context` appends one durable user message per eligible step carrying the sampled instant, the browser zone attached to the open request, and the elapsed time since the preceding model-visible message; the sampled instant is precisely what lets the model turn "tomorrow at nine" into an offset-bearing `at` value, and the reading replays, compacts and appears in exported session logs like any other user message. Transfers to August: an agent that must reason about time should be handed a clock reading inside the transcript rather than be expected to guess or to be handed a fixed string in the system prompt; the cost is stated honestly (line 36 — every session pays four extra tool schemas and one message per step).
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Enforce the context budget where the truncation happens** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-24-web-default-schedule-composition.md:39` — once the preset table grew past the base composition's 12,500-token inline budget, the spill policy was changed to keep the answer's head and tail plus a spill path instead of the complete JSON. Transfers to August: August already truncates tool results per model profile; the transferable piece is the *spill path* — a truncated answer that tells the model where the rest lives beats a truncated answer that looks complete.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **Read metadata without executing the plugin** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-18-localized-package-metadata.md:25` — the Host resolves `locale/en.json` through Node package exports *without evaluating plugin code*, so disabled, client-less and failed plugins still have readable titles; file paths and file URLs (including Windows drive and UNC) skip resolution and return no metadata, and "a file address alone is not a metadata error" (line 33). Transfers to August: metadata for an extension must be obtainable without loading the extension — that is what makes a disabled or broken plugin still listable, and it is the difference between a manager that can repair itself and one that cannot.
- **[dsh-notes-arch#3]** - **A bilingual pair as a hash-pinned, frozen artifact** — `.agents/notes/archived/architecture/2026-09-17-settings-pages-as-companion-packages.i18n.yaml:1` — every document is a triplet (`.md`, `.zh.md`, `.i18n.yaml`) whose sidecar records the git blob hash of each side "as of the last confirmed-consistent state", re-recorded with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <pair>`, and archived triplets are frozen and sealed by their own verifier. Transfers to August: the mechanism (not necessarily the Chinese) is a *reviewable act of confirmation* — a hash diff proves two artifacts are in sync, and the archive rule ("do not treat it as authority for current behavior") stops a frozen decision record from being read as live behaviour.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Make the compaction summarisation call a true prefix-extension of the last routed request** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-21-compaction-summary-prefix-cache-reuse.md:14` — the summarisation directive moves from the *front* of the auxiliary request (a fresh `system` prompt) to the *end* (a trailing `user` message), and the request replays the routed request's `system` + `tools` + history byte-identically, so the provider reuses the warm KV cache. The `tools` ride along even though the summariser never calls one, because dropping them shortens the token sequence and breaks alignment (`:18`). August should build its compaction summary the same way: same system prompt, same tools, same leading messages, instruction last — otherwise every compaction pays double prompt-processing on the largest part of the conversation, exactly when the context is biggest.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Classify a provider's degenerate empty completion as a retryable failure at the adapter boundary** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-24-empty-model-response-is-retryable.md:16` and `:19` — a terminal `stop` with zero content blocks becomes `finish {kind: 'error'}` with a canonical `EMPTY_RESPONSE` code, and that code sits in the provider-owned *normal* retryable set because "the attempt produced nothing durable, so repeating it is safe". The scope is deliberately `stop` finishes only (reasoning-only and whitespace-only responses stay successful) to avoid retry loops on models that intentionally stop after reasoning. August's turn loop should treat an empty assistant message as a bounded retry, not a silent `completed` turn.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Choose crash-recovery boundaries that are semantic, and distinguish "not started" from "outcome unknown"** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-21-semantic-session-checkpoints.md:14` and `:22` — flush before the next request is derived, after `request/header` is logged but before the adapter stream is constructed, and after pre-execute policy but before the tool body; then classify a crash by durable evidence, so an assistant tool request with no `tool/call` becomes `TOOL_NOT_STARTED` (retryable) while a durable `tool/call` with no result becomes `TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, whose model-visible result permits retry only for read-only or idempotent operations. August's `turn_outcomes` ledger and its "re-read then retry" remedies are exactly this shape; the durable-evidence split is the part worth copying.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Enforce a tool-restriction mode at the executor, not at the schema** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-07-ptc-executor-collapse.md:12` and `:16` — the package contract states the rule outright: "schema omission is not enforcement when a direct caller can bypass it; denial must be tested through the executor". The collapse is applied inside `resolveExecution`, so a model-direct native call resolves to `undefined` and surfaces as `UNKNOWN_TOOL`, and it terminates at `createExecution` *before* the extensible policy pipeline — so approval prompts, pre-execute listeners and guards never see a call that is deterministically denied, and no human is asked to approve it. August's "schema is the whole tool surface" assumption needs the same audit: every advertised-tool restriction should have a matching executor-side denial, tested through the executor.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Bound background work with a per-owner bucket whose occupancy is derived from the registry's own status records** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-11-bounded-background-job-admission.md:22` and `:30` — `running` *and* `stopping` both occupy capacity and release only when the producer's `done` settles (a `stopping` producer may still own its process), and when the bucket is full `start()` throws *before* producer execution and id allocation, so a rejection creates no execution resource, queue entry or reservation. Bucketing is by exact `Agent` object identity, matching owner cleanup. August's job/automation surfaces need a per-owner ceiling, not a global one, and the "cancel requested" state must not be mistaken for "resource released".
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Render the whole `cause` chain at every diagnostic boundary, from one shared renderer in the leaf package** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-20-error-cause-chain-diagnostics.md:17` and `:19` — undici's `fetch` wraps every transport failure in a bare `TypeError: fetch failed` and puts the actionable detail on `error.cause`; a single `errorChain(value)` in the leaf `dsh-llm` package (chosen because every consumer already imports that package, so sharing costs no new dependency edge) then replaces `error.message`/`String(error)` at the loop's durable `turn/end` message, its logger warnings, the TUI notice and the stdio startup lines, and three per-package `renderThrown` copies are deleted. Routing stays on `HarnessError.code`; the renderer is diagnostic output only. August's error surface should do the same — one chain renderer, applied everywhere, with the structured code kept separate from the human string.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Separate the human projection from the model projection, and let the event's own marker decide which one it belongs to** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-29-human-transcript-append-origin.md:16` — a compaction's replacement node is a *model-only* copy, and using the model-visible surface as the human transcript made the terminal erase every message the replacement shadowed. The split is `isAppendSurfaceEvent` / `isReplacementSurfaceEvent` over the two `SurfaceOp` variants; everything that must send exactly what the model sees keeps reading the surface. The browser twin of the same fix is in `2026-07-30-web-transcript-log-ordered-projection.md:16`, which also shows the compile-time half: a shared predicate moved into a cordis-free leaf subpath and pinned by a **type-only** import, so renaming the plugin id becomes a client-side compile error. August's transcript and its log are the same shape of hazard.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Fold a projection that lacks a price claim *neutrally* rather than throwing, but keep a contradictory adjacent claim loud** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-06-token-surface-unpriced-replace-compatibility.md:16` and `:18` — a replace with no armed shadow-price claim folds as `deltaTokens: 0` so a pre-protocol session stays replayable, while an *armed* claim naming a different range still throws, because there the metering event was adjacent and the producer wrote contradictory events. The overcount that results can only trigger an *earlier* compaction, which is the safe direction. This is a reusable rule for August's O(1) checkpointed projections: historical data folds neutrally, live contract violations still fail loud.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Let the composer's two text layers share one scrollport instead of keeping them in sync** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-31-composer-text-layers-share-one-scrollport.md:18` and `:24` — the note's core observation is that "no listener can close that gap, because the gap is the definition of a listener: it runs after the thing it reacts to"; the mirror was correct *at rest* and wrong in motion, measured at 203/202/203px of caret-to-glyph separation in chromium/firefox/WebKit. The fix is structural: one scrollport holds both layers, the textarea gets `overflow: hidden` so it cannot hold an offset at all, and the browser applies one offset to both in the same frame on the same compositor. The decisive test reads the separation *before the task ends*, before any `scroll` listener could have run. August's textarea-plus-overlay composers have the same two-layer hazard.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Latch a wake-up that lands in a cancellation's convergence window, and replay it at the old driver's own settlement boundary** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-07-cancel-convergence-wake-latch.md:14` — the `running` phase carries a `wakeRequested` latch, armed only when the current activity cannot deliver the wake; the replay lives in the exiting activity's `finally`, which guarantees `turn/end N` lands before the replayed driver opens `turn/start N+1` and that `whenIdle()` sees the replayed driver. The `signal.aborted` discriminator separates pre-abort queued work (parked) from post-abort explicit wakes (run after convergence), and the replay only fires while `inbox.hasPending`. August's cancel/queue paths have the same window.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Make a bounded overwrite's diff basis a provider-owned, descriptor-enforced bound — and treat a partial read as no basis at all** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-30-bounded-overwrite-diff-basis.md:14` — `before` is supplied only when the replacement and the *descriptor-checked* prior file are both under `diffBasisMaxBytes`; a size change after the descriptor stat returns `null` even if the final size fits, because a partial prefix would be an incorrect diff basis; and any descriptor-phase errno returns `null` rather than failing a write the caller already committed to. Trusting the earlier path `probe()` was rejected because that size can go stale before the read. August's write path needs the same "the bound must be enforced on the object you actually read" rule.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Say out loud what a tool's status word means, and make the word describe the *action available*, not an outcome** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-06-list-agents-residency-vocabulary.md:20` — `list_agents` reported `complete` for a child with no resident Activation but an intact conversation, and a model reading `complete` looked for a result that did not exist; the model-facing vocabulary became `running | idle | ready`, where `ready` means "the same conversation accepts another turn", while the service layer kept its accurate `'running' | 'inactive'`. The note's rule: *the line the model scans must carry the correct distinction itself* — a description saying "`complete` does not mean complete" fights the rendered status on every read. August's tool outputs deserve the same audit.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Give the subagent's output one canonical selection rule, shared by every consumer** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-10-subagent-empty-terminal-message-output.md:14` — three consumers selected the child's output independently and diverged, so `dsh-subagent` owns one rule (last non-empty Assistant message, else accumulated `text-delta`, ignore empty-content messages) used by the in-process driver, the continuable Activation, the SDK backend, the ACP backend and the foreground delegation tool. The rule tests *content length*, not text presence, so a reasoning-only message still wins over streamed text. August's subagent/child results should have exactly one selector, in one place, with the stop reason kept separate from the partial text.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Preserve a fail-loud path's ability to release the terminal — and keep the timeout timer referenced** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-07-31-fail-loud-releases-the-terminal.md:31` — the diagnostic is written *before* the release so a wedged disposer cannot swallow the reason, a *latch* keeps the first rejection the reported one, and the bounded release timer must stay referenced: an `unref`'d one lets Node reach an empty event loop and exit 0 on the very failure being reported, because an `unhandledRejection` listener suppresses the default fatal exit. August's crash paths should treat "the process may exit 0 on a fatal error" as a real failure mode.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Bound the whole tree at the launcher, not just the known offender** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-03-cli-signal-shutdown-escalation.md:24` — a telemetry disposer that never settled turned a one-way boolean latch into an unkillable CLI; the fix has two layers: the OTel backend bounds its own provider shutdown (3 s) and the launcher owns the outer guarantee (5 s backstop, a second signal forces immediate exit, and normal shutdown sets `process.exitCode` rather than calling `process.exit()` so Node can retire its own async handles). The note's rule: any current or future disposer can wedge, so the process boundary — not the plugin — must preserve both a graceful first attempt and a user-controlled way out.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Share a scroll-position ledger instead of enumerating input devices** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-06-reader-scroll-attribution-observed-top-ledger.md:14` — bottom-follow recognised only wheel gestures, so touch, scrollbar and keyboard readers could not take ownership from a streaming tail; the fix records the last `scrollTop` written or delivered at every programmatic write site and treats a position deviating from `min(ledger, floor)` by more than half a pixel as reader input, so *one* `scroll` listener covers every input source. Enumerating devices was rejected because native-scrollbar dragging exposes no input event to latch before its scrolls arrive.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Fail the executor before the policy pipeline, so a denied call never reaches a human** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-07-ptc-executor-collapse.md:16` (repeated because the mechanism is the transferable part) — the collapsed call terminates at `createExecution`, so `tools/pre-execute` listeners, approval `ask` and guards never observe a call that is deterministically denied. August's approval prompts should only ever fire for calls that could actually succeed.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#1]** - **Make the model-visible status of a subagent reflect the *live* scope chain, not a header snapshot** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-10-child-agents-join-their-parent-preset.md:22` and `:26` — a child's preset is recorded from the parent's live scope chain (`composedPreset()`) rather than the parent's creation header, because a parent that switched preset while blank runs on the newer composition while its header still names the older one; and the same note catches the second defect — a scope's restriction exempt set is "the tools this scope registers *itself*", not "the global layer", which is what made a child's `toolFilter` stop constraining anything once every model-facing row became an ancestor contribution. August's delegation and capability filters need the same re-reading of what "inherited" means.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Put environment facts *after* the reusable instructions, so the cacheable prefix is byte-identical across users** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-06-environment-prompt-suffix.md:14` - The system-prompt registry is ordered `identity (0) -> reusable instructions -> HARNESS_SOURCE (10000) -> WEB_SURFACE (10100) -> DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_SUFFIX (10200)`, and only `Your working directory is {{cwd}}.` is demoted to the suffix. August's prompt builder is one flat string today, so the *mechanism* transfers directly: give every environment-specific fact its own section key, sort sections by an explicit numeric order, and the per-install part of the prompt stops poisoning the provider's prefix cache. The note is honest that hit rate is not measured — the win is structural, not proven.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Emit reasoning content on every reasoned turn, not only on tool-call turns** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-19-deepseek-reasoning-passback-every-turn.md:16` - A gateway that re-encodes a DeepSeek conversation for another vendor has no slot for the upstream thinking signature and recovers it by *hashing the replayed chain of thought*; a plain-answer turn that withholds reasoning reaches the gateway with no chain at all, so the reconstructed conversation diverges from the recorded one and the failure looks intermittent (it only shows on turns the model did not call a tool). August's `llm-deepseek` adapter has the same shape, and August runs on cheap local models behind gateways — the rule "a reasoned turn replays its reasoning, always" is a two-line change with a large blast radius avoided.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Make pricing and payload come from ONE solver, and let the provider own the projection** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-10-deepseek-v41-request-image-projection.md:16` - `llm-deepseek` keeps the provider's published token-grid solver and derives the request image's *target dimensions* from it; the attachment store only resizes and encodes to the target it is handed, and pricing prices the same target. The note also records the rejected alternative in detail: a `token-grid` projection kind inside the provider-neutral `dsh-attachment` package was *built first* and then thrown away, because it put one provider's layout formula and patch constants into a generic-looking name and needed an `unscaled` flag to distinguish "send the source" from "send the solved size". August's `dump_openai_upstream_body` / `dump_anthropic_upstream_body` and per-model pricing have exactly this shape of risk — the transferable rule is "the provider package computes the target; the store moves bytes".
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Derive a context budget from the *live* model, and spill what the budget dropped** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-05-session-reference-model-budget.md:16` and `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-05-session-reference-spill-reuse.md:18` - The budget is `max(65536, floor(contextWindow x 4 x fraction))` with a 64 KiB floor, and the model route is learned by observing the *completed* `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall into a WeakMap keyed by Agent (line 14) — not by re-reading the session header, which can be stale after a live model switch. The spill side then saves the *same captured projection* the preview was derived from, so the artifact and the preview can never disagree, and records the omission in a notice that lives **outside** the bounded preview JSON so a tiny budget cannot hide it. August's compaction/relief ladder is currently one fixed budget; the pair of notes is a complete recipe for making it model-relative without letting a small budget hide the fact that content was dropped.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Cap in-flight work per macrotask, after the microtask queue drains — and re-check at the settlement door** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-29-code-runtime-python-call-backlog-and-binding-metadata-snapshot.md:16` - The child flooded calls against a binding whose promise never settled; the cap counted only *resolved* calls, so one async closure accumulated per frame until the wall clock. The fix counts outstanding calls, releases the slot in the `finally`, and checks **once per macrotask** (after microtasks drain) rather than per frame or per event, because a per-frame check kills a legitimate 1025-call `asyncio.gather` and a per-event snapshot is stale when several `data` events fire in one macrotask. The `done` handler independently re-checks the count before accepting the frame, closing the same-batch window. August's `MAX_MANAGED_TOOL_ROUNDS` and the Bot-to-Bot ceiling are per-turn counters; this is the same discipline for *in-flight* work, and the "check after the microtask queue drains" rule is the part that is easy to get wrong.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Bound a parse by the host heap, not just by a byte cap** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-29-code-runtime-python-call-backlog-and-binding-metadata-snapshot.md:32` - `JSON.parse` of a wide-object frame materializes several times the raw bytes in V8's property storage (measured 6.4x for a 3,000,000-key frame; a 256 MiB host OOMs outright), so the effective frame cap is `min(protocol cap, floor((heap_size_limit - baseline) / 16))` derived from `v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit`, and the load gate *rejects* a budget whose frame could not be parsed safely. August's `/v1` proxy and MCP surfaces accept caller-supplied bodies; a "bytes on the wire" ceiling is not a "bytes in the parser" ceiling, and this is the arithmetic that closes the gap.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Split a fallible fold into plan/commit so retry identity is preserved by ordering, not by copying** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-24-token-meter-surface-fold-plan-commit.md:14` - The copy existed for exactly one property (a throw must leave the caller's `ReplayState` untouched so a malformed event fails identically on every retry) and cost ~99.9% of an append, giving an O(S^2) term on the streaming path. The plan/commit split keeps the property by *ordering* — plan (all fallible work) -> validate -> commit in place (infallible by construction). August's `turn_outcomes` / `replay` handling and the token-meter fold have the same coupling; the generalisable trick is that "atomicity" can be a sequencing property rather than an allocation.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Record an unknown tool outcome instead of leaving a tool call unanswered** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-19-failed-step-tool-results.md:14` - A committed assistant message can request tools whose scheduler fails before all results are recorded; closing the step with those calls unanswered makes every later provider request invalid, and because the error turn is already closed, crash-tail repair cannot recover it. The driver therefore records `TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` (with text warning against blindly retrying an operation that may have side effects) or `TOOL_NOT_STARTED` *before* closing the step — the only window in which a failed turn can still be made valid. August's tool-boundary guard and its `_stuckRequestEscape` ladder both assume paired call/result histories; this is the upstream half of that assumption.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Give a child agent exactly one delivery mode, so ordering cannot vary by deployment** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-17-subagent-message-settlement-ordering.md:16` - Every model-authored child message uses fixed Steer delivery; there is no quiet and no next-turn *model* option, because a later settlement notice entering a different queue could reach the parent before the earlier child message. The wake generation is renewed *before* the send returns, so a receiving activation cannot settle over an accepted waking send. August's subagents and Bot DMs have the same two-queue reality (`next-step` vs `next-turn`); the transferable rule is "the model does not choose a delivery mode, so ordering is a property of the system, not of the caller".
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Make a stale config *repairable*: tolerate catalog diagnostics at registration, be strict on writes** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-07-pi-ai-settings-catalog-recovery.md:14` - An installed provider catalog can invalidate unchanged user settings; rejecting the whole namespace at registration makes unrelated providers disappear and *removes the controls needed to fix the configuration*. The fix splits the two moments (registration tolerates catalog diagnostics, writes strictly validate only changed providers), keeps per-model diagnostics next to the model, and reports `INVALID_CONFIG` before credentials or network I/O. August has the same shape in its brain-config + provider tables and its `check:brain-config` gate; "a broken config must stay *editable*" is the idea to steal.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Degrade the cache conservatively: a cache miss must never hide a conversation** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-13-bounded-cold-blank-verification.md:18` - A cached `blank: true` is rejected (the cache deliberately permits the log to advance past its checkpoint), and a cache *miss* is served as non-blank so the row stays visible. Every failure direction is chosen so the UI may show one extra empty row but can never hide a real conversation or promote one merely because it was opened. August's `turn_outcomes` ledger and its brain projection caches need the same one-way conservatism.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Stale-while-revalidate, with the pending window made an explicit no-op** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-28-trigger-menu-stale-while-revalidate.md:16` - The menu keeps the previous rows and marks the groups pending instead of collapsing to a skeleton on every keystroke; `pick()` requires the group to be `ready`, and Enter during the pending window is an explicit `'consumed'` no-op — it neither picks the stale row nor falls through to send the draft. The note's reason is the transferable part: with retained rows the user is looking at a highlighted candidate, so a few hundred ms of dead key is safer than sending the whole draft under it. August's file/reference picker and its composer `@`-mention path are the same shape.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Let the *target element* be the completion signal of a scroll/reveal, not the caller** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-03-session-search-result-reveal.md:16` - A matching mounted row scrolls itself into view and acknowledges the target id, which prevents later renders from repeating the scroll; the parent cannot complete the operation before a folded target row mounts, so it must not try. August's session list and transcript surfaces have the same "the element that owns the DOM does the work" requirement, and the note shows how a one-shot reveal is cancelled and re-armed without a second state machine.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Normalise a model-facing error at the model boundary, and keep the machine code intact** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-03-normalized-unread-fs-tool-diagnostic.md:14` - `remediateFsError` replaces every `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` message with one actionable string while preserving the structured code and chaining the source as `cause`; the machine-readable code and the model-readable text are deliberately decoupled, and the provider/policy keep their own wording because other consumers do not share the tool's presentation. August's `FS_NOT_OBSERVED`-style tool errors reach the model with source-specific wording today; this is the exact seam to normalise at.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Declare a durable state the *model* may not undo** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-03-user-owned-goal-pause-activation.md:18` - `update_goal resume` refuses a durable paused goal with `GOAL_TOOL_RESUME_PAUSED` before it reaches the goal service, while still resuming an active-but-disarmed goal; activation is kept process-local (never in the durable snapshot or a checkpointed projection) and exposed through a dedicated `goal/activation-changed` event. August's `update_state(phase=…)` is explicitly only progress tracking — the transferable lesson is that a *user* control and a *model* control over the same object need two doors, with the model door closed at the tool.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Cherry-pick a community fix verbatim and keep the author** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-23-win32-utf16-nul-truncation.md:16` - The UTF-16 terminator fix was adopted byte-identical from a community branch, with both upstream commit hashes recorded in the note and the original author named, because "a byte-identical cherry-pick preserves provenance and credit" — and rejecting a community patch to rewrite it locally was explicitly refused. Small, unglamorous, and worth copying: August's Windows host layer has the same class of bug.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Write the *measurement design* into the note, and publish a benchmark without a CI wall-clock gate** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-11-incremental-terminal-retention.md:24` and `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-08-28-linear-stream-queue-drain.md:39` - The terminal note documents the benchmark's inputs, what is excluded (shell startup, PTY transport, model latency, browser rendering), and the exact reference expectations it scales; the deque note ships a reproducible benchmark script but states that "CI does not enforce a wall-clock threshold — deterministic unit coverage owns the algorithm and compaction paths". The August repo has no test suite at all, which makes this pair the most directly usable: publish the measurement recipe and the deterministic assertions, and do not pretend a flaky timing budget is a gate.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Test the *absence* of a read, not the shape of an output** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-19-declared-session-attachment-carriers.md:14` - Attachment readers select content by built-in event type and keep every other field opaque; the refusal tests assert that attachment storage is *never read*, and the archive test additionally compares the exported log text to prove the complete logical log survives. The note's rule — "a plugin needs a supported content occurrence or its own reader" — is a clean ownership boundary for any capability that authorises bytes.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#2]** - **Read the model route from the completed assembly, not from a cached header** - `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-05-session-reference-model-budget.md:14` - The route is captured by a *local prepend listener* on the completed `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall into a WeakMap keyed by Agent, because a header or options can be stale after a live model switch, and reassembling or redispatching routing during pre-step would repeat plugin effects. August's per-model pricing resolution (`price_for_model`) and its "single source of truth" rules are the same shape; the mechanism — a disposable observer on an existing waterfall — is cheaper than a new routing API.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **A stale lock is recoverable when you can PROVE the holder is gone — and the proof is a signal probe, not a timestamp** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-24-exited-holder-lock-takeover.md:17` (implementation: `packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:112-127`, `packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:150-178`) — The mechanism: the lock file records the holder's PID; a contender sends signal 0 to that PID; `ESRCH` means the process is gone (take over), `EPERM` means it exists under another user (keep waiting), and a record that is empty, non-numeric, PID 0, or out of int32 range proves nothing (keep waiting). Takeover is then serialised by a **claim file named after the SHA-256 of the lock record**, and under the claim the claimant re-reads the lock and re-probes the PID before removing — so a holder that reused the PID cannot be mistaken for the dead one. Why it transfers to August: August writes `providers.json`, `config.json`, the brain SQLite file and the encrypted secret store from the UI, the backend and the Bot path, often in separate processes, and a crashed holder there wedges every later writer until a human deletes a file. The three-part rule — *prove with an OS-level signal, serialise with a content-addressed claim, re-prove under the claim* — is language-agnostic and works on a plain `O_EXCL` lock file with no dependency.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **Bound a child process by SILENCE, not by duration — and treat the process's own exit as completion, never the pipe EOF** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-23-bounded-pnpm-runs.md:19` and `:26` (implementation: `packages/boot/plugin-manager/src/operations.ts:367`, `packages/boot/plugin-manager/src/operations.ts:377-385`, `packages/boot/plugin-manager/src/operations.ts:431-448`) — The mechanism: (a) a run completes when the process exits, so the completion signal is the raw child's `exit` event raced against the library's promise, because a descendant that inherited stdout holds the pipe open forever; (b) the pipes then drain under a fixed 2000 ms grace and are closed, with only *this* close ignored so a pre-cut read failure still surfaces; (c) a captured run that prints nothing for `idleTimeoutMs` is terminated, and it is classified `timeout` regardless of the exit status the signal left, so the caller rolls back instead of activating a half-written manifest; (d) the whole process *tree* is stopped and awaited before the rollback, because an approved `postinstall` outlives its parent. Why it transfers to August: August's `run_command`, its code-mode sandbox, its MCP server launches and its background jobs all spawn children that can wedge. A silence bound separates *stalled* from *slow* — a duration bound would kill a legitimate slow native build — and the "exit, then drain, then cut" ordering is the part that is easy to get wrong and expensive to debug.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **Keep an optimistic local echo alive until a durable, ORDERED watermark proves the stale duplicate can no longer appear** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-22-input-echo-admission-ownership.md:18` (implementation: `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/session.ts:817-838`, `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/session.ts:846-873`) — The mechanism: the optimistic bubble is keyed by the submission's `rpcId`; the durable `user/message` echoes that `rpcId`; the Inbox projection carries a monotonic sequence number; the client keeps the local suppression identity until the Inbox projection's watermark has passed the sequence at which this submission was claimed — and only then retires the echo. Crucially the watermark is re-read at retirement time, so an *older* accepted row cannot reappear after the identity retires. Why it transfers to August: August's chat shows the user's message immediately and the durable row later; any implementation that deletes the optimistic bubble on the first `user/message` will double-render whenever the projection is late, and any implementation that deletes it on a timer will flicker under CPU throttling. The watermark is the only evidence that does not depend on wall-clock timing, and it needs no new persisted field when the transport already carries a sequence.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **Price tool output in TOKENS, and price images with the SAME estimator that prices the request** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-21-multimodal-tool-result-retention.md:16` and `:31` (implementation: `packages/spill/spill-policy/src/retention.ts:48-104`, `packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:56-74`) — The mechanism: the result budget is a token count, not a byte count; the block pricer is a per-block callback that uses the text estimator for text and the *active route's* image calculator (`visualTokens` plus the descriptor text) for images; retention keeps the two **contiguous ends** and omits the middle; text may be split at a UTF-16 code-point boundary; images are indivisible and keep their original positions; the omission notices are reserved out of the budget before the split; and the *complete* spill file records a **readable attachment path** at each image position so an omitted image can be re-read rather than re-sent. Why it transfers to August: August's context is measured in tokens and it already has a per-model token estimator and a per-model cost table; a byte budget under-prices a screenshot by two orders of magnitude and over-prices a log tail. The specific transferable detail is the *indivisible-block* rule: an image either fits whole at a retained boundary or that boundary's space is left unused — never half-kept, never moved.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **A protocol constant has exactly ONE owner, and a consumer that re-installs it breaks the fast path silently** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-21-persistent-pwsh-keeps-controlled-prompt.md:16` and `:36` (implementation: `packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/sanitize.ts:9`, `packages/shell/tool-pwsh-persistent/src/index.ts:395-401`) — The mechanism: the backend owns the prompt and installs it during `spawn`; the client tool must not install a second copy *and must not import the constant* (a consumer that matches a provider's protocol string couples itself to that provider). When the tool did re-install its own prompt, the readiness check silently failed and every call fell to the slow tier: 8493 ms -> 1340 ms. The regression test asserts the **settle reason** (`stdin_read` at least 6 times, `inferred_idle` zero) rather than a duration, so the report is by mechanism and survives machine-speed changes. Why it transfers to August: August's backend has its own prompt/readiness protocol and the terminal drawer, the code-mode runner and the shell tool all consume it. Two owners of one protocol constant is exactly the shape of bug that costs 6 seconds per call and shows up as "the model is slow".
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **Accept the OS's "I delegated this" exit code, but never read it as "it worked" — assert on the arguments the peer actually received** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-22-windows-open-through-shell-resolution.md:44` (implementation: `packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts:116-123`, `packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts:136-145`) — The mechanism: the path is handed to `explorer.exe` as **one argv element** with commas and equals signs percent-encoded (the shell splits its own command line at both) and nothing else encoded (Explorer rejects percent-encoded non-ASCII and falls back to Documents); Explorer's exit code 1 means "handed off to the running desktop process" and is accepted, while every other failure rejects. The negative control is the lesson: with a raw comma the shell opened the *Documents folder* and **still exited 1**. The verification then reads the shell's own window and selection state rather than pixels. Why it transfers to August: August's desktop is a Tauri shell that shells out to Explorer, the browser and the OS opener for "open file / reveal in folder". Any opener that checks only the exit code will report success for the wrong target; the fix is to assert on the exact argv the peer received, and to treat the exit code as evidence of *delegation* only.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **Give a privileged in-page action a PRIVATE capability channel, not the shared document's event surface** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-20-windows-embedded-mandatory-update.md:16` and `:22` (implementation: `apps/desktop/src/preload-mandatory-overlay.ts:37-61`) — The mechanism: the isolated preload creates a `MessageChannel`, transfers one port to the shell frame with a transfer list, keeps the other, and **only messages arriving on that paired port may invoke the privileged IPC**; a synthetic `window` event in the shared product document cannot, because source/origin are constructible by product scripts. The overlay is a closed shadow root inside the main window, so there is no second native window to keep in sync with the parent. Why it transfers to August: any future August feature that must interrupt the user from inside the app (a mandatory update, a dangerous confirmation, an approval prompt) needs exactly this split — the *display* lives in the product document, the *authority* lives on a private port. The note is honest that the DOM overlay is not a tamper-proof surface, which is the right amount of claim to make.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **A follow controller per scrollport, and "the user scrolled" is a claim that native animation can invalidate** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-22-chat-scroll-follow-and-footer-geometry.md:22` and `:29` (implementation: `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/chat/use-scroll-follow.ts:22-171`) — The mechanism: each scrollport owns an independent controller holding *intent* (not a React flag); the controller keeps an **outstanding animation target** separate from the current position, so the browser's own scroll events during a smooth animation are not counted as reader movement; a reader gesture interrupts the native motion *before* the browser applies it, and the actual displacement afterwards decides whether following stops or resumes; `scrollend` settles and an off-target stop releases following. Why it transfers to August: August's chat is a transcript scrollport plus per-process-group scrollports plus a terminal section; one shared "following" flag pulls a capped group away from the reader whenever the outer transcript follows, and treating every non-bottom scroll event as reader input breaks native smooth follow outright.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **`overflow-y: clip` clips without creating a scroll container; `hidden` silently becomes one** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-22-chat-scroll-follow-and-footer-geometry.md:20` and `:25` (implementation: `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/chat/ChatView.module.css:18-19`) — The mechanism: an `overflow-y: hidden` ancestor becomes the *nearest scroll container* even when the reader is scrolling a different outer element, which breaks `position: sticky` for code banners and compaction headers and makes floating controls measure transcript geometry instead of viewport geometry; `overflow-y: clip` constrains the overflow without that side effect — but only while the horizontal axis stays `visible`, because pairing vertical `clip` with horizontal `auto`/`hidden` computes the vertical overflow back to `hidden`. Why it transfers to August: August's chat has the same sticky headers, the same floating controls and the same nested scrollports, and the failure is invisible in review (nothing overflows, the content is simply shorter than expected).
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **Degrade to `unknown` rather than refuse the record — and never let a missing discovery field make readable history unavailable** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-19-v3-incomplete-child-catalog-evidence.md:14` and `:24` (implementation: `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/facts.ts:46-64`) — The mechanism: a child's *header* establishes identity and parentage; its *descriptor* carries discovery fields (mode, label). A catalog entry is backfilled only when **exactly one** supported own descriptor exists; zero or several, or an unsupported version, yield an `unknown`-mode membership instead of an invented mode, and never a refusal of the whole parent. The exactly-once requirement exists because two consumers disagree on which descriptor wins (`foldSubagentDescriptor` takes the first, the identity projection takes the last), so a backfill must not pick a side. Why it transfers to August: August migrates and reads session JSONL with subagent children; a rule that "refuses to open a conversation because a discovery field is missing" turns a cosmetic gap into data loss, and inventing the field turns a gap into a durable lie.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-bugfix#3]** - **Say what the mechanism does NOT prove, in the note itself** — `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-24-exited-holder-lock-takeover.md:20` and `.agents/notes/archived/bug-fix/2026-09-22-input-echo-admission-ownership.md:47` — The mechanism: the lock note states that takeover proves only that the *recorded process* exited, not that the processes it started stopped writing, and immediately pairs the limitation with a second mechanism (the run record) that closes it. The echo note states that the multi-input replay "does not assert that optimistic ordering predicts Host order". Why it transfers to August: August's own notes (and the repo AGENTS.md) make a habit of stating the limit and then saying which sibling decision owns the rest; a fix whose note claims more than the mechanism delivers is how a second reader ships a false guarantee.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Compaction summarises by replaying the routed request's own prefix and appending the directive as a trailing user message, so the provider's warm KV cache is reused instead of thrown away** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-06-18-compaction-capability-seam.md:37` - The August harness compacts by summarising a range with a *fresh* request, which re-reads the whole prefix and pays full input cost every time. DSH instead reuses the exact provider/model that served the failed request and re-sends its prefix, so the KV cache stays warm and only the summarised span is new work. Directly transferable: the August `compactMessages` path could build its summariser request from the last routed request's prefix instead of the full history.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **A session-stable opener is frozen per instance so the provider's prompt cache holds *by construction*, not by discipline** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-07-session-prefix.md:23` - "Reuse is structural, not disciplined: the cached product cannot change mid-session, so the provider's prompt cache holds by construction." The August harness has a per-session frozen memory index for exactly this reason, but DSH generalises it into a first-class seam (a request-only, header-logged prefix) with an explicit rule that a mid-session content change is *not* re-read until the next instance. Worth stealing as a rule for any August prompt section that must not churn: a change notice goes through the append-only history, not through a mutated prefix.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Canonicalise tool order *before* the assemble waterfall, so the request bytes — and therefore the cache prefix and the durable header — are deterministic** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-06-explicit-tool-order.md:23` - The default is lexicographic code-unit order (locale-independent, needs no configuration), and canonicalisation happens *before* the `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall so the deterministic list flows into the request header, the frozen request and the reconstruction checks. August's `toolDefinitions` ordering is the same class of hazard: a plugin-registration race changes request bytes, busts the provider cache and breaks request reconstruction. The one-line fix (sort before the waterfall) is cheap and the note also names the rejected alternative ("canonicalize in `llm.stream()`") and why it fails: it runs *after* the header is logged.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **A misconfigured tool name fails the TURN, not the boot** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-06-explicit-tool-order.md:47` - "Every turn fails identically until the config is fixed; the process itself stays up (matching the repo rule that explicit config references must not be silently ignored — the enforcement point is the assembly because no earlier universal moment exists)." This is the exact shape August needs for its brain-config keys: reject at the first point where the referenced thing provably exists, keep the process alive, and make the failure *identical* on every attempt so it cannot be mistaken for a transient provider fault.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Provider and transport error text must never enter model context** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-24-provider-retry-policies.md:62` - "a transport or provider diagnostic is operational state, not conversation content. It can expose sensitive provider details and changes the retried request instead of repeating the failed request." Two transferable properties at once: the retried request must carry *the same derived context* as the failed one (so the retry is a true repeat), and the diagnostic must stay out of the prompt. August's stuck-request ladder and its `_stuckRequestEscape` reshaping are exactly this class, and this note gives the crisper statement of the invariant.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Retry policy is route-owned and captured at the final adapter boundary, so an in-flight request's recovery contract cannot be changed retroactively** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-24-provider-retry-policies.md:16` and `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-24-provider-retry-policies.md:44` - The policy is *registration state* on the provider route, not a retry-executor setting; `ctx.llm` binds the serving registration's immutable policy to the call at the last adapter boundary, so disposing or replacing the route mid-flight does not change the request's contract. Each scheduled retry appends a **non-surface** `llm/retry` event carrying the failed provider, the policy mode, a canonical resolved-policy key, the retry number and the delay — durable, observable, and invisible to the model (the UI renders an unbounded limit as `∞` rather than persisting `Infinity`). The canonical-key trick — retry history continues only for the same provider *and* the same resolved-policy key, so replacing a route with different limits starts a fresh count — is a cheap way to make a policy change observable.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Start-time capability mismatches are rejected LOUD, never accepted-then-ignored** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-06-21-subagent-capability-seam.md:49` - The service checks every requested start-time feature (`agentOptions`, `outputSchema`, `depthLimit`, `toolFilter`, `persona`) *before* delegating and raises `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` if the provider lacks it. This is the "a knob that always refuses is a lie" rule generalised: advertise only what the provider can honour, and refuse at the boundary rather than degrading silently. August's agent-permission model (where an empty permission list means "inherit", not "nothing") is the same family of confusion, and DSH's loud-rejection shape is the right answer.
