- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Delegation snapshots the parent's policy at spawn time, and the snapshot is expressed as ordinary log events so existing folds order it correctly** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-25-subagent-policy-inheritance.md:16` and `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-25-subagent-policy-inheritance.md:34` - The inherited facts become `permission/preset` / `sandbox/mode` / `approval/policy` events in the child factory's *unpublished setup*, so the constructor's `firstLiveSeq` stays fixed and the fork lineage cut is unchanged, while the existing last-event-wins folds make the delegation snapshot beat stale fork history. The note names the alternative it rejected and why: "Live resolution walking `parentSession` at each call — it breaks the 'two sessions never see each other's state' isolation invariant … and makes a mid-run parent switch retroactively change a running child." Two August-relevant properties: a subagent cannot widen past its parent, and a mid-run parent tightening does not silently change a running child.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Loop hygiene is detected at exactly one seam and delivered as ADVICE, never as a block** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-08-repeat-tool-guard.md:20` and `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-08-repeat-tool-guard.md:25` - The guard counts on `tools/post-execute` — the one point where `(exec, result)` are seen together, so no cross-event pending map is needed, and it also fires for *denied* calls — and delivers reminders by prepending to the downstream decision's `additionalContexts`, never by replacing result content. The chain key is `(tool name, canonical arguments)` with canonicalisation being a deep key-sort plus `JSON.stringify`, so reordered argument keys are not new work. August's repeat/stagnation detection is the direct analogue, and the "post-execute also runs for denied calls" detail is exactly the kind of thing August's `_recordWorldDelta` credit must get right.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Instruction files are tracked by content digest, never by parsing rendered text, and there is deliberately no filesystem watcher** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-06-24-workspace-context.md:52` and `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-06-24-workspace-context.md:60` - "Every workspace context event stores versioned metadata with `{ action, scope, path, digest? }`, where `digest` is SHA-1 over the loaded content … The model-facing prompt has no HTML comments, hidden markers, or headings that are parsed back into state." And on detection: no watcher, only a "next successful structured touch, resumed-baseline reconciliation, or entering pre-step that restores a shadowed baseline"; "A provider failure produces no removal; absence is only accepted when all configured candidates in that scope were probed successfully." The "absence requires positive proof" rule is the transferable half — a read that failed is not evidence that a file was deleted.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **A compatibility bridge's context injection is not a veto, and it must delegate before it enriches** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-06-30-hook-bridges.md:45` - "returning `enter` from a waterfall listener WITHOUT calling `next()` short-circuits every later `agent/pre-step` / `tools/post-execute` listener, so a policy/sandbox plugin registered after the bridge would never see the prompt." Each bridge therefore calls `next()` first and only a real `deny`/`block` short-circuits. This is a general waterfall-ordering bug class (August's gate-participation rule is the sibling), and the fix — delegate, then enrich — is a one-line discipline every hook/middleware author should be held to.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Model-facing search tools expose NO cursor; the harness follows cursors internally and caps the result count, and the spill mechanism owns output size** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-24-model-facing-session-query-tools.md:32` and `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-24-model-facing-session-query-tools.md:34` - "Neither search tool exposes a cursor, offset, page size, or model-controlled result limit … A capped result tells the model to narrow its query or filters; a generation change reports that the whole search must be retried." The rejected alternative states the reason plainly: a cursor is usually stale before the model can reuse it, because recording a tool result changes the generation. The spill half is equally transferable: the consumer neither imports `ctx.spillStore` nor implements a second truncation format — one generic `tools/post-execute` spill policy serves every tool. August's `retrieve_relevant_facts` / `brain_query` pagination is the exact place this transfers.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **The durable log copy of a tool result is NOT model context, so it may be truncated even where the model-facing copy may not be** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-26-ptc-dispatch-log-spill.md:20` - "the model-result listener skips `read` to prevent a `read → spill → read again` loop. The dispatch-log listener also replaces oversized `read` sub-call content because a log copy is not model context, so that loop cannot occur, and `read` is the tool most likely to produce a large log entry." A small but genuinely transferable distinction: the same content can be governed by two different rules depending on whether it is headed for the model or for the transcript, and the reason (a re-read loop) is about the *destination*, not the content.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **A progress phase is presentation state derived from live events, never a durable event** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-21-tui-verbose-status-line.md:15` - "`step/start` enters `waiting`; an `assistant/chunk` reasoning delta or reasoning block-start enters `thinking`; a text delta or text block-start enters `responding`; a `tool/call` enters `executing`. The event map is merge-extensible, so every other event kind falls through a default and leaves the phase unchanged." The reason it is not a session event is stated in the note: a durable, model-visible phase would demand a new session event for no model benefit. August's `update_state(phase=…)` is exactly this shape, and this note is the cleanest available statement of when a phase *should* become an event (it should not) and how to derive one that cannot desync.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Modes and enforcement knobs are orthogonal axes that never read or write each other** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-07-plan-mode.md:20` - "Modes are one axis and the enforcement knobs — the sandbox mode, the approval policy — are others: they never read or write each other, matching how Codex keeps its Plan/Default collaboration presets separate from its sandbox and approval settings." August's `set_agent_mode(chat|agent|code|orchestrator)` and its separate sandbox/approval knobs are the same design; this note is the citation for *why* they must stay independent, and for the "mode definition is deployment-configured guidance the model sees, while the mode IN FORCE is session state folded from its log" split.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **A UI registry that plugins extend without a global bus event: store strings, coalesce the notification, and keep the observer list inside the service** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-24-configurable-tui-prompt-theme.md:16` - "Values are stored strings rather than callbacks … a registration, mutation, or disposal schedules one coalesced notification … That subscription is a direct in-service callback, not a Cordis event, so a value changing on its own schedule still repaints without a bus entry other consumers would never use." The rejected alternative is the interesting half: a global typed event was refused because it has exactly one consumer and would add a scoped-dispatch surface nobody observes. The containment detail is also worth stealing — a broken observer (synchronous throw, rejected promise, or an error hostile to string rendering) cannot starve the rest, and liveness is re-checked during delivery so a listener that unsubscribes another in the same burst silences it immediately.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#1]** - **Rendering must not fabricate a duration: unknown timing is drawn hollow and labelled, never as zero** - `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-26-code-mode-trajectory-waterfall-spans.md:19` - "Each lane carries a `timing` provenance tag: `measured` (pair observed), `running` (settle pending — extends to the window end at reduced opacity), or `unknown` (settle-only replay window, `callTime: null` — drawn hollow and titled 'duration unknown', never a fabricated 0 ms)." The three-valued provenance tag is a genuinely reusable pattern for any telemetry UI: distinguish *measured* from *inferred* from *unknown* in the data model, not just in the styling, so a consumer cannot mistake one for another.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Append changing runtime state as a full snapshot at the TAIL of the retained history, never as a system-prompt section** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-30-current-sandbox-policy-context.md:20` — the mechanism is a "context contribution" that renders all active contexts as ONE full snapshot with an explicit supersession statement, appended as a sourced `user/message` after retained history and before `step/start`, so a changed policy preserves the system+conversation cache prefix. August has exactly this bug class (policy/permission state changing mid-session); the measured cost of the wrong design is in the same note at line 26 — a first-time permission switch dropped cache reads to **256 tokens** against ~14.7k uncached input, because the change was in the FIRST wire message. The rule that transfers: only facts that change go in the tail, and the tail is a *replacement* snapshot, not a delta.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Say only what the resolver can actually establish** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-30-current-sandbox-policy-context.md:18` — the model-facing policy statement lists only facts shared by every enforcement dialect, and explicitly omits backend-selected temp paths, `/dev/null`, runner readiness and exact tool availability "because `resolve()` cannot establish them at request assembly". A policy block that overclaims is a liability; a policy block that underclaims is a prompt the model will contradict.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Pre-register the experiment AND the positive control, and refuse to conclude when the control fails** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-30-current-sandbox-policy-context.md:30` — the note pre-registered "preemptive refusal" as the primary endpoint and required the OLD wording to produce at least one refusal in twelve fresh sessions before any replacement could be judged; the control produced zero refusals both times, so the candidate arms were never run and the note explicitly declines to select wording on that basis. This is the pattern August needs for any "the model now behaves better" claim: a control that must fail before the treatment is allowed to be evaluated.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Make the durable event itself the lock — no process-local mutex** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-30-queued-manual-compaction.md:51` — `compaction/start` is the ONLY compaction lock: no `WeakSet`, no wrapper mutex, no locked/unlocked method split, because two authorities can disagree after replay. The same note's `Agent.runMaintenance` claims the idle phase *before* invoking the task (line 30) so a wake-up send and a maintenance task have exactly one owner of the boundary, and the end-seed scan distinguishes a LIVE unmatched start from a STALE one (line 69) so a crash-recovered session is not wedged. August's context-relief paths are exactly this shape of problem.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Markers are time points, not event containers** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-30-queued-manual-compaction.md:61` — `compaction/start`/`compaction/end` mean lock acquisition and release; they do NOT claim exclusive ownership of the events between their seqs, so a non-waking `inject()` may legitimately land inside the interval, and stability is checked only over the selected span. A design that treats a marker as a container has to forbid valid concurrent context writes.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Two event kinds, one invariant: *started ⇔ settles exactly once*** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-26-ptc-live-parallel-dispatch.md:18` — the start event is appended when the scheduler ACTUALLY starts a call, not at submission, precisely so a queued call abandoned at run settlement logs nothing and no third "abandoned" terminal event is needed (line 27). The timing pair is then the single source for duration. This is the cheapest possible pattern for August's parallel tool calls and background jobs: a start/settle pair with a stated pairing invariant and no reconciliation state.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Split a tool's "strict" and "best-effort" paths explicitly, and let the UI treat a refusal as a convergent success** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-30-web-queue-steer-action.md:28` and `:58` — the queue-row steer is STRICT (it proves `acceptsNextStep` and refuses with `steer-unavailable` rather than falling back to the best-effort alias, because a closed window would create a NEW queued occurrence at a different position and identity), while newly typed composer input uses the best-effort path because it has no existing occurrence to preserve. Both negative outcomes are then treated by the UI as "converged through Queue" with no failure notice, because that is what actually happened.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Give every accepted item its own identity, and keep the wire a full snapshot** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-29-addressable-queue-operations.md:14` and `:44` — a `MessageId` is insufficient because one immutable message may be enqueued twice, so each FIFO acceptance gets its own `InboxItemId`; the wire then carries complete queue snapshots on every change because queues are expected to be short and deterministic recovery beats delta semantics. Full snapshots also let the client apply **no optimistic edit**, which is what makes a race reportable as a real race.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Project structured results onto a persisted channel with its OWN byte budget, and be honest about truncation** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-30-search-render-card.md:26` and `:28` — the card and the model-facing text consume the SAME retention outcome (the inline cap runs once), `total` is the pre-cap count and `truncated` says the page is capped, and the meta is bounded by a separate byte cap because the item-count cap does not bound the payload. The transfer: August's structured tool outputs need (a) one retention pass shared by every renderer, (b) an explicit `truncated`/`total` pair so no UI claims completeness the model never had, and (c) a byte budget on the structured copy that persists in the log.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **One derivation per render intent, consumed by every render site** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-28-web-terminal-card.md:16` — a single `*-card-model.ts` turns the snapshot's `callView`/`resultView` pair into props so the chat row and the details panel cannot disagree about a command, its cwd or its exit status, and it returns the generic path (`null`) for every shape it does not recognise — including a `card` value this client version does not know, which arrives over the wire and cannot be trusted to be a compiled variant.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Type-check the table-pair invariant instead of documenting it** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-31-ptc-language-dispatch.md:41` — two parallel lookup tables are both `satisfies`-checked against ONE union, so a language added to one and not the other fails `typecheck`; the runtime `Object.hasOwn` guards (line 21) would only catch the drift once a second backend actually ships, i.e. at the consumer's integration point rather than where the drift was introduced. August's per-model and per-provider capability tables need the same mechanical pin.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Bound the candidate set outside the database, and fail closed at a call budget** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-27-web-session-search.md:16` — the large authorization set is kept OUT of the SQLite bindings (avoiding the portable variable ceiling) while global ranking is preserved; the provider's page size is learned downward on `SESSION_QUERY_INVALID_LIMIT` (20 → 10 → 5 → 2 → 1) and retained across continuations and stale restarts; limit probes and stale retries share one budget of 100 provider calls, and a page larger than requested, a repeated cursor or an unexhausted stream at that budget fails closed as a business error.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Model-facing wording at the model boundary, machine wording at the seam** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-03-fs-tool-error-remedy.md:14` — the recovery instruction ("— re-read the file, then retry") is appended by the TOOL package, after the sandbox mapping, while the structured `FsError` code and the `cause` chain are preserved for the retry/permission/UI layers. The rejected alternative is the instructive one: putting the remedy in the provider message leaks model-facing wording into every consumer of the seam vocabulary, and putting it in the prompt is unreliable because the failure arrives mid-task.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Enumerate the evidence tiers a third-party integration must satisfy, and refuse the cheap tiers** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-04-claude-code-and-codex-subagent-backends.md:12` — a keyless real-product test proves the official integration and teardown, a Loader composition test proves the package and documented configuration load without starting the product, and a credentialed e2e proves the production path end to end; "direct model HTTP or a product double cannot replace either product-running tier". This is the tiering August should apply to any external model/agent backend it wants to support.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Prove the model was actually sent the catalog, by reading the persisted request header** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-31-even-out-shipped-tool-rosters.md:38` — the shipped-composition smoke boots the real tree in a pseudo-terminal and reads the tool names out of the `request/header` the session log persisted, so the assertion is the catalog the model received, not the config that was supposed to produce it. The same note pins `glob`/`grep` as FIXED members because the search package registers both unconditionally (line 46) — a host-dependent pair would be an untestable surface.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Let a deployment choose a policy that the tool cannot observe, and put the choice in the tool's description** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-26-todo-parallel-in-progress.md:27` — whether several tasks may be `in_progress` depends on runtime concurrency the tool cannot see, so it becomes a REQUIRED `Config` field rather than a constant; the flag moves the model-facing description and the accepted input TOGETHER (splitting them teaches the model a rule the tool does not hold), and the durable-log invariant deliberately does NOT follow the flag so history written under one policy still replays under another.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Resolve the producer's name from the LOG, never from a client-side table** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-04-web-context-source-and-steer-marks.md:20` — the transcript names each injected context row by reading the durable `user/message.source`, so a resumed, forked or foreign log projects exactly like a live session and a renamed producer is identifiable without a client release; a dictionary keyed by plugin id drifts silently and cannot name a producer from a foreign log at all.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Hash-stamp both sides of a translated pair so translation drift is detectable** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-26-ptc-live-parallel-dispatch.i18n.yaml:5` — the `.i18n.yaml` sibling records the git blob hash of the English and the Chinese side of a note "as of the last confirmed-consistent state", re-recorded by `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <file>`. A drift check for any doc set maintained in two languages, with a command that makes the re-record trivial.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Ship privacy and telemetry decisions as a RULING TABLE, one row per decision** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-07-31-telemetry-anonymous-user-id.md:16` — the table pairs each ruling (id source, storage form, IO form, concurrency, loss semantics, write failure, report position, semconv dependency, home, separate switch) with its value and a one-line rationale, and a second table gives every rejected alternative a one-line reason. This format makes a privacy posture auditable at a glance and is directly reusable for August's own credential/telemetry decisions.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#2]** - **Assert the EFFECTIVE roster, not the configuration** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-01-windows-pwsh-default.md:42` — the unit test composes the REAL shipped bundle layers through the boot's patch algorithm and pins the effective per-platform roster (win32 pwsh, POSIX bash, base-only), rather than asserting on a config file; the effective roster is the contract. The same note refuses a second override channel (an env escape hatch) so there is one source of truth for roster decisions (line 31).
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **A cancelled turn must not destroy the work it was running** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-06-continuable-subagent-interrupt.md:14` — `Agent.cancel(cause, { keepInbox: true })` stops *only the current turn*, leaves the Activation, the handle, the descendants and the unclaimed queue intact, and returns `void` because "the cancel signal is guaranteed issued, target quiescence is not awaited". August's `message_agent` / delegated-worker path has the same shape of problem: a stopped child should keep its queued follow-ups and its identity. The transferable trick is the **parked queue**: `keepInbox` parks the pending work at idle so an interrupt never auto-starts the next queued item — the human gets a window to redirect, and an explicit waking send resumes the preserved FIFO.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Deliver a settlement notice BEFORE the ownership release, not after** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-06-manager-owned-subagent-settlement-delivery.md:34` — the failure mode is a *silently missing message with no error anywhere*: after `releaseOwnership` the settlement predicate can succeed, a watcher resumes one microtask later, finds itself childless and disposes an Agent whose `cancel()` clears the very inbox the notice is sitting in. August's `message_agent` wake-up path has the identical structure (a parent waiting on a child that settles), so the ordering rule and the "the manager holds the parent reference throughout disposal" principle transfer directly.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Derive "did the child's work actually run" from the durable inbox log, never from live state** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-06-manager-owned-subagent-settlement-delivery.md:58` — "The missing fact was never the turn's; it was the inbox's." `Inbox` logs every mutation with `removedCount` and marks cancellation `outcome: 'canceled'`, and `foldConsumedWork()` folds both vocabularies into one answer. An earlier version sampled the manager's own Activation immediately before cancelling, which could only ever see cancellations that manager was about to perform — so an ancestor's interrupt or an unloading plugin left the sample false and the notice still saying `finished`. August's `turn_outcomes` ledger and settlement notices are exactly the place this belongs.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Make the reconnect budget reset on *uptime*, not on a successful connect** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-06-mcp-client-auto-reconnect.md:20` — the stability window is *derived* from `maxDelayMs` rather than being a fifth tunable, and a connection that survives it resets the outage budget. This is the difference between "an occasionally-crashing server recovers indefinitely" and "a crash loop whose connects briefly succeed launders its budget into a restart storm" — a distinction a naive consecutive-failure counter cannot make.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Fence stale generations and serialize the resync queue** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-06-mcp-client-auto-reconnect.md:18` — a fresh transport and `Client` per generation, an `isCurrent` fence that makes stale generations inert, and one per-supervisor queue that serializes every `syncTools` call. Without the queue, two rapid `list_changed` notifications re-synced concurrently and the dispose-previous/register-next swap could double-dispose one generation and leak another. This is the general shape August needs for any reconnection or re-registration path (MCP, provider, plugin).
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Choose the completion-delivery lane from the owner's state, not from a preference** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-11-background-job-completion-wakes-an-idle-owner.md:22` — "A busy owner is injected, unchanged. An idle owner is woken with `followup()`." This is the exact fix for August's documented symptom that the model is told "you are notified in-session when a task finishes" and then the turn ends before the notice exists. The note also supplies the bound: an opt-in `maxConsecutiveWakes` cap restored by *claiming* a user message (not by its arrival), because the chain is self-exciting — a woken turn can start the job whose completion wakes it again.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **A timeout should bound the WAIT, not the work; and nothing should change hands at the timeout** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-26-shell-execute-projection-and-jobs-at-start.md:26` — "Nothing changes hands at the timeout: not the process, not the abort signal, not the output." A foreground call starts the *same* job it would have started in the background and waits on it; if the wait expires the call returns `{ kind: 'promoted', jobId, timeoutMs, output }` and the job simply keeps running. August's foreground shell currently *kills* a timed-out command and discards the work, which the note identifies as "the single most common way a long build or install failed under the agent". The companion rule — register the job **at start**, not at the timeout — is what makes a human kill possible from the first second.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **A human's cancellation must not claim the model's delivery** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-26-human-job-kill.md:18` — "A delivery claim means 'the terminal state has a committed delivery path to the model'". A human kill records the reason and leaves the settlement to the normal reporter, so the model still learns the task stopped. The note names the exact failure this prevents (Claude Code's shape: "the model learns nothing") and notes that a `notify: boolean` option was rejected because the registry cannot promise a notice — quiet delivery, unowned jobs and owner teardown all legitimately drop one.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Give the human a NON-CONSUMING read of the same stream the model drains** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-24-activity-observation-seam.md:36` — "The model keeps its consuming cursors (`job_output` semantics unchanged, zero prompt or tool changes anywhere in this work); observers get absolute offsets any number of readers can hold." The companion invariant is stated as a test, not a convention: "**No web path calls `ctx.jobs.read()`.** It consumes the single output cursor, so a browser read would silently take bytes the model's `job_output` will never see" (`.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-08-web-background-job-display.md:101`). August's `job_output` has exactly this single-cursor property, so the two-regime split is a direct template for adding a live "watch this build" panel without stealing bytes.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Price compaction pressure with the ROUTED model's own projection, while storing route-neutral facts** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-24-route-priced-image-request-pressure.md:18` — the meter's surface fold stores route-neutral facts per node and `measure()` prices them under the effective envelope's route on every call; the anchor holds its *raw materials* rather than a precomputed baseline, so a matching header reprices both the anchor and the current surface and the signed delta compares like with like. This is the template for August's image-dense compaction trigger, and for any future per-model cost difference: the replay stays single-pass and measurement stays O(surface).
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Make the config's key set literally the set the model may choose** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-08-pi-ai-per-model-reasoning-declarations.md:16` — "each key is a level selectors offer, its value the spelling dispatch sends on the wire", with `off` as a deliberate three-state key. August's per-model reasoning-effort support has the same failure mode waiting: a route-level default that a model cannot take fails the request, and the operator needs a way to say "this model accepts exactly these levels, spelled this way on the wire" without knowing the provider SDK's asymmetric absent-key rule.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Refuse an unknown configuration key instead of warning about it** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-18-pi-ai-wire-compat-surface.md:42` — "That is the posture that hid this defect for the life of the surface: an accepted write and an unchanged failure teaches the operator that the switch does not work, not that the name is wrong." The companion mechanism is a **drift gate** that classifies every upstream field as `offer` or `withhold` (`:18`) so a provider SDK upgrade fails compilation until someone classifies the new field. August's provider-adapter config has the same exposure: a schemastery-passthrough unknown key that validates, persists and is then silently dropped.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Make a user gesture a host-side pre-step injection with closed-set matching** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-08-user-explicit-skill-invocation.md:16` — scan the step's claimed messages for whitespace-bounded `/name` tokens, resolve them against a *registry* (never a guess), check `isUserInvocable`, and append the injection after every other injection of the step. The transferable part is that the gesture works identically from every entry point (typed, menu pick, TUI) and cannot be forged by external text, because only `source.kind === 'user'` messages are scanned.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Do not let a route change silently destroy a fork's prefix cache** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-18-model-selected-subagent-routes.md:24` — a fork inherits the parent's provider and model "so its copied conversation prefix remains eligible for provider-side KV Cache reuse", and changing either component "requires the new route to prefill that inherited history again, and that recomputation can dominate the delegated task's cost". This is a direct, quantified answer for August's "cache-preserving forked children" question, and the note names the only acceptable future change: a route change that retains reuse, or an interface that makes the recomputation cost explicit and bounded.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Declare delegation concurrency-safe only when it is structurally safe** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-09-parallel-subagent-delegations.md:16` — `isConcurrencySafe: () => true` justified by structure (a child works in its own session; the run never mutates the parent session; the one shared write is a commutative insertion) rather than by a runtime check. August's fail-closed parallel tool-call scheduler needs exactly this kind of structural argument, and the note's gate test (two children blocking until both have started, so hidden serialization deadlocks rather than passing silently) is the shape of test that proves it.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Pin a delegated child's approvals to `never` and TELL the child so** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-10-subagent-approval-pinned-never.md:18` — "Every in-process child is told, not trapped": a scoped `subagent:delegation` runtime-context statement says the scope was fixed at start, approval-requiring operations are rejected automatically, and a task needing wider access should end with a reported limitation instead of retries. The statement is a runtime-context contribution rather than a system-prompt section, so the deployment's system prompt stays uniform across parents and children.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Let the durable child log own the delegation-time policy snapshot** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-10-continuable-subagent-policy-inheritance.md:16` — capture before the first await, and on cold resume append nothing, because "replaying the log IS the state". The consequence is the one August needs: "a parent switch between residency epochs never retroactively changes a durable child."
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Exploit the forward-only, line-based nature of tokenizers to make streaming cheap** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-20-web-streaming-fence-highlight.md:17` — "a line's tokens depend only on its own text and the grammar state entering it, so appended text never changes a completed line's tokens", so the session caches completed lines' spans *plus* the grammar state after them and publishes only newly completed lines. The general lesson — look for the monotonicity in the expensive operation and cache the boundary, not the result.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Refuse to show a partial subtotal where a complete bill is implied** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-24-web-per-turn-token-usage.md:16` — every started attempt must close with safe non-negative integer usage *and* an exact total; "incomplete or contradictory evidence produces no row", because "a lower-bound subtotal presented in a completed Turn footer is indistinguishable from a complete bill". Directly applicable to August's per-turn usage chip, where the same reasoning applies to the *cached-hit* percentage.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Disambiguate "finished while you were away" with three disjoint signals** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-06-session-completed-done-dot.md:14` — green = finished and unviewed, amber = awaiting the operator's input, blue = running, with the reminder owned by the manager (so every surface projects the same bit), surviving connection generations but not a page reload, and detected eagerly at every list mutation and pull because "a snapshot-build-time-only pass would collapse two consecutive status frames into one observation and miss the completion".
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Give the model a *reversible* stop on a child, and keep the human's window open** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-06-continuable-subagent-interrupt.md:14` (see first bullet) — the authority union is deliberately *wider* for stop than for delivery, because stopping is idempotent and delivers no content; and the address-based `{kind:'user'}` variant touches no live parent, which is what keeps a child stoppable while its parent is offline.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#3]** - **Model-visible and human-visible surfaces need separate seams, and the provider owns both** — `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-07-web-inline-file-mentions.md:18` — the renderer owns no vocabulary; the provider behind an optional service decides what names a file *and* registers the prompt paragraph that asks the model to use the accepted spelling. The result is a feature whose model-visible half is a **constant** prompt section, so it "remains cacheable across Turns" — a UI nicety that does not damage the provider prefix cache.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Never make a bound silently park work the model cannot see — prefer an observable cost over an unobservable stall.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-22-unbounded-completion-wakes-by-default.md:18` — the shipped cap of 3 woke an idle owner three times, then injected the fourth notice into a next-step inbox that nothing would ever drain, while the client rendered no pending indicator: the session sat with an invisible notice that looked like a hang, and the `tool-jobs` prompt's promise ("notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll") had quietly become false. The fix was to make the cap **default-off** and to state the trade outright — the chain spends model requests the user can watch and stop, an invisible stall costs a night. August's turn bounds, subagent caps and budget ladder should each be audited for the same shape: a bound that *defers* work to a place the model (or the user) never looks at is worse than no bound.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Project a run/event stream from the durable log at its commit points, and bound every field.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-09-headless-machine-readable-run-surface.md:55` (projection only from a committed `assistant/message`, never live attempt deltas) and `:58` (every string/object key ≤ 8 KiB, every serialized line ≤ 32 KiB, nested payloads cut at 64 levels, `__proto__` copied as data, `1e400` kept as raw text, the terminal `final` event deliberately unbounded). August's `turn_end`/`turn_outcomes` records and any SSE frame the harness emits for an external supervisor should be built as a *projection* of the session log, not a parallel writer — and every field should have a stated bound, because an unbounded field in a supervisor stream is a denial-of-service vector against whoever parses it.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A tool result that is not an append must not be projected as one.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-09-headless-machine-readable-run-surface.md:57` — a compaction replacement of an older `tool_result` is *history*; projecting it emits a call id with no matching `tool_call`, and the consumer's pairing logic breaks. August's `surfaceOp` / compaction paths should carry the same discriminator, and any consumer that pairs calls with results must filter on it.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Adopt-only session identity: refuse to create a session under an id the caller named.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-09-headless-machine-readable-run-surface.md:67` — creating the requested id when no log exists "would let a mistyped or stale id silently open an empty history that the supervisor believes it is continuing". The companion checks are worth copying wholesale: the requested id must match the persisted cwd, must not be a preset/fork/subagent session, must not already be live in the process, and is re-checked after the idle wait. August's session-resume and MCP-session paths should treat "the caller named this id" as a *claim about the past*, and verify it rather than honour it.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Tell the model when the route changed, as history — not as a system prompt.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-07-model-switch-notice.md:14` — `installModelSelection` compares the selection captured during prompt assembly with the latest durable request header, and on a mismatch appends an identified user-role message `[model changed: assistant turns above this point were generated by <previous>; the session continues with <next>]` to the `agent/pre-step` decision that would send a request. The stated reason for not using the system prompt is the transferable part: a transient prompt change "would not be reconstructable from the session log and would not mark the exact point where ownership of assistant turns changed". August swaps models mid-session too (per-model profiles, family fallbacks) — the fact belongs in the transcript, at the seam, or the new model will mis-attribute a previous model's limitation to itself.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Bound WIDE delegation with a live pool, and reject rather than wait when the pool is full.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-15-continuable-activation-capacity.md:26` — "Waiting for capacity can deadlock when every slot belongs to a parent waiting for a descendant. Full pools reject with an actionable diagnostic instead of retaining queued activation requests." The pool is per live parent, shared by reference through continuable parent links, and the owner is excluded (`:14`) — a cumulative child count was rejected because it does not release capacity when useful work finishes, and counting model requests was rejected because it omits waiting parents, queued inbox work, reconstruction and cleanup. August's subagent spawner should carry a *live* concurrency budget with a reject-and-diagnose path, never a cumulative counter and never a blocking wait.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A run belongs to the job registry, not to the tool step that started it.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-01-workflow-run-in-background.md:18` — the engine starts inside the job starter with **no** `exec.signal`, so the returning tool step's abort cannot kill work the model deliberately detached; `job_kill`, the job list's stop control and owner teardown are the only cancellation paths, and each forwards its reason into `run.cancel`. August's background-tool surface has the same trap: bridging turn-abort into a detached job turns "cancel this turn" into "kill my long job".
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Snapshot the working tree with a PRIVATE git index so the user's repository gains no objects and the user's uncommitted work becomes the baseline.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-11-turn-changed-files-card.md:16` — `add --all` into a private index seeded from the repository's index, then `write-tree`, both writing into a Session-owned temporary object directory with the repo's object store attached read-only as an alternate; the two tree ids are diffed with `diff-tree -r -M --numstat`. Because the baseline includes the user's earlier uncommitted work, the summary contains exactly the turn's changes and a commit the model makes mid-turn cannot hide them. August's "files changed this turn" card should use this shape rather than diffing against `HEAD` (which attributes the user's work to the turn).
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **The card's lifetime equals the content's lifetime, not the log's — so the log carries only an index.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-11-turn-changed-files-card.md:26` — "The log deliberately carries nothing but the turn number. Summaries, snapshot trees, and captured copies live only as long as the Session in the Host process … a card whose content the Host can no longer open should not appear at all." August's session log is durable and its UI is not; anything the UI offers must either survive a restart or be explicitly scoped to the live process. The same note's per-Session temp directory replaced a shared per-repository store because the shared store "needed two configuration fields, and made a Session's snapshot fail when another Session discarded the store".
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Compare uncovered files from whole-file copies, with a hard byte cap and a timeout that degrades to a coarse hunk.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-15-changed-file-diff-preview.md:18` — `maxFileBytes` caps a copy and a snapshot blob read, a larger file is listed `oversized` *without counts* and its comparison is refused, and `diffTimeoutMs` (100 ms) degrades the comparison to one hunk replacing every line, marked `coarse`. Two sides that both exceed the cap are listed `oversized` rather than dropped, "since unread content is never known to be unchanged". August's diff surfaces should degrade *visibly* rather than silently truncate.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Configuration that grants a capability must be withheld until an accepted value arrives, and an absent response is never consent.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-20-developer-tools-default-on.md:16` — "Host-backed clients publish disabled until an accepted schema-resolved value arrives. Loading, failed initial reads and an unavailable namespace do not grant interactive-preview capabilities … the client does not interpret an absent response as consent to enable scripts." The reason is the one August repeats in its own docs: "unmounting a scripted HTML iframe cannot undo scripts or requests already executed". Any August toggle that turns on script execution, network access or a tool surface must be fail-closed at the moment of uncertainty, even when the eventual value is permissive.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Classify an error at the route that owns the credential, and keep the durable record provider-neutral.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-18-account-quota-top-up.md:14` and `:16` — the account plugin's credential callback releases the token only for the configured inference origin, and it rewrites the provider-neutral `QUOTA` into `ACCOUNT_QUOTA` for both HTTP 402 and in-band SSE errors, while the API-key route keeps `QUOTA`; the durable terminal-error record keeps the request-time code so the transcript, history paging and session log "do not depend on current credentials". The rule behind it — "current endpoint, key, and login state may differ from the facts of a historical failed request" — is exactly August's problem when a provider key is rotated and old sessions are reopened.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Classify tool-call surface by *configuration*, not by connection health.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-13-mcp-resources-in-profiles.md:18` — "Connection health does not determine this visibility. An active client remains configured through failed requests and reconnect attempts; its shared resource tools and server-name guidance stay available, and calls report connection failures." The rejected alternative is instructive: filtering by *negotiated capability* would make visibility require a successful capability exchange, so the tool set would flicker. August's MCP and provider surfaces should keep their schemas stable across a reconnect and let the call fail instead.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A redundant permission request that asks for nothing new must not be fatal.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-16-sandbox-same-mode.md:14` — `approveEscalation` returns the effective mode immediately when the requested mode matches it; wider modes still require approval and narrower or unsupported targets still fail. The stated reason: rejecting every non-widening request "prevents authorized work without preventing any permission increase". August's `sandbox_permissions` re-assertion path is the same case, and the ACP `fs-same-mode` snapshot is a good shape for a regression: verify an unrestricted write with **no approval events**.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A path is addressed by machines; a label is addressed by people — never let one string be both.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-23-language-neutral-default-workspace-naming.md:16` — the directory name and stored title are one fixed, language-neutral constant (`default-workspace`), published from a pure import-free subpath "so client bundles inline it rather than requesting a module-table row the package does not publish"; only the on-screen label is localized, and the rename dialog decides "did this change?" by comparing the **stored** title, not the displayed one. August's workspace/root naming is addressed by shell commands, tool arguments, `@path` references, session logs and backups — it must not depend on the UI language that happened to be active at install.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Apply a vocabulary only after the message settles, or a frozen streaming block will cache it.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-07-session-prose-local-media-display.md:16` — "Like `fileMentions`, it applies only after a message settles so frozen streaming blocks cannot cache a vocabulary handler." August's markdown renderer has the same hazard with any post-settle transformation (file links, media, code fences): a handler installed during streaming gets captured by the frozen block and applied forever.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Per-tab state, not per-file state, when two views of one thing can be open at once.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-05-sidebar-text-preview-and-file-tree.md:40` — "Bucketing by tab, not by file, is deliberate — two tabs of one file scroll independently"; and `:44` — "A changed file is announced, not applied", because reloading under the reader loses their place and an agent-written file changes repeatedly. August's own "two tabs of one file" case (a file preview and a diff review of the same file) should keep two independent view states, and any live-refresh of a file the user is reading should be an announcement rather than an in-place replacement.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Announce a change, do not apply it, when the file is changing under the reader.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-05-sidebar-text-preview-and-file-tree.md:44` — the body compares the loaded version with the observed version and shows a change bar; "Reload rereads only this tab … and does not mutate shared resource metadata or another tab." The rejected alternative is the interesting part: refreshing under the reader "loses their place, and a file the agent is writing changes repeatedly."
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **One constant for a bound, read by every place the bound is stated.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-24-fixed-rate-floor-one-minute.md:14` — `MIN_EVERY_INTERVAL_SECONDS` is read by the Host decoder, the create and update validation, the `every_seconds` tool parameter description and the refusal message, "so one change moves the bound everywhere the Host states it"; the client keeps its own copy for per-unit floors. August's budget/round/tool-output ceilings are stated in many places (tool descriptions, refusal messages, UI hints, docs) — this is the shape that keeps them from drifting.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Read the environment from the account record, interactively, and protect the app's own namespace.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-28-desktop-login-shell-environment.md:14` — one delimited `env -0` dump through `<shell> -ilc` using the **account record's** login shell (not `$SHELL`, which a Dock launch inherits from launchd), in interactive mode (because `~/.zshrc` is only read by interactive shells), with `DSH_*` and `ELECTRON_*` protected from being replaced — "Desktop resolves `DSH_HOME` and its profile paths before the read". The delimiter is the right completion signal: "waiting for stdout to close" turns every read into a timeout when a startup file backgrounds a process.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Publish the *preference*, not the resolved value, when a native surface must keep following the OS.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-13-macos-hidden-titlebar-vibrancy.md:20` — `html[data-ds-theme-source]` carries `light` / `dark` / `system`, and forwarding `system` "lets macOS keep following the OS appearance natively", while forwarding `light`/`dark` would "freeze the window material at the value resolved at send time". August's theme and native-window decisions should carry the intent, not the resolution.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Suppress only the ring paint; keep the DOM focus.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-20-focus-ring-brand-primary.md:22` — in pointer modality, `:focus-visible:not(:read-write)` controls use a transparent ring colour while "selected-state borders and elevation shadows remain, and editable text controls keep their own focus feedback on click. DOM focus stays on the control." The rejected alternative explains it: calling `blur()` "would hide its ring but also remove the target for subsequent Enter or Space activation". A generalisable UI rule for August's desktop surface.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A dismissed surface stays dismissed: give the dismissal an identity, not just a flag.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-14-composer-selection-keyboard.md:28` — `InputTriggerController` records the identity of the hit the user closed (Escape / Shift+Tab, a pointer dismissal, or a settling pick), and a re-track of that same token with the same query leaves the menu closed, "so restoring the caret after a dismissal (or a settled command closing the surface it opened) cannot revive it. A new query or another token re-arms it." August's composer/panel surfaces reopen on focus and re-render; a token-keyed dismissal rule is what stops a dismissed panel from springing back.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A keyboard contract that mirrors the surface it belongs to, applied once and inherited everywhere.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-14-composer-selection-keyboard.md:18` — Enter/Tab settle, Escape/Shift+Tab leave, and the *shared* `Menu` primitive adopts the pairing, so the composer's permission seat, the preset chip, file cards and the settings dropdowns all get it "at once"; and the composer's own `focus()` is used to restore the caret "where the draft left it rather than at the start", because "the owner of the caret is the only party that can restore it". August's own composer surfaces should share one primitive and one focus-return method rather than each re-implementing dismissal.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A denial that asks for no additional permission should return immediately; a denial that asks for more must not be silent.** (Sandbox and update-policy pairing.) `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-11-desktop-mandatory-update-client.md:18` — a flattened `40005` establishes blocking independently of the optional title/detail/page fields, and "Transport, JSON, business-code, or HTTP failures cannot clear a known block. Only a valid fresh no-force response clears it." The transferable pattern: a *block* may be established by a minimal code, but only a complete, fresh, valid response may lift it — every failure mode must leave the block in place.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A failure that is confirmed but unsuccessful is a distinct outcome from a failure that is not confirmed.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-11-desktop-mandatory-update-client.md:32` — "Host exit and successful task teardown are separate outcomes. The process owner reports confirmed but unsuccessful exit with a dedicated error type. Backend cleanup can complete for that outcome while installation still fails; the shell restores the current-version Host and requires fresh installation confirmation without clearing mandatory policy." August's turn-end reasons (`finished | length | cap | stall-stop | budget | error | interrupted | awaiting-input`) already encode this idea; the transferable part is the *cleanup* half — a confirmed teardown still permits backend cleanup, and the retry does not need to redo it.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A change is announced by a diffable, bounded artifact, not by a re-render of the thing under the user.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-11-turn-changed-files-card.md:14` — the `workspace/changes` event "is log-only and never model-visible", and the summary is served through a service rather than the log. August's turn summary should be served, not logged, whenever it carries content — and the same split explains why the log carries only a turn number.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Give a model a *code* to look up, and a durable id to group by — never encode structure in free text.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-08-feedback-dialog-and-categories.md:26` — "a prefix in free text is not filterable without parsing and would leak into the verbatim note that telemetry uploads; a durable id in the payload is what a consumer can group by." The companion rule is that the taxonomy must be **restated** in the client as a `Record<Category, true>` because the client-bundle purity gate forbids a value import from a Host package, with completeness checked by the compiler. August's skill categories, memory kinds and tool taxonomies should follow both halves.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A tool call that asks for the mode already in force must not be fatal — and the argument contract stays mandatory.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-16-sandbox-same-mode.md:14` — `approveEscalation` returns the effective mode when the requested mode matches it, while "Argument pairing remains mandatory at the tool. Wider modes still require approval; narrower and unsupported targets still fail."
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Model-input changes are applied through a *draft* until the user starts, and the completion marker is written last.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-16-desktop-onboarding.md:18` — "Completion applies Chat and shared developer-tool preferences before saving the done marker, so a refused preference write cannot silently finish onboarding"; and the three writes are ordered but **not one transaction**, so a retry can re-apply the same preference after a failed completion write. August's own settings+onboarding paths should use the same order and be honest that the sequence is not atomic.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **Per-model capability declaration must be non-empty and must be the same gesture in every adapter.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-16-unified-model-input-controls.md:24` — "DeepSeek rejects an empty list and pi-ai treats it as inheritance. Keeping a nonempty selection prevents the same gesture from meaning different things across adapters." The companion: an undeclared field must *display* the inherited capability without materialising an override on open, and disabling a capability must also clear the settings the adapter refuses to save with it (DeepSeek's image limits).
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A shared "capability" switch that changes *what is rendered*, not merely what is visible.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-17-developer-tools-settings.md:18` — turning the switch off filters the available View roster and **remounts** the HTML context, because "previously selected diagnostic content and already-running scripts would survive the toggle"; the basic mode strips `href` attributes, resource hints and SVG animation and mounts an iframe with a CSP denying scripts and external resources, while the advanced mode gains no parent-origin, popup, form or top-navigation privileges.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A file that changed under the user is not an error — it is a different file.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-08-file-display-through-filesystem.md:30` — "the local sandbox provider constrains mutations and permits reads; an authenticated client therefore has broader access than registered workspace roots." The same note's "Encoded byte limits do not bound decoded pixel dimensions" is the kind of limit that must be *stated* rather than assumed: a 20 MiB compressed image can still be a decompression bomb.
- **[dsh-notes-arch-feature#4]** - **A `present`-style delivery must be a snapshot, and the authorization must be a saved coordinate triple — never a browser-supplied path.** `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-09-present-filesystem-access.md:18` and `.agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-09-08-web-explicit-file-delivery.md:16` — download and native-open requests authorize a reference by "the viewed Session, event sequence, and file index"; the event stores no Session ID, so a forked history uses the child's own log. And a native open must require a *verified round trip* through the composed filesystem — "a same-named local file never substitutes for an unmapped provider file."

- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **One Steer send operation for a whole roster, and say explicitly what `accepted` does not mean** — `.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-08-30-team-send-message-steer.md:16` — Every Team member gets one `send_message({target, message})` with fixed Steer scheduling (running target → next step boundary; idle → new turn; inactive → cold resume); the durable snapshot has no scheduling field, and `accepted`/`queued` are defined as *inbox* outcomes that explicitly do not mean the target completed the work. - **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Delegate interruption and teardown to the one owner of the child's lifecycle** — `.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-08-12-trim-agent-teams-read-and-lifecycle-surface.md:30` — Team `interrupt()` resolves the roster name and delegates to `SubagentService.interrupt()` with exact ancestor authority (the old code called `Agent.cancel()` directly, bypassing authorization); teardown selects the roster's exact live direct-child ids and calls `drainContinuableChildren(parent, childIds)`, which releases descendants child-first, leaves siblings and parent-wide admission alone, and treats absent targets as no-ops. Why it matters for August: August has both an Agent.cancel-style door and a continuation/roster door; the note shows the exact shape of "the roster chooses *which* children; the lifecycle owner does the releasing" — and why draining the whole lineage (the tempting simplification) would stop unrelated work.
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **A check is worth publishing only if two observations can independently diverge** — `.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-08-28-omit-unneeded-invariant-companions.md:18` — 209 packages published an `./invariant` companion that asserted nothing, and one published a probe that mutated and inspected the same route table it claimed to verify. The criterion kept is "can compare observations that may independently diverge" (cross-event protocols, event-vs-authoritative-state, multi-producer assembly, durable data folded by a different operation). Why it matters for August: August's `check:*` static gates have exactly this shape; the note supplies the test for "is this gate real?" — if the only observation comes from the same writer, it is a unit test wearing a gate's clothes — plus the governance rule that the omission is recorded in the package's README with a package-specific reason.
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Measure the hot path, then measure it again with alternating pairs in fresh processes** — `.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-09-07-file-content-scan.md:14` — `contentHasFile` replaced recursive `Array.some` with direct iteration: nine **alternating** original/candidate pairs, each in a fresh plain-Node process receiving a copy of one native-V3 seed; the median improved 11.54% and all nine pairs improved (4.871–12.243 ms), with a separate five-pair scan probe over 5,601 frozen messages. Why it matters for August: the method transfers verbatim — alternating pairs kill drift, fresh processes kill warm-cache bias, and "the hot source is identical at both sampled revisions, so these observations do not establish PR causality" is the honesty clause that keeps a benchmark from becoming a story. The same pairing discipline is applied to the request-freeze note, which reports a contaminated run as *retained but not used as calibration evidence*.
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Never validate the same input twice on two sides of the wire** — `.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-09-15-host-only-remote-input-validation.md:16` — The client checks descriptor *integrity* at mount time but does not execute invocation codecs; the Host Gateway is the single runtime input-validation authority (exact named fields, strict codecs, JSON verification, lookup before business call). Why it matters for August: August's FastAPI backend is already the validation authority, so any client-side re-validation is duplicated cost and a second failure path — and the note names the security consequence honestly (undeclared properties may cross the carrier before the Host codec removes them, so callers must construct the declared DTO rather than rely on client parsing as a redaction step).
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Collapse every overdue recurrence into one batch and catch up only the latest occurrence** — `.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-08-09-bounded-fixed-rate-schedule.md:16` — Pure integer arithmetic picks the latest creation-anchor-aligned occurrence at or before one decision time; every distinct overdue record contributes exactly one occurrence and the whole batch shares one decision time; missed occurrences are never enumerated, persisted or replayed. Why it matters for August: August has scheduled automations and a Bot path that nobody watches; this is the shape that bounds a cold start to *current* work instead of a backlog whose size depends on downtime.
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Replace JS layout probing with CSS width bands** — `.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-09-01-css-produced-file-layout.md:16` — The produced-files row became an inline-size query container: CSS bands hide trailing chips and select a pre-rendered localized `+ N files` label, so `ProducedFiles` has no resize observer, layout effect, layout state or geometry read. Why it matters for August: August's chat UI renders produced-file chips and pays a forced layout on mount and on every resize; the note's rejection of the "observe the row" alternative ("one observer and width-driven React state per mounted result row even though CSS already receives the same width") is the argument for pushing this decision into the stylesheet.
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Fixture clocks must be pinned on both sides and re-applied, not frozen** — `.agents/notes/archived/testing/2026-09-26-web-conversation-clock-fixture-day.md:24` — `pinBrowserClock` re-applies one frozen instant from the anchor **on an interval** because product code reads two `Date.now()` values to decide how long to hold a rendered value (a 150 ms title hold, a 10 ms composition guard); a permanently frozen clock means the hold never elapses and the settled text never renders. Why it matters for August: any golden that asserts relative time ("2 minutes ago") needs both the browser clock and the Host clock pinned, and the pinning must not stop time from advancing for two-reading holds. The note also shows the wrong fix being measured and rejected (collapsing the date prefix in the ARIA normaliser broke three other goldens).
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **One environment variable, one budget — for cases *and* hooks** — `.agents/notes/archived/testing/2026-08-29-windows-lane-hook-and-lefthook-budget.md:20` — `coverageTestTimeoutArgs` now emits `--hookTimeout` beside `--testTimeout` and `--expect.poll.timeout`, because setup and teardown pay the same contention and raising only the test budget "moves a contended suite's failure from the case to its teardown rather than removing it". Why it matters for August: August's CI story is entirely static checks today; when a budgeted test lane appears, this is the shape that avoids two knobs describing one property of the host, and the note is explicit that the trade (losing detection of a real slowdown into tens of seconds) is deliberate.
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Property-test the protocol-shaped code, with generators biased toward adversarial interleavings** — `.agents/notes/archived/testing/2026-06-11-property-based-testing.md:8` — One `fast-check` suite per protocol-shaped package (chunk assembly, event log, schema conversion, agent-loop scheduling), with generators tuned for *realistic-but-adversarial* inputs, `numRuns` bounded so the suite stays under ~10 s, and failures printing a reproducible seed. Why it matters for August: the motivating evidence here is the transferable one — "a block-assembly ordering bug once survived 100% line coverage of the happy paths" — and the suite found a real duplicate-`block-end` bug on its first run. For August's stream assembler and inbox scheduler, per-file 100% coverage is exactly the evidence that does *not* prove interleaving correctness.
- **[dsh-notes-archived-rest#3]** - **Read the roster from the bundles; never copy it into the test package** — `.agents/notes/archived/testing/2026-09-06-client-assembly-test-line.md:20` — `bundleRoster` parses each bundle's `dsh.bundle.patch` with the include plugin's own `entryListSchema` and composes the layers with its `applyEntryPatches`, keeping enabled rows whose package declares the web client platform; the whole-client tier then boots those rows through the production `bootClient`/`mountClient` with a single Connection substitution. Why it matters for August: a copied roster in a test helper is a second source of truth that silently drifts; deriving it from the composition means "the product's default tool set" is always the product's default tool set. The same note's discipline — assert against *product facts* (the real section list, the real declarer, a Loader rebuild) — is what makes such a tier worth the five-seconds-cold boot it costs.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Make the LLM message history a *projection* over an append-only event log, so replay, fork and compaction are structural rather than bolted on.** `2026-06-11-event-sourced-sessions.md:13` — "A `Session` is an append-only log of typed `SessionEvent`s — the single source of truth. The LLM message history is *derived* from the log (`deriveMessages()`)". Why it transfers to August: August already persists a session log, but its model history is a separately maintained list; making the list a fold over the log makes "what did the model see" a question with one answer, and makes fork a seed rather than a copy. The same note's rejection of "a mutable message array with events fired as notifications" (line 21) is the argument: with event sourcing, log/state divergence is structurally impossible.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **State the cache goal as a corollary, not a feature: "Model-visible ⟺ durably referenced", with prefix stability emerging from an append-only log projected by a pure per-node function.** `2026-07-05-reconstructable-requests.md:17` and `:19` — "Prefix-cache stability is corollary #1, not the headline: an append-only log projected by a per-node pure function yields requests that are append-extensions of their predecessors whenever the header is unchanged — stability is emergent, not managed." Why it transfers: August's prompt caching is currently managed by hand (keeping tool schemas and the system prompt stable). The mechanism to copy is *not* a cache hack — it is (a) the system prompt becoming a log-owned surface node, (b) the request "header" (config + tool schemas) being snapshotted durably on every real change, and (c) per-call request scalars being **forbidden** (the note rejects them at line 41 because "a listener could flip the model per call with zero accounting, silently abandoning the provider cache this design exists to protect"). The bonus is the production cache signal it derives: per-step usage, where "a header change or compaction appears as a cache-read drop on the next step" (line 31).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Put the system prompt on the surface as node 0, so a prompt change is a surface *replacement* and the prompt can never be shadowed by compaction.** `2026-09-02-system-prompt-as-surface-node.md:17` ("The system prompt lives on the surface"), `:33` (`assertSystemHeadRewrite` rejects a replacement covering node 0 unless the replacing event is itself a `system/message` covering exactly that node), `:81` ("node 0 is never compacted" is enforced in the replace operation itself). Why it transfers: August currently carries the system prompt in a place that is neither the message list nor the event log, so every reader re-derives it, and a compaction that anchors at the head can swallow it. The "protected head" trick (`:31` — an *empty* rendered prompt still occupies node 0, projecting to `null`) is the part that is easy to miss and hard to reinvent.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Normalise every provider failure into ONE structured, JSON-serialisable payload at the runtime boundary, and log the retry as a durable event so a silent backoff is visible.** `2026-06-21-bounded-llm-request-recovery.md:32` (the `LlmFailure` shape: `message`, `code`, `status?`, `providerRetryAfterMs?`, `requestId?`) and `:102` ("adapters report facts while deployment policy decides action" — the payload deliberately has no `retryable` field; the same refusal is stated at `:41`). The durable-status mechanism is at `:63` and the UI consequence at `:85` ("the Web countdown anchors the scheduled delay to browser receipt rather than the Host event clock"). Why it transfers: August's `_retryWaitRefusalMs` and its eight-family error taxonomy are exactly this shape but currently live in prose; adopting a single serialisable failure fact plus a durable retry event would let August's UI show *why* it is waiting and for how long — the note's diagnosis is that "a long silent wait looks like a stalled loop" (`:19`).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Split timeout into "the library notifies" and "the capability kills", and never race a promise against a deadline.** `2026-07-06-timeout-deadline-library.md:19` ("there is deliberately no central 'timeout service' that would have to know how to stop every capability's work") and `:114` (a `withTimeout(promise, ms)` wrapper was rejected because it "resolves the *tool-call* promise on deadline without stopping the underlying work — the child process or fetch socket leaks on"). The classification rule at `:71` (`timeoutOf(signal, code)` — "`code` scopes the match to this deadline's timer", so a nested deadline does not steal the outer one's classification) is the transferable bit. Why it transfers: August's tool timeouts are per-implementation; this turns the common half into one library and forces every capability to state *how it actually stops* — and the division-of-labor table at `:79-88` is a ready-made checklist for finding August's missing timeouts.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Enforce the tool-call budget as a plugin on a new around-dispatch waterfall, and put the catch *inside* the base `next()`.** `2026-07-07-tool-call-timeout-policy.md:37` ("That the catch is the base `next` — not something outside the waterfall — is load-bearing: when a provider sees the timeout signal and throws its own upstream-abort error, registry dispatch first converts it to a normal error result, and only then can `timeout-policy` replace the final result with `TOOL_TIMEOUT`"). The mechanism detail at `:57` is that the deadline is installed by *in-place mutation of `exec.signal`*, because a Cordis waterfall's `next()` ignores arguments and re-invokes downstream listeners with the shared payload. Why it transfers: August's per-tool timeout fields are exactly the "budget declared on the tool" shape this note adopts (`:43`), and the `exec.signal`-mutation trick is the part that is non-obvious enough to be worth stealing outright.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Record whether a cancelled tool body ever ran: `ABORTED` vs `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH`.** `2026-07-19-cooperative-tool-cancellation.md:31` and `:33` — "It applies whenever cancellation prevents body invocation, including pre-aborted entry, cancellation during pre-policy or approval, an aborted wrapper signal, a wrapper success overtaken by caller cancellation before delegation, and agent-loop siblings skipped after turn cancellation." Why it transfers: August's receipts and its `is_error` classification both need to know whether side effects were possible; a single undifferentiated `ABORTED` cannot say it, and the note explains why that matters for durable consumers (`:13`).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Collapse the two representations of a provider failure (throw vs terminal `finish` chunk) into one, and delete the sidecar.** `2026-07-29-terminal-llm-stream-failures.md:17` — "`LlmRuntime` is the normalization boundary for one adapter attempt. It catches only final-adapter selection, synchronous dispatch, iterator construction, and `next()` failures, converts the thrown value to immutable `LlmFailure`, and emits one terminal `finish`." The scope rule at `:19` ("The adapter-owned catch ends before each yielded chunk") is what keeps middleware and assembly bugs from being misfiled as provider outages. Why it transfers: August's provider adapters speak at least three wire formats (OpenAI, Anthropic, responses) and its error handling has to work across all of them; one normalisation boundary plus one terminal protocol is the mechanism, and the note's stated benefit is deletion (`:37`).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Make a cancelled stream *finalise* the prefix the user already saw, as a durable `assistant/message` with `interrupted: true`.** `2026-08-10-cancelled-stream-prefix-finalize.md:15` — "It appends that prefix as the step's `assistant/message` with `interrupted: true`, `surfaceOp: 'append'`, and the exact embedded timed stream. The append precedes the committed `agent/assistant-stream` end frame, `step/end`, and the aborted `turn/end`." Why it transfers: August's cancel path currently loses text that the user read — the note's diagnosis is exact: "A follow-up such as 'expand on your second point' then lacks text the user read, and a fork at the cancelled turn inherits the same gap" (`:9`). The negative decision at `:27` (no synthetic aborted tool results, because those "would claim an execution outcome that did not occur") is the part that keeps the record honest.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Keep the provider-side cache alive across subagents: the child gets the *same* tool schema and the *same* system prompt, and the return instruction rides the child's initial user task.** `2026-08-27-adjacent-agent-steer-messaging.md:49` and `2026-08-10-fork-children-stay-one-shot.md:17` — "The globally registered model tool is registered globally for every Agent in a composition. A continuable forked child therefore receives the same tool name, description, schema, and ordering as its parent. Its initial task is appended after the inherited Session seed." The rule at `2026-08-27-adjacent-agent-steer-messaging.md:49` is that a child-only tool or prompt section "preceded every inherited fork turn … forcing the provider to prefill the entire copied transcript again" (`:13`). Why it transfers: August has a fork and a subagent path; this is the concrete rule for not defeating the prefix cache when a child needs to talk back to its parent.
