- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Route by *provider*, keep model ids out of the registry, and make replay state portable only within the adapter that owns both providers.** `2026-07-14-provider-routed-llm-adapters.md:25` ("A provider has exactly one adapter owner in a Cordis context … loading both owners is a configuration error rather than an ordering rule or fallback") and `:82` (replay state is portable only within the adapter instance that owns *both* the historical and target providers; a different adapter receives provider-neutral content only). The "provider is the registration key" rule at `:23` is the fix for August's per-model `apiFormat` sprawl: August currently overrides the provider format per model, whereas this note makes the *provider* the unit of ownership and treats "one adapter per provider" as a configuration error.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Let the adapter own exact-route capacity; let the consumer own compaction policy; keep the token meter model-agnostic with one fold and no model profiles.** `2026-07-20-routed-model-context-and-compaction-policy.md:17` (`LlmAdapter.resolveModel(provider, model, signal?)` returns capacity metadata), `:23` ("`dsh-token-meter` has no configuration and no model profiles … prevents replay accounting from becoming another model registry") and `:27` (`modelPolicies` keyed by the exact `{provider, model}` pair, with `thresholdRatio` default 0.8 and `retainRatio` default 0.16). Why it transfers: August compacts per model with a configurable ratio; the transferable piece is the *ownership split* plus the two-cap trigger at `:29` (`floor(min(W × thresholdRatio, W − O − headroomTokens))`, default headroom 65,536) — the second cap is the one most implementations miss, and it exists to leave room for the compaction *output* after a full generation.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Version the session log with one integer, read *directionally*, and make an unknown event refuse by default unless it is explicitly marked ignorable.** `2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md:19` (direction-aware refusal: equal reads normally, newer refuses and names the direction, older runs the adjacent chain in memory and leaves the source bytes and inode untouched) and `:21` ("the default is *required*: forgetting the marker over-refuses a resumable session (an inconvenience), while a default of ignorable would make the same mistake silently resume a gutted one (a safety failure)"). Why it transfers: this is the forward-compatibility contract for a durable log, and the asymmetry — *refuse by default, opt in to ignorance* — is the rule August would want if it ever ships a format other readers must open. The follow-up pair (`2026-08-30-retain-ignorable-external-session-events.md:15` and `2026-08-31-alpha-historical-unknown-event-refusal.md:15`) shows the second half: *equal-version read* tolerates a marked event, *migration* refuses it anyway because an opaque payload may hold references a format edge cannot validate.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Migrate a released log format with a stateful streaming stage pipeline, not a whole-artifact conversion — the numbers are the argument.** `2026-08-31-released-session-format-migrations.md:52` (one input may emit zero, one or many outputs *without* allocating a temporary return array or retaining an internal output queue) and the measured table at `:194-199` (the whole-artifact path OOMs a 16 GB process at ≥7.219 GB on a 116 MB log; the streaming path restores in 6.241 s with 477 MB retained, folding 9,143,111 v0 events into 72,784 v2 events). The companion preparation note gives the second half: prepare once, publish only for a writer — `2026-09-05-read-only-session-migration-preparation.md:29` ("Read open waits only for preparation. Write open reuses a matching preparation and waits for publication before returning a writable handle"), with the measured 53 % faster first content (`:132-145`). Why it transfers: any harness that must migrate its own log format should do it as a stage pipeline, and a read-only "open history" should never pay for a write publication.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Do not let a live-only frame carry durable state across two independent streams; make it a replayable projection instead.** `2026-07-29-projected-token-usage-and-request-context.md:41` — the note records implementing an atomic request-boundary snapshot and then *rejecting* it, because "the Host and mux are independent SSE streams with no cross-stream ordering, so a request emitted before a removal could arrive after `host/session-removed` and revive a dead session's telemetry." The fix is a monotonic lifecycle generation on the frame, the subscription and the removal, plus a client watermark comparison (`:57`). Why it transfers: August's usage/token/pressure displays and its SSE surfaces have the same hazard; the rule is that anything the UI must show *after* a reload has to be derivable from the log, not carried by a frame.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Enforce browser trust once at the carrier for the whole API prefix — media-type fence plus a `Host`/`Origin` authority fence — and then authenticate every method uniformly.** `2026-07-28-api-browser-trust-boundary.md:13` ("Enforce browser trust once, at the carrier, for the entire `/api` prefix") and `:16` ("Deliberately no shortcut for unmarked requests: over plain HTTP a browser attaches neither `Origin` nor Fetch-Metadata to reads … and Host is the one header rebinding cannot forge"). The authentication half is `2026-08-24-browser-token-authentication.md:15` ("`dsh-client-connection` authenticates the complete Host API before dispatch. Every API Proxy method, Remote unary call, generic Connection channel, and Remote WebSocket stream requires the same browser session; endpoint ownership and method names do not alter authority"). Why it transfers: this is the shape of a local, tool-capable HTTP API that a browser can reach — the two halves together mean a new route is covered by construction rather than by remembering to add it to a guard list.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Install one outbound proxy policy before anything can request, and gate regressions with an AST check on the call sites.** `2026-08-27-outbound-proxy-policy.md:17` ("One policy, resolved once from the launch environment, installed as the global dispatcher") and `:57` (`verify-no-bare-dispatcher` "proves the gate rejects the exact shape this package was introduced to fix"). Why it transfers: August's outbound traffic (model requests, web search, MCP over HTTP, OTLP) is scattered; one global dispatcher installed at boot covers every `fetch()` including future call sites, and the AST gate is what keeps it that way. The two traps worth stealing too: undici's `EnvHttpProxyAgent` tunnels a scheme the package meant to keep direct (`:31`), and a bypass list needs both `::1` and `[::1]` because undici's matcher reads a bare `::1` as host `:` port `1` (`:35`).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Give the model-visible image set a durable decision: per-occurrence indexes, not a watermark or an attachment id.** `2026-09-10-image-offload-events.md:17` ("Each target identifies a current `user/message` or `tool/result` node. Its strictly increasing, zero-based indexes enumerate every image in depth-first content order, including tool-role result content and previously omitted images. Equal attachment ids remain distinct occurrences.") and `:19` (the event has no `surfaceOp`, so message identity survives). Why it transfers: the underlying rule is general and August has the same problem with large tool outputs: "Recomputing the omitted prefix for each request lets a route switch, inline fallback, or compaction restore previously omitted images. The model-visible image set then depends on unlogged request preparation" (`:9`). The same argument justifies August's `maxToolResultChars` pruning becoming a durable event rather than a per-request computation.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Keep a feature-specific message transformation in the feature, and let the core own only acceptance, folding and cache invalidation.** `2026-09-11-plugin-owned-message-projections.md:13` ("The event-owning plugin supplies a pure `SessionMessageProjection`: one event type and a synchronous interpreter of the preceding history. It validates the complete durable payload and returns immutable updates for existing messages, preserving their identities.") and `:15` (the `@messageProjection` tag *generates* the required-interpreter inventory, so a missing definition rejects append, seed, restore and pure folding). Why it transfers: this is the exact seam August needs if it ever wants a durable, plugin-owned effect on model history without growing the core session module; the "tag generates the inventory" trick is what makes the invariant checkable rather than conventional.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Make the whole client UI copy pass through one locale seat, and enforce it with an AST gate that refuses a narrowed corpus.** `2026-08-23-locale-owned-client-ui-copy.md:13` ("Locale dictionaries own all product-authored client UI wording") and `:21` ("Discovery refuses a narrowed corpus, unit fixtures pin admitted and excluded forms"). The transferable twist is `:19` — "Localized display text is never an identity": models and stores keep discriminants and stable ids, and renderers translate *after* matching. Why it transfers: August's desktop UI is bilingual and this rule prevents a language switch from changing selection, grouping or lifecycle state; the "refuse a narrowed corpus" clause is the part that stops the gate from going falsely green.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Use one error class and one code table for a whole RPC surface, and discriminate by `code`, never by `instanceof`.** `2026-08-28-ctx-remote-failure-vocabulary.md:19` (one `RemoteError<Code>` class plus a merge-extensible `RemoteErrorDetailsMap`) and `:48` ("discrimination always reads `code` and never uses `instanceof`, because client and host are separately bundled programs and several copies of the class exist"). The code shape at `:33` (`<domain>/<reason>`, e.g. `session/not-found`, `gateway/cancelled`) is the part that transfers: the code itself says who owns it, so relaying another domain's code needs no awkward unprefixed name.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Keep plugin UI composition to a single `register` call that simultaneously occupies a slot, authorizes child slots, declares the store and injects the business face — with the child slot's render authority settled at load, not at render time.** `2026-07-22-slot-type-chain-implementation.md:17` and `:37` ("the `children` object both **declares** the child slots into existence and **authorizes** this component to render them"). The `chain` kind at `:58` is the clever part: a new takeover package registers with **zero owner edits**, because the owner dispatches one common currency of owner props and never learns who takes over. Why it transfers: August's desktop app is a plugin host; this is a complete, statically-checked answer to "how does a plugin put UI in a place the plugin does not own".
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Assemble business UI nodes from raw events with a per-business `match(event)` that can see only the current event — and separate state updates from publication cadence.** `2026-08-09-client-conversation-node-assembly.md:56` ("`match(event)` reads **only** the current event and cannot access a Context, history, a Reader or a Location, so matching cost depends only on the number of Definitions and ingestion direction cannot change the fold") and `:135` (publication cadence `immediate | animation-frame | none` separated from the state update). Why it transfers: this is the architecture for a token-streaming chat that must not remount rows — the "business identity, state evolution and final presentation" separation (`:9`) and the "Contexts stay in ascending first-`seq` order regardless of page-loading direction" rule (`:68`) solve the exact remount bug August's ActivityGroup work is fighting.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Give a UI component live data it knows only by *address*, and keep content out of the observation stream.** `2026-09-05-client-resource-model.md:15` ("Anything a consumer reads live is a **resource**, a resource is identified by its **address** and nothing else") and `:52` (the stream carries metadata, not payload; content is read separately). Why it transfers: August's "the file the agent just wrote" and "the terminal" surfaces are exactly this; the address grammar `dsh-resource://file/session/<sessionId>/<path>` with the session in the *path* is a clean way to make the scope part of the identity.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Separate "observe" from "resume", per method, and never let a transport lookup activate an Agent.** `2026-08-18-session-history-and-event-transport.md:13` — "If transport performs a general Typert lookup whenever an argument contains a Session or Agent, opening a page, switching tabs, or reconnecting the network implicitly resumes an Agent, so observation gains execution side effects." The per-method activation table at `:154-164` is the mechanism: each Remote method explicitly chooses cold inspection, live-only lookup, or resume-capable resolution. Why it transfers: August's session list, file browser and project view all want to *read* a session; if reading resumes it, an unattended agent starts just because a tab opened.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Give the harness one configuration ladder, and refuse to let a discovered `.env` decide anything that governs how the process launches.** `2026-08-04-configuration-source-ownership.md:21-30` (the six-tier ladder) and `:47-49` (a discovered `.env` is refused if it sets anything governing how the process launches, what ambient programs handle, what code a runtime executes before the program, where model-visible instructions load from, or how the network is reached — organised by what a variable *does*, not by which runtime owns it). Why it transfers: August reads a project `.env`; the transferable rule is that a *repository* must not be able to redirect the harness's own launch policy, expressed by behaviour rather than by an enumerated variable list (the note says enumerating is "a losing game one variable at a time", `:49`).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Own the config root in exactly one place, with a precedence, an "empty means unset" rule and a symbolic display name.** `2026-07-24-single-harness-home-resolver.md:18-24` — `configured ?? $DSH_HOME ?? ~/.dsh`, with an empty/whitespace `$DSH_HOME` treated as unset (because `resolve('')` would silently place the home at the cwd) and `dshHomeDisplay()` naming the root symbolically so a user-facing label never leaks an absolute machine path. Why it transfers: August has several config roots (data dir, workspace, brain DB); the "two resolvers for the same cross-cutting fact means there is no single home policy" framing (`:14`) and the explicit rejection of XDG in favour of one obvious root (`:36`) are both directly usable.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Normalise the credential plane so a record is scoped by its *owning plugin*, and let the authorization flow own the write.** `2026-08-13-credential-records-and-authorization-flows.md:21` ("The key is `<scope>/<id>` where the scope is the **owning plugin's registered name**, not the provider's") and `:23` ("Records do not layer … presence of the record is the whole fact"). Why it transfers: August's provider keys, service-connection tokens and `mcpGlobalEnv` secrets are separate stores today; the plugin-scoped key space plus "no layering" removes the whole class of "which value wins" bugs this repo's AGENTS.md keeps hitting.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#1]** - **Give the client one remote error vocabulary and one fixed-facts accessor, so a method migrating between transports cannot change its caller set.** `2026-08-28-ctx-remote-failure-vocabulary.md:15` ("Fixed Host facts bypassed `ctx.remote` too: the Host home came from `(ctx.get('connection') as ConnectionHandle).generation.getSnapshot()?.host.home`, so every page that needed one fixed fact injected the carrier and understood its generation store") and `2026-07-28-api-browser-trust-boundary.md:33` ("Host and Origin remain request-routing evidence only. The process token and signed cookie establish the browser identity used by every Host method"), with `2026-08-24-browser-token-authentication.md:45` adding that "a method migration between API Proxy and Typert Remote cannot change its caller set". Why it transfers: this is the shape of a local API that will grow methods and transports.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **A byte-bounded upload watermark that drains a backlog instead of resending it** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-24-bounded-session-log-upload.md:12` - `session-log-deepseek.Config.maxBytes` (8 MiB) bounds the serialized `dsh_session_log` field; each request carries the *longest contiguous run after the watermark* that fits, and acceptance advances the watermark to that run's `throughSeq`. This is the transferable shape for August's own telemetry/log shipping: a naive "send everything pending" design fails catastrophically because one oversized payload makes the adapter's `JSON.stringify` throw `RangeError`, the provider reports `TRANSPORT`, the retry policy repeats the same serialization, and *every* model request in that session fails. A contiguous-run watermark (not a per-event one) means a single event that exceeds the cap blocks its own run without failing the request, and the measured numbers (269 MiB / 34 s, 182 ms vs 10 ms) tell you what the alternative costs.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Two cache identities: a lifecycle identity for reads, a fold identity for continuation** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-19-projection-cache-listing-identity-and-cached-rows.md:52` - the same on-disk record is matched on `formatVersion + createdAt + cwd + isSeeded` when *read* and on that plus `inheritedEventCount` when *used to continue a fold*, because the cut is not derivable from a header-only read. The lesson generalises: a cache record often needs two identity tuples, one for "is this the same thing" and one for "may this continue from here", and conflating them produces exactly the bug this note fixed — 44 of 241 seeded sessions showing no title after a restart. The companion decision at line 57 is the other half: comparability is expressed by a *separate* `kind` field (`cached` vs `sequenced`), never by overloading `asOfSeq` (the sentinel alternative is rejected at line 131 because one field then carries two meanings).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Three-phase tool calls keyed by callId, with preparation never persisted** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-22-tool-call-three-phases.md:19` - one Tool owns `preparing` (a live delta with a call id and name) → `start` (`tool/call`, complete arguments) → `result`, and a named live delta creates the preparing row while a historical `tool/call` creates the dispatched stage directly. Two rules matter for August: (a) "equal durable events produce equal final state; intermediate presentation and preparation-group identity need not match" (line 37), so the live view may show a stage the replay never shows without the transcript diverging; and (b) preparation is deliberately *not* persisted, because durable calls and results already suffice to reconstruct the final presentation (line 57). This removes the "the model is visibly waiting and the UI shows nothing" interval without adding a persisted state.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Measure what the model actually generates, then encode the order in the schema** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-24-preparing-tool-arguments.md:11` - 310 controlled requests against the real API showed that reordering a JSON schema's `properties` changed nothing (0/20 for bash, 0/20 for run_code), while reordering `required` *together with* `properties` forced the description first in 10/10 forced-choice and 7/10 free Pro calls but **0/20 free Flash calls**, and only adding one sentence to the parameter description ("Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments") took free Flash to 19/20 and 20/20. The shipped fix is therefore both an ordering change in the schema DSL *and* one instruction string in the description (line 52). For August: when a UI depends on a field arriving first, measure the generation order on your real model tier before assuming the schema controls it.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Default-deny method-level access with a resource identity the caller cannot forge** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-10-12-peer-principal-and-remote-access.md:155` - a non-owner is allowed only when a binding's role explicitly lists the action, and *every* resolved resource must be allowed; there is no implicit Peer (a required parameter makes a missed Peer a compile error rather than a silent owner grant, line 579) and no wire field can set the principal (line 500). Two details are worth stealing verbatim: authorization runs **before** lookup and Context resolution, so an unauthorized call never activates a session or leaves a side effect (line 398); and a throwing policy is *isolated* — `bindings()` throwing means the principal has no grant, so a broken rule cannot break the shared event source or the page (line 332). The frontend's visibility snapshot is computed from the same bindings as `decide()`, so the two cannot disagree (line 451).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **A bounded per-stream uplink inbox that fails the whole stream, not the item** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-19-remote-duplex-stream.md:300` - each logical stream's uplink is metered in UTF-8 bytes (default 262144); on overflow the entire stream fails with `gateway/uplink-overflow` and the `uplink()` iterator ends with the same error, with *no data discarded*. The reasoning is the transferable part: a method that does not read its uplink while the client keeps sending is a usage error, and the failure exposes it explicitly rather than degrading silently. August's duplex channels (terminal input, approval answers) want exactly this: one meter, one failure, one error code — rather than per-item backpressure that lets one stuck consumer accumulate.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Bounded telemetry by bytes measured with the real serializer, not by record count** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-25-session-log-otel-byte-limits.md:15` - each record is measured *once* with the SDK serializer including a full envelope, and the sum conservatively bounds a combined request; greedy packing avoids full-candidate serialization and recursive re-encoding. Counting compressed bytes or characters is rejected for a specific reason: collector limits can apply after decompression, and characters omit UTF-8 and escaping overhead (line 25). One event per record is also kept deliberately, because one large session would otherwise exceed the ceiling even when each event fits (line 21).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Document-relative routes: the served document is the only authority on its own mount** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-14-web-document-relative-app-routes.md:15` - exactly one `<base href="./">` is spliced into the served index, and browser references become document-relative while *server* route keys stay absolute. The reasoning is the transferable part (line 11): the mount cannot be recovered from the transport — a configured base URL is deployment input, forwarded-prefix inference makes a request header authoritative for routing, and proxy rewriting reimplements the same fact in fragments. One bundle then serves the origin root and any prefix-stripping proxy mount. The implementation detail worth copying is the boundary strip (`KEY.slice(1)`) with the browser form living beside the key constant as `*_ROUTE` (line 17).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **A retired field is declared `never` with `@persistenceReserved` so its *history* forbids it** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-17-developer-session-changes.md:17` - `ToolAdditionBlock.tool` is an optional `never` with `@persistenceReserved`, so the schema history records the rejected field: permitting a value later is a value-type change requiring a format bump, while unrelated optional metadata stays additive. The same trick appears at `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-17-native-v4-read-validation.md:23` (`EpochHeader.system`). For August's persistence schemas this is a cheap way to make "we will never add this field" checkable rather than a comment.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **A single shared translation record per note, hashed per section** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-11-subprocess-control-pipe.i18n.yaml:1` - every note carries a machine record of per-heading-section en/zh digests, recomputable with one command (`pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <note>.md`). The digests cover only text *outside* code blocks and generated regions (line 2), and subsection headings are hashed separately (see `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-22-tool-call-three-phases.i18n.yaml:1`, which has ten hashes for five decision subsections plus the standard five). August's docs are bilingual; this turns "is the Chinese copy still the same decision?" from a review question into a CI check, and the header line names the exact file and the exact command to re-record it.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Retain only what the invariant needs — and prove the smaller state is equivalent** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-10-13-context-breakdown-system-prompt-state.md:24` - the context breakdown kept one entry per surface node so any replacement could subtract its exact price; 151,122 entries over 836 sessions made the unit 7.13 MB and every cached listing validated all of them. The fix keeps only the surviving system prompts, one surface total and at most one armed shadow-price claim — 110 KB, at most five prompts per session — and is *verified* by folding all 836 logs with both definitions and getting identical breakdowns after every event. The verification pattern (old and new implementations over the same corpus, compared event by event) is what makes this a steal rather than a guess; a faster validator was rejected precisely because it kept the 7.13 MB (line 28).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **An "exclusive" match claim instead of a precedence order** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-10-12-exclusive-conversation-matches.md:19` - one extra optional field (`exclusive?: true`) lets a business Definition claim an event on its target, so a generic Definition does not also build a node for it. The dispatcher evaluates *all* matches of an event before accepting any, then settles claims, so the outcome is independent of registration order (line 25). Precedence (`specific`/`default`) is rejected because it turns dispatch into a priority order and needs the generic Definition's cooperation (line 32); the shipped bug was a duplicate `turn-trigger` node for a late question reply that Chat had been working around by deduplicating by message id in two separate grouping paths, leaving the duplicate in the Node Store (line 11).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Retain a shared service, isolate the state** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-10-09-cua-shared-native-helper.md:13` - one native service per executable *content digest* is shared across Agents and Hosts, while each Agent connection owns its application handles, AX snapshots, limits and cancellation state. The root cause is worth noting because it is a general class of bug: the underlying system derived capture-client identity from the executable *path*, so two live helpers at the same path replaced each other's connections even for sequential screenshots, and two symlinks to one executable reproduced it (line 9) — identity derived from a mutable path is not identity.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#2]** - **Turn a layout convention into an executable contract with one owner and a manifest** - `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-19-window-drag-coverage-contract.md:15` - the composition rule becomes an executable model ("a point is draggable when the last collected app-region box containing it declares `drag`"), the shell declares the surface exactly once, and a manifest gate refuses a mark on any element the manifest does not name. Publishing measured rectangles from JavaScript is rejected because "one stale frame is exactly the swallow class this work removes" (line 24). August's drag/hover regions and its context-meter overlays can use the same shape: one CSS-derived rule, a manifest that names every participant, and a browser lane that executes the model rather than a checklist.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Put a subagent/team-member's identity in a `required` dynamic context contribution, not in the initial task and not in the system prompt** — `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-10-13-team-identity-runtime-context.md:13` (impl `packages/experimental/tool-agent-team/src/index.ts:178-190`; the required-context rule is enforced at `packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts:591`, and a *missing* required registration is restored in registry order at `:594-600`). The identity provider re-renders from **current** membership on every read, so a compaction that deleted the identity, or a fork that inherited a stale role, both self-heal; the system prompt stays byte-identical across members because the per-member text lives in the runtime-context snapshot, not in the prefix. For August this is directly transferable: a delegated worker whose "you are reviewer, address the lead" line is currently embedded in the initial task is exactly the failure this removes.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Re-send the *whole* runtime-context snapshot only when it changed, and append it after the inherited history** — `2026-10-13-team-identity-runtime-context.md:15` (impl `packages/core/agent-loop/src/runtime-context.ts:152-162`, where `project()` returns `undefined` when `this.retained?.text === snapshot`, and `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:427-440`, where the snapshot is appended as a `user/message` after the claimed messages). The snapshot text itself declares its own precedence — "Current runtime context. This snapshot supersedes earlier runtime-context snapshots." (`packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts:317`) — so the model never has to reconcile two context blocks. This is a *diff-free* re-admission protocol: whole-value comparison, no partial patching, no per-subsystem retention state, and it survives compaction for free.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Keep the cached request prefix stable by splitting fixed policy (a prompt *section*) from per-run facts (a dynamic *context*)** — `2026-10-13-team-identity-runtime-context.md:13` and `:23` (impl `packages/experimental/tool-agent-team/src/index.ts:173-177` for the section vs `:178-190` for the context; the projection that decides whether a changed prompt is appended after cached history or normalizes the head is `packages/core/agent-loop/src/runtime-context.ts:88-103`). The note's stated reason is that per-member system text "can rewrite the inherited request prefix on routes without in-history system updates" — for August, whose provider-prefix cache is explicitly a design concern, this is the same trade-off stated in a mechanism.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Let the provider publish its own image geometry instead of re-deriving it in the Host** — `2026-10-13-cua-hover-routes-and-coordinates.md:17` (impl `packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:248` and `:692-693`; the DeepSeek and pi-ai implementations at `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:45` and `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/adapter.ts:238`; consumed by CUA at `packages/experimental/cua/src/index.ts:133`). The note's reason is exact: "making the model convert them duplicates provider geometry rules". August's screenshot/attachment path has the same hazard — a Retina capture, an attachment normalization step and a model-request resize all sit between the pixels and the pointer.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Convert model-facing coordinates once, in the Host, and make the failure modes typed** — `2026-10-13-cua-hover-routes-and-coordinates.md:15` (impl `packages/experimental/cua/src/coordinates.ts:55-76`, with `STALE_SNAPSHOT`, `SCREENSHOT_REQUIRED` and `INVALID_ARGUMENT` as distinct error codes, and `packages/experimental/cua/src/protocol.ts:17` for the `relative: z.literal(true)` schema). Two coordinate modes coexist — screenshot pixels by default, integer thousandths 0..1000 on explicit request — and the unit is never guessed from the value (:23). The relative path is resolution-independent and clamped inside the window, so a screenshot that was resized for the provider cannot silently mis-aim a click.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Make the tool's guidance text a recovery protocol, not documentation** — `2026-10-13-cua-hover-routes-and-coordinates.md:13` and `2026-10-13-cua-continuous-hover.md:13` (impl `packages/experimental/cua-macos/src/guidance.ts:40-42`). The guidance enumerates each error code and the exact next action: `STALE_APP` requires `getApp` again, `STALE_SNAPSHOT` requires `getState` again, `SCREENSHOT_REQUIRED` means capture a fresh screenshot, `WINDOW_CHANGED` requires fresh state before any retry, `PERMISSION_DENIED` requires the user to grant access and then observe fresh state — and it says "A successful action means dispatched, not verified completion" and "never retry uncertain input without observing". This is the tool-call-reliability lens answered in the tool's own schema text, where the model actually reads it.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Prefer a background/alternate route that does not disturb the user, and report which route ran** — `2026-10-13-cua-continuous-hover.md:13` and `2026-10-13-cua-hover-routes-and-coordinates.md:13` (impl `packages/experimental/cua-macos/native/Sources/CuaNative/AXHover.swift:12-35`, which walks up to an ancestor advertising both `AXShowAlternateUI` and `AXShowDefaultUI`, performs `AXShowDefaultUI` to restore and `AXShowAlternateUI` to reveal, and falls back only when no such element exists; the result identifies `hoverRoute` as `accessibility` or `system-pointer`). The note's "Problem" section is the transferable part: treating *every* hover as a system movement unnecessarily disturbs the user's pointer, and the fallback is gated on a foreground-PID check plus an AppKit mouse hit test that excludes input-transparent overlays.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Serialize the operation, not the application — no cross-call ownership** — `2026-10-13-cua-continuous-hover.md:15` and `:19` (impl: the shared native helper the note names, `2026-10-09-cua-shared-native-helper.md`). The stated reason is that "cross-call application reservation would block other tasks throughout observation and model inference without evidence that the first task deserves priority", and that "waiting for the model does not reserve the application". For August this is the multi-agent concurrency rule in one sentence: a long inference must not hold a resource another task needs, and ordering is explicit task coordination, not arrival order.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Make a not-yet-arrived artifact fail *explicitly* with a typed code, and make only the async face wait** — `2026-10-14-webworker-preview-profile-parity.md:58` (impl `packages/experimental/webworker-runtime/src/storage/memory.ts:383-394` for the `ERR_DSH_VFS_DEFERRED` refusal and `:331-336` for the single shared fetch). The rule: synchronous reads and every mutation of a registered-but-absent file are refused with a code that names the archive, while `fs.promises.readFile` / `open` / `cp` / `createReadStream` wait; the first waiter fetches once for everybody; a failed fetch leaves the registration so the next read retries; and a directory rename that would move a registered file is refused *before* the destination changes. That last clause is the steal — refusing *before* mutating is what keeps a partial failure from corrupting state.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Refuse a platform capability with one error code, and let only that code trigger a degraded mode** — `2026-10-14-webworker-preview-profile-parity.md:50` (impl `packages/experimental/inspector/src/host/plugin.ts:68-76`, where `isUnavailableOnPlatform(error)` is the only branch that survives a startup failure, and `:190` for the code check that inspects the code and never the message). A degraded Inspector warns once, keeps a bootstrap route that answers 503, registers no DevTools route, and loads no Node-only package — while *every other* startup failure still rolls the fiber back.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Reproduce the production launch path in the preview instead of special-casing it, and confine the difference to one enumerated patch** — `2026-10-14-webworker-preview-profile-parity.md:21-34` (impl `packages/experimental/webworker-packer/src/repository.ts:107-113` for the roster read from app-boot's `PROFILE_TEMPLATES` + `OPTIONAL_BUNDLES`, and `:124-132` for the single home-patch row per `PLATFORM_ENTRY_CONFIG` entry). The measurable acceptance criterion is the interesting part: "with no bundle enabled, the two compositions differ in only one of 188 rows" (:17) — a *row-level diff between the preview and production* as the parity test. August has the same class of problem (the packaged desktop app vs the dev web app) and could adopt a row-diff as its parity gate.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **Split the artifact by scanning for the literal request form, and make an unpublished request a build error** — `2026-10-14-webworker-preview-profile-parity.md:54` (impl: the packer's `lazyChunksOf` scanning every page asset for `require.async("./client.<name>.js")`). The subtle bit is that a chunk requested *by another chunk* is found without tracing requests from the entry point, and a target named by a package's `./client` export under any condition stays in the base image; a request for a chunk the package does not publish fails the pack. Per-chunk deterministic `lazy/<sha256>.tar.gz` archives (:55) then make the split cacheable and reproducible across packs.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **State the invariant you do *not* check, in the same note** — `2026-10-14-webworker-preview-profile-parity.md:57` and `:96` ("The digest in the archive name is not verified"; "the Worker checks only the registered paths and sizes of an arrived archive, not the digest that names it"). August's own notes repeatedly argue that a gate that cannot see a defect should say so; this note generalises it to *security-relevant* invariants — the archive's content hash is not checked, only its path/size manifest.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **A bilingual pair is three files, and the consistency record's diff IS the act of confirmation** — `2026-10-13-team-identity-runtime-context.i18n.yaml:1-4` (impl `scripts/translation-pairing-record.ts:149-199` for the per-section hash that excludes fenced code blocks and generated regions, and `docs/i18n/README.md:11-22` for the contract). The properties worth stealing: the record is **section-keyed**, so two branches editing different sections do not conflict in Git; regenerating a region or editing a code block on both sides leaves the record unchanged; and `--write` requires naming the pairs you confirmed, because "that yaml diff is the reviewable act of confirming consistency". The owning contract also states the limit flatly: "a green gate means the pair was confirmed consistent at these exact contents, not that the confirmation was sound."
- **[dsh-notes-impl-arch#3]** - **A note names exactly which part of an older decision it supersedes** — `2026-10-13-team-identity-runtime-context.md:17` ("This supersedes only the initial-task identity decision in …; its roster, mailbox, and task decisions remain active"). A blanket supersession would silently retire three other live decisions; the partial, named supersession is what makes a decision log safe to extend. This is the same discipline August's `AGENTS.md` demands when it says a change "ships under that part's number" rather than minting a new one.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Append the changed system prompt instead of rewriting message 0, when the route declares the capability** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-09-02-in-history-system-prompt-replacement.md:11` and `:17` — DSH records the exact model fact ("a DeepSeek model accepts a `system` message at any position of the conversation and treats the latest one as the complete effective system prompt, replacing the leading one") and then makes the *route* declare `systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'`, so a prompt change appends a new `system/message` node instead of rewriting node 0 and the provider prefix cache survives. August currently re-renders its system prompt every step and any byte change busts the DeepSeek cache from token 1; this is a one-capability, one-routing-rule change with a documented fallback for incapable routes, and the note even specifies the accounting side (`dsh-token-meter` prices the last surviving system node as `systemTokens`).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Treat the system prompt as an append-only surface, and move every volatile fact out of it** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-09-02-in-history-system-prompt-replacement.md:36` (`startsSeries` rules) and `.agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-10-11-process-specific-prompt-values-in-runtime-context.md:9` — the second note gives the *hard* failure that makes this non-negotiable: Claude binds historical thinking-block signatures to the conversation prefix *including the system prompt*, so a changed prompt returns `400 Invalid signature … bound to a different conversation` and the Session cannot continue. August already freezes its memory index per session for cache stability; this generalises the rule to every volatile value (ports, paths, URLs) and supplies the exact symptom to design against.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **A per-tool, unary, fail-closed concurrency classifier, evaluated at dispatch time** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-10-parallel-tool-call-execution.md:17`, `:29`, `:45` — each tool may expose `isConcurrencySafe(args)`, a synchronous pure function; only an explicit `true` opts in, anything else (missing, throwing, wrong type) is exclusive. Consecutive parallel calls form a group, an exclusive call is a barrier, and only *dispatch + body* overlap while `pre-execute`/`post-execute` stay in model order because middleware may hold ordered state. August's parallel tool execution needs exactly this and cannot ship a resource-aware contract, so the unary form is the realistic ceiling.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **One resolver for tool visibility AND tool execution — and the explicit statement that visibility is not authority** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-12-subagent-persona-tool-filter-and-depth.md:39` and `:76` — the same live registry predicate drives wire schemas, lookup, execution and PTC SDK generation, so a model cannot execute a tool the prompt says does not exist; and the note refuses to call that a security boundary ("they do not authorize it … no parent-to-child grant lattice, no requirement that a child be a subset of its parent"). This is the conceptual frame August's deny-set / `currentSubagentDenied` design needs, and it is the sentence that keeps a visibility filter from being mistaken for confinement.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Canonical tool results separated from their rendered prose, with typed handles and an explicit over-limit failure** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-20-ptc-typed-tool-returns.md:54`, `:62`, `:70` — bindings resolve to the tool's canonical `JsonValue`, failures reject with a real `ToolCallError` (not a string), background jobs return `{ kind: 'background', jobId }` instead of prose, and an over-cap completion fails as `output-limit` rather than being silently truncated. August's `job_output` / background-job path currently makes the model parse ids out of English sentences; this is the same idea at the message level and it composes with the fact that August already has a `ToolCallError`-shaped need in its PTC/code-mode path.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **One inbox, one ordering authority, and an explicit durability statement** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-28-continuable-subagent-conversations.md:90` and `:140` — "The Agent inbox is the only queue" (agent messages Steer, human prompts Queue-or-Steer), and "Only messages written to the child Session log are reconstructable with the source that supplied them; inbox acceptance alone provides no restart guarantee". August's Bot-to-Bot DM path is exactly the place a second FIFO would appear, and this note gives both the fix (one queue) and the honest limit (accepted-but-unlogged work is lost and is *not* replayed).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Compare-and-set on shared task state plus a blocking wait edge instead of model polling** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-08-05-agent-teams.md:47` and `:49` — every task mutation carries `expectedRevision`, only the Lead assigns, and `wait_agent` blocks on one roster/mailbox/task/status edge registered *after* the call starts, so callers never poll. August's Bot rooms currently bound work with `rooms.MAX_ROUNDS` plus a stall detector; this replaces polling with a primitive, and the note's refusal to treat ownership or `writeScopes` as locks ("False mutual exclusion is more dangerous than an explicit warning") is the right posture for a shared checkout.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Producer-declared context *shape*, separate from producer identity, with opaque as the documented default** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-08-05-context-form-vocabulary.md:17` and `:44` — `MessageSource` gains a small tagged `form` vocabulary (instructions / catalog / snapshot / notice / relay / recall) that says *what kind of thing was added*, and anything unknown, absent or unreadable renders as the opaque body. August renders every injected context row as one blob; adding a `form` field to the durable message source is a small change with a large rendering payoff, and the "opaque is the default, so old logs still render" rule is what makes it safe to ship.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Separate a policy DENIAL from a technical FAILURE, and let a human arbitrate the denial** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-09-24-auto-review-user-approval-fallback.md:13` and `:17` — a reviewer denial is routed into the existing `ask` decision so a human can `allowed-once` it, while a reviewer *failure* produces a different message carrying the finish kind, failure code and provider message. August's self-heal already learned this lesson the hard way (a refusal text that read as success); this note is the generalised form, and the reasoning for *not* asking after a failure ("a failure says nothing about the action's risk") is directly transferable.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Execution-time authority for model-facing state-changing tools** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-19-model-facing-goal-tools.md:29` and `:31` — every call requires an `exec.agent` that is the exact live registry object, the current driver initiator, with an open turn; and "User source is a host attestation" (every `followup()`/`steer()` input must carry an explicit source). August's `_authority_refusal` and `agentId`-vs-`agentId` derivation bugs are the same class; the two ideas worth taking verbatim are the *host attestation* of message source and the durable-paused escape hatch (the model cannot resume a paused goal — the user-facing path owns that transition).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Refuse-by-default when the hidden work is still running, then stop after the write** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-09-21-archive-stops-running-session-work.md:15` and `:16` — `archiveSession` rejects when `workspace/session-activity` reports anything running; with `stopActivity: true` the archive is written *first* and the stop dispatched afterwards, so every wake the stop induces is already blocked; and an `agent/pre-step` gate rejects any model step proposed for an archived Session or its descendants. August's Bot/background path can hide work the same way, and the ordering (write the durable state, then stop) plus the pre-step gate is a two-part fix that needs no new event type.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Kernel arbitration for cross-process write ownership instead of a TTL record** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-08-31-cross-process-session-write-lease.md:13` — `flock(2)` on POSIX and a named kernel semaphore on Windows, with the POSIX inode re-verification ("a POSIX lock names an inode rather than a path"), and no expiry bookkeeping because the kernel releases on process death. The alternatives section records why the TTL+rename design was replaced and why Windows byte-range locks (`LockFileEx`) and `CreateFileW` share-mode denial were both rejected *with CI evidence*. If August ever runs two writers over one session log, this is the shape to copy.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Make a gate measure the thing it claims to measure** — `.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-28-dual-release-install-layout-work-budget.md:13` and `.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-10-11-lossless-build-speedups.md:11` — the first replaces a wall-clock timeout with a *growth unit* (`dshPackagesPerVersion * checkedDshEdges` against `MAX_RESOLUTION_WORK_UNITS = 875_000`) because "that deadline measures the runner, not the graph"; the second fits a dose-response curve (Check ≈ 26.9 + 0.494·N s) so the fix targets the variable that explains the cost. August's `check:*` gates are mostly static form checks; a gate expressed in *units of the thing that grows* is the version that catches drift before a timeout does.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Version a persisted format by READER compatibility, not by schema difference** — `.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-10-08-session-reader-compatibility-review.md:13` — a same-version change is permitted when older readers either resume correctly, safely ignore optional features while preserving their records, or refuse required features *before* execution, mutation or tail repair; feature absence must preserve existing behaviour; removing a required field is not automatically a bump if the replacement stays distinguishable. August's session format and migrations would benefit from this exact test, because it separates "the bytes differ" from "an old reader is now unsafe".
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Give the note corpus a principled retention boundary** — `.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-frozen-agent-note-archive.md:13` — small UI adjustments and mechanical changes are **deleted** as complete triplets (with inbound links repaired), only shipped-complete + low-future-value + historically valuable notes are archived, and "Foundational boundaries, durable and wire semantics, security rules, recurring design temptations, and unresolved reintroduction conditions remain active regardless of age or word count". August's AGENTS.md is 68 KB and its own rules forbid minting a new Part number; this gives a principled way to keep the corpus small without losing the reasoning that stops a tempting mistake.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **A deny-list for a whole vocabulary, applied to code and filenames as well as prose** — `.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-26-ban-ambiguous-origin-label.md:13` — one ambiguous token had accumulated eight unrelated meanings and the prose policy could not remove it because "it allowed the same ambiguous label to remain in APIs, durable compatibility fixtures, filenames, generated catalogs, and new prose". August has exactly this hazard in terms like "source", "origin", "evidence" and "provenance" across the brain, transcript and audit surfaces; the transferable move is to ban the *token* everywhere and force each site to name its exact local concept.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#1]** - **Assert capability, don't infer it** — `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-09-07-deepseek-messages-adapter.md:15` and `:23` — DeepSeek effort is `output_config.effort`, not an Anthropic thinking budget, and the Messages system-update behaviour is declared per endpoint/model because "capability inference from protocol or model names is insufficient". August's per-model capability profiles (`toolSurface`, `maxTools`, `maxToolResultChars`) already work this way; the transferable part is the *refusal to infer* — and the same note records that a JSON syntax failure after a 200 is `INVALID_RESPONSE`, not `TRANSPORT`, and earns no retry, which is a precise error-taxonomy rule August could adopt verbatim. ---
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **One send is at most one turn — grouping must not depend on scheduling** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-07-17-one-send-one-turn.md:17` — the mechanism is that each `send()` becomes its own FIFO queue item and the *next* send's turn may not start until the previous turn recorded `turn/end` **and** its durability checkpoint settled, so turn B's model request always sees turn A's closed result in the same session log. August's own AGENTS.md shows the same class of hazard (a tool call's result must be visible to the next turn) and this gives the exact ordering rule plus the three exceptions (`steer`, `inject`, whole-agent `cancel`) — and it names the cost honestly: more model requests, more checkpoints.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Coalesce *publication*, never *ingestion* — rAF instead of microtask batching** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-08-03-opt-in-reasoning-chunk-browser-stress.md:15` — the mechanism: fold every raw chunk into State immediately (so live state never diverges from the durable embedded stream) but publish one accumulated snapshot per `requestAnimationFrame`, with structural events and durable settlements preempting. August's streaming Think/assistant rows re-render per delta; this is the transferable boundary — "microtask batching alone" degrades to one notification per chunk because each async `yield` drains the microtask queue.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **A barrier *stack*, with `whenIdle()` first and `networkidle` banned outright** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane.md:27` — the mechanism: host-side `await agent.whenIdle()` keyed on the in-process `turn/end` (the idle flip follows the persistence flush, so one await covers turn completion *and* durability), then a browser settled poll; polling persistence files as a durability barrier is banned, and `networkidle` is banned because it never resolves while an SSE stream is open. August's SSE/TUI surfaces have exactly this barrier problem, and the "which barrier is wrong" table is the transferable part.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Fail the test on any pageerror and on connection-loss console warnings — a self-healing client must not certify a dead wire** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane.md:35` — the mechanism is that reconnect + history resync would otherwise heal a broken SSE path and the suite would go green on a broken product. August's harness has the same reconnect-plus-resync shape; this is a one-line guard with a stated reason.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **A replay consumption assertion as a teardown tripwire** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane.md:35` — `ReplayHandle.assertConsumed()` checks that every recorded script was bound and every cursor drained at scaffold close, turning "silent underrun / shifted binding" into a crisp diagnostic. This is the pattern that makes a recorded-fixture harness safe: the fixture is *owed* a consumption.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **A keyless lane that boots the *real* composition, with the adapter row disabled rather than faked** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane.md:21` — the mechanism: disable the `llm-deepseek` row in the real config tree and install the replay adapter into the *empty* adapter registry (never catch-all, or `resolveModelInfo` becomes unroutable and `compaction-basic` warns every step); a scenario with no fixture leaves the registry empty so a stray stream fails loud with `NO_ADAPTER`. "Honest keylessness" beats a placeholder API key — the placeholders satisfied a fail-loud key check with a lie.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Bind port `0` so the OS allocates atomically** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-08-24-session-log-snapshot-corpus.md:27` — the mechanism: each scenario-owned HTTP fixture binds loopback port 0, lets the OS allocate and bind atomically, then maps the recorded URL to that listener. Pre-probing a port is a TOCTOU race; a fixed numeric port makes concurrent snapshot jobs race on one host.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Performance budgets as reviewed source constants, calibrated against positive *and* negative controls** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-04-session-open-performance-gate.md:40` — the mechanism: `ciTimeBudget()` = reference expectation × 2× CI time scale × 1.25× variance headroom, with a pre-stack reference implementation as the positive control and a repeated-snapshot regression as the negative one (which exhausts the heap), and no environment-variable override. "A business-implementation change must not relax a budget without new positive and negative control data." August has a cost/usage surface but no calibrated perf gate; this is the whole recipe in one paragraph.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Measure the user-visible endpoint, not only the components, and separate first-open from reopen** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-04-session-open-performance-gate.md:30` — the mechanism: four phase budgets (`openMs`/`readMs`/`sessionRestoreMs`/`projectionMs`) for attribution plus separate end-to-end budgets for first history and Agent resume, with the phase *sum* marked "diagnostic only"; and two lifecycle access kinds (first open with migration vs post-upgrade reopen in a fresh process) because migration is a one-time cost that cannot protect later opens.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **A constrained-heap run as an *independent* transient-allocation limit** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-04-session-open-performance-gate.md:23` — the mechanism: normal-heap mode runs five samples and enforces the median; a second child runs the same path under a fixed 128 MB old-space limit and checks only that it *completes*, so the extra GC under pressure never pollutes the timing baseline. Combined with explicit GC before/after and reachable long-lived objects, this separates "retained memory" from "transient spike".
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Wait on the state you read, anchored at the hand-over — not on a wall-clock window** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-27-observation-waits-on-observed-state.md:17` — the mechanism: `observingChild` stays in flight until the test has read the record, and the bounded wait starts at the mocked launcher's hand-over rather than at test start, with the bound set *below* the case budget so a missing record fails as "the assertion that names it" rather than as a runner timeout.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Put the whole readiness timeline in the failure message** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-27-observation-waits-on-observed-state.md:19` — the mechanism: every decoded chunk with its marker verdict, every poll, every write, each send's settle reason and elapsed time, the replayed prompt evidence and the host/shell/PSReadLine/console-host versions, printed by `onTestFailed` when the runner budget expires first. A count-only assertion ("no send fell back to the silence tier") could not say *which* send failed.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Prefer a keyboard-driven interaction over a geometry-bound pointer click whose result feeds a later layout assertion** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-27-spreadsheet-selection-by-keyboard-before-reflow.md:15` — the mechanism: a pointer press resolves its target from `getBoundingClientRect()` *inside* a `useState` updater, and React re-runs updaters when the hook queue holds a lower-priority update ahead of them — so one click executed four times across a sidebar reflow and resolved to a different cell. Keyboard selection computes from committed state and is idempotent under re-execution.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Native literal scan for detection, JavaScript for decisions; memo per *text*, not per query** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-10-11-user-text-credential-matching.md:17` — the mechanism: all starting literals in one literal-only alternation scanned with `test` (no quantifiers, so no backtracking), a hit table keyed by the last two code units, per-instance `Int32Array` run/digit/`END` memo cleared when a query names another text, and pruning keyed on the *formats* only so text with any character distribution pays the same linear cost. Directly relevant to August's per-chunk scrubbing of streamed text.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Use the benchmark itself as a rejection oracle against the naive implementation** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-10-11-user-text-credential-matching.md:51` — "the same benchmark fails when pointed at the regular-expression implementation or at an implementation that rebuilds its memo per query." A benchmark that only proves the fast path passes is half a gate; the same harness pointed at the old code must fail.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **A truthfulness rule for capability advertisement** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-07-23-acp-automation-only-protocol.md:21` — advertise image capability only when a durable store exists *and* the configured exact route resolves with explicit image input; "Unknown capability is false at initialization; prompt admission rechecks the live route." Protocol vocabulary ("the SDK has an image block") is not evidence the deployment can do it.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Emit only committed semantic facts on the wire** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-07-23-acp-automation-only-protocol.md:23` — raw chunks, todos, plans, titles, retry markers, terminal metadata and diffs stay off the transport; a per-session promise chain preserves reasoning/assistant/tool/configuration/usage ordering while assistant images are asynchronously re-read and integrity-verified. August's SSE surfaces would benefit from the same "committed vs provisional" split.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **One identity per agent/session pair, with the config label kept as metadata** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-06-20-unify-agent-and-session-id.md:19` — the mechanism plus the operational rule: a config-driven start mints `${label}-session-${uuid}`, and the "resume-or-create" form lets a config-created agent and the UI share one opaque identity across loop reloads instead of guessing from a prefix. Every translation map between two ids disappears.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **No second delivery owner beside the inbox** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-09-26-team-direct-inbox.md:13` — Team sends return the accepted inbox `MessageId` or throw; acceptance "neither confirms model processing nor adds a synchronous flush guarantee"; no unaccepted intent is retained and no retry happens after restart. August's bot-to-bot messaging has the same shape of risk (two acceptance states).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Subagent result delivery must not depend on model compliance** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-09-17-unified-subagent-activations.md:21` — the parent completion notice includes final text *regardless* of whether the child called `send_message`, because "tool availability cannot establish that the child sent its answer"; an answer already sent through the tool may appear twice, and that duplication is accepted rather than requiring a second delivery ledger. One activation entry point (`startActivation()`) owns admission, cancellation, ownership and release across local, ACP, SDK, Codex and Claude Code providers (`:13`).
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Do not open a turn just to obtain a durability checkpoint** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-07-28-remove-synthetic-log-only-turns.md:17` — log-only events are appended between turns and flushed explicitly via `ctx.sessions.flush(session)`; the synthetic-turn rule existed only because persistence once treated the last `turn/end` as the committed boundary. August's `turn_end` reason vocabulary and outcome ledger depend on turn counts meaning *model-loop executions*.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **One tool-invocation form per agent, and reject the mixed configuration loudly** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-10-05-native-or-ptc-presentation.md:13` — the registry rejects `both`; silently mapping it to another mode is rejected because either mapping changes how existing programs or direct calls execute. August has a very similar native-vs-PTC (`run_code`) fork in `app/services/workbench/code_runner.py`.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Reject removed configuration keys at load, including empty values** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-10-09-preset-owned-subagent-composition.md:15` — "deleting Schemastery fields alone does not reject unknown configuration," so `dsh-tool-subagent` rejects `persona` and `toolFilter` explicitly; the same note is careful to *not* claim a provider cache-hit win for the change (`(:19)`) — a useful model for August's per-model tool-surface work, where cache-prefix stability is the actual currency.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **A preflight that turns a missing secret into a loud failure, so a self-skipping suite can safely be a gate** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-06-19-real-api-e2e-ci.md:44` — plus step-scoped secret env (`:50`) so checkout/install never see the key, and a Dependabot gate keyed on the PR *author* rather than `github.actor` (`:35`). August's e2e smoke has the same "skip when no key" shape that silently disables the net.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Test the installed artifact, and prove you tested the installed artifact** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-08-23-installed-python-wheel-black-box-ci.md:17` — the identity check (venv, no repo-relative cwd, no source/editable import, equal distribution versions, exactly pinned runtime dependency, executable inside the installed package) runs *before the first agent request*, "so a behavior pass cannot conceal that the wrong code ran."
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **A two-turn live-provider test** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-08-23-installed-python-wheel-black-box-ci.md:27` — turn 1 writes an exact sentinel file through the platform shell, turn 2 reads it back; the test then verifies the file content, final responses, completed turn reasons, model-requested tool calls and the Zstandard-framed session log. One turn proves nothing about persistence; two turns do.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Electron's `close` event is not HTTP completion** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-10-desktop-local-updater-qualification.md:43` — Electron 44 emits a writable `close` before response headers, so an inactivity deadline must be released by response completion, abort or error and refreshed by received bytes. A transport-level detail that silently breaks every timeout if assumed.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Whitelist fields in an update journal instead of redacting secrets** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-14-desktop-installed-update-journal.md:13` — "unknown authentication values and private paths cannot be exhaustively enumerated," so raw errors, URLs, request headers and chat content are omitted and known error tokens become fixed classifications; storage failures propagate rather than claiming complete evidence.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Corpus shape from measured quantiles, not from a uniform synthetic** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-28-session-corpus-performance.md:17` — rank `r` takes the first anchor at or above quantile `(r+1)/n`, so every synthetic quantile is at least the measured one, and all three dimensions share the rank ("a long Session is long in every dimension").
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Re-run the benchmarks under a real memory cap** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-10-07-memory-limited-benchmarks.md:13` — a cgroup v2 with `memory.max` 4/8 GiB and swap disabled, containing Vitest, every worker, the scaffold Host and Chromium, so page-cache eviction from Session logs shows up in the timings; `--max-old-space-size` cannot model it because the workers' resident memory is mostly native.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Turn a benchmark number into user impact** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-10-07-scaled-benchmark-report.md:13` — a self-contained HTML report scales each measured median onto reviewed machine profiles using a *measured* storage/CPU split (`io = max(0, 1 − cpuMs/ms)`) and shows peak RSS as a share of 4 GB and 8 GB, with every default's source visible and adjustable — and it labels the output "estimates rather than measurements."
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Bind loopback ports with `0` and make the fixture own the mapping** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-08-24-session-log-snapshot-corpus.md:27` (also `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-06-frontend-performance-budgets.md:15`) — the recorded URL/authority stays stable while the listener port is OS-assigned per sample.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Make the translation-pairing check mechanical** — `.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-06-19-real-api-e2e-ci.i18n.yaml:1` — per-heading `en:`/`zh:` hashes plus the exact re-record command. The mechanism is cheap and catches the failure mode (one language drifting) that a human reviewer never notices.
- **[dsh-notes-impl-rest#2]** - **Do not require active plugins on `Loader.create()` alone** — `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-09-09-nontransactional-loader.md:33` — callers that need an activated plugin must *audit after settlement*; a plugin activation failure may leave new options and a failed fiber in place, and that is an accepted, documented consequence. ---
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Encode the state in the path and forbid the generated index; let the tree be the registry.** `.agents/notes/README.md:19` — "Do not add a centralized `INDEX.md`: it duplicates path metadata and makes unrelated note changes contend on one generated file." The enforcement is a one-line error at `scripts/agent-note-tree.ts:47-49` that turns the existence of `INDEX.md` into a build failure, and an unknown lifecycle folder into an error at `scripts/agent-note-tree.ts:53-54`. *Why it transfers to August*: August's own docs layer already fights a "one generated file everyone touches" pattern; a path-encoded state machine (`lifecycle/class/date-title.md`) makes `git log --oneline -- <dir>` the query, makes status legible from a file listing, and removes a whole class of merge conflicts — and the "no index" rule is only ten lines of gate code to enforce.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **A required section with a dated, exact, self-terminating exemption.** `.agents/notes/README.md:111` makes `## Alternatives considered` mandatory in every note; `.agents/notes/README.md:113-117` defines the exact escape hatch — `<!-- agent-note-format: alternatives-not-recorded (pre-format Agent Note) -->` — and the gate accepts it **only** for notes dated before `2026-07-05` (`scripts/verify-agent-note-format.ts:13`, `:79-82`), while also refusing a file that carries *both* the section and the comment (`:80`). *Why it transfers*: this is the exact shape August needs for "every August plan doc must record the alternatives it beat" without grandfathering a growing pile forever, and it teaches the paired rule — a grandfathering escape hatch must carry an exact string, an exact date bound, and a mutual-exclusion check, or it becomes a permanent loophole.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Ban stale spec-speak by heading name, per lifecycle.** `.agents/notes/README.md:103` — in `implemented/`, the headings `## Proposal`, `## Plan`, `## Migration plan`, `## Acceptance criteria` are forbidden, because "an 'accepted in amended form' note is body content" and the filename/git already carry the timeline. The gate is one regex (`scripts/verify-agent-note-format.ts:36`) and one loop (`:72-76`). *Why it transfers*: this is August's "no Part 28 in a comment" rule turned from a convention into a mechanical ban; the same trick generalises to any documentation that must stop describing shipped behaviour in the future tense.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Cross-check the self-declared status against the folder that holds it.** `.agents/notes/README.md:68` — the `Status:` value "must agree with the lifecycle folder the file sits in — the gate cross-checks them" — implemented at `scripts/verify-agent-note-format.ts:22-26` (per-lifecycle regex) and `:57-60`. *Why it transfers*: August has exactly this failure mode in the brain (a fact that says "implemented" living in a "proposed" bucket, or a doc that says "shipped" for an unbuilt feature). A duplicated state in two places is a bug generator; make the second copy *checkable* rather than trusted.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Never edit a decision into its opposite — supersede and cross-link instead, with a full-absence test for removals.** `.agents/notes/README.md:48` ("An Agent Note is never edited into a *different decision*: supersede it with a new one, and keep both notes cross-linked"), the consolidation contract at `.agents/notes/README.md:50` (preserve every unique rationale, alternative, consequence, verification and named coverage gap; repair every inbound link; delete the counterpart **and** the sidecar in the same change), and the feature-removal test at `.agents/notes/README.md:52` (absent from production code, configuration, schemas, durable/wire formats, migration and compatibility behaviour; no current doc presents it as available; no test exercises it as supported behaviour; "removing one transport, default, implementation, or presentation is partial supersession"). *Why it transfers*: this is the missing mutation law for August's durable memory. August's `remember` overwrites a fact in place, so a decision that changes is silently restated; and August's "forget" retires a row with no record of what it displaced. A supersession rule (new fact + link to the fact it replaces) plus a full-absence checklist for deletion would make the brain's history legible and would make "I removed the feature" auditable in the same way the note tree makes it auditable.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Make a bilingual/dual-source contract a mergeable, reviewable artifact instead of a gate assertion.** `.agents/notes/README.i18n.yaml:1-4` — the sidecar names itself, its scope, and the exact command that re-records it; `.agents/notes/README.i18n.yaml:5-46` is one entry per heading section with an `en` and a `zh` hash. The design rationale is in `scripts/translation-pairing-record.ts:1-6`: "one entry per heading section with translated content, so independent edits to different sections change separate record lines and merge with Git's default text merge." *Why it transfers*: the generalisable mechanism is **section-scoped, hashed, committed sidecars for any two artifacts that must agree**. August's `check:brain-config` asks the backend which brain keys it accepts and what ranges they take; a sidecar of `{key: {backend_hash, panel_hash}}` recorded per key would turn "the Settings panel and the backend agree" into a diff a human reviews — and, because it is per key, two PRs touching different keys merge cleanly instead of colliding on one generated blob. The same trick works for the desktop/backend protocol contract, where the frontend and `backend-py` are two copies of one schema.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Seal the frozen history with an append-only, hash-manifested archive that can only grow.** `.agents/notes/README.md:40` (archival permits only the triplet move, the `Archived: YYYY-MM-DD` line in both language files, the sidecar re-record and inbound-link repair) and `.agents/notes/README.md:42` ("`verify-archived-agent-notes` enforces the closed class tree, complete triplets, archive metadata, sidecar hashes, and the append-only frozen-content manifest"). The enforcement is `scripts/verify-archived-agent-notes.ts:87-99` (compare against a trusted baseline — `DSH_ARCHIVE_BASE_REF` in CI, `HEAD` locally — and only *extend*) and `:107-112` (write mode adds new artifacts and leaves existing seals unchanged). *Why it transfers*: this is the pattern for August's own audit trail. An append-only manifest of hashes for decisions, prompts and tool schemas gives (a) tamper-evidence — you can prove a shipped prompt was not quietly edited, (b) a cheap diff for "what changed since the last release", and (c) a migration story for the next version, because a seal that may only be extended is a seal whose *history* is reconstructible. The `DSH_ARCHIVE_BASE_REF` detail is the one to copy: CI must compare against a **trusted pre-change commit**, not against whatever the working tree happens to contain, or the check is theatre.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Make the vocabulary closed, and document why the tempting class is absent.** `.agents/notes/README.md:23` (the class set is closed in `scripts/agent-note-tree.ts`; the gate rejects other folders), `.agents/notes/README.md:30-34` ("`architecture` is about the source we ship; `process` is about the surrounding tooling" and "`refactor` is deliberately absent — it overlaps `simplification`, whose discriminator, 'does observable behavior change?', already covers it"), enforced at `scripts/agent-note-tree.ts:19` and `:71-73`. *Why it transfers*: the pattern is not "have a taxonomy", it is "have a closed taxonomy, a gate that rejects anything outside it, and a written answer to the one question a reader will ask — why isn't X a category?" August's brain `kind` values and its tool-name vocabulary have the same drift pressure, and the same answer.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Use size only as a discovery aid, never as a criterion — and calibrate with worked examples.** `.agents/notes/README.md:38` ("Use the calibrated `dsh-archive-agent-notes` workflow rather than word count, age, or a target quota") with the examples in `.agents/skills/dsh-archive-agent-notes/SKILL.md:35-52`: a 533-word note is deleted while a 628-word note is kept, a 334-word note is kept because it names a reintroduction condition, and a 972-word rejected note is deleted because its premise is obsolete. *Why it transfers*: this is exactly the rule August's memory consolidation needs. Any automatic "keep the top-N facts by score" or "retire facts older than N days" policy is size-as-criterion, and the August AGENTS.md already shows the failure mode (a fact dropped for budget silently vanishing from the recall tail).
