A semantic keep/delete/archive classification with calibrated examples is the alternative — and the "keep it because it names the *reintroduction condition*" criterion is a good one to steal verbatim for durable facts.
- **[dsh-notes-index]** - **Freeze the archive's *outbound* links too — a historical snapshot may not be repaired, only preserved.** `.agents/notes/README.md:42` ("Documentation gates skip archived sources, including their outbound links; active prose may still link into an archived note when it intentionally cites history") and `.agents/notes/archived/AGENTS.md:5` ("Do not inspect, verify, or repair links out of archived notes"). *Why it transfers*: the link checker in `scripts/verify-md-links.ts` demonstrably ignores broken links inside archived notes (see its fixture at `scripts/verify-md-links.spec.ts:53`). Any August archive — a frozen prompt, a retired tool schema, a superseded plan — should be excluded from live linting, because "fixing" a frozen artifact is how a historical record starts lying.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Split the compaction checkpoint into frozen index stubs plus exactly one mutable state checkpoint** — `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-07-06-recallable-compaction.md:53` — the request prefix becomes `[system][stubs…][state][tail]`, and because frozen stubs are byte-stable across passes the prompt-cache miss starts at the token replacing the previous state checkpoint instead of at position zero. August's compaction currently rewrites a head checkpoint every pass, which is exactly the position-zero miss this removes; the same note's inflation guard (line 33) gives August a cheap "did compaction actually help?" check by comparing one metric (provider usage, else the character estimator) on both sides.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Make shadowed history reachable with code-composed pointers plus two pure-log tools** — `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-07-06-recallable-compaction.md:25` — every checkpoint ends with `[checkpoint c<summarySeq>: shadows conversation span #<start>–#<end>; originals retrievable via history_read]`, assembled by *code* from the summary event's seq and shadowed range so the model never writes a pointer it could get wrong; `history_read` / `history_search` then re-read the shadowed span from the log. Recall stays a pure function of the log (line 90) because an LLM call in the recall path breaks keyless replay determinism — exactly August's requirement that a session log reconstructs identically.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **The whole-value event rule, with a generic seq-guarded client store** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-27-session-projection-and-command-log.md:23` and `:92` — a state-carrying log event carries the complete post-change state, never a delta, so a consumer can treat the latest pushed value as final (out-of-order immunity by seq, self-healing because a missed update is corrected by the next). The client then keeps one generic `key → { value, seq }` store under a single higher-seq-wins rule, and the host is the only place a projection is computed (`:58`) — a domain ships with **zero client code**. August's brain/permission/goal state could adopt this to collapse the per-domain fences it currently maintains.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Ride the baseline on the tail page so the client has no refetch decision** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-27-session-projection-and-command-log.md:77` — the moments a client needs a fresh baseline (open, reconnect resync, gap repair) are exactly the moments it already pulls the history tail page, and the only path that never needs one (`loadOlder`) is the only path that passes `beforeSeq`. August's front-end currently re-derives "what is current" separately; this deletes that decision instead of managing it.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Log command outcomes durably, as `command/run` + `command/done`** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-27-session-projection-and-command-log.md:126` — a slash command's outcome is currently a transient notice that a refresh or a second tab loses; two log-only events make refresh persistence, multi-tab sync and fork/resume recovery free (`:132`). August's `/compact`, `/brain`, `/memory` commands have the same loss.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Require an `AbortSignal` on every tool-reachable async capability, enforced by the compiler** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-19-required-cancellation-through-tool-capability-seams.md:17` — omission must fail TypeScript compilation, not be discovered at runtime; the note also forbids ambient async-local cancellation (`:39`) and never-abort defaults (`:41`), because both hide the missing owner. August's own cancellation story (turn cancellation, tool timeouts) currently relies on every intermediate layer remembering to forward a signal; this makes forgetting impossible to compile.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Declare derived media and reset them on a closed damage-class list; keep authoritative media loud** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-28-storage-root-and-derived-medium-recovery.md:27` and `:29` — `DomainSpec` gains `recovery?: 'reject' | 'reset'`, and only three deterministic parse-time codes (`version-mismatch`, `malformed-medium`, `invalid-record`) may trigger a destroy-and-reopen; ENOENT and every I/O error stay loud. This is the generalisation August needs for its projection caches, usage ledger and brain-derived tables, where a corrupt derived file must never brick boot while a corrupt authoritative one must.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Keep cleanup dependencies alive until consumers finish — and prove it with one controlled promise** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-10-09-cordis-cleanup-dependency-lifetimes.md:15` and `:81` — the rule is that a resource's owner retains it through the consumers' complete asynchronous cleanup, and the test recipe is a controlled-promise regression: pause the real consumer before its last dependency use, start provider disposal, release the pause, await both. The reproduced failures are concrete and DSH-shaped: `domain 'audit' is closed` (`:35`), `NOT_COMMITTED` after a successful credential write (`:41`), `SSH connection is closed` during subprocess termination (`:49`). August's shutdown path has the same class of ordering hazard around the brain DB, the session writer and credential commits.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **A pre-tool input rewrite must be atomic across three readers** — `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-06-30-pre-tool-input-rewrite.md:13` — `assistant/message` (model history), `tool/call` (durable audit) and the presentation layer all read pre-execution arguments *before* the tool runs, so a partial rewrite would make the UI show one command while another ran. The registry's structured-clone + deep-freeze + non-writable identity makes a partial rewrite *unrepresentable* (`:19`), which is the part worth copying: if August wants to rewrite tool arguments, the rewrite must happen before identity creation, not via a mutable execution object.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Two-stage refactor: mechanical extraction first, behaviour second, with an honest table of what stage one did NOT achieve** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-14-composer-model-and-draft-editor.md:65` and `:53` — stage two is forbidden from moving files, renaming, extracting helpers, reordering tests or cleaning formatting, and stage one publishes a table stating that two editors per session, independent IME/Undo origins and multi-view picker routing are *not* achieved. August's own recent refactors would benefit from the "isolation achieved vs. not achieved" table: it stops a directory move from being reported as a state separation.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Byte-identical system prompts for forked/side sessions, and a sourced message as the merge-back carrier** — `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-07-08-interactive-side-sessions.md:16` — "Keeping the system prompt byte-identical preserves the provider prefix cache over inherited history", and the advisor framing plus the merge-back note are both plugin-sourced `context/message`s, so no new session event is needed and replay stays exact. August's subagent/spawn paths currently pay for a distinct system prompt; this note shows how to get a separate conversation without paying a separate prefix.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **A bounded, versioned, declarative UI model instead of bespoke panels or generated code** — `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-08-04-task-surface.md:32` and `:78` — the model contains "no code, callbacks, selectors, HTML, CSS, URLs to executable assets, or expression language"; limits are schema-backed configuration (64 KiB model, 64 blocks, 32 fields, 200 table rows, 32 KiB submission); unknown versions fall back to the generic tool result rather than being partially interpreted (`:72`); and the Markdown block forces `remoteImages: 'alt-only'` with no model-supplied URL dereferenced without explicit user activation (`:74`). This is directly transferable to August's "ask the user a structured question" surface.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Quarantine unreadable history instead of letting it brick every later request** — `.agents/notes/proposed/bug-fix/2026-08-20-attachment-read-quarantine.md:13` — one missing or corrupt attachment makes every subsequent model request fail on the same object; the fix records a durable `attachment/quarantine` event, replaces the image with deterministic text, skips the read on later requests, and only restores it after digest + metadata verification (`:17`). August has the same shape of problem with tool outputs that reference vanished files.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Per-domain backend routing so a hot domain can move off the human-readable backend without touching consumers** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-24-domain-kv-storage-and-workspace.md:101` and `:293` — `routes: { workspace: 'sqlite' }` selects a backend per domain; "routing is configuration; consumers unchanged", and the migration cost is "migrate the data by hand once". August's brain DB and session sidecar tables are exactly this shape.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Serialise writes in the domain layer and let the backend promise only per-call atomicity** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-24-domain-kv-storage-and-workspace.md:49` and `:160` — the backend does not promise ordering within a unit ("the caller serializes"); the domain owns one promise chain per domain and `update(key, fn)` runs its fn on that chain so concurrent read-modify-write cannot interleave. This is the cleanest statement of the ordering boundary anywhere in the shard.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Staged abstraction refactor with a switchable enforcement gate (warn → enforce)** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-logical-session-storage-rebuild.md:94` — the gate that reports bindings of the concrete class ships as `warn` (prints, emits one `::warning` annotation per finding, exits 0) so in-flight branches merge, and an env var flips it to `enforce` for one run. August can use the identical shape to migrate a wide surface without blocking anyone's branch.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **A universal replay-invariant fixture, and no wall-clock sleeps in tests** — `.agents/notes/proposed/testing/2026-06-11-deterministic-and-stress-testing.md:18` and `:17` — a shared harness replays every test's session log into a fresh `Session` and asserts `deriveMessages()` equality automatically, so the invariant is checked hundreds of times per CI run instead of twice; a lint rule bans `setTimeout` in `packages/*/tests`. August's own "session.messages is what the next turn sends" invariant deserves the same universal assertion, especially given that August has no test suite left.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Mutation testing as the counterweight to a coverage gate when the tests are agent-written** — `.agents/notes/proposed/testing/2026-06-11-mutation-testing.md:9` and `:17` — a per-file 100% coverage gate proves every line *executes*, not that any assertion would notice if the line were wrong, and "under agent-written tests, coverage pressure can produce execution-without-assertion". The surviving-mutant loop ("an agent picks a survivor, writes the killing test, repeats") is exactly the autonomous work item shape August already uses for skills.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Freeze the negative dependency verdicts** — `.agents/notes/rejected/simplification/2026-07-26-dependency-swaps-rejected-by-nih-audit.md:9` — the negative verdicts "carry equal value … but would otherwise live only in a PR body", and a future proposal for any item "must beat its recorded reason, not just re-cite the policy" (`:13`). August's own "why not use library X" reasoning is scattered; a single frozen catalogue of ~30 rejected swaps (each with the concrete reason — wrong execution model, cannot express a needed bound, inverts teardown semantics, breaks the test fakes) is directly reusable.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Record a rejection with the reason the implementation failed, not just the argument against** — `.agents/notes/rejected/simplification/2026-07-26-builtin-timer-promises-for-hand-rolled-sleeps.md:3` — the Status line reads "implementation (PR #679) falsified the parity premise: vitest's fake clock does not intercept `node:timers/promises`, so the swap costs deterministic fast tests for ~10 deleted lines". This is the most useful form of a rejected note: it prevents the next person from re-deriving the failure.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Keep durable boundaries that record facts the log otherwise cannot reconstruct** — `.agents/notes/rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-drop-durable-step-boundaries.md:11` — `step/end` is "concrete information: a reader can tell whether a model request finished, crashed, or is being repaired without deriving that state from the next event", and a bare `step/start` covers "a model request that began but produced no chunks before failing". August's turn/step boundaries should be judged by the same test: can the log answer "did this finish, crash, or get repaired?" without inference?
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Preserve the tail of an interrupted turn rather than truncating it, and say what the future feature must look like** — `.agents/notes/rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-truncate-interrupted-turns.md:30` — the rejection accepts that a crash can lose real work and explains that a future "recover partial crashed work" feature "should be designed as an explicit user-facing recovery view, not as synthetic events silently inserted into the canonical transcript". The distinction — synthetic repair events versus a recovery view — is the part worth carrying into August's resume path.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **An ecosystem survey doubles as a self-audit of your own gaps** — `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-10-03-pi-plugins-compatibility.md:96` and `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-10-03-pi-extensions-bridge.md:79` — the plugin note's "runtime differences the plugin model exposes" table compares Chord and DSH on provider replacement, fault isolation, remote declaration, shared state and runtime loading, and admits these differences "also apply to DSH work that has nothing to do with Pi"; the bridge note produces a 15-row ranked gap table of DSH mechanisms narrower than Pi's, each with a tracking issue. Mapping a foreign harness onto your own services is a cheap way to find your own seams.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Two Chord mechanisms worth stealing regardless of Pi** — `.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-10-03-pi-plugins-compatibility.md:108` and `:109` — *stable service handles* (a consumer keeps its handle while a provider is replaced, so a plugin reload does not restart its dependents and lose their state — DSH's equivalent unloads and re-runs the fiber) and *declaration before activation* (the host rejects a missing provider, a duplicate provider, or a cycle before any facet activates; "Cordis resolves dependencies as services appear, so a fiber with a missing provider stays pending until an audit after startup reports it"). Both are direct answers to August's plugin-reload and missing-dependency problems.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Untrusted content in an agent prompt needs a nonce, not a warning** — `.agents/notes/proposed/process/2026-07-13-human-review-skill-maintenance.md:47` — feedback is wrapped in a nonce-tagged `<untrusted-feedback nonce="…">` block that every prompt instructs the model to treat as data, and "the 128-bit nonce prevents an untrusted body from forging the closing tag". The same note refuses to run when the two reviewer executables are byte-identical (`:47`) and scrubs the environment for every `git`/`gh`/gate spawn so a pre-push hook cannot redirect the maintainer.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **A per-heading hash pairing record for bilingual docs, with an explicit regenerate command** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-07-27-session-projection-and-command-log.i18n.yaml:1` and `:4` — each heading section gets an `en:`/`zh:` hash of its block (excluding code blocks and generated regions), and `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <file.md>` re-records after an edit. August has no equivalent, and the same sidecar mechanism could track *API-contract* drift between two implementations instead of two languages.
- **[dsh-notes-proposed]** - **Separate "required" from "unknown": report a missing total honestly instead of fabricating a percentage** — `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-29-session-migration-follow-redirect.md:38` — "Unknown totals produce no fabricated percentages", and the redirect ("302" as a business result, not an HTTP redirect, accepting no arbitrary URL, `:13`) keeps migration progress out of the session log entirely (`:17`). August's long-running operations (backend updates, brain maintenance) could use the same typed-redirect shape instead of pushing progress into the transcript.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **A "capability façade" that denies by default and *teaches* each denial** — `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/guard.ts:718` — a `Proxy` over an empty object exposing only lifecycle verbs and *declared* services, where a denial names the fix ("Declare it: inject: ['x', …] on your plugin, so cordis parks this dynamic package if the provider later goes away"). August's sandbox equivalents (code runner, tool surface) can adopt the same shape: a whitelist facade whose every refusal carries the exact declaration the caller must add.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Deny a service that returns a live context handle, on both the sync and the promise path** — `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/guard.ts:669` — `denyContext` wraps every service method and checks the *resolved* value, which closes the "service.ctx.root" escape that a naive `instanceof` check on the raw return would miss. The browser half repeats the rule against *its own* `Context` class, and the file explains why the duplication is deliberate (guard.ts:663-667) — each half must test against the class of its own face.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Expose a tool's *schema*, never its `execute`** — `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/guard.ts:648` — `ctx.tools.get(name)` returns the same name/description/parameters view as `schemas()`, so untrusted code cannot call another tool directly and bypass the dispatch-time guards (identity protection, pre-policy, monotonic guards, post-policy, result normalization). August's tool registry should expose a read-only view to any sandboxed caller, not the live definition.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Make a *withheld capability* throw a message that names where it really lives** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/evaluator.ts:43` — the closure's parameters shadow `setTimeout`/`fetch`/`require` with traps whose error text redirects to the sanctioned route ("Declare inject: ['timer'] on the returned plugin …"). This converts a silent failure into a self-correcting model turn, and it is the same pattern August needs for "you cannot shell out directly; use the sandboxed `run_command`".
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Reuse one redirect table to enrich a *later* error the model actually sees** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/runtime.ts:504` — a render crash whose text merely *names* a withheld global gets the same redirect appended (and only if it is not already there). The author gets the same advice whether they hit the trap directly or reached the global around it.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Converge loads by identity against live state, and always answer** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/runtime.ts:288` — re-issuing the exact activation already live is a no-op that still returns a success receipt, because "a replayed run must not look unacknowledged". August's tool/subagent registries should answer a duplicate request from live state rather than from history, and should never leave a caller waiting.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **A per-item operation queue whose tail survives a failure** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/runtime.ts:334` — `this.queues.set(id, next.then(() => {}, () => {}))`: one rejected operation would otherwise wedge every later operation on the same item. A one-line pattern that removes a whole class of "the tool is stuck forever" bugs.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Attribute a crash by the *identity of the thing that crashed*** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/runtime.ts:202` — a `WeakMap` from the seated component to its owner, with a comment enumerating why each alternative (a parallel ledger, `entry.registrant`, the assigned priority) fails. Any August subsystem that lets a caller register a callback and later wants to report "your callback crashed" should key on the callback's identity.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Progressive API disclosure with a *referenced type closure*** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/api-catalog.ts:1101` and `:1128` — list a compact directory of services and method signatures, then one exact contract, then **only the types that contract mentions**, transitively. This is the pattern to copy for any model-facing API surface: directory first, exact contract second, transitive types third.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Pin a capability's *identity* so a caller cannot impersonate or evict another** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/guard.ts:154` — `theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)`'s `source` argument is *replaced* with the package id, and the disposer is hung on the calling fiber so unload restores even when the caller drops the handle. The same "you may not name yourself" rule appears for the `tool.view.cordis` slot key (guard.ts:119).
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **A per-verb, per-service facade for a client half that mirrors the host half** — `packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/guard.ts:1` — the two halves implement the *same* whitelist contract in two programs, which is what lets an author meet "one contract on both halves". August's browser/host split (if it has one) should define the contract once in prose and implement it twice, rather than inventing one per plane.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Refuse a resolution that names a run that is not the live one** — `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/index.ts:438` — `resolveRequestRun` returns `{accepted: false}` when the resolution's `pluginRunId` is not the live activation. A stale success is not accepted, and the caller is told why; the browser half does not read the acknowledgement, so the *host* must be the authority. August's approval round trip needs the same rule.
- **[dsh-platform#1]** - **Report a runtime failure to the owning session *once* per (kind, message)** — `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/index.ts:1136` — `claimRuntimeFailure` keys on a NUL-joined string and checks the attempt's status, so a repeatedly failing handler cannot spam the transcript with the same message. The steering message is a *user* message, so the model's prompt prefix is untouched (index.ts:1075).

- **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **Never parse a tool call's arguments while the call is still streaming** — `patches/@earendil-works__pi-ai@1.1.0.patch:9` — DSH deletes `block.arguments = parseStreamingJson(block.partialJson)` from *six* provider accumulators (Anthropic, Bedrock, Mistral, OpenAI-completions, OpenAI-responses, pi-messages) so the argument string is accumulated but only parsed when the call completes. **Why it transfers to August:** today a partial JSON fragment is "best-effort parsed" and can silently become `{}` or a half-built object that then executes. - **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **Detect a capability by exercising it, not by asking its version** — `native/system/packages/entry/src/index.ts:116` — `probe()` spawns `landlock-run --probe`, which installs a *maximal* ruleset in a short-lived child and exits 0 only if the running kernel actually enforces it. A capability that reports itself as present and then fails at first use is worse than one that reports itself absent.
- **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **Make the confinement decision depend on state that the model cannot influence** — `native/system/packages/entry/src/index.ts:12` and `native/system/packages/entry/src/index.ts:80` — "which binary confines a process must never be decidable by the ambient environment"; the fallback launcher path is absolute precisely so "a spawnable relative path here would hand cwd control over which binary confines". **Why it transfers to August:** the same rule applies to August's sandbox backend selection, its credential store, and its provider registry — none of them may be steered by an environment variable, a relative path, or a `cwd` that a tool call can change. August already fights this battle for the credential scrub (env collection is `*_API_KEY` only, the cache is stamped on `providers.json`); DSH shows the generalisation — make the *choice* of the mechanism environment-independent, and make the *fallback* an absolute path that cannot resolve.
- **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **Separate "our failure" from "the child's failure" by requiring a second signal** — `native/system/docs/cli-contract.md:22` — every launcher-level failure exits `125`, but after a successful `exec` the child's own 125 passes through unchanged, so "consumers therefore require both status 125 **and** a `landlock-run: ` fatal line to attribute launcher failure". **Why it transfers to August:** August wraps subprocesses (bash, pwsh, node-pty, the sandbox launcher) and reuses exit codes across layers. - **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **Bound a recurrence search by the calendar's own repeat period** — `packages/schedule/schedule/src/domain.ts:51` — `CRON_SEARCH_HORIZON_YEARS = 400`, with the reasoning: "The proleptic Gregorian leap-year and weekday alignment repeats every 400 years, so a rule that matches any local date has a match within this window; walking further can only reach a rule that never matches. August's compaction, retry and scheduling code all have such scans.
- **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **Give a recurring task only its latest missed occurrence** — `packages/schedule/schedule/README.md:12` — "each recurring task contributes only its latest missed occurrence", and due recurring tasks in one Session share a single message (`packages/schedule/schedule/src/domain.ts:1883` renders one `[SCHEDULE REMINDER BATCH]` frame carrying a JSON array). **Why it transfers to August:** after a long outage or a cold resume, the naive behaviour is to replay N missed reminders into the context window, which is both wrong (the user wants the current state, not a backlog) and expensive. - **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **Distinguish "delivered" from "executed", and commit the receipt only after the durable write** — `packages/schedule/schedule/src/runtime.ts:85` and `packages/schedule/schedule/README.md:65` — delivery resolves the Session, appends to the inbox synchronously, awaits the Session flush, and only then writes the receipt: "The receipt confirms inbox delivery, not model execution." - **[dsh-repo-root#2]** - **A publish step that is idempotent per content, and refuses a silent content change** — `native/system/scripts/publish-release.mjs:117` — after a failed publish the script re-reads the registry: the same integrity means "it landed despite the reported failure" (success), different integrity means "already published with different content … Bump the version, or investigate why the build is not reproducible" (hard failure). **Why it transfers to August:** August releases a desktop installer; a partially-completed publish must be resumable, and a rebuild that changes the bytes must not be silently published under an existing version. - **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **A config change that only touches volatile fields is applied to the RUNNING fiber instead of remounting it** — `vendor/loader/src/config/entry.ts:146`. The decision is made by a pure comparison (`equalExceptVolatile`) plus three guards (the only changed key is `config`, the fiber is `ACTIVE`, the context prototype is unchanged); if it is volatile-only, `_commitVolatile` re-parses the candidate through the fiber's own `internal/config` hook, verifies the *ordinary* effective values are unchanged, commits the new values into the live references and emits `loader/volatile-update` with the changed paths. August's equivalent problem — a settings change that must reach a live agent without destroying its conversation, its tool handles or its provider prefix — has the same shape: decide "is this a value change or a reference change?" *before* tearing anything down, and make the reference update a single auditable commit.
- **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Compare two configurations using the schema's metadata, without executing anything** — `vendor/loader/src/config/diff.ts:17`. `equalExceptVolatile` walks the schema's `dict`, treats a `meta.volatile` node as equal, uses a node's **declared default** for a missing/null value, and falls back to strict raw equality for unknown fields, `!!js` expression nodes, opaque values and schema back-edges. The important part is the negative space: no validator, no transform, no `internal/config` waterfall and no expression evaluation runs during a change decision. A change-detection pass that can fire side effects is a change-detection pass that can hang.
- **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Register an effect's owner-list wrapper BEFORE running its setup body** — `vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:520`. An unload begun from inside the setup then awaits the setup and every collected cleanup; a synchronous setup failure removes the wrapper and rolls back the collected cleanup; async teardown stays owner-visible until it settles. This is the pattern August needs wherever a disposer can be re-entered (a tool call that disposes the session that owns it).
- **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Let a structural owner JOIN a cleanup another caller already started, while the public disposer stays single-shot** — `vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:112`. - **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Contain a teardown-notification failure per observer** — `vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:120`. `emitPluginDisposed` dispatches the event, then invokes each callback inside its own try/catch and attaches a `.catch` to any returned promise, logging failures through the logger. - **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Detect a runtime's capabilities, never its version** — `vendor/loader/src/internal.ts:138`. `ModuleLoader.fromInternal()` classifies Node's internal loader by *which module-job API it owns* (`getOrCreateModuleJob` → v2, `getModuleJobForImport` → v1), because v2 landed in 24.12.0 and a major-version test mistags every 24.0–24.11.1 loader; arity cannot discriminate the two shapes, and a loader owning neither API is left **unclassified** rather than guessed. The recorded symptom of that bug was a Web UI that served an empty client graph behind a warn-level log. August's per-model `apiFormat` and its provider-family detection should use the same rule: branch on the API you actually observed, and when you cannot tell, take the documented fallback instead of guessing.
- **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **A bounded, serialized write queue with a retry ladder for transient OS failures** — `vendor/include/src/index.ts:299` and `vendor/include/src/index.ts:318`. Writes go to `<file>.tmp` and are then renamed; a rename that fails with `EACCES`/`EBUSY`/`EPERM` is retried up to 10 times with a linear backoff (Windows can briefly retain the destination handle after a child disposes); a terminal failure stays on the queue so `Include.stop()` rethrows it rather than silently declaring persistence complete. This is the shape August's "write a fact, write a skill, write a session file" paths want: never lose a write to a transient Windows error, and never report success you did not have.
- **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Reject a configuration file that is not a top-level list, and commit content only on success** — `vendor/include/src/index.ts:230`. An empty or truncated file (editors and `sed -i` write through temp states) parses to `undefined` rather than raising, so the shape is validated explicitly and one "invalid file" signal is emitted. Because `content` and `data` commit only on success, an edit that is later reverted to the exact last good content correctly reads as "unchanged" — no spurious restart, no spurious rewrite.
- **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **A hot reload must never take the process down** — `vendor/include/src/index.ts:279`. `refresh()` catches every error, logs "config reload at %C failed; keeping the running tree", and leaves the last good tree in place. - **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Make the patch algorithm a pure exported function so an offline tool cannot drift from the runtime** — `vendor/include/src/index.ts:57`. `applyEntryPatches(data, patches, warn)` is exported and the class method delegates to it, precisely so `dsh --dump-config` composes and prints exactly what the include would mount: "config tooling must never reimplement (and drift from) the patch algorithm." It also `structuredClone`s its input, because patching shared entry objects would bake earlier patch values into the cached parse and a repeated application could never revert a removed patch. - **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Enforce a *placement* rule for mutable config at validation time** — `vendor/schemastery/src/index.ts:493`. `validateVolatileSchema` throws "volatile fields require a fixed object path without an enclosing volatile field" — a volatile field may not sit inside another volatile field, nor inside an array, dict or tuple, because the runtime commits by *path* and a path is only stable in a fixed object shape. - **[dsh-repo-root#3]** - **Strip defaults when persisting, and let the schema be the UI contract** — `vendor/schemastery/src/index.ts:422`. `simplify(value)` walks the schema backwards and removes every value equal to its declared default, so the saved config stays minimal; it unwraps a volatile reference first so a reference is stored as plain data. Two pieces transfer directly: (a) a version boundary is a **package with a manifest**, not a `switch` statement, so it can be versioned and published independently; (b) the migration chain is validated by a generator that refuses a gap or a non-continuing codec, rather than by the runtime when it fails.
- **[dsh-scripts#1]** - **Make the failure of a batch migration a structured, grouped report rather than a log line** — `scripts/migrate-sessions-to-v4.ts:60` (`summarizeFailures`) and `scripts/migration-failure-summary.ts:23` (`classifyMigrationFailure`). The mechanism: failures are classified into a **closed** reason vocabulary (`unexpected_member`, `unknown_event`, `sequence_gap`, `source_changed`, `write_locked`, `unsupported_input`, `corrupt_log`, `other`) by matching the diagnostic text, and the report groups them while retaining each input's own diagnostic. The docstring states the boundary: "classification never changes migration admission." **Why it transfers:** this is the shape an August tool-failure report should take. A model that sees "seven sessions failed" learns nothing; a model that sees "three failed with `sequence_gap`, two with `write_locked`, one `unknown_event`" can act. And the rule that classification must not gate admission is what keeps the reporter from becoming a new way to lose data.
- **[dsh-scripts#1]** - **Defer the inputs that lost a race, and retry them exactly once after the initial pass drains** — `scripts/migrate-sessions-to-v4.ts:148` (`runMigrationJobs`). The mechanism: bounded workers pull indices from a shared cursor; a worker that hits a source-changed error returns `true` and its index is pushed to a deferred list; after every worker has settled, the deferred indices are retried **serially**, in order. An unexpected rejection drains the workers and aborts the retry pass. **Why it transfers:** this is a precise pattern for the August agent loop. A tool call that races another writer (a file being edited, a memory being updated) should not be retried blindly in parallel — defer it, let the initial pass drain, then retry once. And a genuine crash must abort the retry pass rather than silently half-finishing.
- **[dsh-scripts#1]** - **Refuse to trust a search that returns nothing, and require the corpus to be non-empty** — `scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts:593` (`checkExperimentalDependencyIsolation`, where an optional bundle may be depended on only if the launcher names it) and `scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts:1131` (the walk backstop requiring every declared key to be rendered *or* exempted). The pattern: an allowlist with a *named* exemption for each absence, and an exemption that must be live in both directions (an exemption for something that is now rendered is an error). **Why it transfers:** in August, "the tool exists but is not advertised" and "the tool is advertised but does not exist" are the two failure modes that make a model loop. An exemption table that must be maintained in both directions is the cheapest way to keep an inventory honest.
- **[dsh-scripts#1]** - **Isolate the tool cache, the interpreter and the credentials of a child process from the host** — `scripts/ci-compatible-toolcache.mjs:6` (the `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE` redirect), `scripts/primary-runtime/prepare.ts:245` (`smokePrimaryRuntime`'s credential-scrubbed environment) and `scripts/benchmark-npm-resolution.ts:375` (the stripped `npm_config_*` set). The mechanism in all three: the child's environment is constructed explicitly, not inherited by accident. **Why it transfers:** an August agent that spawns a shell tool must scrub the parent's credential-shaped variables from the child's environment. The August backend already has a precedent for this (the tool-boundary secret guard), but the *reverse* direction — not letting the agent's subprocess read the harness's own secrets — needs the same explicit-environment discipline at every spawn site.
- **[dsh-scripts#1]** - **Fail the build when a plugin registers fewer tools than it claims** — `scripts/gen-tool-catalog.ts:744` (`assertToolsHarvested`) and `scripts/gen-tool-catalog.ts:718` (`assertManifestComplete`, which checks the manifest against every on-disk `tool-*` package). The mechanism: the manifest is a *claim*; the runtime registration is the *fact*; the gate compares them in both directions. **Why it transfers:** the same two-direction check belongs on August's tool registry — every tool the harness advertises to the model must exist at runtime, and every tool that exists must be advertised (or explicitly withheld). The check is nearly free and catches the two most expensive agent failures: a model calling a missing tool, and a model never discovering an existing one.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A gate runner with two levels of dependency — "must pass" and "must settle"** - `scripts/run-gates.ts:1142` - `predecessorsReady` requires every `needs` gate to have **passed** but every `after` gate only to have **settled** (passed, failed or skipped). This is the dependency primitive August needs for "a diagnostic must still run after its sibling fails": today every August check either blocks or does not, and a failed dependency silently suppresses the evidence you wanted. The `after` edge is what lets a Windows lane run `built-bin-smoke` on an existing build even when `doc-graphs` failed (`scripts/run-gates.spec.ts:560`).
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Kill the whole process tree, and prove the tree is quiescent before reporting** - `scripts/run-gates.ts:1350` - `confirmGroupGone` refuses to settle the gate until the POSIX process group *and* every captured descendant pid are confirmed gone, polling for 8 s and then failing **loud** ("gate tree not quiescent after 8s") rather than reporting a quiescent tree. August's Windows subprocess teardown has exactly the failure this prevents: the wrapper dies, a grandchild keeps the stdio pipe open, and the harness reports "passed" over a live leak. The companion detail that makes it work — zombies do not count as alive (`scripts/run-gates.ts:1414`) — is the same class of bug as a zombie `kill(pid, 0)` probe in a Windows child tracker.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A descendant cache that MERGES rather than replaces, because an exited intermediate orphans its children** - `scripts/run-gates.ts:1317` - `descendants = [...new Set([...descendants.filter(processAlive), ...fresh])]`. The comment explains it: re-enumeration alone drops a descendant that an exited intermediate reparented out of the parent chain, so the cache is the source of truth once the child is gone. August's process supervision should keep the same union semantics, plus the 5-second sampler (`scripts/run-gates.ts:1325`) that captures a descendant before it can escape.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A gate that produces no evidence is `skipped`, never `passed` — and a child that trapped the signal still counts as aborted** - `scripts/run-gates.ts:1130` and `scripts/run-gates.ts:1386` - `skippedByFailFast` records `status: 'skipped'` with `error: 'aborted by fail-fast: <cause>'`, and `runGate` sets `result.aborted = true` independently of the exit code, so a child that traps SIGTERM and exits zero cannot be reported as passed. The Windows analogue of your own lesson ("a killed process is indistinguishable from a failed one by exit code alone") is generalised here into a first-class field.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Fingerprint an assertion by its SYNTAX TOKENS, and consume the allowance** - `scripts/verify-no-unknown-casts.ts:25` - `syntaxFingerprint` hashes the assertion's token stream with comments and whitespace excluded, so a baseline allowance is tied to the exact shape of the assertion rather than to a file, a line or an occurrence order; `verifyNoUnknownCasts` then *decrements* the allowance per occurrence (`scripts/verify-no-unknown-casts.ts:155`), so an old allowance can never launder a new assertion and a leftover allowance is an error requiring `--prune`. August's ratchet gates (lint:ratchet, the coverage floor) should key on a content fingerprint, not on a count per file.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **"A scanner gate that passes on zero matches is not a gate"** - `scripts/verify-no-unknown-casts.ts:91` and `scripts/verify-concrete-terms.ts:56` - Both gates assert that their *discovery* still covers a required area (`packages/`, `apps/`, `scripts/`, `website/`; `AGENTS.md`, `docs/`, `vendor/`, the archived notes) and throw if a glob stopped matching. `verify-no-bare-dispatcher.ts:206` does the same for its corpus. August's `check:*` gates are exactly the kind that can silently start scanning nothing.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A growth budget expressed in the SYSTEM'S OWN work units, with the hang guard derived from it** - `scripts/verify-npm-install-layout.ts:33` - `MAX_RESOLUTION_WORK_UNITS = 875_000` is "packages × internal edges", chosen because npm's hoisted placement re-checks every internal edge against the incoming edges of its peer target, so resolution time grows with the product and not with the package count. The wall-clock hang guard is computed *from* the same constant (`scripts/verify-npm-install-layout.ts:48`) "so a raised budget cannot silently shrink the guard's headroom". August should price its context-window and compaction work the same way: count the work, budget the work, and derive the timeout from the budget.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Prove an edit is PARSE-NEUTRAL, or re-parse** - `scripts/translation-pairing-record.ts:96` - `isParseNeutralEdit` accepts an edit only when it exchanges characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._/:#%-]` inside a complete, title-free destination that does not start a line; only then are node offsets moved arithmetically (`normalizedTopLevelBlocks`, line 125) instead of re-parsing. August rewrites model-visible JSON and Markdown in several places; this is a cheap, provable way to keep offsets correct after a rewrite.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **"Any line that LOOKS like a region marker must parse as one"** - `scripts/translation-pairing.ts:25` - A loose detector (`GENERATED_REGION_MARKER_HINT`) sits next to the strict parser, so a typo'd `<!-- BEGIN GENERATED … -->` is a loud error instead of unmarked text that silently escapes the region comparison. - **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Keep filename context OUT of the model request and correct the switcher afterwards** - `scripts/translation-prompt.ts:74` and `scripts/translation-prompt.ts:252` - The pipeline retains the source basename, derives the target filename and the correct language switcher itself, and the model's job is only the document body. The same principle is visible in the SDK snapshots: the target path is never model-visible. August's prompt construction should keep paths out of the prompt and substitute them after the model returns, so the model cannot invent one.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Normalise the volatile, keep the diagnostic — and keep the repair id** - `scripts/smoke-python-runtime.py:2702` - `normalize_snapshot_value` tokenizes ids, timestamps and paths, but explicitly preserves an `interrupted-tool-result-<callId>-<n>` id (line 2763) because that id is deterministic and is itself the evidence that a tool result was repaired. This is the shape a golden needs: everything unstable is normalized away, and every fact that *means* something is kept.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Compare golden files by ROLE, not by name** - `scripts/smoke-python-runtime.py:3027` - `role_name` maps `session.1.v4.jsonl` to the role `session.1.jsonl` and the comparison selects the highest generation present on each side. A fixture can therefore gain a new session-format generation without the golden going stale, and the corpus keeps the old generations as migration inputs. August's session-format goldens need exactly this when the format version moves.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A corpus policy that names the migration coverage it keeps, and caps it** - `scripts/session-snapshot-corpus-policy.ts:96` - Every historical generation must be covered by a *named* retained scenario (`multi-hop`, `packed-row`, `retry-failure`, `shipped-profile` for v0; `adjacent-migration` for the rest), retained roles are capped at 13, and `baseline + current` must outnumber `retained`. A corpus cannot fossilize, and "we kept the old fixture" becomes a reviewable sentence rather than a folder of forgotten files.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Point a failure at the line a human can open** - `scripts/session-fixture-layout.ts:187` - `fixtureDiagnosticLine` maps a codec error ("released Session row 3", "Session event 7", "inherited Session cut 2") back to the physical source line of the fixture file. August's session decoder errors currently name an event index; naming the file line turns "the fixture is wrong" into "fix this line".
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A packed row carries N events, so the sequence counter must advance by the CARDINALITY** - `scripts/session-fixture-layout.ts:83` - `projectedRowCardinality` counts the texts/args in a `text-chunks` / `reasoning-chunks` / `tool-call-chunks` row, and the sequence number advances by that count. This is the single most transferable detail in the shard for anyone reading a *streamed* session log: one physical row can be many logical events, and an off-by-one there corrupts every later sequence number.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **The reason a rule exists is written next to the rule, with the measured number** - `scripts/verify-no-bare-dispatcher.ts:4` and `scripts/verify-mermaid.ts:83` - The dispatcher gate states the concrete defect it prevents ("its DNS-pinning agent silently bypassed every proxy") and records the cost of the naive approach ("21 of 1597 files survive the filter"); the Mermaid gate records *why* the edge limit was raised rather than trimming the graph ("The graph passed 1000 the same way it passed 500"). August's gate comments are usually conclusions; these are measurements.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **An escape hatch that is greppable and reviewable** - `scripts/verify-no-bare-dispatcher.ts:36` - `proxy-exempt:` on the offending line or the line directly above excuses the violation, and the reason for placing it on the line above is written down ("a syntax-aware match anchors on the property or `new` expression rather than the statement"). August's sandbox and tool gates need an escape that a reviewer can find with `grep`, not one buried in a policy file.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Cross-product policy equivalence as a first-class check** - `scripts/verify-skill-invocation-metadata.ts:94` - The gate asserts `disable-model-invocation === true` ⟺ `policy.allow_implicit_invocation === false` and that a manual-only skill stays user-invocable. August ships several front-ends over one core; this is the pattern for "the same rule, spelled two ways, must agree".
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A release is published only when EVERY target carries its own evidence** - `scripts/ssh-helper/release.ts:35` - `prepareSshRelease` requires four archives, each digest-matched, `dirty: false`, from the same commit, plus per-target evidence reports (Linux: no-Node + glibc 2.28 + landlock; macOS: restricted worker), and writes `SHA256SUMS` from the digests it just verified. The `dirty: false` assertion alone — a release artifact may not come from a dirty checkout — is worth taking.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A binary that must run with NO Node and an EMPTY environment** - `scripts/ssh-helper/worker-probe.ts:22` and `scripts/ssh-helper/worker-probe.ts:59` - The Seatbelt profile denies read and exec of the checkout and the host Node, and the probe asserts `result.env` deep-equals `[]`. - **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Assert the ground truth you actually depend on, not the convenient one** - `scripts/run-memory-pressure-bench.ts:85` - `memoryLimitViolation` compares the cgroup's `memory.max` AND `memory.swap.max` AND `process.constrainedMemory()` (which reflects *ancestor* cgroups), and refuses to run if any disagrees. A benchmark that silently ran unconstrained would produce a meaningless number, and the third check is exactly the one an ancestor cgroup would defeat.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Model the retry/denial ladder in the GOLDEN, not in prose** - `scripts/smoke-python-runtime.py:363` - The scheduler-recovery scenario pins the exact `is_error` sequence `[False, True, True]` across three tool results, that the *unstarted* third call was never dispatched, and that the failed call's `is_error` stayed true after the next turn. Your own lesson — "the refusal text was read as success by every downstream consumer" — is exactly what a golden of this shape catches: the marker vocabulary is checked against every emitter, one emitter at a time.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **Two spellings of one policy must agree; a third must be added, not inferred** - `scripts/verify-skill-invocation-metadata.ts:94`, `scripts/verify-client-ui-i18n.ts:33` - The UI gate has a hard floor: `MINIMUM_CLIENT_UI_SOURCES = 450` (`scripts/verify-client-ui-i18n.ts:15`), so the rule cannot be defeated by the corpus shrinking. A minimum-size assertion on every i18n / copy gate is the cheapest way to stop a copy rule from becoming a no-op.
- **[dsh-scripts#2]** - **A gate that is also a "did the toolchain regress?" tripwire** - `scripts/verify-node-next-types.ts:146` - tsc is invoked through `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc` rather than the `.bin` shim, with the reason recorded: the extensionless shim is not spawnable on Windows (CVE-2024-27980) and the `.cmd` variant needs `shell:true`, which space-joins arguments unescaped (DEP0190). The same file explains that `skipLibCheck: true` is scoped to third-party noise because "the explicit scan above owns our regression" — i.e. the gate disables exactly as much of the checker as it has replaced.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **A "checkpoint the side effect, not the outcome" barrier at three named seams** — `packages/session/session-checkpoint-policy/src/index.ts:64` — the model request is flushed *before the adapter stream is even constructed*, the top-level tool call is flushed *before the tool body runs*, and `agent/pre-step` flushes the previous step's response/results. This is exactly the shape August needs for "a crash between a recorded tool call and its result" — and the nested-call exemption (`exec.parent !== undefined` → skip) means a nested dispatch inherits the outer call's durability instead of paying for it twice.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Fail-closed unknown-vocabulary gate with an actionable message** — `packages/session/session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:75` — an event type this build does not know, unless its writer marked it `ignorable: true`, refuses the whole log with "it was likely written by a newer harness". August's session/event readers should refuse rather than skip: silently skipping an unknown *required* event reconstructs a wrong conversation, and the user is told to upgrade rather than told the file is corrupt.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Direction-aware refusal text** — `packages/session/session-persistence/src/errors.ts:134` — newer format → "the log was written by a newer harness — upgrade the harness to open it"; older format → "this build ships no upgrade path for it". - **[dsh-session#1]** - **Validate-and-snapshot in ONE traversal** — `packages/session/session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:131` — `materializeAppendBatch` refuses "a check followed by a copy could reread accessors into a different record". The value that is *checked* is the value that is *persisted*. August's tool-argument and event-batch writers have the same TOCTOU exposure if they validate then copy.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Whole-value event rule for anything a projection folds** — `packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts:13` — "a state-carrying log event MUST carry the complete post-change state, never a bare delta — it keeps every unit's transition trivially cheap and every served value self-describing". August's `update_state` and todo events could adopt this: a delta forces every reader to maintain history, a whole value makes the read O(1) and the log self-sufficient.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Reference identity as the change gate** — `packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts:66` and `packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts:690` — a unit that returns the *same state reference* for an uninteresting event produces zero downstream work, and the wire view is compared with `Object.is` across two retained slots. This is a zero-cost, allocation-free way to keep a change feed quiet; August's SSE emitters could use the same two-slot comparison instead of diffing.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Cache is a fold shortcut, never an authority — and the write order proves it** — `packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/index.ts:10` and `packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/index.ts:266` — "a row is possibly stale (its `seq` says how stale) but never wrong"; every write path is fail-soft; a `ver` mismatch *discards* rather than migrates. And the write order flushes the **session log before** the checkpoint row, so "a crash can leave the cache behind the log (longer tail replay) but never ahead of it (phantom values folded from events no stored log contains)". This is the single most transferable ordering rule in the shard.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **A session id names a SLOT, not a LIFECYCLE** — `packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/spec.ts:38` — the cache record binds `formatVersion` + `createdAt` + `cwd` + `isSeeded` + `inheritedEventCount`; "a deleted-then-recreated id, or a persistence root swapped under a surviving cache, would otherwise let an old record pass every watermark check and seed state folded from an unrelated log". August's brain/session caches should bind a lifecycle identity, not just a row key.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **A protected system head that no compaction may shadow** — `packages/session/session-format-v2-to-v3/src/validation.ts:43` — the first appended surface event becomes the head; a surface replacement must replace *exactly* that head ("system/message must replace exactly the current system head"), and neither a surface replacement nor a compaction span may include it. This is the session-log form of "the system prompt must never be compacted away" and it is enforced at the data layer, not by convention.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **An allow-list of sequence references** — `packages/session/session-format-v2-to-v3/src/references.ts:30` — only `command/done.sourceEventSeq`, `compaction/*.{shadowedRange,shadowedSeqs}`, `session/title*.messageSeqs` and the envelope fields are remapped, and the comment says why: "Delivery watermarks and session-reference captures identify their original generation. August's compaction/prune path needs exactly this discipline.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Refuse rather than guess** — `packages/session/session-format-v2-to-v3/src/payload.ts:50` and `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/migration.ts:24` — an unclassified event type, an unclassified message content kind, or a body migration without explicit child evidence is a hard refusal, each with a message naming what was missing. August's format migrations should have the same "there is no safe default" posture.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **The system prompt is emitted only on CHANGE** — `packages/session/session-format-v2-to-v3/src/migration.ts:53` — `if (prompt !== this.prompt) this.emitSystem(prompt, …)`. August's request-header persistence should do the same: the prompt prefix is stable, and the log should not grow a duplicate copy of it every turn (this is also what keeps the provider's prompt cache warm).
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Immutable generations + exclusive successor publication, verified by a second process** — `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/generation.ts:894` and `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/migration-verifier.ts:108` — the successor is written to a synced temp file, verified by a **fresh Worker thread** that decodes it independently and reports a digest, the source identity is re-checked *after* verification, and publication is a no-overwrite rename; a competing publisher is accepted only if its bytes and digest are identical. August's "publish a new format generation" path needs the same four steps: stage, verify independently, re-check the source, publish exclusively.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **A kernel lock with an inode re-verification and NO expiry** — `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/lease.ts:99` and `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/lease.ts:11` — POSIX `flock` names an inode, so after locking the holder verifies the locked inode is still the file at the lock path and retries otherwise; and "there is deliberately no expiry that could expropriate a stalled writer whose resumed appends would tear the log". Two lessons: verify the lock still refers to the file you think, and never time out a lock whose holder might still be writing.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Crash recovery produces an UNKNOWN OUTCOME, not a retry** — `packages/session/session-checkpoint-policy/README.md:116` — "a persisted call without a result cannot prove whether its external effect completed, so recovery records an unknown outcome instead of retrying"; the recovery message permits retry for read-only or idempotent work and requires verification for side-effecting work. August's interrupted-tool recovery should be worded and behaved the same way, and the repair result is appended *after* the reusable prefix so it does not invalidate the provider's cache.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Provider-attribution becomes producer-owned, and unknown producers survive** — `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/sources.ts:59` and `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/extension-identities.ts:76` — a historical `plugin` source is rewritten to the *producer's own* kind (with an explicit rename table and an explicit same-name table), unknown producers become `plugin:<name>`, and an unknown ignorable event type is namespaced `plugin:<type>` so it can never collide with a future first-party type. August's message-source model should carry the producer, not the plugin wrapper.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Extension fields are re-owned, not dropped** — `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/tool-role.ts:10` — unknown fields on a message and on a wrapper are renamed `plugin:message:<key>` / `plugin:result:<key>` so the two owners' extensions can never merge. - **[dsh-session#1]** - **Validate the wrapper BEFORE dropping it** — `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/tool-role.ts:29` — "Validate the wrapper before dropping it so malformed historical content is rejected instead of being silently truncated." - **[dsh-session#1]** - **Re-derive the model output from the stored stream and compare** — `packages/session/session-format-v1-to-v2/src/testing/validation.ts:61` — re-expand the embedded Assistant stream, push it through a fresh `BlockAssembler`, and require the stored message content, usage and replay state to agree with the assembled result. The transcript carries the stream *and* the assembled message redundantly, and the redundancy is verified — a genuine "the persisted transcript still means what the model produced" check.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **Fold the chunk stream without joining token boundaries** — `packages/session/session-format-v1-to-v2/README.md:46` — the compaction must not merge two text deltas. Reasoning/text deltas are the one thing a log may compact but never merge, because merging changes the model's token stream.
- **[dsh-session#1]** - **A frozen event-type list that must NOT inherit from the current list** — `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/extension-identities.ts:5` — "This historical list must not inherit additions or removals from the current Session event list."
