Transfer value: August changes its sandbox/permission mode under the agent; DSH shows the three pieces — abort the in-flight work, log the change as a session event, and re-state the policy to the model.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **Subagent delegation becomes an asynchronous settlement protocol, not a blocking call** - `snapshots/session/subagent-agent-preset/session.v4.jsonl:19` - the `subagent` tool result is literally the two words `started subagent {{session:2}}`; the child's answer arrives later as a `subagent-settled` notice spliced into the parent's inbox (`session.v4.jsonl:25`) and re-emitted as a `user` message at the start of the next turn. August's `subagent` currently returns the child's final answer inline; moving to a settlement-notice contract is what makes background workers, per-child progress in the UI, and "the parent may finish before the child" all possible — and the transcript shows exactly the event sequence to implement.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **The settlement notice's summary and body are separate, and the summary is a closed vocabulary** - `snapshots/session/subagent-max-tokens-partial/session.v4.jsonl:24` - three sibling scenarios pin three distinct summary strings for the same template: "finished and will do no further work unless you send it more", "failed before it finished" (`subagent-depth-two-rejection/session.v4.jsonl:24`), and "ran out of room before it finished" (`subagent-max-tokens-partial/session.v4.jsonl:24`). August's `turn_end {reason}` vocabulary is the same idea; what transfers is that the *child's* fate gets its own closed vocabulary rather than being paraphrased in prose.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A per-tool depth budget is published to the child AND separately enforced** - `snapshots/session/subagent-depth-two-rejection/session.2.v4.jsonl:12` - the runtime context carries one section per delegation tool name (`tool:subagent:depth` says "current 2, maximum 2, remaining levels 0"; `tool:subagent_fork:depth` says "current 2, maximum 1" — the two tools have *independent* caps), and the runtime still refuses the third generation (`session.2.v4.jsonl:18`, "Error: subagent depth 3 exceeds maxDepth 2"). August publishes one global delegation depth today; publishing it per tool, with current/max/remaining, gives the model the information it needs to stop trying without giving it the authority to go deeper.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **Tool-surface filtering is enforced at dispatch and the refusal is typed** - `snapshots/session/subagent-tool-filter/session.1.v4.jsonl:19` - a filtered tool produces `Error: unknown tool "write"` with `error: {name: "ToolNotFoundError", code: "UNKNOWN_TOOL"}`, and the child recovers in the next step. August's `tool_call` dispatch can name any tool, so this is the shape that makes a filtered child *observably* filtered rather than silently starved: one human-readable line for the model, one stable code for telemetry.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **The system prompt is a versioned artefact, and a mid-session prompt change appends rather than replaces** - `snapshots/session/system-prompt-in-history/session.v4.jsonl:20` - the second `system/message` record is *appended* after the cached history instead of replacing node 0, because the route declares `systemPromptUpdate: in-history` (`session.v4.jsonl:13`); the fixture then asserts the cache still hits by scripting `cacheReadTokens: 10` on the second request (`replay.override.json:18`). August rebuilds its prompt each turn; appending a delta instead is what keeps the provider prefix cache warm, and it is directly transferable.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **The prompt's rule set is a function of the mounted tool surface, and both halves are pinned** - `snapshots/session/workspace-dependencies/system-prompt.expected.md:8` - bash is disabled in this composition and the "[exit code: N] marker on every bash result" line is *gone* from the prompt; the same happens for `web_search` in `snapshots/session/web-fetch/system-prompt.expected.md:22` (no `web_search` rule, only the `web_fetch` one). August's AGENTS.md is a very large prompt contract with rules for tools that a given session may not have; deriving the rules from the tool surface and pinning both artefacts per composition is the mechanism.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A concurrency assertion built from real lifecycle events instead of sleeps** - `snapshots/session/subagent-parallel/execution-order.mjs:50` - the fixture gates the second `subagent` call on the first one's `tool/result` event, then asserts `children.every(id => ctx.agents.get(id) !== undefined)` (line 43) — i.e. *both children existed at the same time*, which is the real meaning of parallel — and releases the second child's first step only after the first has settled (lines 62-68). August cannot currently assert that two subagents overlapped; this is a complete, clock-free recipe for it.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A replay adapter that fails loudly when the script is exhausted** - `snapshots/session/subagent-depth-two-rejection/session.1.v4.jsonl:30` - "llm-replay: script exhausted — session requested model call #3 but its script has only 2; re-record the scenario", recorded as an `assistant/attempt` event (a model call that produced no message) and as the turn's `reason: {kind: "error"}`. A replay harness that returns an empty answer instead would green a broken fixture; this one names the fix.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **One scenario holds both the OLD on-disk format and the current writer's output** - `snapshots/session/subagent-multi/writer.expected.jsonl:18` - the retained generation is v0 (`session.jsonl`, whose assistant stream is stored as individual chunk records), and `writer.expected.jsonl` is the same run re-serialised by the current writer in v4; `snapshot.yml` declares `sessionFormat: {version: 0, coverage: [multi-hop, shipped-profile]}` so a writer bump cannot rewrite it. August's session persistence has no equivalent oracle, so a migration can change the on-disk shape with nothing to compare it to.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **Deterministic external services: real transport, faked authority, real recorded URL** - `snapshots/session/web-fetch/web-fetch-fixture-server.mjs:48` - the resolver maps only the recorded hostname `public.test` to `127.0.0.1` and the transport URL differs from the recorded URL *only in its port* (line 79), while the result is rewritten back to the recorded URL (line 62); the served page carries named entities, a GFM table and nested formatting so the markdown path is exercised too. August's web tools can be made deterministic this way without stubbing the tool.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **Interception that refuses to restore a global it no longer owns** - `snapshots/session/web-search-endpoint-guidance/web-search-error-fixture.mjs:56` - the cleanup throws if `globalThis.fetch` is not the fixture's own wrapper ("global fetch owner changed before cleanup"), and the URL rewriter throws on any *other* host under the recorded authority (line 31). A test that patches a global and restores it later can restore the wrong thing; both of these turn silent cross-test corruption into a named failure.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **Failure is a typed event, not just a string** - `snapshots/session/subagent-child-question-rejection/session.1.v4.jsonl:18` (`error: {name: "UserQuestionError", code: "DELEGATED_CALLER"}`), `snapshots/session/team-targets/session.v4.jsonl:22` (`TeamError` / `TEAM_SELF_MESSAGE`), `snapshots/session/subagent-tool-filter/session.1.v4.jsonl:19` (`ToolNotFoundError` / `UNKNOWN_TOOL`), and the ACP refusal whose *diagnostic* is a separate line of the error text (`snapshots/session/subagent-acp-diagnostic/session.v2.jsonl:16`). August's error strings are consumed by the model but are not machine-classified; these three codes are enough to route a denial, a policy refusal and a missing tool differently in logs and in the UI.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A delegated child cannot ask the human, and the refusal says how to recover** - `snapshots/session/subagent-child-question-rejection/session.1.v4.jsonl:18` - "human interaction is unavailable while the calling agent is owned by another live agent; include the unresolved question or decision in the child agent's final result", and the child duly answers "UNRESOLVED: Should deployment use the CUDA fallback?" (`session.1.v4.jsonl:21`), which reaches the parent as a settlement notice (`session.v4.jsonl:24`). August's Bot/room turns can deadlock on a question; this contract (refuse at the seam, name the recovery path, deliver the question in the child's result) closes the loop without a UI.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A parent can steer a running child mid-run, at a step boundary** - `snapshots/session/subagent-structured-parent/session.1.v4.jsonl:18` - the parent's correction arrives as an `agent-message` inbox notice ("Correction: submit answer 42 instead."), the child revises, and the second `structured_output {answer: 42}` succeeds (line 24); the parent's structured payload then arrives inside the settlement notice (`snapshots/session/subagent-structured-parent/session.v4.jsonl:18`). August's subagent result is final on arrival; this is the mechanism for a supervisor changing a worker's plan.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A structured result is a tool call, and the prompt says so** - `snapshots/session/subagent-structured-parent/system-prompt.1.expected.md:32` - "When you have your final answer, you MUST report it by calling the `structured_output` tool with arguments matching its parameter schema exactly. Do not finish with a plain text answer: only the tool call counts as your result." August parses subagent output as prose; making the answer a typed tool call means the parent never parses it, and the child's "closing message" and its "result" become two different things.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **Every shell command is an observable job, even an instant one** - `snapshots/session/tool-call-turn/session.v4.jsonl:17` - `job/registered` and `job/settled` bracket the result of a one-line `echo`, carrying `jobId`, `owner`, `kind`, `label`, `startedAt` and the originating `toolCall`. August runs commands through its own executor; this pair of events is what makes a background-job list (`snapshots/web/background-job-list/running.expected.md:3`) and a "stop this command" button possible without special-casing long commands.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **Approval is a two-event handshake with a *scoped* outcome** - `snapshots/web/approval-composer/session.v2.jsonl:20` - `approval/asked {id, toolName, callId, reason}` followed by `approval/decided {outcome: "allowed-once"}`, with the model's own justification in the `reason`. The decision is part of the transcript, so a replay reproduces exactly which commands ran; and "allowed-once" is not a policy change, so the next escalation asks again.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A cwd change is an event with a notice, and a deleted cwd is recovered automatically** - `snapshots/session/working-directory/session.v4.jsonl:56` - the harness detects that the current directory vanished and moves the session back to its root, announcing "The working directory \"{{cwd}}/second\" is unavailable. The working directory is now \"{{cwd}}\"."; the runtime-context message is re-emitted after *every* change (line 43), so the model always sees the current directory. August's session cwd is fixed at creation; this is the shape for a harness that lets the agent move.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A failing external call is reported as guidance, and the model is forbidden from retrying** - `snapshots/session/web-search-endpoint-guidance/session.v4.jsonl:17` - the tool error names the endpoint that failed ("The web search request used endpoint \"http://127.0.0.1:43118/anthropic/v1/messages\"…"), and the fixture pins the model's markdown report beginning "The single `web_search` call failed; no retry was made." — the *shape* of a failure report is frozen, so "don't retry on 401" is an assertion rather than a hope.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **The UI oracle is an accessibility tree with normalised volatile tokens** - `snapshots/web/auto-review-denial/ui.expected.md:82` - the trajectory is a table of typed rows (`USER`, `Request #1 ASSISTANT`, `TOOL`, `SUBTOOL`) with an arrow notation, and the event-details panel has Summary / Payload / Result / Schema / Timing tabs; volatile values appear as `{{duration}}`, `{{clock}}`, `{{workspace}}`. August's UI checks would get role/name/state assertions instead of screenshots, and would stop breaking on timing.
- **[dsh-snapshots#6]** - **A collapsed run of tool calls stays one line; the details are on demand** - `snapshots/web/auto-review-denial/ui.expected.md:14` - one button "Called tools, ran code, ran commands" collapses the run, and expanding reveals each call's `IN { … } OUT Error: …` line plus an "Inspect" button (lines 42-48). This is the same shape as August's ActivityGroup, with the addition that the *kind* of each call is named in the collapsed phrase.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Collapse the whole tool surface into one call, and give the model a typed SDK instead of a bag of schemas** - `snapshots/web/ptc-round/system-prompt.expected.md:5` - in `web-ptc` mode `run_code` is the *only* directly callable tool ("a tool call naming any other tool fails") and every other tool becomes a typed binding inside the program. This transfers to August directly: one schema means one stable provider prefix no matter how many tools exist, the model can batch and branch tool calls in ordinary TypeScript instead of one-call-per-round, and `Promise.all` becomes a *concurrency primitive* the model controls ("Independent read-only calls MAY overlap under `Promise.all` (safe calls run concurrently; mutating calls run alone, in submission order)" — `:41`).
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Type the tool RESULT, not just the tool arguments — including the error arms** - `snapshots/web/ptc-round/system-prompt.expected.md:355` - the prompt carries a full `ToolOutputMap` whose entries are discriminated unions (`{kind: "background"} | {kind: "promoted"} | {kind: "foreground"}` for bash at `:363`; `invalid_prompt | invalid_selector | invalid_rule | invalid_time_zone | not_future | time_out_of_range | frequency_too_high | subagent_session | internal_error` for `schedule_create`, first error arm at `:594`). August's tool results are mostly free text today; a typed result lets the *model* branch on failure without parsing prose, and lets the harness's own tests assert on structure.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Give the model a typed rejection instead of a stringified error** - `snapshots/web/ptc-round/system-prompt.expected.md:921` - `declare class ToolCallError extends Error { readonly toolName: ToolName }` plus the prompt sentence "A FAILED tool call rejects with `ToolCallError`, whose `toolName` identifies the failed tool and whose `message` is human-readable — `try/catch` it to handle and continue" (`:40`). August's `[Validation Error] … Do NOT stop` self-heal is the opposite: it aborts the tool and hopes the model retries. A rejection the model can catch inside one turn is strictly better.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Record the token-level stream, not just the final text** - `snapshots/web/fresh-round-trip/session.v4.jsonl:16` - the `assistant/message` event carries a `stream` array with `block-start`/`block-end`, `reasoning-chunks` holding a per-token `dt[]` timing array and `texts[]`, `tool-call-chunks` holding the argument deltas as `args[]`, plus `usage` and `finish`. That makes the *streaming* behaviour of reasoning and tool-argument assembly replayable and assertable — the token cadence, the reasoning trace and the tool-call argument stream are all part of the recorded truth. August currently has no equivalent of this.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Make the request header say WHY it was re-sent** - `snapshots/web/fresh-round-trip/session.v4.jsonl:13` - `request/header` carries `reason` ∈ `{initial, series, change}`; `series` means "same header, keep the cache" (turn 2 of the goal run, `snapshots/web/goal-multi-turn-actions/session.v4.jsonl:63`), `change` means "the prefix changed, the cache is gone" (`snapshots/web/plan-review/session.v2.jsonl:23`). The corpus gate counts exactly the `change` headers (`packages/test-support/session-snapshot/src/suite.ts:607-615`) and requires one tool-schema set per header change (`:1513-1515`). August's "cache hit %" chip is derived from a number nobody can audit; this is the auditable version.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **One inbox, typed by cause, with the insertion point named** - `snapshots/web/cordis-tool-round/session.v3.jsonl:33` - `agent/inbox/spliced` carries `target: "next-turn" | "next-step"` and the `source.kind` of what is being delivered: `goal` (a new goal round), `plugin` (an async plugin result), `subagent-settled` (a background child finished), `user-approval` (the approval policy changed), `compact-checkpoint`, `tool-goal`. August has several of these concepts scattered; this is one door with a typed cause and a declared insertion point, and the "the world changed, continue" message is a first-class transcript citizen.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Say what a failed call means, in a form the model can act on** - `snapshots/web/permission-policy-context/session.v4.jsonl:69` - the denial is literally `Error: [sandbox: file access denied under read-only mode] [sandbox: escalation available — retry this exact op…]`, and the model's retry (`:73`) is the *same operation* plus `sandbox_permissions` + `justification`, producing `approval/asked` → `approval/decided {outcome: "allowed-once"}` (`:74-75`). The phrase "retry this exact op" is a contract: the harness can verify the retry was the same op, and August's marker-table lesson ("a marker table has to be checked against every emitter") is exactly this shape — a machine-readable marker plus a required response.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Make compaction a first-class event with a structured summary** - `snapshots/web/minimal-compact/session.v4.jsonl:19` - `compaction/start` → `compaction/summary` (an array of content blocks, not a string) → a `compact-checkpoint` user message (`:21`) → `compaction/end`, each carrying `compactionId` + `sourceCommandId`, and a `command/done` reporting "Compacted 2 history items (~354 tokens)". August's compaction currently rewrites history silently; here the summary is a durable, labelled, countable artefact in the same log as everything else, and the UI can render it as a disclosure.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Let a replay fixture capture a runtime id from an earlier request** - `snapshots/web/file-upload-round/replay.override.json:20` - the override's tool call carries `"file_path": "{{fromRequest:saved at \"([^\"]+)\"}}"`, a **regex capture taken from an earlier request** and substituted at replay time; `snapshots/web/goal-multi-turn-actions/replay.override.json:140` does the same for `{{fromRequest:goal-[0-9a-f-]+}}`. This is how a fixture can exercise a real coupling (upload → read the uploaded file; create goal → complete that goal) without freezing a uuid that changes every run.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Pin the prompt and the schema once per header class, and let every scenario borrow them** - `snapshots/web/fresh-round-trip/snapshot.yml:1` - one scenario per composition/header class carries `pin: true` and owns the `system-prompt.expected.md` + `tool-schemas.expected.json`; every other scenario resolves them from that owner. The corpus gate rejects a duplicate pin and rejects a scenario with no pin for its class (`scripts/session-snapshot-corpus.corpus.ts:116-120`). The payoff is that a prompt change is a one-file diff, and the *presence* of the sidecar is itself a test that the class still exists.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Keep the effect oracle independent of the model's prose** - `snapshots/web/changed-files-turn/workspace.expected/intro.md:1` - the expected final bytes live in `workspace.expected/`, and `snapshots/AGENTS.md:15` says it plainly: "Record and refresh do not rewrite this independent oracle. Model prose and tool-result text do not prove the external effect." The corpus gate ties the oracle's existence to `workspace.final: true` and requires the `.empty` marker exactly when the tree is empty (`scripts/session-snapshot-corpus.corpus.ts:146-153`). August's diff gates assert on structure; this asserts on the *world*.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Make the sidecar carry the tool set per request header, not per turn** - `snapshots/web/fresh-round-trip/tool-schemas.expected.json:997` - the schema file is `{initial: Tool[], changes: Tool[][]}` and the `changes` array has one entry per `request/header` whose reason is `change`. `snapshots/web/minimal-compact/tool-schemas.expected.json:49` shows the `changes` entry present even when the tool set is unchanged, while `snapshots/web/minimal-preset/tool-schemas.expected.json:49` has `changes: []`. The file is therefore a *prefix-stability ledger*: a reader can tell exactly which requests changed the model's world-view, and a diff in that file is a diff in the provider prefix.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Keep the trajectory (raw event ledger) separate from the chat (projection)** - `snapshots/web/navigation-panes/trajectory.expected.md:1` - the Trajectory tab shows `SYSTEM | USER | ASSISTANT | TOOL` rows including the SYSTEM row the chat hides, an `Event details` pane with `Summary | Payload | Result | Schema | Timing`, and a Timing panel that separates TTFT from Generation (`snapshots/web/navigation-panes/timing.expected.md:1`). August's transcript is a projection; having the source ledger one tab away is what turns "the model behaved oddly" into "the `request/header` changed here".
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Keep the tool-set growth visible in the UI** - `snapshots/web/collapse-timing/next-message.expected.md:14` - the second turn renders a `Tools updated 31 added` disclosure. The thing that breaks a provider cache is the tool set changing between requests; surfacing it as a first-class transcript line makes a cache regression visible to the user rather than leaving it as an unexplained `Cache hit 51%`.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Type the failure at the wire boundary and name the failing field** - `snapshots/web/message-feedback-protocol/protocol.expected.json:20` - an invalid rating produces `code: "gateway/input-invalid"`, `message: "typert gateway: messageFeedback/put: wire field \"request\" failed boundary validation"` and `details: {endpoint, field}`. And the concurrency conflict (`:142`) returns `code: "version-conflict"` **together with the current stored row**, so the client can show what is actually there and let the user decide.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Give the queue a typed payload, not just text** - `snapshots/web/question-composer/queued.expected.md:22` - a queued message can be `{"kind": "answer_to_pending_question", "tool": "ask_user_question", "callId": …, "questions": [...], "answers": [...]}`: a *structured* reply to a tool that is still waiting, with the original question embedded so the row is self-describing. August's queue is text-only; a typed queue payload is what lets a queued message satisfy a pending interaction instead of confusing it.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Name the other product surfaces in a busy error** - `snapshots/web/queue-actions/writer-held.expected.md:1` - "This session is already in use, possibly by another running DSH instance (such as dsh web or the desktop app). Quit other running DSH instances and try again." A user-facing lock error that names the programs to quit is worth more than "busy".
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Tell the user how long the wait will be** - `snapshots/web/live-interactions/retry-request.expected.md:13` - the request panel shows `Retry: 1 of 5` and `Retry delay: 25 ms`, and the retry group in the transcript reads `Retried model request (1/5)`. A harness that refuses a server-requested wait should still *show* the wait it is about to take; August's rule that a 3600 s `Retry-After` is refused rather than absorbed is the same instinct, and this is how it is made visible.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Give the queue steer/edit/remove, and a keyboard gesture** - `snapshots/web/queue-actions/collapsed.expected.md:15` - each queued item exposes Edit / Remove / **Steer**, and the composer says "Cmd/Ctrl+Enter steers all queued messages"; `snapshots/web/queue-actions/sending.expected.md:17` shows the sending state disabling all three. Steering (inject into the *running* turn) is the capability August's queued-message model does not have.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Express a tool's timing union in JSON Schema so malformed input is rejected at the schema** - `snapshots/web/fresh-round-trip/tool-schemas.expected.json:486` - `schedule_create` carries a `oneOf` of `after_seconds | every_seconds | daily | weekly | cron | at`, with `additionalProperties: false` on each object and `required` lists. The harness never has to parse a malformed reminder; the provider's own schema layer refuses it.
- **[dsh-snapshots#7]** - **Keep a corpus policy that forces a migration baseline and caps history** - `scripts/session-snapshot-corpus-policy.ts:105` - retained historical roles are capped at 13 repository-wide, and the corpus must keep a baseline/current majority (`:108-112`); a retained generation may sit at the *current* version only if it pins retired tools (`:75-80`). The pinned expectation is `retainedRoles: 13, retainedScenarios: 10` (`scripts/session-snapshot-corpus.corpus.ts:212-215`). This is the mechanism that lets August keep old session fixtures loadable without letting the fixture corpus rot. ---
- **[dsh-snapshots#8]** - **A tool call's *stream* is recorded as per-fragment argument deltas, not just the final JSON** — `snapshots/web/seeded-history/session.v3.jsonl:8` (the `tool-call-chunks` record carries `"args":["","{","\"","file","_path","\"",": ","\"","a",".txt","\"","}"]` plus a `dt` array of inter-fragment delays, alongside `reasoning-chunks` and `text-chunks`). *Why it matters for August:* August's whole tool-call reliability story depends on arguments arriving in fragments and on models emitting malformed JSON mid-stream. DSH makes the *wire* replayable, so a test can drive a partially-streamed, badly-escaped argument string and assert the UI and the accumulator both behave. August's `json_salvage.parse_tool_arguments` salvage path (per AGENTS.md) has no equivalent recorded input in this repo — building a fixture that replays a *fragmented* malformed argument stream would pin the salvage ladder, not just the function.
- **[dsh-snapshots#8]** - **Steering is a *targeted* injection into the agent inbox, with the re-route recorded as a cancel + a re-splice** — `snapshots/web/steering/session.v4.jsonl:16` (splice for `next-turn`), `:17` (the same splice cancelled with `"outcome":"canceled"`), `:18` (re-spliced for `next-step`), and `:25` (only now does it become a `user/message` on the surface). *Why it matters for August:* August's "interjection" concept (and any mid-turn steering) needs an explicit statement of *where* the message lands — this turn vs this step — and a record of the decline, so a user message that arrives at the wrong moment is diagnosable from the log rather than inferred from a symptom. The two-event re-route is a cheap, high-value audit trail.
- **[dsh-snapshots#8]** - **A policy refusal is a successful tool result, not an exception** — `snapshots/web/subagent-fork-schedule/session.1.v4.jsonl:32` (all four `schedule_*` calls return `{"code":"subagent_session","message":"A delegated subagent cannot use reminders."}` with `"isError": false`). *Why it matters for August:* August's authority/denial rules (the `_authority_refusal` door, the subagent deny set, the refusal-marker table that AGENTS.md says was wrong for 52 rounds) are exactly this shape of decision. Encoding a refusal as a *uniform, non-error, machine-readable* result means the model can read the rule and stop, the transcript shows the guardrail firing, and the receipt vocabulary does not have to learn a second "error" spelling. This file is a concrete worked example of the uniform-refusal pattern August's `Blocked:` vs `[Blocked]` bug got wrong.
- **[dsh-snapshots#8]** - **A delegated child's authority is narrowed *by the delegation*, explicitly** — `snapshots/web/subagent-fork-schedule/session.1.v4.jsonl:22` (`{"type":"approval/policy","data":{"policy":"never","source":"delegation"}}`, against the parent's `"policy":"ask"` at `session.v4.jsonl:4`) and `:1` (`"delegationDepth":1`, `"parentSession"`, `"origin":"subagent"`). *Why it matters for August:* August's inheritance rules (`permissions: []` meaning inherit, `_effectivePermissions`, the deny-set-not-withheld-surface decision) are subtle and were, per AGENTS.md, wrong in the dangerous direction at least twice. DSH's rule — the parent grants the child a *narrower, pre-decided* scope, with the narrowing attributed to a named source — is the shape August wants, and `source: "delegation"` is the kind of attribution that makes a refusal explainable.
- **[dsh-snapshots#8]** - **The parent learns about its child from a log EVENT, not from a query** — `snapshots/web/subagent-fork-schedule/session.v4.jsonl:19` (`{"type":"subagent/catalog","data":{"childId":"{{session:2}}","mode":"continuable","label":"…","childCreatedAt":…}}`) and the matching `subagent/descriptor` at `session.1.v4.jsonl:20`. *Why it matters for August:* a cold-resumed parent must still know it has children, and a child must know its own mode ("continuable" vs "one-shot") and its label. Putting the roster in the event log means the tree survives a restart with no extra state and no reconciliation step. The `mode` field is also the *UI contract*: `snapshots/web/subagent-conversation/tree.expected.md:2` shows "continuable" spelled out in the row, so a user knows whether they can follow up before they click.
- **[dsh-snapshots#8]** - **The subagent's delivery contract is stated in the prompt, including the liveness guarantee** — `snapshots/web/subagent-conversation/ui.expected.md:16` ("Your parent agent id is \"session-{{uuid}}\". Before you finish, send your result to that agent with send_message({…}). The parent shares your workspace but does not automatically receive your transcript, tool output, or reasoning. Send earlier messages as well when a finding changes what the parent should do next; sending a message does not end your turn."). *Why it matters for August:* the "sending a message does not end your turn" clause is a *liveness* rule that prevents a delegate from finishing early; and the explicit list of what the parent does NOT get prevents the model from assuming it can just stop and be understood. The golden pins the exact wording, so the contract is versioned like code. August's `send_message` / `subagent` split would benefit from the same explicit contract text, golden-pinned.

Every post-dispatch failure appends the resolved endpoint, names the settings page, names the config field, offers a deployment-config alternative, and ends with "Only the user should choose or change the endpoint." August's harness has the same need (a provider baseUrl the user must change) and the same hazard (a model that edits its own endpoint).
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **One settings snapshot per operation so a mid-flight settings write cannot cross-contaminate** — `packages/web/web-search-deepseek/src/provider.ts:220-242` (the snapshot is taken *before* the credential await) and `packages/web/web-search-deepseek/src/index.ts:99-137` (the options thunk). The test at `packages/web/web-search-deepseek/tests/deepseek.spec.ts:355-380` proves the key resolved from the *before* section never reaches the *after* section's origin. August's `providers.json` / `config.json` hot-reload path has the identical hazard.
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **A bounded output ring with absolute offsets, a UTF-8-safe tail, and "lossy" instead of "error"** — `packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/ring.ts:27-112`. Offsets never move once assigned (so an observer's cursor survives eviction), a lone oversized chunk is trimmed to a code-point-safe tail and marked `gapBefore`, and a reader below the retained window gets `lossy: true` rather than an exception. This is the shape August's tool-result spill/read path wants: bounded memory, stable cursors, and an explicit "you missed bytes" flag instead of a hard failure.
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **Settlement is first-wins, the event is last, and it reports whether it released a waiter** — `packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:603-637`. The earliest terminal outcome records once, the ring is trimmed (never below the bytes the model cursor has not consumed), every waiter is released, and only then does the `settled` event fire — carrying `awaited`, so a completion reporter never re-announces a result a waiting caller already collected. August's turn-end event ledger would gain a lot from the `awaited` idea.
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **Refuse to start work that nobody can collect** — `packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:209-211` and `packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:382-386`. `start()` throws "no job controller serves this agent (load @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs in its composition)" rather than launching work that no one can read or stop, and the check is *owner-relative* (scope layers) rather than process-wide. August's "start a background task" tools should refuse a start whose completion nobody would be told about.
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **Cap the self-exciting chain of background-completion wakeups** — `packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:296-308` and `packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:212-218`. `maxConsecutiveWakes` bounds how many turns one owner may have opened by a completion wake; past the cap the notice degrades to injection; only a *user-authored* claimed message refills the budget. This is precisely the failure mode of August's unattended Bot path, expressed as a per-owner turn budget with an explicit, documented cost (a notice past the cap waits silently for the next user input).
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **Teardown that cannot deadlock: a throwing cancel force-fails only the record and says the work may be orphaned** — `packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:694-714`. The registry never claims the work stopped; it force-fails the *record* and warns. A cancel that returns without settling cannot be distinguished from a slow stop, and the README states that limit instead of hiding it. August's shutdown paths should adopt "force-fail the record, report the possible orphan" rather than awaiting a producer that may never return.
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **An abstract service that refuses to be loaded directly** — `packages/jobs/jobs/src/index.ts:89-95`. `if (new.target === JobRegistry) throw new Error('… is the abstract job registry seam; load an implementation such as @deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs-local instead')`. A composition row naming the seam would otherwise register a service with no method implementations and fail far from the misconfiguration.
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **A projection that keeps the kind an open string** — `packages/jobs/jobs/src/view.ts:68-72` and `packages/jobs/jobs/tests/service.spec.ts:131-138`. A browser bundle or a generated Remote codec sees only the `JobKindMap` merges its own program compiles, so a literal union would reject `pwsh`, `pty-send` and every kind another package registers. August's tool-kind and provider-kind vocabularies should stay open at the projection boundary even if they are closed at the registry.
- **[dsh-web-context#2]** - **The consumer owns the model-facing schema; the seam owns the vocabulary** — `packages/web/tool-web/README.md:96-97` and `packages/web/web/README.md:96-101`. The tools never call a provider's `available()` and never enumerate providers; the service never renders. The consequence is that a *tool* schema can stay stable while the provider set changes, which is exactly the property August needs when it swaps a gateway adapter underneath a running conversation.
